*ēn stūnag ī pad āsmān paydāg bawēd kē mardōmān sanwar xwānēnd harw čē
dabr zard sabz ud suxr ud xšēn ud [harukēn]{.underline} waxšōmand*

"this column that appears in the sky, which people call the Bow, (is)
everything that (is) violet (?), yellow, green, red, and dark blue (?),
they are [all]{.underline} blazing (?)" (*Bd*.21e.5) (rainbow colors:
red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet)

## The use of Pre- and postpositions with enclitic pronouns 2

This section deals with what may seem like a counter-intuitive use of
the *aziš*, etc., so study it well!

### *aziš*, *padiš*, and *awiš* as postpositions

When *az*, *pad*, and *ō* become postpositions, an element *-iš* is
added that has no meaning of its own (*aziš*, *padiš*, and *awiš*).
\[Compare Old Persian *patiš mām* "against me," where we have *patiš*
instead of *patiy*.\]

Unfortunately, these are spelled just like the prepositions + governed
enclitic pronoun, which makes this one of the trickier aspects of
Pahlavi grammar. The student should examine the examples below very
carefully.

\... *aziš* ÍcÅ \<hcš\> "from \..."

\... *padiš* ÍTP \<ptš\> "on \..., with \..., etc."

\... *awiš* ÍBwA \<'wbš\> "to \..."

An additional complication occurs in relative clauses, since *kē-š(ān)*
can be a relative by itself 'who his/their' (see Lesson 5 on "Whose").
Here, it needs to be determined from the context whether the
postposition goes with the relative, with the enclitic pronoun, or with
both.

Examples:

#### *awiš* postposition

##### With personal pronouns:

*u-[m]{.underline} rēmanīh [awiš]{.underline} abganēnd*

"they throw impurities [at me]{.underline}" \[not, e.g., "they throw my
(*-m*) impurities at him (*aw-iš*)"\] (after *PR*.18d.12)

*spazgīh ma kun kū-[t]{.underline} dusrawīh ud druwandīh
[awiš]{.underline} nē rasēd*

"do not slander, so that bad fame and wickedness may not come [upon
you]{.underline}" (*MX*.1.8-9)

*ō tō bē daham zarduxšt kē-[t]{.underline} hōm ud zōhr
[awiš]{.underline} rēzēd*

"I give to you (= a river!) Zarduxšt, who will pour *hōm* and libations
[into you]{.underline}" (after *Bd*.11C.1)

*ast grōh kē-[mān]{.underline} [awiš]{.underline} hamē āyēnd*

"there is one group (of people) who keep coming [to us]{.underline}"
(*DD*.65.17)

*ud anāgīh ī-[šān]{.underline} nūn az mardōmān bē [awiš]{.underline}
hamē rasēd*

"and the evil that (here and) now comes [upon them]{.underline} from
people" (*PR*.14.2)

Note both *bē* and *hamē*!

##### With relative pronouns:

*pursišn. mard-ēw kē duxt-ēw pad duxtarīh pad ō mard dahēd ēg-iš sālārīh
pad kē.*

*passox. pad ōy [kē-š awiš]{.underline} dahēd*

"Q.: a man who gives a daughter to some man to be his daughter, then,
with whom does her guardianship rest?

A.: With him [to whom]{.underline} he gives (her)" (*RAF*.6.1)

Note: *kē-š awiš* could also be analyzed as "to whom (*kē*) he gives her
(*-š*), but similar examples show that the above interpretation is more
likely. -- *pad ō* may be for *bē ō*.

*ud abar [kē-šān]{.underline} wināh tōzišn [awiš]{.underline} nē bawēd*

"and about '(those) [for whom]{.underline} there will be no redemption
for (their) sins'" (*Dk*.8.31.41)

Note *awiš-išān*:

*ud az ōz ud zōr ud nērōg ud rāy ud xwarrah [ī]{.underline} wisp-tuwān
dādār Ohrmazd [awiš-išān]{.underline} dād estēd was burdār hēnd nēkīh*

"and, from (= because of) the strength, power, and might and Light and
Xwarrah [which]{.underline} the almighty Creator Ohrmazd has given [to
them]{.underline} (the fravashis), they are carriers of much goodness"
(*StS*.19.6)

for:

*\... ī-[šān]{.underline} wisp-tuwān dādār Ohrmazd [awiš]{.underline}
dād estēd \...*

##### With *kū* "where':

*ud grift ī ān ī abartom mizd [kū]{.underline} rāh ī [awiš]{.underline}
abē-āhangīh az wināh frāz-āhangīh ō kerbag*

"\... and seizing the supreme reward, [whereto]{.underline} (to which)
the road is being without inclination from (= toward) sin (and) having
forward inclination toward good deeds" (*Dk*.5.9.2)

*harw 2 (rōd) pad zrēy ī Frāxkerd ō ham rasēnd ud abāz ō bun-xān rasēnd
[kū aziš]{.underline} bē tazīd hēnd*

"both (rivers) come together in the Frāxkerd ocean and come back to
their sources, [wherefrom]{.underline} (whence) they flowed" (*Bd*.11.5)

#### *aziš* postposition

##### With personal pronouns:

*ēn-iz guft estēd kū harw kas bē abāyēd dānistan kū az kū bē mad ham ud
čim ēdar ham u-m abāz ō kū abāyēd šudan u-[m]{.underline} čē
[aziš]{.underline} xwāhēnd*

"this too it is said: everybody should know: from where did I come, and
why am I here, where must I return to, and what will they ask [of
me]{.underline} (ask me)?" (*PT*.11.11)

*u-[š]{.underline} āsmān [aziš]{.underline} bē tarsīd čiyōn gōspand az
gurg*

"and the sky was afraid [of him]{.underline} (the Evil Spirit), like a
sheep of the wolf" (*Bd*.4.10b)

*pas Sām abar āxēzēd ud padīrag ī Ažidahāg šawēd u-[š]{.underline}
saxwan [aziš]{.underline}* \<MNš!\> *nē āšnawēd u-š gad ī pērōzgar ō sar
pahikōbēd ud zanēd ud ōzanēd*

"then Sām (Karsāsp) rises and goes against Ažidahāg (a dragon); and he
hears no word [from him]{.underline} (the Evil Spirit); and he strikes
the victorious cudgel at its head and strikes and kills it" (after
*ZWY*.9.22)

*kū-[mān]{.underline} anāgīh ī Ganāg Mēnōy [aziš]{.underline} abāz dār*

"i.e., keep the Foul Spirit's evil away [from us]{.underline}!"
(*PV*.8.21a)

Note *aziš-išān*:

*ud handarz ī ō mardōmān abar pahrēz ī az pasīy ī ōy ahlomōγ ud nē
niyōšīdan ud nē xwastan ī [aziš-išān]{.underline} Abestāg ud Zand*

"and the advice to mankind about watching carefully the heretic from
behind and not listening to and not learning (lit., "threshing") [from
them]{.underline} the Avesta and the *zand*" (*Dk*.9.31.22**)**

for:

*u-[šān]{.underline} nē niyōšīdan ud nē xwastan ī [aziš]{.underline}*

##### With relative pronouns:

*kas-ēw nē dānam [kē]{.underline}-m nēkīh ēdōn [aziš]{.underline} ciyōn
az ašmāh*

"I know no one [from whom]{.underline} there is goodness for me like
(there is) from you" (*PY*.29.1c)

*duš-rawišnīh ī ān mēnōy [ī-š]{.underline} gannāgīh ī dāmān ī Ohrmazd
[aziš]{.underline} būd*

"the evilness of that spirit, [from whom]{.underline} the stench of
Ohrmazd's creatures came" (*Bd*.1.48)

*abar āxēz pid ī amāh čē ān kārēzār kunam ān [ī-š]{.underline} Ohrmazd
ud amahrspandān tangīh anāgīh [aziš]{.underline}*

"get up, our father, for I shall do that battle, the one [from
which]{.underline} (there will be) 'dire straights' (and) evil to
Ohrmazd and the amahrspands" (*Bd*.4.2)

*tis ān ast [ī]{.underline} ān kē andar estēd [aziš]{.underline} bē nē
ayāsēd ud ān kē andar nē estēd [awiš]{.underline} ayāsēd*

"there is that (one) thing [which]{.underline} that one who stands in
(it) does not long (to be away) [from]{.underline} and someone who does
not stand in it longs [for]{.underline}" (*Dk*.6.57) \[lit.: from it, to
it\])

Note:

*5-ēwēnag gōspand kē-š padiš 282 sardag [kē aziš-išān]{.underline}*
\[for *[kē-šān aziš]{.underline}*\] for *was gōnag padēxwīh ud nēkīh
hu-zīyišnīh ō dāmān ī Ohrmazd rasišnīg*

"five species of animals, in which (there are) 282 kinds, [from
whom]{.underline} many kinds of prosperity, goodness, and good living
will come (*rasišnīg*) to Ohrmazd's creations" (*StS*.14.5)

#### *padiš* postposition

##### With personal pronouns:

*bē gētīy nē šawam čē-[m]{.underline} anāgīh was [padiš]{.underline}
kunēnd*

"(the Fire says to Ohrmazd:) I am not going to the world of the living,
because they will do much evil [to me]{.underline}" (*PR*.46.30)

*bē hilēd kū-[š padiš]{.underline} andar tazēnd*

"permit that they set [upon him]{.underline} (attack him)!" (after
*Bd*.6c.4)

*ka-[tān]{.underline} aǰdahāg [padiš]{.underline} ōftēd*

"when the dragon falls [upon you]{.underline} (all)"

##### With relative pronouns:

*tērag ī Harburz ān [kē-š]{.underline} star māh ud xwaršēd
[padiš]{.underline} andar wardēnd [padiš]{.underline} abāz āyēnd*

"the top of Hariburz (is) the one [upon which]{.underline} the stars,
moon, and sun turn around (and) [to (which)]{.underline} they come back"
(*Bd*.9.6)

*kār ī didīgar nē dānēd kerdan [kē]{.underline}-š sazāgīh
[padiš]{.underline} ast*

"he knows (how) to do no other work [for which]{.underline} he has (*-š
\... ast*) suitability (= for which he is suited)" (after *DD*.43.3)

*ānōh was zarrēn gāh ud wistarg ī xūb ud bālišn abāg bōb passazag wēnam
[kē-šān padiš]{.underline} nišast hēnd kadag-xwadāyān ud dahīgānān
ruwān*

"there I see good seats and carpets and pillows with fitting
\*pillow-cases [on which]{.underline} the souls of the petty kings and
land-owners were seated" (*AWN*.15.4)

##### With nouns (rare):

*[Damū]{.underline} Asūrestān kadag-xwadāyīh [awiš]{.underline} dād*

"[to Damūg]{.underline} the rule over Assyria was given" *or* "(as for)
Damūg \... was given [to him]{.underline} (*aw-iš*)" (*Bd*.35.46)

*[Wispān-frīy]{.underline} Kay-Husrōy [aziš]{.underline} zād*

"from Wispānfrīy Kay-Husrōy was born" (*Bd*.35.21)

*ēd ast ān xwarrah kē-š [mardōm awiš]{.underline} dahīhist*

"this is the Xwarrah which was given by him \[agential\] [to
mankind]{.underline}" (*WZ*.3.74) \[rather than: "to which mankind was
given"\] (*WZ*.3.74)

***ašmāh ō awēšān Ohrmazd hayārīh dahēd Ašwahišt ud Šahrewar** kū
[Zardušt ud hāwištān ī Zardušt]{.underline} nēkīh [padiš]{.underline}
kunēd*

"'you, Ohrmazd (and) Ašwahišt and Šahrewar, give help to them! i.e., do
(some) goodness [for Zardušt and Zardušt's pupils]{.underline}!"
(*PY*.29.10) \[recall that bold type indicates Pahlavi rendering of
Avestan text\]

*[Ērān šahr]{.underline} was wišōbišn ud awērānīh [padiš]{.underline}
kerd*

"much destruction and laying waste was done [to Iran]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.33.6)

##### With implicit reference:

*harw čē kām[ēnd awiš]{.underline} nimāyēnd*

"(the gods) will show [to]{.underline} (them) everything
[they]{.underline} wish for" (*Dk*.6.44)

*pad nēkīh [awiš]{.underline} madārīh spāsdārīh weh*

"in order that goodness may come [to]{.underline} (one), gratitude is
the better (thing for [one]{.underline} to do)" (*MX*.1.72)

### 

### The verb

#### The pluperfect

The past tense "he (has) asked, went (has gone)" and pluperfect "he had
asked, gone" are formed with the past stem of the main verb + present
and past tenses of "to be." The past indicative forms of *šaw-* *šud*
are therefore as follows:

##### Paradigm of the pluperfect:

Simple past Pluperfect

Singular

1st *šud ham* "I went" *šud būd ham* "I had gone"

2nd *šud hē* "you went" *šud būd hē* "you had gone"

3rd *šud* "he, she, it went" *šud būd* "he, she, it had gone"

Plural

1st *šud hēm* "we went" *šud būd hēm* "we had gone"

2nd *šud hēd* "you went" *šud būd hēd* "you had gone"

3rd *šud hēnd* "they went" *šud būd hēnd* "they had gone"

#### 

#### Uses of the pluperfect

The pluperfect is used to indicate that an action or incipient state was
completed [before something else happened in the past]{.underline},
e.g.:

##### Intransitive verbs:

*ka ān dō rōd ī Ārang rōd ud Weh rōd bē [tazīd būd]{.underline} pas
abārīg ābīhā az ān nāydāgān frāz tazīd hēnd*

"when those two rivers, the river Ārang and the river Weh, [had
flowed]{.underline} out, then the other waters flowed forth from those
deep ones" (after *Bd*.6b.21)

*kū [šud būd hēnd]{.underline} abar ō ān ī murw pus ēg franaft ān ī
Zarduxšt frawaš*

"when (the snakes) [had set]{.underline} upon the child of that bird,
then Zarduxšt's fravashi went forth" (after *Dk*.7.2.27)

*ka Mānuščihr [uzīd būd]{.underline} did Afrāsyāb āmad*

"when Mānuščihr [had passed away]{.underline}, (then) Afrāsyāb came
again" (*Bd*.33.6)

##### Transitive verbs without "performer" (passive):

*ka dēw ī māzandar ud abārīg druz wisp [zad būd hēnd]{.underline} Hōšang
ō Čīnestān pad ōzadan ī aždahāgān ī amar šud*

"when the giant *dēw* and all the other lie-demons [had been stricken
down]{.underline}, Hōšang went to China to kill countless dragons"

### 

### The Subjunctive

In addition to the indicative and imperative, the Pahlavi verb also has
a subjunctive and optative.

The subjunctive stem is formed by changing the vowel of the ending to
*-ā-*. Endings:

##### Paradigm of the subjunctive:

Singular Plural

1st *-ān(ī)* Y\>wA- , YwA- , WwA- \<-'n\', -'ny, -'nd\> 1st *-ām* µA-
\<-'m\>

2nd *-āy* îÅ- , !A- , Ä- \<-'y, -'[d]{.underline}, -'y[d]{.underline}\>
2nd *-ād* WtÅ- \<-'t\'\>

3rd *-ād* WtÅ- \<-'t\'\> 3rd *-ānd* YwA- \<-'nd\>

The first singular ending is often written Y\>wA- as if it were the 3rd
plural, but probably has \<-d\> for final *-y*: *-ānī*.

##### Subjunctive of "to be":

Singular

1st *hān(ī)* WwAWNwA , YwAWNwA \<HWE'n(y)\>

3rd *hād* WTWNwA , WtÅWNwA \<HWE\''t\', HWE\'t\'\>

Plural

3rd *hānd* YwAWNwA \<HWE\''nd\>

Note: The 3rd sg. form WTWNwA (HWE\'t\') is not uncommon, especially in
compound tenses, but it is more common as the particle *hād*, see below.

On the use of *hād* \<HWEt\'\> for *hē* as irrealis, see Lesson 16.

Note also the short form *bād* \<b't\'\> beside *bawād*.

##### Paradigm of the subjunctive:

Present Past Pluperfect

Singular

1st *šawān(ī)* WwAWwlZW , YwAWwlZW *šud hān(ī)* *šud būd hān(ī)*

2st *šawāy* !AWwlZW

3rd *šawād* WtÅwAWwlZW *šud hād* *šud būd hād*

Plural

1st *šawām* µAWwlZW

2st *šawād* WtÅWwlZW

3rd *šawānd* YwAWwlZW *šud hānd* *šud būd hānd*

### Uses of the subjunctive

The subjunctive is used in both main and subordinate clauses.

#### In main clauses

##### Expressing an exhortation:

*dagr [zīyād]{.underline}* "long [live]{.underline}!"

*ka nēkīh-ēw bē handēšišn zūd bē [kunāy]{.underline} ud ka wattarīh-ēw
bē handēšišn az xwēš bē [spōzāy]{.underline}*

"when something good is to be considered, [you shall do]{.underline} it
quickly; when something bad is to be considered, [push it]{.underline}
away from you!" (*Ōšnar* 48)

***[dahāy]{.underline}-im Ašwahišt ān tarsagāyīh ī pad Wahuman ābādīh**
kū-m tarsagāhīh ēdōn [dahād]{.underline} ī pad tan ī pasēn abāz nē
[abāyānd]{.underline}* (*abāyānī*?) *ōzad*

"'[you shall give]{.underline} me, Ašwahišt, that respect which is lucky
through Wahuman', i.e., [he shall give]{.underline} me respect in such a
way that they shall not need to kill (me) *or*: I shall not need to be
killed again at the Final Body!" (*PY*.28.7)

*ēn az tō šašom yān hōm zayam ī dūr-ōš kū pēš az duzz ud pēš az gayg ud
pēš az gurg [wēnām]{.underline} mānišn čārag*

"this is the sixth boon I ask of you, death-averting Hōm: [let us
see]{.underline} a means to dwell (here?) before the thief, before the
highwayman, and before the wolf (sees *us*?)" (*PY*.9.21)

*pad rāstīh ud pad frārōnīh bowandag-āgāh [bē būd hānī]{.underline}*

"[let me have become]{.underline} completely aware in truthfulness and
good behavior!" (*PY*.28.10a)

##### Subjunctive with negation *ma*:

*ohrmazd guft kū-t garān [ma sahād]{.underline} zardušt*

"Ohrmazd said: [do not let it seem]{.underline} heavy to you, Zardušt!"
(*PR*. 18f.36)

*passox ō ōy dōyīd duš-dānāg Gannāy-Mēnōy kū [ma]{.underline} ēn ī man
dām [marnǰēnāy]{.underline} ahlaw Zardušt*

"the evil-knowing Foul Spirit answered him: [you shall not]{.underline}
destroy this creation of mine, Righteous Zardušt!" (*PV*.19.6)

*[ma kū hād]{.underline} ōy kas duš-xwadāy ud zūr-dādwar*

"[may not]{.underline} that person [be]{.underline} a bad ruler and a
crooked judge" (*Dk*.3.387.2)

##### Subjunctive with *ē* instead of with indicative::

This is found notably in the *ZFJ*, e.g.:

*bē [ē kunānd]{.underline} astōdān-ēw*

"let them make an ossuary!" (*ZFJ*, ms. p. 502)

*ēdōn awēšān kē mazdēsn hēnd ān wastarg [frāz-iz ē
kirrēnānd]{.underline} kū [bē ē brīnānd]{.underline} ud [bē-iz ē
nigānānd]{.underline}*

"in this way, [let those]{.underline} who are Mazdayasnian [cut it
off]{.underline}, too, i.e., [let them cut]{.underline} (it)
[away]{.underline}, and [let them bury]{.underline} (it), too!" (*ZFJ*,
pp. 512--13)

*ōy abar pad ēn zamīg bē [ē dahānd]{.underline}*

"[let them place]{.underline} him on this earth!" (*ZFJ*, ms. p. 503)

##### Subjunctive expressing future (intent):

***pad ahlāyīh ō amāh bē rasād** pad frārōnīh \... **abar
[rasānī]{.underline} ud hunsand [hānī]{.underline} ud
[padīrānī]{.underline}** kū-š bē [padīrānī]{.underline} ud hunsandīhā ōh
[kunānī]{.underline}*

"'in Righteousness [it shall come]{.underline} upon us', (i.e.) in
goodness \... '[I shall come]{.underline} upon and [I shall be
content]{.underline} and [shall accept]{.underline},' that is, [I shall
accept]{.underline} it and [shall]{.underline} contendedly
[do]{.underline} so" (*PY*.7.24)

*tō Ohrmazd **andar axwān xwadāy hē** kū pad wināh ud kerbag āmār
[kunāy]{.underline}*

"you Ohrmazd 'are lord in the (two) worlds', i.e., [you shall
do]{.underline} the accounting with respect to sins and good deeds'"
(after *PY*.31.8)

*čiyōn gōwēd kū az Srōš hamāg dēw akāmagīhā pad stōw ō tom
[dwārānd]{.underline}*

"as it says: from Srōš all the demons [shall run]{.underline}
unwillingly (and) in defeat into the darkness" (after *Bd*.26.49)

#### In subordinate clauses

##### In temporal clauses expressing future:

*kū-t mizd ēdōn stabr dahēm kū [ka]{.underline} pad mayān
[estāy]{.underline} ō kanārag nē wēnē zamīg-pahnāy ud rōd-dranāy* \[=
*-drahnāy*\] *ud xwaršēd-bālāy*

"i.e., we shall give you a reward so big that, [when you shall
stand]{.underline} in the middle, you will not see (all the way) to the
borders the thickness of the earth, the length of a river, and the
height of the sun" (*Dk.*9.35.17)

##### In subordinate clauses expressing purpose, etc.:

*ān čē-t pad bun bē padīrift [kū]{.underline} bē [hāzāy]{.underline}
harwisp ox ī astōmand ō a-dōstīh ī Ohrmazd dōstīh ī xwēš*

"that which you (Ahrimen) have received to be yours [so that you shall
induce]{.underline} the entire existence with bones not to be Ohrmazd's
friends, (but) your own friends" (*WZ*.34.35)

*čiyōn-imān ēdar pad gōšt ān ī meh bahr kunēnd [kū]{.underline}-mān
pāduxšāyīh [dahānd]{.underline}*

"in the way that here they give us the greatest share in the meat
(offering), [so that they may give]{.underline} us sovereignty"
(*Dk*.7.8.26)

*yazdān pad-iz uzwān ī gōspandān srūd andar gēhān wistard* *[kū
tā]{.underline} ān-iz gugāh [bawād]{.underline} abar-iš waxšwarīh*

"the gods also proclaimed (it) with the tongue of animals (and so)
spread (it) throughout the world [so that]{.underline} that too [should
be]{.underline} a testimony to his (Zardušt's) prophethood"
(*Dk*.7.2.61)

*šud pēš ī Zarduxšt nišast u-š sar ī Zarduxšt saxt pēčīd [kū
tā]{.underline} bē [ōzanīhād]{.underline}*

"he went before (baby) Zarduxšt, sat down, and twisted Zarduxšt's head
strongly [in order that he should be killed]{.underline}" (*WZ*.10.2)

*xīr ī gētīy ān ī frāy az paymān frāz hištan [kū tā]{.underline} gētīy
rēbagīh rāy ān (ī) weh kū gētīy az-iš appār [ma bawād]{.underline}*

"(and also:) to let go of stuff in this world that is more than the mean
[in order that]{.underline}, because of the cheating in this world, that
which is better than this world [should not be taken]{.underline} from
him" (*Dk*.6E.16)

*[tā]{.underline} gōhr ī Zarduxšt bē ō pidarān [rasād]{.underline} ēg az
ān ī amahrspandān nixwārišn ō awēšān urwar abar rawēnīd Pōrušasp 6 gāw ī
spēd ī zard-gōš*

"[in order that]{.underline} the substance of Zarduxšt [should
come]{.underline} to his parents, at the instigation of the amahrspands,
Pōrušasp was induced to drive six white, yellow-eared cows to those
plants" (*Dk*.7.2.39)

##### In indefinite relative clauses:

*dōyīd Gannāg Mēnōy ō ǰahī kū-t čē kāmag [hād]{.underline} xwāh tā-t
daham*

"the Evil Spirit lied to (= told) eh: whatever your wish [shall
be]{.underline}, ask (for it) so I may give it to you" (*Bd*.4.6)

*harw kār ud kerbag [ī]{.underline}-t tuwān [hād]{.underline} kerdan,
harw ham rōzgār ī mad estēd bē kun*

"every work and good deed [that you shall be]{.underline} able to
perform, do that on that very day every (day) it occurs!" (*PR*.28b.1)

##### With impersonal expressions of necessity, etc.:

*bē abāyēd [abesihād]{.underline} wis ī Pōrušasp* "it is necessary
(that) the house of Pōrušasp [should be annihilated]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.7.2.57)

##### In conditional clauses expressing potential future (rare):

*[agar-it kāmag hād]{.underline} Zardušt awēšān bēš tarwēnīdan \... ēg
ēn ī man nām dranǰēn kū warm bē kun*

"[if you have the wish]{.underline}, Z., to overcome their harm \...
then hold on to these names of mine, i.e., learn (them) by heart (*warm
kun*)!"

##### Past subjunctive in temporal clauses expressing (potential) completed future:

*[ka]{.underline} ōy dast frāz [šust hād]{.underline} tā 3 bār*

"[when he has washed]{.underline} (his) hands up to three times (then
let him \...)" (*PV*.9.15)

##### 'Explanatory' *hād*:

The form *hād*, usually spelled \<HWEt\>, occasionally \<HWE't\'\>, is
used to introduce exegetical explanations, "that is, that will be,"
sometimes it appears to mean something like "yes, and" or "yes, but" or
"so be it!," e.g.:

*ō man ōy passox guft Hōm ī ahlaw ī dūrōš*

*[hād]{.underline} dūrōšīh-iš ēd kū ōš az ruwān ī mardōmān dūr dārēd*

*Rōšn guft [hād]{.underline} ahōšīh pad Hōm bawēd*

"he answered me, the Righteous Hōm, the 'death-averting one' (*dūrōš*);

[that is]{.underline}, (Hōm) is said to be '*dūrōš*' for this reason:
(he) keeps death (*ōš*) far away (*dūr*) from people's souls;

Rōšn said: '[yes, and]{.underline} being 'deathless' comes about through
Hōm" (*PY*.9.2) --- Explanation of Hōm's epithet *dūrōš*, Av. *duraoša*
(whose meaning is unknown).

*zamīg kadār gyāg mustōmandtar guft:*

*[hād]{.underline} Arzūr grīwag pad dar ī dōšox kē-š hamdwārišnīh ī
dēwān padiš bawēd*

"which place of the earth is said (to be) the most oppressive?

[That will be]{.underline} the ridge of (Mount) Arzūr, at the gate of
Hell, upon which the demons run together" (*Bd*.9.11)

### Personal forms of impersonal verbs

Personal forms of some of the impersonal verbs (see Impersonal
expressions in Lesson 9) are also found, e.g.:

##### *abāyistan*

*čiyōn hēnd kū gōwēnd kū pad dastwar [abāyēnd]{.underline} dāštan*

"as there are those who say that [they need]{.underline} to be (= should
be) regarded as (spiritual) guides" (*Dk*.7.4.47)

##### *kāmistan*

*harw čē [kāmēnd]{.underline} awiš nimāyēnd*

"(the gods) will show them everything [they wish for]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.6.44)

##### *sahistan*

*ka-š tis andar nēst ī ān rāy juttar ōwōn [saham]{.underline} kū \...*

"when (= if) there is nothing in it that differs from it, [it seems to
me]{.underline} that \..." (*DD*.48.2)

##### *šāyistan*

*ud pas āb ud ātaxš ud urwar pēš ī Ohrmazd ī xwadāy pad garzišn estēd ud
garzišn ēn kunēd kū Frēdōn zīndag abāz kun tā Ažidahāg bē ōzanēd čē agar
tō Ohrmazd ēn nē kunē amāh pad gētīy nē [šāyēm]{.underline} būdan*

"then the water, fire, and plant stand before the lord Ohrmazd with
complaints; they complain (saying): make Frēdōn alive again so that he
may strike down Ažidahāg; for if you, Ohrmazd, do not do this, then [we
will not be able]{.underline} to be in this world!" (*ZWY*.9.18)

*ka awēšān ēdōn was-marag hēnd pad čē abzār bē [šāyēnd]{.underline}
abesistan*

"when (= if) these are so numerous, by what tool [are they
able]{.underline} to annihilate = [can they]{.underline} be
annihilated?" (*ZWY*.7.1)

##### *wurrōyistan (wirrōyistan**)***

*hamāg mardōm pad weh dēn ī mazdēsnān bē [wurrōyēnd]{.underline}*

"all people [will believe]{.underline} in the Good *dēn* of the
Mazdayasnians" (*ZWY*.9.7).

Note that *[passandīdan]{.underline}* "be pleased with" is always
personal, e.g.:

*ka gōwēd kū ān ī tō sahēd ayāb ān ī tō kāmēd ayāb ān ī tō
[passandē]{.underline} ayāb ān ī tō abāyēd harw 4 ēw-ēwēnag*

"when one says: 'That which seems (good) to you or that which you wish
or that which [you are pleased with]{.underline} or that which you
need', all four are one kind" (*MHD*.43.2)

*ud agar ka-š wēmārīh-ēw padiš wasān biziškān nigerīd ud dānāgān
[passandēnd]{.underline} čand abērtar pad yōǰdahrēnīdan ī az ōwōn
wizendīg nasuš dīd nē āhōg*

"and, if many doctors have looked at an illness in her (afflicting her,
the woman who has had an abortion) and the wise [are
pleased]{.underline} (with it), (then), all the more so, in order to
purify her of such a harmful *nasuš* (the carrion demon), there is no
fault in seeing (the genitals)" (*Dk*.5.24.22)

## Exclamations (Interjections)

Pahlavi has a few exclamatory words, some more common than the others,
e.g.:

##### *āfrīn/āfrīnišn (ō)* WwYWcÅ \<'p̄ryn\'\> (rarely WwïÒWcÅ \<'p̄lyn\'\>) "blessing on!, blessed be!"

*[āfrīn ō]{.underline} Srīd awestād dagr zīyād*

"[blessed be]{.underline} Srid, the teacher! May he live long!"
(*ŠnŠSup*. 22.32)

*[āfrīnišnīh]{.underline} abēzag weh dēn ī mazdēsnān*

"[blessed be]{.underline} the pure Mazdayasnian *dēn*!"

*[anāg]{.underline}* WkAwA \<'n'k\'\> "evil to \...!"

See below under *nēk*.

##### *drōd* WTwlY , MwÍ \<dlwt\', ŠRM\> "health, greetings!"

*ašmāh rāy [drōd]{.underline} az Ohrmazd xwadāy ud amahrspandān ud
[drōd]{.underline} az ahlaw Zarduxšt ī Spitāmān*

"[greetings]{.underline} to you from the lord Ohrmazd and the
*amahrspand*s, and [greetings]{.underline} from Spitamān Zarduxšt!"
(*AWN*.3.6)

*az Wištāsp-šā ī Ērān dahībed ō Arzāsp ī Xyōnān-šā [drōd]{.underline}*

"[greetings]{.underline} from King Wištāsp, Land-lord of the Iranians to
Arzāsp of the Xyōns!" (*AZ*.17)

Cf.: *drōd pursēnd ud āfrīn kunēnd* "they ask about his health and
bless/congratulate him" (*AWN*.10.3)

##### *drīst (drust) awar* nMWcÒ (WtJWwY) Wt∆DWwY \<drw(y)st\' LPNE̲\>, *drīst (drust)*, *pad-drōd awarēd* "welcome!"

On the use of *awar(ēd)* as imperative of "to come," see Lesson 7.

*[drīst]{.underline} ud weh ud [pad-drōd awarēd]{.underline}*

"[come healthy]{.underline} and good and [in health]{.underline}! =
Welcome, you (all)!" (*KN*.13/12.4)

*[ma drust awar]{.underline} sēmspār ī ǰādūg čē tō mād ǰādūg u-t pid
drōzan būd*

"[you are not welcome]{.underline}, you sorcerer stargazer, for your
mother was a sorcerer and your father a liar!" (*AZ*.51)

##### *farrox* WwaÒP \<plhw\'\> "fortunate \...!"

*[farrox]{.underline} ōy mard kē pad rāh ī šāh rawēd*

"[fortunate]{.underline} the man who walks on the path of the king!"
(*Dk*.6.173)

##### *nēk* WKwYW \<nywk\'\> "good for \...! hail!"

*[nēk tō]{.underline} kē rādān ruwān hē*

"[good]{.underline} for you, who (are) the soul(s) of the generous!"
(*AWN*.12.3)

*ruwān ō tan ēdōn gōwēd kū ay tan ī sazōmand ahlāyīh stāy pad
ul-ēstīšnīh*

*ud ka tan hamgōnag kunēd ruwān šādīhēd ud ō tan āfrīn kunēd kū [nēk tō
bawād]{.underline} ay tan ī sazōmand*

*ud ka tan ān ī ruwān āfrāh nē padīrēd ud anāg-rawišnīh gōwēd pad
ul-ēstīšnīh kū [anāg tō]{.underline} tan ī seǰōmand*

"the soul says to the body: O transient body, praise Righteousness when
you get up!

And, when the body does like that (i.e., as told), the soul is made
happy and blesses the body: [may it be good for you]{.underline}, O
transient body!

And, when the body does not accept to the instruction of the soul and
speaks 'evil to you' when getting up: [evil to you]{.underline}, O
transient body!" (after *Dk*.9.19.3-5)

##### *pahrēzōmandīh* aJNwAcdlaÅP \<p'hlyc'wmndyh\> "beware!"

*[pahrēzōmandīh]{.underline} saxwan ī dēwān ma āšnaw ud dēn bē padīr*

"[beware]{.underline}! do not listen to what the *dēw*s say, and accept
the *dēn*!" (*PR*.31c.3)

##### *pargast* Wt∆dLP , WtjïÒP \<plgst\'\> "god forbid!"

*ud tā ristāxēz ud tan ī pasēn pad was anāgīh ud pādifrāh ī ēwēnag
ēwēnag pad dōšox abāyēd būdan.*

*ud [pargast]{.underline} kū ānōh xwarišn šāyēd xwardan bē pūdag
hangōšīdag xōn homānāg*

"and until the resurrection and the final body, (they) have to be in
hell, in much evil and (suffering) various kinds of punishments; and
[god forbid]{.underline} (they) be allowed (other) food there except
rotten (things) just like (*hangōšīdag \... homānāg*) blood!" (after
*MX*.1.194)

*ud tō rāy gōwam pus ī man kē ǰahišn-hayār pad mardōmān tis ī xrad weh*

*čē [agar pargast]{.underline} xwāstag bē šawēd ayāb čahārbāy bē mīrēd
xrad bē mānēd*

"and I say to you, my son: (among the things) that help destiny among
men, the things of wisdom is best,

for if, [god forbid]{.underline}, property should go away or the
quadrupeds (= cattle) die, (then still) wisdom remains" (*Andarz ī
Ādurbād Mahrspandān* 104)

##### *šnāyišn*, *xšnāyišn* WwßÄwßA , WwßÄwÍ \<šn'dšn\', hšn'dšn\'\> "hail to \...!"

*[xšnāyišn]{.underline} dādār Ohrmazd ī rāyōmand ī xwarrahōmand ī
harwisp-āgāh ī dānāg ī tuwānāg ī mahist humad hūxt huwaršt pad menišn
gōwišn kunišn*

"[hail]{.underline} to Ohrmazd the creator, luminous and full of
Xwarrah, all-knowing, wise, who is greatest (with respect) to having
thought (good thoughts) in his thought, having spoken (good speech) in
his speech, and having performed (good acts) with his action!"
(*Bd*.0.0)

##### wāy "woe!"

*wāy ō mardōm bawād* \[subj.\]

"*woe* to mankind!"

##### *xunak* WKWwA \<hwnk\'\> "happy (he who \...)!"

*[xunak]{.underline} ōy tan ī wispān-dānāgīh-pēsīd dēn mazdēsn āgāh ud
rāh-nimāy bawēd*

"[happy]{.underline} that body (= person) who is aware of (= familiar
with) the Mazdayasnian *dēn*, (which is) adorned with the knowledge of
all (beings), and (is) a guide (to/in it)!" (*Dk*.5.24.30a)

*ābād* WtÅcÅ \<'p̄'t\'\> "prosperous, lucky"

This is often used with *gōw-* (also *hangār-*, *kun-*, *pad \... dār-*;
MacKenzie s.v. *āzādīh*).

*az wehān [ābādīh]{.underline} ud spās [gōwišn]{.underline}*

"one should say ['be properous!']{.underline} and gratitude (coming)
from good people" (*Dk*.6.286)

*[ābād-gōwišn]{.underline} hēnd kū saxwan čarbīhā gōwēnd ud druwand
hēnd*

"they say ['be prosperous!']{.underline}, i.e., they are mild-spoken,
but wicked" (*Dk*.7.8.13)

*[ābādīhā]{.underline} ī ka-m anāgīh ēn čē az ēn wattar šāyēd būdan*

this, for it could be worse than this!" (*WAM*.27)

#  Texts 12

### Text 12.1

From the *Mēnōy xrad*: *MX*.4.3. -- Orthography as in ms. K43 fols.
140r-141v. --- (\...) means missing in ms.

![](media/image26.jpeg){width="3.611111111111111in"
height="0.9861111111111112in"}

![](media/image27.jpeg){width="3.611111111111111in"
height="3.1527777777777777in"}

*pursīd dānāg ō mēnōy ī xrad kū zamīg kadām šādtar*

*mēnōy ī xrad passox kerd kū*

*zamīg ān šādtar kē-š mard ī ahlaw ī rāst-gōwišn mānišn padiš kunēd.*

*didīgar kē mān ī ātaxšān padiš kunēnd.*

*ud sidīgar ka**-**š gāwān ud gōspandān padiš xufsēnd.*

*čahārom a-warzīd ud an-ābādān zamīg ka abāz ō warz ud ābādānīh
āwarēnd.*

*ud panǰom kē gilistag ī xra(f)starān aziš kanēnd.*

*šašom kē ēzišn ud rasišn ī yazdān ud nišast ī wehān abar bawēd.*

*haftom ka ān ī awērān ābādān kunēnd.*

*haštom ka az xwēšīh ī wattarān ō xwēšīh ī wehān rasēd.*

*nohom ka bar ud bēd ī az-iš bawēd yazdān ud wehān ī arzānīgān bahr
kunēnd.*

*dahom kē zōhr ud ēzišn padiš kunēnd.*

### Text 12.2

From the *Dēnkard* book VI: *Dk*.6.16. -- From Madan's edition.

![](media/image28.jpeg){width="5.0in" height="1.6805555555555556in"}

*u-šān ēn-iz ōwōn dāšt kadāmīyān-iz mardōm andar harw gāh ud zamān tis ī
mēnōy pad ayād dārišn* \[ed. *dārēd*\] *ud nēkīh ī wahišt ud anāgīh ī
dōšox andar ān gāh ka āsānīh ud nēkīh ud rāmišn aw-iš mad estēd*

*ēn-iz handēšišn kū nēk-iz hād ānōh pad wahišt ka ēdar-iz ēdōn nēk*

Any person at all, in every place and time, should remember the matters
of the other world and the goodness in paradise and the evil in hell at
that time when comfort and goodness and joy has come to him,

and he should also think (as follows): 'it will be \[it is bound to be?
or let it be good!\] in Paradise, since it is so good also here!'

Notes:

*dārišn* "one should keep" and *handēšišn* "one should think" (Lesson
14).

Note the different meanings of *gāh* "place, time."

### Text 12.3

From *Dēnkard* book VI: *Dk*.6.23. -- From Madan's edition, p. 477.

![](media/image29.jpeg){width="4.25in" height="2.0555555555555554in"}

*u-šān ēn-iz ōwōn dāšt kū andar dēn 5 tis ī pahlom ēn-iz ēdōn*

*rāstīh ud rādīh ud hunarāwandīh ud tuxšāgīh ud ǰādag-gōwīh*

*rāstīh ēd pahlom kē andar dām ī ohrmazd ān kunēd ī ōy kē padiš kunēd
ōwōn sūdōmandtar ka-š padiš kunēd.*

*rādīh ēd pahlom kē dāšn ō kas kunēd kē az ōy kē padiš kunēd pad gētīy
tis-iz pādāšn nē ēmēd kū-š awiš rasēd.*

\[3rd-4th lines:\]

(As for) truthfulness, this is the best: (he) who, among the creatures
of Ohrmazd, does that which (*ān \... ī*) is thus more profitable to him
to whom (*ōy kē padiš*) he does (it) when he does (it) to him (*-š \...
padiš*).

(As for) generosity---this is the best: (he) who gives a gift to
somebody (and) who has no hope in this world that any counter-gift will
come to him (*-š awiš*) from (him) to whom (*az ōy kē padiš*) he gives
(it).

### Text 12.4

From the *Mēnōy xrad*: *MX*.1.187--194. --- Ms. K43 fol. 139v.

![](media/image30.jpeg){width="4.0in" height="3.4722222222222223in"}

*ud drāyēd Ganāy-Mēnōy ō dēwān kū-š ma saxwan aziš pursēd*

*kē az ān ī grāmīg tan ǰudāg ud pad ān ī wattar widarg bē āmad estēd.*

*bē-š awiš barēd rēmantom ud wattartom az xwarišnān, xwarišn ī pad dōšox
parwārd estēd.*

*āwarēnd wiš ud zahr ī mār ud gazdum ud abārīg-iz xrafstar ī pad dōšox
u-š xward dahēnd*

*ud tā ristāxēz ud tan ī pasēn pad was anāgīh ud pādifrāh ī ēwēnag
ēwēnag pad dōšox abāyēd būd.*

*ud pargast kū ānōh xwarišn šāyēd xward bē \*pūdag hangōšīdag, (xōn)
homānāg.*

Note: in the last line *pūdag* has been restored for \<PWN\> and *xōn*
supplied according to the Pazand *pū* and *xun* and Sanskrit
*durgaṃdhi-rakta-pratirūpāṇi* "similar to foul smell and blood.

11.3. Translate into Pahlavi and write in Pahlavi at least one of the
longs sentences:

1.  At the Renovation, God will leave nobody to the torment of Ahrimen
    and the demons.

2.  Ahrimen and the demons in hell do everything to harm and destroy
    Ohrmazd creation.

3.  When the soul (*ruwān*) goes out of the body, there will be no
    discomfort for the body at all.

4.  Do not slander, so that infamy and evil do (does) not come to
    (*ras-*) you.

5.  In paradise, Ardā Wirāz sees those souls of the Righteous from whom
    a light like a shining star kept blazing.

6.  When it became clear to Ardawān that Ardaxšīr had fled with his
    daughter, he became very angry and went after him with a large army.
    Thus he says to his general: That contract-breaker is the enemy of
    gods and men. God forbid the Xwarrah of kingship has reached him!

7.  To whom does this wonderful chariot belong on which you are
    standing, and where are you going in it? --- It belongs to Spandyād,
    brother of Zarēr and son of King Wištāsp, ruler of the Iranians, and
    I am going to the land of the Xyōns, because my beautiful sister and
    wife has been taken from me and now dwells there.

8.  How many horses and how many men were in that army with which King
    Wištāsp had gone to Turkestān to do battle with the enemies of the
    land of the Iranians, and when will they come back to their wives
    and children?

# Lesson 13

## Grammar 13

### Simple adverbs

Many adjectives are also used as adverbs, e.g., *ēwar* "for certain,"
*nōg* "anew," *rāst* "true, truly," *rōšn* "brightly," *saxt* "firmly,
intensely" *škeft* "hard, strongly," *xwaš* "pleasant, pleasantly":

*u-m ēn dēn grift ud [saxt]{.underline} dāšt*

"and I took (*-m \... grift*) and held this *dēn* [firmly]{.underline}"
(Kerdīr) (ergative, see below and Lesson 14)

*ka [ēwar]{.underline} dānēd kū nē Ādur māh ud [ēwar]{.underline} dānēd
kū nē Frawardīn rōz mīrēd*

*ā-š māh Day ud rōz Warahrān abāyēd dāštan*

"(when one does not know the actual date someone dies, then,) when he
knows [for certain]{.underline} that he does not die in the month of
Ādur, and he knows [for certain]{.underline} (it is) not on the day of
Frawardīn,

then he has to hold (= celebrate) the day of Warahrān in the month of
Day" (*PR*.1.3)

### Adverbs in *-īhā*

Other adverbs are formed from nouns, pronouns, adjectives, and simple
adverbs with the ending aåD- \<-yh'\> *-īhā*. This is identical with the
plural ending of nouns, but the use of the adverb is very different from
that of the plural nouns in *‑īhā*, so there is hardly ever any danger
of confusion.

All the simple adverbs above can also take this ending (*ēwarīhā*,
etc.).

See also expressions of manner, time, and measure Lessons 17-21.

Examples:

*Pāzag mādayān abar gōspand [dādīhā]{.underline} pad ēzišn ī ātaxšān ud
ābān zōhr \... kuštan*

"the Pāzag (*nask*) is mainly about killing cattle [according to the
law]{.underline} for the sacrifice to the fires and the libation to the
waters" (*Dk*.8.7.1)

*ka pad gētīy šēwan mōyag ud grīstan [adādīhā]{.underline} ma kunēd*

"when you (are) in this world, do not wail, sob, and weep (lit.: do
wailing, sobbing, and weeping), (thus) [breaking the law]{.underline}!"
(*AWN*.16.7)

*ašmāh [xwēšīhā]{.underline} bē nišīnēd*

"go and sit by yourselves!" (*AWN*.1.18)

*ka J̌am āmad ud mast būd [anāgāhīhā]{.underline} abāg J̌amag ī-š xwah būd
bē xuft*

"when Jam came and was drunk, he [unwittingly]{.underline} slept with
Jamag, who was his sister" (*PR*.8e.10)

*3 rōz-šabān [tanōmandīhā]{.underline} andar dōšox pādifrāh kunēnd*

"for three days and nights, they punish (them while) [in bodily
form]{.underline} in hell" (*Bd*.34.13)

*tis ī mēnōy ōwōn hamēšag [menišnīhā ud tuxšāgīhā]{.underline} kunišn
čiyōn ka dānē kū ēk rōz zīyam*

"matters of the other world should always be performed (*kunišn*) [in
thought]{.underline} and [diligently]{.underline}, as when you know: "I
shall live (only) one (more) day" (*Dk*.6.151)

***pad** [rāstīhā]{.underline} ud ō hamāg kustag
[niyābagīhā]{.underline} hāwand-**āyišnīh** ī Abestāg*

*ud mayānag gēhān uzwānīg [āšnāgīhā]{.underline} **frēstišnīh** ī zand
purr-bōzišn paydāg andar kadamīyān-iz-ēw*

"because the *Avesta* comes equally (by its equal-coming),
[fairly]{.underline} and to all the regions [as is proper]{.underline},

and, (because) the *Zand* is sent (by its sending) by tongue (orally)
into the world of the living [in known manner]{.underline} (= so as to
make it known), it is evident (that it leads to) full salvation among
whomsoever" (*Dk*.5.24.12)

*stāyišn ud paristišn ast ī [wāspuhragānīhā]{.underline} dādār xwēš pad
dahišnān nē sazēd*

"some praise and worship [specifically]{.underline} belongs to the
Creator (and) is not suitable for (His) creations" (*Dk*.3.241.2)

Note that these adverbs (like prepositional phrases) can be connected to
nouns with *ī* and must then be translated according to the sense
required, e.g.:

*dām-dahišnīh [ī mēnōyīhā]{.underline} gōwam ud pas
[gētīyīhā]{.underline}*

"I shall talk about the creation of the creatures (as it took place) [in
yonder world]{.underline} and then [in this world]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.1.32)

These adverbs sometimes indicate distribution, e.g.:

*zamānag ī-š rāyēnišn abrāz [amaragānīhā]{.underline} pad frāz-āhangīg
ud [hangāmīhā]{.underline} ud [kasīhā]{.underline} pad abāz-āhangīg*

"time whose organization (is in) 'ascendance' is [among the countless
ones]{.underline} (= generally) forward-striving (≈ makes progress), and
(= but) [at various times]{.underline} (= occasionally) and [from person
to person]{.underline} (= individually) backward-striving" (*Dk*.3.68.2)

The adverbs in *‑īhā* are often formed from compounds and can take the
place of prepositional phrases and subordinate clauses, e.g.:

*[mēnōy-wāzišnīhā]{.underline} bē ō wahišt ayāb ō Garōdmān ānōh kū-š gāh
ast franāmēd*

"[flying through the other world]{.underline}, (the soul) proceeds to
paradise or to Garōdmān, there where its place is" (*DD*.30.2)

*gāw [mardōm-saxwanīhā]{.underline} aw-iš pahikārd kū-m bē ma ōzan*

"the bull argued with (*ō*) him [using the speech of
humans]{.underline}: do not kill me!" (*WZ*.4.14)

*spāh ī Kirm kē pad diz būd hāmōyēn ō bērōn mad ud abāg aswārān ī
Ardaxšīr kōxšišn ud kārēzār ī [gyān-abespārīhā]{.underline} saxt kerd ud
az harw 2 kustag was ōzad*

"Kirm's army, which was in the fortress, came out and struggled and
battled (so) fiercely with Ardaxšīr's cavalry [as to surrender their
souls]{.underline}, and many were killed from both sides (*KN*.6.16)

*ud hamāg rāst ud [meh-dādestānīhā]{.underline} ud
[yazdān-šnāyēnīdārīhā]{.underline} guft estēd*

"and it has all been spoken truly and [according to a
greater]{.underline} (= higher) [law]{.underline} and [so as to make the
gods favorable]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.24.12)

*az 3 stēr ī pad bun xwāstag ī stūrīh uzēnīdan ud kāstan nē pādixšāy ud
[tuwān-sāmānīhā]{.underline} barōmand dārišn*

"one is not authorized to spend (any) from the three staters that
constitute the initial amount of money of the *stūrīh* or to diminish
(it), but should keep (it) so that it produces income [to the extent of
one's ability]{.underline}" (*REA*.18.8)

##### From prepositional phrases:

*wād [pad-wād-ēwēnag-čihrīhā]{.underline} frāz wāyēd* (\< *pad wād
ēwēnag*)

"the wind blows forth [according to the *čihr*]{.underline} (\~ nature)
[that is in the manner of the wind]{.underline}" (*WZ*.30.59)

*pad ān ī tēz asp [bowandag-dārōg-paywāsīg-abāgīhā]{.underline}*

"[having with (him)]{.underline} on the fast horse [a bag (containing)
the complete medications]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.157.40)

##### Adverbs in *-īhā* in the **comparative** and **superlative**:

*gōwizārīhātar* "more in detail" \< *gōwizār* "in detail, detailed"

*kam-wināhīhātar* "in such a manner that there is little/less sin"

*āfrāh ī dēn zēnāwandīhā abar tuxšēd tā dānēd* *kadār ayāb ahlaw ayāb
druwand wurrōyēd meh kū kasān ayāb ān ī ahlaw [tuxšāgīhātar]{.underline}
wurrōyēd ayāb ān ī druwand*

"apply yourselves vigilantly to the instructions of the *dēn* until/so
that you know which (it is): does either a Righteous believe [more
diligently]{.underline} than (*kū*) (other) people or a wicked person =
whether the Righteous one or the wicked one believes the more
diligently" (*PN*.53 + *PY*.31.17)

*mardōmān 3 tis ēn [xwēš-kārīhātom]{.underline}*

"for humans, these three things (the ones that should be performed) [the
most according to their 'proper duty']{.underline}" (*Dk*.6.13)

*ēk pad kerdan harw kār [mādagwarīhātom]{.underline} tis tuxšāgīh*

"one thing is [the most especially]{.underline} (needed) for performing
every work: diligence" (*Ōšnar* 4)

##### *čand \... -īhātar* *šāyēd* "as \... as possible":

*čand abēzagīhātar šāyēd*

"as purely as possible" (*DD*.47.37)

*mardōm ud gōspand ud abārīg dahišn ī weh [čand frārōnīhā
šāyēd]{.underline} abzāyēnīdan*

"increasing people, domestic animals, and the other creatures [in as
(morally) good a way as possible]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.13.9)

*mēnōy ī tan xōg ī dagr andar tan būdan rāy a-wišōbišn ōwōn kāmag ī
pad-iš mānist ka-iz-iš hilēnd az māništ*

*pad ham rāh ān ī widerdān tan [čand a-wināhīhātar šāyēd]{.underline}
drīstīhā pāyišn*

"the spirit of the body, because (it is in) its nature to be in the body
for a long time, so much (*ōwōn*) desires not to be shattered that
(*ī*), even when they release it from its abode, (it remains) in its
abode,

in the same way, the bodies of the departed should be guarded firmly [so
as to cause as little sin]{.underline} (contagion) [as
possible]{.underline}" (*DD*.16.4)

### Some expressions of length and duration 

*pad was frasang* "at (a distance of) many frasangs"

*andar zamān* "immediately"

*pad ān zamān* "at that time"

*pad ham zamān* "at the same time, immediately"

*pad gyāg* "on the spot, immediately"

*tā hamē ud hamē-rawišnīh* "for ever and ever"

*tā 3 rōz* "within three days"

Nouns denoting time or space can be used without prepositions to denote
length, duration, or point of time:

*[māh frawardīn]{.underline} [rōz ohrmazd]{.underline} andar dwārist
[nēmrōz]{.underline}*

"[in the month of Frawardīn]{.underline}, [on the day of
Ohrmazd]{.underline} (the Foul Spirit) rushed in [(at)
midday]{.underline}" (= the first day of the first month = spring
equinox) (*Bd*.4.10b)

*ka [dagr zamān]{.underline} Ohrmazd rāy yazišn \... ī frārōn kunēnd
āsānīh az-iš* "when/if they perform good sacrifices for Ohrmazd [for a
long time]{.underline}, there is comfort from it" (*AWN*.4.14)

*[abēr dagr zamān]{.underline} andar ān kār estēd*

"she is at work at that (washing) [for a very long time]{.underline}"
(*ŠnŠ*.3.5)

*[ēč zamān]{.underline} ma pāyēd*

"do not wait [(for) any time]{.underline} (= not even a moment)!"

*Ohrmazd bālistīg \... [zamān ī akanārag]{.underline} abar rōšnīh hamē
būd*

"Ohrmazd was up above in the light [(for) an unlimited
time]{.underline}" (*Bd*.1.1)

*Hariburz tā bowandagīh 800 sāl hamē rust [200 sāl]{.underline} ō
star-pāyag ud [200]{.underline} tā ō māh-pāyag [200]{.underline} tā ō
xwaršēd-pāyag ud [200]{.underline} tā ō bālist ī āsmān*

"Hariburz kept growing until the completion of 800 years; [200
years]{.underline} to the star-level, [200 (years)]{.underline} to the
moon-level; [200 (years)]{.underline} to the sun-level; and [200
(years)]{.underline} to the highest point of the sky" (*Bd*.9.2)

*ud [hamāg gēhān]{.underline} nasāy-nigānīh ud nasāy-wistarišn bē bawēd*

"and in the whole world there will be burying of corpses and laying out
(= ?) of corpses" (*ZWY*.4.23)

*čē ka [hamāg gēhān ābādānīh būd]{.underline} hē agar-išān was-iz zad ud
stō kerd hēnd hē az dāmān wizendīh bērōn nē šud hēnd hē čē-šān nē
tuwānist hē šudan*

"for, when (= if) there were prosperity in the whole world, (then,) even
if they struck and subdued many (evils), (still) they still would not go
out (= disappear), for they would not be able to go" (*Bd*.28.19)

*ka Ēbgad ō dām mad \... pad zamīg homānāgīh ī čašmagīhā ī āb [wasān
gyāgān]{.underline} čašmag ātaxš ul uzēnd*

"when the Adversary came upon the creation \... on earth [in many
places]{.underline} springs of fire come up like springs of water"
(*WZ*.34.48-49)

*abar wihēz ī ō kišwar kišwar ud kustag kustag ī gēhān [ān
dranāy]{.underline} kē dādār ō ān kišwar ud kustag wizīd*

"about traveling to the various continents and the various districts of
the world [that length]{.underline} which (as far as) the creator chose
for that district and continent" (*Dk*.7.1.15)

*kē sag nē dārēd nē šāyēd nāmčišt ān [kē-š mān]{.underline} gōspand*

"he who does not have a dog--it is not appropriate, especially he who
has sheep [in his house]{.underline}" (*ZFJ*, p. 665)

*ān pad abdom āškārag paydāgīhā wēnīhēd [šabān]{.underline} andar
andarwāy*

"in the end that (battle of the gods and demons,) will be seen [at
night]{.underline} visibly and clearly in the atmosphere (sky)"
(*WZ*.34.54)

### Distance in steps

The nouns *gām* and *pay* "step, stride" take the particle *ī* (often
not written!) with the object "from" which, as well as *az*:

*ka bē ō [24 pay ī]{.underline} amahrspandān mad*

"when he came to (within) [24 steps of]{.underline} the *amahrspand*s"
(*WZ*.21.9)

*[30 gām ī]{.underline} čāh yazišn kerdan ud drōn yaštan nē pādixšāy*

"one is not authorized to perform a *yazišn* and *drōn* ritual (within)
[30 steps of]{.underline} a well" (*RAF*.43.2)

*agar-iz ātaxš ēdōn bē tuwān burdan kū [pad 3 gām ī]{.underline} nasāy
bē barēd pas-iz bē barišn \...*

*ātaxš [andar 3 gām]{.underline} ī nasāy burdan tanābuhl-ēw wināh*

"and if it is possible to carry the fire in such a way that one carries
it (at least) 3 steps from the fire, then one should carry it too \...

(for) carrying the fire [within 3 steps of]{.underline} dead matter
(there is) a sin of one *tanābuhl*" (*ŠnŠ*.2.38)

With *az*:

*30 gām az ātaxš ud 30 gām az āb ud 30 gām az barsom pad ahlāyīh frāz
wistard ud 3 gām az mardān ahlawān*

"30 steps from the fire, 30 steps from the water, 30 steps from the
barsom spread out in orderly fashion, and 3 steps from Righteous men"
(*PV*.3.17)

### Compounds expressing length, height, and duration

Distance and length of time are often expressed by compounds with nouns
ending in *-āy* (Lesson 10), exceptionally with *drang* "duration,"
e.g.:

*zan ka zanīh ī šōy nē kunēd pad gyāg tanābuhl ud [pad
sāl-drahnāy]{.underline} margarzān*

"when/if a women does not perform her wifely duty to her husband, she is
immediately (guilty of) a *tanābuhl* sin and is *margarzān* [at the
length of (= after) a year]{.underline}" (after *RAF*.16.2)

*mard-ēw ī abar sang-ēw bē mīrēd ud sang abāg zamīg ēw-kardag sang [pad
andar sāl-drahnāy]{.underline} abāg zamīg pāk bē bawēd*

"a man who dies on a stone, and the stone is connected with the earth,
(then) the stone, together with the earth, becomes clean [within one
year]{.underline}" (*ŠnŠ*.2.15)

*u-š xwāstag ī stūrīh [zīndag-drahnāy]{.underline} ōh dārišn*

"and he should keep possession of the property in *stūrīh* in the usual
way [for as long as he lives]{.underline}" (*REA*.18.13)

*u-m dīd ān ī xwēdōdahān ruwān andar rōšnīh kē-š [gar-bālāy]{.underline}
rōšnīh aziš hamē waxšīd*

"and I saw in the light the souls of those who had performed *xwēdōdah*,
from whom a light shone [the height of a mountain]{.underline}"
(*AWN*.12.8)

*Hugar ī Buland ān kē-š āb Ardwīsūr aziš frōd ǰahēd [1000
mard-bālāy]{.underline}*

"the tall Hugar is (the mountain) from which Ardwīsūr cascades down the
height/depth of 1000 men" (*Bd*.9.7)

*mayān ōy ī xwēdōdah nē kerd ud pahlom axwān, dēwār-ēw čand
[zamīg-pahnāy]{.underline} ud [zōfāy]{.underline} bē estēd u-š ō ān ī
pahlom axwān nē hilēnd*

"between him who has not performed *xwēdōdah* and the Best Existence,
there stands a wall as [wide and deep as the earth]{.underline}, and
they do not let him into the Best Existence" (after *REA*.24.3)

*ka an mard 30-sālag bawēd ān xwaršēd bē estēd pad bālist ī ān asmān [30
rōz šab-drang]{.underline}*

"when that man (Sōšāns) is thirty years old, yonder sun will stand in
the heighest heaven [for 30 days and nights]{.underline}" (*Dk*.7.10.19)

### The Verb. The ergative/agential construction

We now come to yet another tricky aspect of Pahlavi syntax, the
so-called "ergative" construction. It is recommended that the students
study all the examples very carefully and be able to analyze every
example in detail.

Note that the grammar of the construction is not difficult *per se*, it
is in fact quite simple, but the students sometimes have a hard time
getting used to thinking in such an unfamiliar way. Everything they have
learned about nouns, pronouns, verbs, and pre/postpositions must be
mastered in order to understand the syntax and workings of the
construction. These sections of the grammar in preceding lessons should
therefore be carefully reviewed, especially [the section on passive in
Lesson 9 and about the pre/postpositions in Lessons 11 and
12]{.underline}.

#### Active and passive

It is important that the students have a good understanding of how
active and passive work in English and other languages they know.

In English, there are two kinds of passive sentences:

1.  sentences with transitive verbs, but without "performer"

2.  sentences with transitive verbs [and]{.underline} "performer"

In the first kind of sentence, the passive is necessary and can only be
avoided by turning the sentence into an impersonal one (see Lesson 9),
e.g.:

This book [is]{.underline} rarely [read]{.underline} (people rarely read
this book)

A man was seen running in the street (they saw a man running in the
street)

This has never been done before (nobody has done this before)

The other kind of sentence is a stylistic alternative to a corresponding
active sentence:

[My students]{.underline} rarely [read]{.underline} this book = This
book [is]{.underline} rarely [read by my students]{.underline}

[Have you]{.underline} ever [done]{.underline} this before =
[Has]{.underline} this ever [been done by you]{.underline} before?

In modern Persian, and, for instance, the Semitic languages, only the
first kind is used, that is, passive forms of the verb are only used
when the "performer" [is not mentioned]{.underline} (except in a few
idioms).

This was the situation in early Pahlavi, as well, but it was later
complicated by various analogical syntactic developments. Here, we shall
describe the early Pahlavi syntax; later, we shall see how this was
modified.

#### Intransitive and transitive and the past tense

To understand the construction, we need to understand the difference
between [intransitive]{.underline} and [transitive]{.underline} verbs.

An 'intransitive' verb is a verb that [can not]{.underline} take a
direct object, for instance, verbs that usually express state or motion,
like *būdan* "to become" and *šudan* "to go," while a 'transitive' verb
is a verb that [can]{.underline} take a direct object, for instance,
verbs that express actions, like *kerdan* "to do," *ōzadan* "to kill,"
*xwardan* "to eat," etc.

In Pahlavi, as in many other languages, there is a fundamental
difference between intransitive verbs and transitive verbs in the
formation of the past tense. Familiar examples are German and French
(Italian), where intransitive verbs in the perfect take the auxiliary
"to be," Germ. *sein*, Fr. *être*, while transitive verbs take the
auxiliary "to have," Germ. *haben*, Fr. *avoir*, e.g.:

German French

Intransitive *ich [bin]{.underline} gegangen je [suis]{.underline} allé*
"I went, have gone"

Transitive *ich [habe]{.underline} ein Kind gesehen j'[ai]{.underline}
vu un enfant* "I saw/have seen a child"

In English, this distinction has been abandonded, reserving the
construction with "to be" for a very few expressions with specialized
meaning, such as "he is gone."

#### Intransitive and transitive, active and passive

In Pahlavi, the difference between the intransitive and transitive past
looks quite different from the examples above, at least on the surface,
although, in principle, it is of the same kind.

The construction described in the following is what is commonly referred
to as "ergative" (from Greek *ergon* "work"). Since the construction is
only used in the past tenses, and not in the present, it is also called
"*split* ergative."

The construction has also been called an "agential" construction (from
Latin *agens* "actor, performer"), as the "performer" is usually called
the "agent."

## Ergative

This is the construction that [transitive]{.underline} verbs take in
past tenses.

We saw in Lesson 9 that the following sentence is [passive]{.underline}:

**grammatical subject + verb:**

*dušmen ōzad hēnd* "the enemies were killed"

Recall that the 'grammatical subject is what the verb agrees with, that
is, in this case, *dušmen* "the enemies."

In order to say "who" did the deed, the "who," or "performer" = *agent*,
is simply added in front of this sentence, and the sentence [can be
translated in English as active OR passive]{.underline}.

Consider the following sentences in the **PRESENT** tense:

**agent = grammatical subject + direct object + verb:**

*aswār dušmen ōzanēnd* "[the horsemen]{.underline} kill the enemies"

*amāh dušmen ōzanēm* "[we]{.underline} kill the enemies"

These correspond to the following sentences in the **PAST** tense:

**agent + grammatical subject + verb:**

Ergative (Pahlavi) Passive (English) Active (English)

*aswār dušmen ōzad hēnd* "the enemies were killed [by the
horseman]{.underline}" = "[the horseman]{.underline} killed the enemies"

*amāh dušmen ōzad hēnd* "the enemies were killed [by us]{.underline}" =
"[we]{.underline} killed the enemies"

As in the **English passive**, [the verb]{.underline} in the ergative
constructions [agrees with the direct object]{.underline} in the
**English active** sentence, although it is the subject in the passive
sentence.

The word order is usually AGENT - SUBJect - VERB.

Prepositional phrases and indirect objects remain unchanged and are not
affected by the ergative construction.

Thus we have the following Pahlavi structures:

[Present:]{.underline}

agent = **grammatical subject** + direct object + verb (agrees with
grammatical subject = **agent**)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Past:]{.underline}

agent + direct object = **grammatical subject** + verb (agrees with
grammatical subject = **direct object**)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

[Present:]{.underline}

*aswār dušmen ōzanēd* "[the horseman]{.underline} kills the enemies"
\[or "the enemies are killed [by the horseman]{.underline}"\]

*amāh dušmen ōzanēm* "[we]{.underline} kill the enemies" \[or "the
enemies are killed [by us]{.underline}"\]

[Past:]{.underline}

*aswār dušmen ōzad hēnd* "[the horseman]{.underline} killed the enemies"
= "the enemies were killed [by the horseman]{.underline}"

*amāh dušmen ōzad hēnd* "[we]{.underline} killed the enemies" = "the
enemies were killed [by us]{.underline}"

Note that there is [no other]{.underline} way of saying, for instance,
"Frēdōn is/was killed by the dragons."

When we translate such constructions [we may therefore use either active
or passive as best suits **English** style, but most often they should
be translated as **active**]{.underline}.

To understand and get used to the construction it may be useful to think
of it in terms of the English [passive]{.underline}, e.g., "you were
killed by me" = "I killed you," but one should not make it a habit to
translate it with an English [passive]{.underline}, but with an English
[active]{.underline} in most instances.

In fact, since the active is much more common in English than the
passive, the students are expected to use primarily English active
constructions in the translations. If they keep using the passive, it is
to be assumed that they have not grasped the nature of the construction.

It may also be useful for some to keep in mind that the ergative
construction corresponds formally to the "have" constructions in the
European languages.

Similarly, Pahlavi uses its regular "possessive" construction with "to
be," compare:

*man waččag ast* "[I have]{.underline} a child" *man waččag dīd* "[I
have]{.underline} seen/saw a child"

*man waččag hēnd* "[I have]{.underline} children" *man waččag dīd hēnd*
"[I have]{.underline} seen/saw the children"

Here *waččag* is the grammatical subject of the verb, and the verb
agrees with it, while *man* is the one who "possesses" the action.

Those familiar with Syriac will recognize the similarity with the
construction with *lī*: *lī kṯīḇ* "I wrote."

Thus, the English subject has become the "possessor of the action," and
pronouns and nouns (and adjectives) take the same forms as they do in
possessive constructions.

#### Examples of agential constructions

[Present active:]{.underline} [Past ergative:]{.underline}

*mard man wēnēnd* "the men see me" *mardān an dīd ham* "the men saw me"

*mard zan wēnēnd* "the men see a woman" *mardān zan dīd* "the men saw a
woman"

*mard zan(ān) wēnēnd* "the men see the/some women" *mardān zan dīd hēnd*
"the men saw the/some women"

##### Past ergative, agent = noun in the singular:

*frēdōn aǰdahāg ōzad* "Frēdōn killed a/the dragon."

*frēdōn aǰdahāg ōzad hēnd* "Frēdōn killed some/the dragons."

*ēn hēnd aǰdahāg ī Frēdōn ōzad* *hēnd* "these are the dragons which
Frēdōn killed"

*dušmen was mard ōzad hēnd* "(one) enemy killed many men"

*ohrmazd mardōm ud gōspand dād hēnd* "Ohrmazd established/created people
and animals"

*amāh mardōm hēm ohrmazd dād hēm* "we are people; Ohrmazd
established/created us"

*[ohrmazd]{.underline} andar yazišn kunišn dām hamāg bē
[dād]{.underline}*

"during his performance of the sacrifice, [Ohrmazd
established]{.underline} the entire creation" (after *Bd*.3.26)

*pas [Srōš ahlaw ud Ādur yazd]{.underline} dast ī man frāz
[grift]{.underline} ud [guft]{.underline} kū bē āy tā ō tō nimāyēm
wahišt ud dōšox ud rōšnīh*

"then [the Righteous Srōš and the divine Fire took]{.underline} my hands
and [said]{.underline}: Come so we may show you Heaven and Hell and the
light!" (*AWN*.5.4)

*[Ardā Wirāz]{.underline} ka ān saxwan [āšnūd]{.underline} zofr [namāz
burd]{.underline} ō dādār Ohrmazd*

"when [Ardā Wirāz heard]{.underline} what He said, he
[bowed]{.underline} deeply to Ohrmazd the Creator" (*AWN*.101.14)

#### Form of the agent

Since the "agent" is not the grammatical subject, [plural nouns as
"agents" take the ending *-ān*]{.underline}; the *r*‑stems take the
*-ar* forms as "agents"; and the 1st sing. pronoun *man* must be used,
since *an* is only used as "grammatical subject":

*[dānāgān]{.underline} ōwōn [guft]{.underline}* "[the wise men
said]{.underline} as follows"

*[aǰdahāgān]{.underline} Frēdōn [ōzad]{.underline}* "[the dragons
killed]{.underline} Frēdōn."

*[dušmenān]{.underline} was mard [ōzad]{.underline} hēnd* "[the enemies
killed]{.underline} many men"

*andar hazārag sar [dēwān]{.underline} am [kirrēnīd]{.underline}* "at
the end of the millennium, [the *dēw*s cut]{.underline} am in half"
(*Bd*.33.1)

*ēn fradom ardīg [axtarān kerd]{.underline} abāg Gannāg Mēnōy*

"this first battle [the constellations made]{.underline} (fought) with
the Foul Spirit = this first battle with the Foul Spirit was fought by
the constellations" (*Bd*.6.2)

##### Agent = personal pronoun

Examples with *dīdan, wēn-* "to see" all three persons
([non-enclitic]{.underline}):

[Present:]{.underline} [Past:]{.underline}

*an tō wēnam* "I see you" *man tō dīd hē* "I saw you"

*amāh tō wēnēm* "we see you" *amāh tō dīd hē* "we saw you"

*tō man wēnē* "you see me" *tō an dīd ham* "you saw me"

*tō amāh wēnē* "you see us" *tō amāh dīd hēm* "you saw us"

*ašmāh man wēnēd* "you (all) see me" *ašmāh an dīd ham* "you (all) saw
me"

*an ašmāh wenam* "I see you (all)" *man ašmāh dīd hēd* "I saw you (all)"

*ōy ašmāh wēnēd* "he sees you (all)" *ōy ašmāh dīd hēd* "he saw you
(all)"

*awēšān amāh wēnēnd* "they see us" *awēšān amāh dīd hēm* "they saw us"

*[kē]{.underline} tō [dād]{.underline} hē [kē]{.underline} an
[dād]{.underline} ham*

"[who established]{.underline} you, [who established]{.underline} me?"
(*Dk*.7.3.60)

*[kē]{.underline} amāh [dād]{.underline} hēm [kē]{.underline} amāh
[tāšīd]{.underline} hēm u [kē parward]{.underline} hēm*

"[who established]{.underline} us, [who fashioned]{.underline} us, and
[who nourished]{.underline} us?" (*PY*.1.1)

Compare the [non-agential]{.underline} ([passive]{.underline}) version:

*ō ašmāh amahrspandān gōšurūn garzīd kū*

*ō kē [an brehēnīd ham]{.underline} ō kē [an tāšīd ham]{.underline} kū ō
kē [dād ham]{.underline}*

"to you, the *amahrspand*s, Gōšurūn complained:

for whom [was I 'created']{.underline}, for whom [was I
fashioned]{.underline}, i.e., for whom [was I established]{.underline}?"
(*PY*.29.1)

On enclitic pronouns as agents see Lesson 14.

#### 'Zero' direct object

Some transitive verbs do not take normal direct objects, in which case
the direct object can be regarded as "it" and the verb is in the
singular. This happens, for instance, with verbs meaning "say, ask,"
where the "direct object" is what is said or asked about, e.g.:

*[man]{.underline} az āmāsp [pursīd]{.underline} kū kē hē* "[I
asked]{.underline} āmāsp: Who are you?"

*[mardān guft]{.underline} kū bē āy* "[the men said]{.underline}: Come!"

In questions and negations, the grammatical subject may be a pronoun,
e.g.:

*tō [čē]{.underline} guft* "what did you say?"

*man [ēč]{.underline} nē guft* "I said nothing"

#### 

#### 'Raising' ("topicalization") in ergativic clauses:

The word order often differs from the 'normal' one in various ways by
one term being moved toward the beginning of the clause, a phenomenon
referred to as 'raising' or 'fronting' (depending on how the clause is
visualized) or toward the back ('lowering'):

##### verb + agent:

*ud [pursīd ān ī ahlawān ruwān]{.underline} az ān kanīg kū tō kē hē ud
kē xwēš hē*

"and [the soul of the Righteous asked]{.underline} that young woman: who
are you, and whom do you belong to?" (*AWN*.4.10)

##### gr-subject + agent + verb:

*u-t [wars ud rēš wādān wišuft]{.underline}*

"and [the winds have tousled]{.underline} your (*-t*) [hair and
beard]{.underline}" (*AZ*.86)

*[tō dānāg baγ tāšīd hē]{.underline} pad mēnōyīh [tō dānāg baγ bē dād
hē]{.underline} ō gētīy*

"[the wise god fashioned *you*]{.underline} (while) in the world of
thought; [the wise god established *you*]{.underline} into the world of
the living = [you]{.underline} were fashioned by the wise god (etc.)"
(*PY*.10.10)

*az šīrēnīh ī frazend [ēk]{.underline} [mādar ǰūd]{.underline} ud
[ēk]{.underline} [pidar]{.underline}*

"because of the children's sweetness (because they were so sweet), [the
mother ate one]{.underline} and [the father one]{.underline} (one was
eaten by the mother, one by the father)" (*Bd*.14.31)

##### gr-subject + verb + agent:

*sidīgar hazārag bun būd ka Frēdōn [kišwar baxt Salm ud
Tūz]{.underline}*

"it was the beginning of the third millennium when [Salm and Tūz
divided]{.underline} Frēdōn's [land]{.underline}" (*Bd*.33.3)

Note the avoidance of ambiguity in sentences such as *abāz pādixšāy [hē
grift]{.underline}* "[you are]{.underline} authorized to take \[short
infinitive\] (it) back" (*MHD*.43.12) instead of \**abāz pādixšāy [grift
hē]{.underline}*\*, where *grift hē* would have meant "the ruler [took
you]{.underline} again/back."

#### Sequences of verbs

An agent can have a series of verbs with it, without being repeated each
time, e.g,:

##### Sequences of transitive verbs:

*andar ān hazārag [Zarduxšt]{.underline} dēn az Ohrmazd
[padīrift]{.underline} [āwurd]{.underline} [Wištāsp-šāh
padīrift]{.underline} rawāg [kerd]{.underline}*

"in that millennium, [Zarduxšt received]{.underline} the *dēn* from
Ohrmazd (and) [brought]{.underline} (it to W.); [King Wištāsp
received]{.underline} (it and) [propagated]{.underline} (it)"
(*Bd*.33.12)

##### Sequences of transitive and intransitive verbs:

Note that, in a series of clauses, when the gr-subject of an
intransitive verb becomes the agent of a transitive verb it can be
expressed or be omitted (implied), e.g.:

*pas [Afrāsyāb]{.underline} [āmad]{.underline} Mānuščihr abāg ērānagān ō
Padišxwārgar [spōxt]{.underline}*

"then Afrāsyāb (*subject*) [came]{.underline}; (he = *agent*)
[pushed]{.underline} Mānuščihr together with the Iranians back to
Padišxwārgar" (*Bd*.33.5) \[*could* also mean: "(and) M. pushed (him)"\]

On the use of enclitic pronouns in such cases, see Lesson 14.

### The participle of necessity in *-išn*

A 'participle of necessity' is made from the present stem with the
ending *-išn*. The construction is impersonal and the agent (the person
who must/should/ought to do something) is in the oblique case, e.g.:
*man* *kunišn* "I must/ought to do." The construction is therefore
reminiscent of the ergative. Note that, differently from the action
nouns in *-išn* (*kunisn*, etc., lesson 7), this form has verbal syntax
with agent and grammatical subject, e.g.:

*bē [man]{.underline} čē [kunišn]{.underline}*

"but what [do I have to do]{.underline} = but what [should I
do]{.underline}?"

*(ka) xufsēd pad frārōnīh ud abēwināhīh [xuftišn]{.underline} ud
Ašemwohū-ēw bē [gōwišn]{.underline}*

"(when; not in ms.) one goes to sleep, (one) [should sleep]{.underline}
in goodness and sinlessness (= without sinning) and [say]{.underline}
one *Ašemwohū*" (*ŠnŠ*.10.24)

*ān kē tuwāngarīh az frārōn-tuxšāgīh kerd estēd [pad farrox]{.underline}
ud ān kē az abārōnīh kerd estēd [pad dušfarg dārišn]{.underline}*

"he who has made his wealth through hard work [should be
regarded]{.underline} as (*pad*) 'fortunate', and he who has made it
through wrong-doing as 'unfortunate'" (*MX*.49.4)

The participle of necessity in *-išn* can be used in the comparative
(*-išntar*) and superlative (*-išntom*), but there are few certain
examples; most commonly we are dealing with compounds containing a
verbal noun in *-išn*:

*kadār awēšān gurgān [zanišntar]{.underline} hēnd ahlaw Ohrmazd*

"which of those wolves [should be killed more]{.underline} (are more
worthy of being killed), o Righteous Ohrmazd" (*PV*.13.41a)

*sidīgar brīnag Artēštārestān. mādayān abar
[zanišn-arzānīgīh]{.underline} ī gurg ud andar gurgān
[zanišntarīh]{.underline} ī ān ī 2-zang az ān ī 4-zang*

"the third section, *Artēštārestān* (book about soldiers), (is) mainly
about the wolf's [being worthy of being struck down]{.underline} (verbal
noun *zanišn*) and [the fact that]{.underline} (*-īh*), among wolves,
those with two feet [should be struck down more]{.underline} than those
with four feet" (*Dk*.8.26.1)

### The verbal adjective in *-išnīg*

This form, which is derived from the participle of necessity, usually
refers to the future and can refer to active or passive actions ("intent
on \...-ing," "(sth. that is) to be \...-ed").

*ōwōn čiyōn Ohrmazd bālistīg ud Ahrimen zōfāyīg u-š āgenēn nērōg andar
gētīy ēk ō did [kōxšišnīg]{.underline} mardōm-iz 2 wād andar tan*

"just as Ohrmazd is on high and Ahrimen in the depth and his (their)
strengths (= armies) together are [intent on battling]{.underline} each
other in this world, there are also two winds in the body of men"
(*Bd*.28.12)

*ānōh kū tārīkīh zahīy rōšnīh nē [windišnīg]{.underline} tis*

"there where darkness is deep, light is not something [going to be
found]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.142.6)

Note *abāyišnīg* "which will be needed; comely, attractive," *wēnišnīg*
"which can be seen, visible."

##### Substantivized *-išnīgīh*:

The nouns in *-išnīgīh* denote future state ("deserving to be \...,
going to be \..., be bound to \..., be intent on), while the nouns in
*-išnīh* are most common in compounds with nouns in *-išn*, e.g.:

*[a-wardišnīgīh]{.underline} ī čihrēnīdagān az ān ī padiš čihrēnīd
estēd*

"[the fact that]{.underline} those who have been given a (specific)
nature, [are not going to be turned]{.underline} from that for which
they have been given (this) nature" (*Dk*.3.83.2)

*harw rōz 3 bār \... astīh ud hamēyīgīh ī yazdān ud an-astīh ud
[abesihišnīgīh]{.underline} ī Ahrimen ud dēwān bē gōwišn*

"three times every day one should utter the facts that (*-īh*) the gods
*are* and are eternal, but that Ahrimen and the demons *are* *not* and
[are going to be destroyed]{.underline}" (*Dk*.6E.31c)

*[nikōhišnīgīh]{.underline} ī dēwān a-paristišnīh ī uzdēs \... āgāh būd*

"to be aware [that]{.underline} the demons [deserve to be
scorned]{.underline} and idols (are) something one must not offer
worship (to)" (*Dk*.5.13.11)

*andar mardōm Wahuman Akōman mehmānīg ud kē mehmānīg gāh-gīrišnīh ud kē
widārīg [abar-rasišnīgīh]{.underline}*

"in people, Wahuman and Akōman are lodgers; and the one who lodges
(permanently) (is characterized by the term) 'taking the place' and the
one who is transient (by) '[going to come upon]{.underline}'"
(*Dk*.3.63.3)

*čē-m [a-pardazišnīgīh]{.underline} ī abar was darīhā rāy bē ō
nišān-šnāsīh dil nē frahaxt*

"for, because of [my inability to (?) undertake]{.underline} several
issues (at the same time), (my) heart is not trained in recognizing
allusions" (*NM*.2.1.3)

##### Adverbial *-išnīgīhā*:

*yazdān ō amāh [frayādišnīgīhā]{.underline} rasānd*

"the gods will come to us [intent on helping]{.underline}" (*NM*.1.2.14)

13.2. Translate into Pahlavi:

Note: Do not use enclitic pronouns as agents, but the regular ones.

1.  When the Evil Spirit had rushed against (*pad*) every creation of
    Ohrmazd's, he made the world at noon like a dark night, and he made
    the sky underneath and above the earth dark.

2.  Salm and Tūz killed all the children and descendants of Ēriǰ, but
    Frēdōn kept Ēriǰ's daughter hidden for 10 years.

3.  From that daughter a daughter was born. Salm and Tūz killed the
    mother of the daughter, but Frēdōn kept hiding the girl for (*tā*)
    10 generations.

4.  When Ahrimen saw Ohrmazd's light, he rose from the depth and because
    of envy he attacked (it) in order to destroy (it).

5.  Ohrmazd recited the Ahunwar, and the Foul Spirit was stunned and
    fell back into the darkness.

6.  The *hērbed*s and *mowbed*s said to Ardā Wirāz: Welcome, you
    messenger of the Mazdayasnians! who have come back from that dark
    hell. Now tell us what you saw there.

7.  Then the Righteous Srōš and the divine fire brought me to a place
    and showed (to) me heaven and hell.

8.  When Ardā Wirāz came to that place (he) saw a beautiful woman who
    said to him: O young (man), I am your *dēn*! In the world of the
    living, you made me more beautiful than I was.

9.  Ardā Wirāz said to her: O beautiful woman! When did I make you
    beautiful? I have never seen you before.

10. After the death of Zarduxšt, there were many people who left the
    *dēn* of Ohrmazd and the (other) gods and took (accepted) the
    teaching of Ahrimen and the demons.

And give me this attractiveness in everybody's thought; and currency of
work and law; and freedom from fear of every harm and misfortune; and
living at will and succeeding at will in every good necessity.

Let it come as in the most fortunate way in this world as well as in the
other; let it come as in the greatest way, in a way that it is most full
of Righteousness, in a way that is most helpful for being saved and
coming to the Light Garōdmān!

*ān ī-tān wistāxīhā ud wistāxgarīhā abar drāz nibištan ī pursišn ēn-iz
nimūd kū*

*passox pad hangām nibēsam ī-m andar pardazišn bawēd*

*ud ān ī ašmāh pad hučihr-pursišnīh wistāxīh čimīg*

*ud man abar gōkānīg-passoxīh ud spōz-az-gāhīh kām ī taftīg*

*čē spōz ayāb abowandagīhā passoxīh aniyābag ast*

*az ān ī škeft-kōxšišnīh ī druz rāy aweštāb*

*ud wizōyišnīg-menišnīh az ān ī awizīrišnīg ud frēzwānīg kār kam
pardazišnīh ast*

That question of yours (asked) confidently and in a manner to inspire
confidence, regarding (my) writing (to you) at length, showed this, too,

that I should write a response at a time that (it is) within my leisure.

And your confidence in your question being a "pretty" (question) is
reasonable.

And I have an ardent desire for answering in detail and without
\*procrastination,

for putting off or answering incompletely is something inappropriate.

Because of (*az \... rāy*) the severe battling of the Lie there is
haste.

And (for) scrutinizing thinking there is little respite from unavoidable
and obligatory work.
