# Lesson 14

## Grammar 14

### *ham* "same, 'said'"

*ham* "same" is also used to refer to someone or something just
mentioned, as English "said" in legalese. Some text editors tend to read
this \<hm\>, wrongly, as \<'m\> for *im* "this."

*tarsāgīg, kē Yišōy kē [Mašīhā]{.underline}-iz xwānēnd, pad pus ī yazd
\... hangārēnd \...*

*grōh-ēw [ham Mašīhā]{.underline} rāy gōwēnd kū murd grōh-ēw gōwēnd kū
nē murd*

"the Christians who count Jesus, whom they also call
[Mašīhā]{.underline}, as the son of god \...

one group say about [said Mašīhā]{.underline} that he died, another
group that he did not die" (after *DD*.36.76-77)

*ka pad [čāštag]{.underline} ī ēw šāyēd hērbedān kam wardēnīdan ān ī
abāyēd kerdan \...*

*[ham-iz čāštag]{.underline} ō ān kē Abestāg gugāhīh hayārtar ud abērtar
hangāštan*

"when something is appropriate according to the [teaching]{.underline}
of one of the *hērbed*s, little is to be changed in how it should be
done \...

also, [said teaching]{.underline} should be counted to that which is
more helpful for (= supports?) the testimony from the Avesta and more
frequent (better attested?)" (*RAF*.73.4)

### Indefinite expressions with *ast*

Beside its use as "there is" (and derived from it) are several important
constructions, among them the following:

##### *ast (būd) ī*, *ast kē* "there is/was one who \...; some"; *ast kū* "it happens that; some":

*[ast kē]{.underline} ēdōn gōwēd* "[there is one]{.underline} who says
\...."

*[ast kē]{.underline} ēdōn gōwēnd* "[there are some who]{.underline} say
\...."

*[ast kē]{.underline} Wāy ī dērang-xwadāy gōwēd*

"[there is one who]{.underline} says 'Wāy of long dominion'" (*Bd*.1.44)

*mang ī bēšāz kē [ast ī]{.underline} banǰ xwānēd*

"medicinal/healing hemp, which [some]{.underline} call hashish"
(*Bd*.4.20)

*pad ē-mar \... ān ī pad Salm deh [ast ī]{.underline} Hrōm ān ī pad Sēn
deh [ast ī]{.underline} Čīnestān*

"in this number (are) those in the land of Salm, [some
(say)]{.underline} Rome, (and) those in the land of Sēn, [some
(say)]{.underline} China" (*Bd*.14.3)

About the 15 kinds of couples born from Siyāmak, son of M. and M., and
Wašāg.

*ka ō ōy dahēnd padīrišn [ast kū]{.underline} awēšān deh ka xwāhēnd
bēšāzišnīh windēnd*

"when they give him reception (receive him well), [it happens
that]{.underline} those towns (or: some of those towns?), when they ask
(for it), obtain healing" (*Dk*.7.7.37)

##### * **ast čē* "there is something which; some"

*ka az awēšān kē ān paymān kerd mard-ēw ān paymān [ast čē]{.underline}
ǰuttar kerd ān tāywān ō tōzišn ī harw 2 mard rasēd*

"when, of those (two) who made that agreement, [there is
something]{.underline} (of) that agreement that one man has done
differently \[if one of the two \... does something differently\], then
the penalty comes to the paying for both men \[both men are responsible
for paying the penalty for it\]" (*MHD*.20.11)

##### *ast ī \... ast ī*, *ast kē \... ast ī, ast kū \... ast kū* "there is one who \... and another who, one \... another, some \... others"; "sometimes \... sometimes." In these constructions, the *ī* is often omitted:

*xwarrah [ast ī]{.underline} xwēškārīh ud [ast ī]{.underline} pad tan ī
mard*

"(the word) *xwarrah*: [sometimes]{.underline} (it refers to) one's
duties, [sometimes]{.underline} to (what is) in man's body" (*PY*.9.4d)

*abar ān ī harw kadār padiš arzānīg ud ān ī ēč padiš nē arzānīg ud ān ī
[ast kē]{.underline} padiš arzānīg ud [ast ī]{.underline} nē*

"about that which each and every one is worthy of, and that which nobody
is worthy of, and that which [some]{.underline} are worthy of and
[others]{.underline} not"(*Dk*.3.261.1)

*was ruwān ud frawahr andar ān rōd būd hēnd ud [ast ī]{.underline}-šān
pad garān ranǰ hamē widerd ud [ast ī]{.underline} xwārīhā widerd hēnd*

"there were many souls and *frawahr*s in that river; [some]{.underline}
of them passed (across) by heavy toil, [others]{.underline} of them
passed lightly" (*AWN*.16.2)

*was-sardag dad ud dām [ast kū]{.underline} Spēnāg Mēnōy ud [ast
kū]{.underline} Gannāg Mēnōy dām hēnd u-šān abar tō frāz rawišn*

"wild animals and (other) creatures of many kinds, some are the
creations of the Benificent Spirit, others (of) the Foul Spirit, (they
all) have their going forth = go forth upon you (Spandarmad, the Earth)"
(*StS*.5.3)

##### *ast ī* *ka* "sometimes, it happens that":

Note: the *ī* is often not written in the manuscripts.

*čē rāy ka aǰgahān ud duš-āgāh ud wad mard [ast ī ka]{.underline} ō
burzišn ud nēkīh ī wazurg rasēd*

"why (is it) that (lit. when) a lazy and ignorant and bad man
[sometimes]{.underline} comes to honor and great goodness?" (*MX*.50.2)

*kē ān kār ī nē dānēd pad kerdan frāz gīrēd [ast ī ka]{.underline} ān
kār tabāh ud agār bawēd*

"he who undertakes to do something he does not know, [it
happens]{.underline} that the work is destroyed and useless" (*MX*.31.8)

*[ast (ī) ka]{.underline} tēz [ast ī]{.underline} dērang [ast (ī)
ka]{.underline} abāz-rawišn [ast (ī) ka]{.underline} estādag hēnd*

"[sometimes]{.underline} (the planets are) fast, [sometimes]{.underline}
(they are) slow, [sometimes]{.underline} they go backward,
[sometimes]{.underline} they stand still" (*Bd*.5A.9)

Distinguish *(ī) ast* "which is, that is," e.g.:

*u-š az 4 pēšag ī dēn [ast]{.underline} āsrōnīh ud artēštārīh ud
wāstaryōšīh ud hutuxšīh padīrift 4 pēšag [ī ast]{.underline} āsrōnīh ud
artēštārīh ud wāstaryōšīh hutuxšīh* *ud pad-iš frāxēnīd wālēnīd waxšēnīd
gēhān*

"and from the four 'trades' of the *dēn*, [that is]{.underline},
priesthood, soldiery, husbandry, and artisanry, (J̌amšēd) the four
'trades', [that is]{.underline}, priesthood, soldiery, husbandry, and
artisanry received/accepted, and thereby/with them he broadened and made
the world prosper and grow" (*Dk*.7.1.20)

On *[xwad ast]{.underline}* "is itself, is nothing but" and *[ī xwad
ast]{.underline}* "that is, nothing but \... (itself), who/which is
nothing but," see Lesson 15.

### The verb. Ergative constructions with enclitic pronoun as agent

Recall that enclitic pronouns can never be grammatical subject: one
[cannot]{.underline} say "*u-m kunam*"! In the ergative construction,
however, they are very common as agents: *u-m kerd* "I did."

**In main clauses**

*u-[m]{.underline} [pursīd]{.underline} az pērōzgar Srōš ahlaw*

"and [I asked]{.underline} the victorious, Righteous Srōš" (*AWN*.6.2)

Note: *pursīdan* takes the preposition *az* (*az kas pursīdan* "ask
somebody").

*u-[m]{.underline} az ēn and sāl abāz az ašmāh pad nihān
[dāšt]{.underline}*

"and since (for; *az \... abāz*) these many years [I have
kept]{.underline} (him) hidden from you" (*KN*.14.16)

*bē-[m xwāst]{.underline} andar āb ud zamīg ud urwar ud gōspand ud
bālist ī garān ud ān-iz ī zofr rōstāg nē ayāft ǰāmag **kē** mard ī ahlaw
**aziš** bawēd ǰud zan kē ǰeh petyārag*

"(Ohrmazd says: If it had been possible to find one, I would have), but
[I sought]{.underline} in water, earth, plants, beasts and on the
highest of mountains and the deep river (and) did not find a vessel from
which a Righteous man might become (be born) other than (*ǰud*) the
woman, whose adversary is the *ǰeh*" (*Bd*.14a.1)

*ka mard abāg 2 ī pādixšāyīhā ī xwēš paymān kerd kū-[m]{.underline} tō
ud tō hamwindišn [kerd hēd]{.underline}*

*zan ǰud ǰud abāg šōy hamwindišn ud zanān ēk az did ǰud-windišn hēnd*

"when a man has made an agreement with his two 'authoritative' (wives
saying): '[I have made you and you]{.underline} my partners-in-income,'

(then) the wives, each individually, (are) partners-in-income with
husband, and (each) of the wives has separate income from one another"
(*MHDA*.1.3)

*u-[t]{.underline} az 7-sālag abāz frazend ī ēdōn nēkōg az man pad nihān
[dāšt]{.underline}*

"and since (he was) seven-years-old [you have kept]{.underline} such a
good child hidden from me" (*KN*.14.17)

*u-[t]{.underline} hāmōyēn az daxšag bē [hišt]{.underline}
u-[t]{.underline} menišn abāg ōy mihrdruz rāst bē [kerd]{.underline}*

"and [you]{.underline} have [forgotten]{.underline} everything, and [you
have made]{.underline} your thought equal with (made common cause with)
that criminal" (*KN*.10.1/9.6)

*u-[š]{.underline} pas mayānag ī zamīg [suft]{.underline} andar āmad*

"next [he pierced]{.underline} the middle of the earth (and) came
inside" (*Bd*.4.10b)

*u-š wizārišn ēn kū-[š]{.underline} pad ēd [dāšt]{.underline} kū Ohrmazd
andar ōy ačārag*

"and the explanation of it is that [he figured]{.underline} (*pad ēd
dāšt*) that Ohrmazd (was) helpless with respect to (*andar*; = against)
him" (*Bd*.1.22)

*u-[š]{.underline} mēnōyīhā ān dām ī pad ān abzār andar abāyist frāz
[brēhēnīd]{.underline}*

"and [he fashioned]{.underline} forth in the world of thought that
creation which (he) needed as that tool" (*Bd*.1.12)

*ēg-[imān]{.underline} zan [dīd]{.underline} ī was hučihrtar az awēšān
ī-[mān]{.underline} pad gēhān [dīd]{.underline}*

"then [we saw]{.underline} a woman who (was) much more beautiful than
those whom [we have seen]{.underline} in the world of the living" (after
Kerdīr)

*čē-[mān]{.underline} andar-iz pārs [dīd]{.underline} kē-š kār pad nēmag
mizd ī ān ī pēš pad uzēn andar abāyist padīrift ud mizd stad*

"for I have seen, even in Pārs, (someone) who accepted a work at half
the salary of what he previously needed for the expense (of the same
service?) and took the (reduced) salary" (*DD*.65.28)

About payments for religious services.

***wad-[itān]{.underline} ō man [guft]{.underline} andar mardōmān
rawāg-dahišnīh** kū-[tān]{.underline} ēd [guft]{.underline} kū dēn rawāg
kerd dušwār*

"'bad,---[you told]{.underline} me---is the giving (of the *dēn*)
currency among men', that is, [you said]{.underline} this: it is
difficult to make the *dēn* current" (*PY*.43.11d).

Note that *rawāg* means literally "going (forth)"; here,
*rawāg-dahišnīh* renders Av. *zraz-dāiti*, which may have meant
something like "confidence."

*čiyōn gōwēd kū drāyist Ganāg Mēnōy ō dēwān kū ēd wād murnǰēnēd ī čēr ī
tagīg ī Ohrmazd-dād*

*čē ka-[tān]{.underline} wād [murnǰēnīd]{.underline} ā-[tān]{.underline}
harwisp dām [murnǰēnīd bawēd]{.underline}*

"as it says (in the *dēn*): the Foul Spirit howled to the demons:
"destroy this Wind, victorious, fleet, set in place by Ohrmazd; for when
you have destroyed the Wind, then you will have destroyed the entire
creation'!" (*Bd*.21.4)

For *[murnǰēnīd bawēd]{.underline}*, see Lesson 15: Constructions of
result.

*u-š brāh ud payrōg dūr gyāg payrōgīhist rāy ēg-[išān]{.underline} nē
[ayāft hēnd]{.underline} čār*

"and, because its (the *xwarrah*) brilliance and shine shone far away,
they (the demons) did not obtain any means (to harm Z.)" (*WZ*.8.9)

Here, *ayāft hend* either agrees with *čār* "means, ways" or it is a New
Persian construction *yāftand* "they obtained."

*Wāy-hayār guft kū būd kē pahikārišn ēn būd kū tis ī sālārīh ǰuttar bē
būd čē ān zamān ādurōg būd bē-[šān]{.underline} ǰuttar bē nē
[kerd]{.underline}*

"Wāy-hayār said: there was one (lawyer) who had the following argument:
(in that case) the matter of guardianship was different, for at that
time it was (about) a small fire, but they (the lawyers involved) did
not do (≈ decide) differently" (*MHD*.26.24, Macuch, chap. 12, ms. p.
27)

About the ownership of a fire someone has founded and a specific case
that is cited.

##### With direct and indirect objects:

*abar xwānēnd druwandān ō ahlawān kū ān ī man pid ud brād ud šōy ud zan
ud dōst čiyōn kū-[t]{.underline} pad zamīg nē [hammōxt ō
man]{.underline} ān ī abēzag rāh ī rāst u-[t]{.underline} bē (nē)
[wardēnīd ham]{.underline} az wināh u-[t]{.underline} nē [hāxt
ham]{.underline} ō kerbag* "The wicked call out to the Righteous: O my
father, brother, husband, wife, and friend! How come (*čiyōn kū*) [you
did]{.underline} not on earth [teach me]{.underline} (ind. obj.) the
pure straight road and [you did]{.underline} (not) [turn me]{.underline}
away from sin and [you did]{.underline} not [lead me]{.underline} to
good deeds?" (*WZ*.35.42; after the resurrection)

##### Without grammatical subject:

Some verbs that we regard as intransitive are transitive in Pahlavi and
so (sometimes) use the ergative in the past, e.g., *kō(x)š-* "make an
effort, struggle," *xand-* "laugh":

*andar ān wārān-kerdārīh [Aspanǰarūš ud Apaoš kōxšīd hēnd]{.underline}*

"during that rain-making [Aspanǰarūš and Apaoš struggled]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.6B.15) \[intrans.\]

*u-[š]{.underline} abāg druz ī mēnōy [kōxšīd]{.underline}*

"and [he]{.underline} (the Buland-sūd fire) [struggled]{.underline} with
the lie-demon in the other world" (*WZ*.3.83) \[ergative\]

*ēk ēw paydāg kū-[š]{.underline} pad zāyišn bē [xandīd]{.underline}*

"one thing is manifest: [he]{.underline} (Z.) [laughed]{.underline} at
birth" (*Dk*.7.3.2)

*amahrspandān pērāmōn ī ātaxš nišast hēnd u-[šān griyist]{.underline}*

"the amahrspands sat around the Fire and [they wept]{.underline}"
(*PR*.18d.6) (when Ohrmazd had decided to send the Fire down to earth)

#### Verb raised

When the verb is raised/fronted (Lesson 1), the agent may be expressed
by an enclitic pronoun attached to the verb. The auxiliary may then be
separated from its verb:

*[guft-iš]{.underline} Ohrmazd ka-š zan brēhēnīd kū
[dād]{.underline}-iz-[im hē tō]{.underline} kē-t ǰehīn sardag petyārag*

"when Ohrmazd had fashioned the woman, [he said]{.underline}: [I
established you]{.underline}, too, whose opponent is the whore (*ǰeh*)
species" (*Bd*.14a.1)

##### Verb raised and agent a noun with anticipating pronoun

When the agent is a noun, it may be anticipated by a pronoun in the
following way:

*u-[š]{.underline} guft [mēnōy āsmān]{.underline} ō Gannāg Mēnōy*

"and [he]{.underline}, [the divine sky]{.underline}, [said]{.underline}
to the Foul Spirit" (*Bd*.4.12).

*u-[š]{.underline} guft [Ohrmazd]{.underline} kū nē harwisp-kerdār hē
Gannāg Mēnōy kū-t man nē tuwān marnǰēnīdan*

"[Ohrmazd said]{.underline}: you are not omnipotent, O Foul Spirit,
i.e., you are not able to destroy me" (*Bd*.1.23)

*u-[š]{.underline} drāyīd [Gannāg Mēnōy]{.underline} ka-š karzag dād kū
dād-im hē tō kē karzag hē*

"and, when he had established (set in its place) the snake, [the Foul
Spirit howled]{.underline}: I established you, you who are the snake
\..." (*Bd*.23.3)

*u-[š]{.underline} nē ayāft [Gannāg Mēnōy]{.underline} widarg ī
abāz-dwārišnīh*

"and [the Foul Spirit did not obtain]{.underline} (find) a passage to
rush back (through)" (*Bd*.6a.4)

*u-[šān]{.underline} dīd [frawahr ī mardōmān]{.underline} pad ān xrad ī
harwisp-āgāh anāgīh (ī) az druz ud Ahrimen andar gētīy padiš rasēd*

"and [the fravashis of men saw]{.underline} by the all-aware wisdom the
evil which would come upon (them) in the world of the living from the
Lie and Ahrimen" (*Bd*.3.26; they are in heaven discussing with Ohrmazd,
who wants to send them down)

### 

### The ergative construction in subordinate clauses

#### Agent of a subordinate clause is a noun, a relative pronoun, or an enclitic pronoun

When the agent of a subordinate clause is a noun, for instance a proper
name, the agent is often "raised" before the conjunction and often
repeated by an enclitic pronoun attached to the conjunction. Other parts
of the subordinate clause may also be so "raised."

##### In temporal, conditional, and other subordinate clauses:

*[ka-šān]{.underline} am bē [kirrēnīd]{.underline} xwarrah ī am az
dast ī Dahāg Ādur ī Farrōbay bōzēnīd*

"[when they cut]{.underline} Jam in half, (it was) the Farrōbay Fire
(that) delivered am's *xwarrah* from the hand(s) of Dahāg" (*Bd*.18.6)

*[mowbedān mowbed ka-š dīd]{.underline} kū \...*

"(as for) [the supreme *mowbed*, when he saw]{.underline} that = when
the supreme *mowbed* [saw]{.underline} that \..." (*KN*.11.8/10.9)

*[Gannāg Mēnōy ka-š]{.underline} agārīh ī xwēš abesihišn ī dēwān hamist
[dīd]{.underline} stard [būd]{.underline}*

"[when the Foul Spirit saw]{.underline} his own undoing together with
the annihilation of the demons, [he became]{.underline} stunned"
(*Bd*.1.29) \[trans. + intrans.\]

*ān ī andar ōšyārīh (gōwēd) ud ān-iz ī ham mard bē ō duxt dād
[agar-iš]{.underline} ōšyārīhā [dād]{.underline} ka wēmār būd ēg-iz
rawāg dahišn ud [agar-iš]{.underline} nē andar ōšyārīh dād ēdōn bawēd
čiyōn ka an-handarz murd*

"(as for) that which he, while of sound mind, says (in his will) and
that which said man gave to the daughter, [if he gave]{.underline} it
while of sound mind, (even) when he was sick, then too (it was) OK to
give it, and [if he did not give]{.underline} it while of sound mind, it
becomes just as if he had died intestate" (DD.53.8)

> A man has given his property to one of his daughters, and the other
> daughters plead that he did it while in great pain and not while of
> sound mind)

*kanīzag [ān saxwan čiyōn-iš]{.underline} ō Ardawān [guft]{.underline}
.. abāz guft*

"the girl repeated that story as [she had told]{.underline} it to
Ardawān" (*KN*.3.8/2.7)

*ēn pursišnīhā [čiyōn-imān pursīd]{.underline} ēg-**imān** rōšnīhā
**awiš** framāyēd nimūdan*

"please (*framāyēd*) explain **to us** clearly these questions [as we
have asked]{.underline} (them)" (*DD*.65.18)

*[čiyōn-itān]{.underline} amāh [dād hēm]{.underline} amahrspandān ēdōn
amāh srāyišn dahēd*

"[as you created]{.underline} us, O *amahrspand*s, so give us
protection!" (*PY*.58.5)

##### In relative clauses:

*ān ī-[tān]{.underline} [dīd]{.underline} ān gōwēd*

"that which [you saw]{.underline} (have seen), that do tell!" (Kerdīr)

*harw kē-[š]{.underline} pad duščašmīh padiš [nigerīd]{.underline} bē
ōzad*

"whomever [he]{.underline} \[agent\] [looked]{.underline} at (*kē \...
padiš*) with his evil eye was killed" (*Bd*.33.9)

Here, *harw* is gr.-subject of *nigerīd*, the enclitic pronoun *-š* is
the agent of *nigerīd*, and *padiš* governs *kē*.

*was dēw būd hēnd [kē-šān]{.underline} ǰud ǰud duškunišnīh ī xwēš
gōkānīg [ōšmurd]{.underline}*

"there were many demons, [who]{.underline} [enumerated]{.underline}
separately in detail their evil-doings" (after *Bd*.4.3)

*weh dēn ī mazdēsnān [kē]{.underline} [Ohrmazd]{.underline} ō Zarduxšt
[čāšt]{.underline}*

"the Good *dēn* of the Mazdeans, [which]{.underline} \[gramm. subject\]
[Ohrmazd]{.underline} \[agent\] [taught]{.underline} to Zarduxšt"
(*AWN*.12.5)

*nēk tō bawād ay tan ī sazōmand kē-[t]{.underline} man buland [kerd
ham]{.underline} kē-[t]{.underline} man nazdīk [rasēnīd ham]{.underline}
ō ān ī pahlom axwān*

"good for you, o ephemeral body, [who made me]{.underline} (the soul)
tall, [who made me come]{.underline} close to the best existence"
(*Dk*.9.19.4)

A relative pronoun can be the agent by itself, or the nature of the
agent may be specified by an enclitic pronoun:

*ka tō kas dīd [kē]{.underline} \... paristišn ī yazdān
[kerd]{.underline}*

"when you saw somebody [who worshipped]{.underline} the gods \..."
(*AWN*.17.13)

*u-m dīd ān ī awēšān ruwān [kē-šān]{.underline} pad gētīy gāhān
[srūd]{.underline} ud yašt [kerd]{.underline} ud āstawān
[būd]{.underline} (hēnd) pad weh dēn ī mazdēsnān*

"and I saw the souls of those (who they \>) [who]{.underline} in this
world [recited]{.underline} the Gathas and [performed]{.underline}
sacrifices and [believed]{.underline} in the good *dēn* of the
Mazdayasnian" (*AWN*.12.5)

##### Relative clauses with embedded statements

Relative pronouns, with or without enclitic pronouns attached, are often
qualified by other subordinate clauses:

*pas ō āb mad [ī]{.underline}-m guft [kū]{.underline} azēr ī ēn zamīg
[winnārd estēd]{.underline}*

"next he fell upon the water, [which]{.underline} I said that [it was
set]{.underline} up below this earth" = "which I said was set up"
(*Bd*.4.10b)

*kū ast ān mard [kē]{.underline}-t guft [kū]{.underline} ō gētīy
[daham]{.underline}*

"where is that man of yours [whom]{.underline} you said: '[I shall
give]{.underline} (= you would give) to the world of the living'?"
(after *Bd*.4a.2)

*man ān dād fraškerd-kerdār ahlāyēnīdār Sōšāns [kē]{.underline} gōwēnd
mardōm [kū nē rasēd]{.underline}*

"I created that maker of the Renovation, Sōšāns, who will make Order,
[who]{.underline} people say [will not come]{.underline}" (*Dk*.9.33.1)

*ān frazend ī-š ašmāh framūd kū bē ōzan u-[mān]{.underline} nē
[ōzad]{.underline}*

"that child which you ordered (us): 'kill him (*-š \... ōzan*)!' (=
ordered us to kill), [we did]{.underline} not [kill]{.underline}"
(*KN*.11.10/10.11)

Note the distance between the direct object *-š* and the imperative
*ōzan*.

##### Unusual word order:

Unusual word order is found, especially in imitation of Avestan
originals:

*kū-š kār kerbag ān and kerd estēd čand spīg ī urwarān ka pad wahār frāz
waxšēd **kē**-[š dād]{.underline} **was** [Ohrmazd]{.underline} **ān
spīg***

"\... that he has performed as many good deeds as the sprouts of plants
when it (they) grow up in spring, **which** [he established]{.underline}
**many** (of), [Ohrmazd]{.underline}, **those sprouts**" (*ŠnŠ.*12.2)

#### Indefinite agent

An idefinite agent can be expressed by the 3rd plur. enclitic *-šān*,
cf. *gōwēnd* "they say, it is said," etc.:

*Yazdgerd ō Turkestān šud [u-šān]{.underline} ānōh [ōzad]{.underline}*

"Yazdegerd went to Turkistan, [and they killed him]{.underline} (= he
was killed) there" (*Bd*.33.25)

*Uzaw ī Tōhmāspān wārān kerd [ī-šān]{.underline} nōg-wārānīh
[xwānd]{.underline}*

"Uzaw son of Tōhmāsp made rain (after the drought), which they called (=
was called) New Rain" (*Bd*.33.6)

#### 

#### Ergative with a sequence of enclitic pronouns

When we have two enclitic pronouns in an ergative construction, then, as
in non-ergative constructions, the context will determine which is agent
and which is some other part of the sentence, e.g.:

*kū-m-[it]{.underline} gāh meh bē [kerd ham]{.underline}*

"i.e., [you]{.underline} (*-it* agent) [made]{.underline} my (*-m* poss.
pronoun) position greater (higher)" (*HN*.2.14)

*ka kē ō ānōh kāmag ā[-t]{.underline}-iš kāmag [dād]{.underline}*

"when (it was someone) whose wish (was) toward yonder (the other world),
then [you]{.underline} (*-t* = agent) [gave]{.underline} him (*-iš* =
ind. obj.) (his) wish" (*PY*.31.11)

#### Sequences of transitive and intransitive verbs with agent = noun

*[Wehdād]{.underline} ī Ādur-Ohrmazdān ī mowbedān mowbed \... frāz ō
gyāg-ēw [mad u-š]{.underline} hērbed mard 2 [dīd]{.underline} kē esm az
kōf pad pušt ī xwēš hamē kašīd*

"[Wehdād]{.underline} son of Ādur-Ohrmazd, the chief mowbed,
[came]{.underline} to a place [and he saw]{.underline} to *hērbed*s, who
were carrying (lit. "dragging") firewood from the mountain on their
backs" (*Dk*.6D.5)

*[mardōm]{.underline} kē-šān dōšīd ān ī wattar ī pad menišn ēdōn abāg
xešm ō ham [dwārīd hēnd u-šān wēmārēnīd]{.underline} axwān ī mardōmān*

"[people]{.underline} who chose the worse (things) in thought, thus
[ran]{.underline} together with Wrath, [and they sickened]{.underline}
the worlds of men" (*Purs*.4.2)

#### 

#### Sequences of intransitive and transitive verbs with agent = noun and/or enclitic pronoun

When a noun is the agent of a sequence of coordinated or subordinated
clauses with transitive verbs, it can be resumed by an enclitic pronoun,
but not necessarily:

##### In main clauses with agent:

*pas [Ohrmazd]{.underline} Ādur Gušnasp pad Ādurbādagān pad warahrānīh
bē [nišāst]{.underline} u-[š guft]{.underline} kū*

"then [Ohrmazd established]{.underline} the Gušnasp fire as a Warahrān
("victorious" fire) in Azerbaijan, and [he said]{.underline}: \..."
(*PR*.46.31-2)

##### In main clauses without agent:

*ud pas [awēšān haft mard]{.underline} bē [nišast hēnd]{.underline} ud
az haft 3 ud az 3 ēk-ēw Wirāz nām bē [wizīd]{.underline}*

"and then [those seven men sat down]{.underline} and [chose]{.underline}
three out of the seven and (then) one out of the three, whose name was
Wirāz" (*AWN*.1.19) \[intrans. + trans.\]

##### In complex sentences: agent repeated

*[Pābag]{.underline} ka-[š]{.underline} nāmag [dīd]{.underline} andōhgen
būd u-[š]{.underline} pad passox [ī]{.underline} ō Ardaxšīr
[kerd]{.underline} [nibišt]{.underline} kū*

"when [Pābag saw]{.underline} the letter [he became]{.underline} sad,
and [he]{.underline} (*-š*) [wrote]{.underline} in the answer [which
(he) made]{.underline} to Ardaxšīr that \..." (*KN*.2.24-25/1.41-42)

*[Pābag]{.underline} ka-[š]{.underline} pad ān ēwēnag [dīd]{.underline}
abd sahist u-[š]{.underline} dānāgān ud xwamn-wizārān ō pēš
[xwāst]{.underline}*

"when Pābag [saw]{.underline} in that way he marveled, and [he
called]{.underline} the wise men and the dream interpreters (to come)
before (him)" (*KN*.1.11/1.12)

*mowbedān mowbed ka-[š]{.underline} [dīd]{.underline} kū Ardaxšīr az ān
kār ō pašēmānīh [mad]{.underline} pad rōy [ōbast]{.underline} u-[š
guft]{.underline} \...*

"when [the supreme *mowbed* saw]{.underline} that Ardaxšīr regretted
that matter, [he fell]{.underline} upon his face, and [he]{.underline}
(*-š*) [said]{.underline}" (*KN*.11.8/10.9) \[trans. + intrans. +
trans.\]

*ēg [ān čarātīg]{.underline} [estād]{.underline} u-[š]{.underline} bē-iz
[nigerīd]{.underline}*

"then that woman [stood]{.underline} and [she looked]{.underline}
around" (*Dk*.7.2.12) \[intrans. + trans.\]

##### 

##### In complex sentences: agent not repeated

*ud pas ōy [Wirāz]{.underline} čiyōn-išān ān saxwan [āšnūd]{.underline}
abar ō pāy [estād]{.underline} ud dast pad kaš [kerd]{.underline} ud
[guft]{.underline}*

"and then that [Wirāz]{.underline}, when [he heard]{.underline} that
speech of theirs, [got up]{.underline}, [placed]{.underline} his hands
under the armpits, and [said]{.underline}" (*AWN*.1.20) \[trans. +
intrans. + trans. + trans.\]

In the following example, the subject of the intransitive verb *šud*
"went" becomes grammatical subject of the transitive past verb *ōzad*
"killed," resulting in an agentless = passive construction *u-šān ānōh
ōzad* "and they killed (him) there" = "and he was killed by them there":

*Yazdgerd \... ō Xwarāsān ud Turkestān [šud]{.underline} asp ud mard ō
hayārīh xwāst u-[šān]{.underline} ānōh [ōzad]{.underline}*

"[Yazdegerd]{.underline} [went]{.underline} to Xwarāsān and Turkestān,
[called]{.underline} for horses and men (to come) to (his) aid, and
[they killed him]{.underline} there" (*Bd*.33.20) \[intrans. +
trans./pass.\]

#### The "indirect affectee"

Occasionally we find constructions (especially in relative clauses) in
which the verb agrees, not with the grammatical subject, but with
whoever is more logically affected by an action, even if this person or
thing is grammatically a possessive pronoun or governed by a
pre/postposition, with which compare English "[I was given]{.underline}
a book = a book [was given to me]{.underline}":

*u-š guft Ohrmazd kū wēmār [hē]{.underline} Gōšurūn az ān ī Gannāg Mēnōy
wēmārīh ud [kēn ī dēwān abar burd hē]{.underline}*

"and Ohrmazd said: you are sick, Gōšurūn, with the Foul Spirit's
sickness and the malice which [you were brought upon]{.underline} by the
demons = which the demons [have brought upon you]{.underline} (implicit
in *hē*)" (*Bd*.4.31)

*u-[šān]{.underline} pas petyārag pad menišn abar dwārist [u-š menišn bē
āhōgēnīd hēnd]{.underline} u-šān drāyīd kū Gannāg Mēnōy dād āb ud zamīg
ud urwar ud abārīg tis*

"then the Adversary rushed into their thoughts, and he fouled their
(implicit in *hēnd*) thought, and they howled: the Foul Spirit
established the water, the earth, the plants, and the other things"
(*Bd*.14.15)

*ēd ast ān xwarrah kē-š mardōm [awiš dahīhist]{.underline}* (*awiš* +
implicit "them" in *\[hēnd\]*)

"this is the Xwarrah that [men were given]{.underline} by him"
(*WZ*.3.74)

*az ēn 350 drahm [awiš dād ham]{.underline}* (*awiš* + implicit "me" in
*ham*)

"from these 350 drahms [were given to me]{.underline} (implicit in
*ham*)" (*DD*. 65.15)

Also English: "I was given 350 drahm"

*ēg-**it** zaxm ud pādifrāh čē rāy [padiš nē kerd ham]{.underline}*
(*padiš* + implicit "me" in *ham*)

"so why did you not hurt and punish me?" (*AWN*.68.9)

*ā-**šān** Ohrmazd pušt-ēw [**abāg** bē kerd hēnd]{.underline}*

"then Ohrmazd sent with them (implicit in *hēnd*) something to help them
(accept)" (*PR*.14.3)

Animals agree to be used as sacrificial victims.

*mēnōy āsn-xrad ō dānāg guft kū*

*ēd ī-[t]{.underline} pad dārišn ī tan ud bōzišn ī ruwān rāy
[pursīd]{.underline} [u-m xūbīhā awiš guft ud handarzēnīd
hē]{.underline} awiš nēk pardaz*

*ud pad kār dār čē-t ēd ast mahist rāh pad dārišn ī tan ud bōzišn ī
ruwān*

"the divine Inborn Wisdom said to the knowledgeable (man):

this which [you asked]{.underline} about the upkeep of the body and the
salvation of the soul and (which) [I told you]{.underline} (*-m \...
awiš guft \[hē\]*) well and [advised you]{.underline} (about)
(*handarzēnīd hē*), set about it well!

and keep working at it! for this is your greatest way to the upkeep of
the body and the salvation of the soul" (*MX*.1.195-198)

#### Ergative in the pluperfect of transitive verbs

The agential pluperfect is construed just like the past tense, e.g.:

*pas az ān ī [Ardaxšīr]{.underline} ān Kirm [ōzad būd]{.underline} abāz
āmad*

"after [Ardaxšīr had killed]{.underline} that Kirm he returned"
(*KN*.10.1/9.1)

*ka-[š]{.underline} bē [kerd būd]{.underline} ā-š andar ō tan burd*

"when [he had made it]{.underline}, he brought it into the body"
(*PR*.46.3)

*ka-[š dād būd hēnd]{.underline} 3 rad \...*

"when [he had established]{.underline} the three *rad*s *\...*"
(*Bd*.1.52)

*pas Ohrmazd Ahunwar frāz srūd \... ka-[š]{.underline} 2 bahr [guft
būd]{.underline} Gannāg Mēnōy pad šnūg andar ōbast*

"then Ohrmazd recited the Ahunwar \... when [he had spoken]{.underline}
two parts \... the Evil Spirit fell on his knees" (*Bd*.1.30)

*pad gōwišn ī Ohrmazd paydāg kū guft ō awēšān ka-[š dād būd
hēnd]{.underline} kū mard-ēd* \[for *hēd*\] *dād-im* *hēd pid ī harwisp
ox ī astōmand* "it is manifest by the word of Ohrmazd that he said to
them when [he had made them]{.underline}: 'you are men; I made you
father of the entire existence with bones'" (*Dk*.7.1.9)

#### Mixed ergative/active constructions

In a few texts we encounter the influence of modern Persian, in which
transitive verbs are construed just as intransitive verbs in the past
tenses:

*andar ān stardīh kamālīgān dēwān ǰud ǰud [dōyīd hēnd]{.underline}*

"during that unconsciousness (of the Evil Spirit) the demons with
(demon) heads individually [shouted]{.underline}" \[instead of *dōyīd*\]
(*Bd*.4.2)

*Salm ud Tūz andar pidar a-burd-framān [šud hēnd]{.underline} ud Ēriǰ ī
brād ī xwēš rāy bē [ōzad hēnd]{.underline}*

"Salm and Tūz became (*šud hēnd* = Persian *šodand*) diobedient toward
(their) father and killed their own brother Ēriǰ (*rāy* dir. obj.)"
(*Māh Frawardīn* 15) --- Persian: *barādar-e xod rā be-koštand*.

*Ardawān aswār frāz rasīd hēnd ud ka-šān zanišn pad ān ēwēnag dīd abd
sahist ud pursīd kū ēn zanišn kē kerd*

*Ardaxšīr guft kū [man kerd ham]{.underline} pus ī Ardawān guft kū nē čē
[man kerd ham]{.underline}*

"Ardawān and the horsemen arrived, and when they saw that kind of
striking \[Ardaxšīr had shot a wild ass straight through the stomach\],
they wondered and asked: 'who made this strike?'

Ardaxšīr said: '[I did]{.underline}!'; Ardawān's son also said: 'no! for
[I did]{.underline}!'" (*KN*.2.15-17/1.34-36)

### Sentence Connectors

#### The conjunction *ud*, *u-*

Main clauses following subordinate clauses are often introduced by *ud*
or *u-* with enclitic pronoun, for instance in ergative constructions,
where a particle is often needed to attach an enclitic agent. It can
often be translated as a weak "and yet, but," e.g.:

*Kay-Wištāsp ka az wistar frāz būd u-š ō Hudōs guft kū \...*

"when Kay-Wištāsp got up from bed [he]{.underline} said to Hudōs (his
wife): \..." (*Dk*.7.4.86)

*J̌am ī šēd ī Wiwanghān \... ka az druz frēbīhist u-š* *az Ohrmazd
bandagīh bē ō abardom xwadāyīh ārzōgēnīd*

"radiant Jam son of Wīwangh, when he was deceived by the Lie, (then)
from being Ohrmazd's bondsman, desired (*-uš \... ārzōgēnīd*) the
highest kingship" (*DD*.38.19)

Occasionally, *u-* \<AP̄-\> may just be a connecting vowel for enclitics:

*gyāg-ēw paydāg kū Zarduxšt az Ohrmazd pursīd kū [haguriz
u-t]{.underline}* \[*haguriz-ut*\] *miyazd kerd*

"it is manifest in one place (in the *dēn*) that Zarduxšt asked Ohrmazd:
'Did you ever perform a *myazd* (ritual)?" (*PR*.16b.1)

#### The enclitic particle *-iz* (C-) "and, too, also"

This particle is used alone or combined with *ud* (*ud \... -iz*).
Enclitic pronouns follow *-iz*, e.g.:

***kē-m** **būd** **hēnd** abarmānd az pidarān ud kē-[iz]{.underline}-im
hēnd handōxt ī xwēš*

"'those that were for me', the inheritence from my parents and also
those (things) that are mine (as) what I myself have accumulated"
(*PY*.33.10)

*guft-iš Ohrmazd ka-š zan brēhēnīd kū dād-[iz-im]{.underline} hē tō kē-t
ǰehīn sardag petyārag*

"Ohrmazd said when he had fashioned the woman: '[I]{.underline} gave you
[too]{.underline} (to the world), who (will have) the *ǰeh* species as
your adversary'" (*Bd*.14a.1)

*ud ka-[iz-išān]{.underline} ham-gumēzišnīh kerd ēg-išān
frazend-zāyišnīh nē būd*

"[and]{.underline} also when [they]{.underline} had mingled together
(had intercourse), then they had no birth of children" (*Bd*.14.29)

Double [*-iz \... -iz* "both \... and"]{.underline} is often found in
imitation of Avestan:

\[Av.:\]

*āa ahe paitiiārəm frākərəṇta aŋrō mainiiuš pouru.mahrkō*

*[ažimca]{.underline} yim raoiδitəm [ziiąmca]{.underline} daēuuō.dātəm*

Then the Evil Spirit full of destruction whittled forth as its
antagonist

a dragon, the red, and the winter made by the evil gods.

***u-š pad ān ī ōy petyāragīh frāz kirrēnīd Gannāg Mēnōy ī purr-marg***

***[az-iz]{.underline} ī rōdīg** was bawēd **[zamestān-iz]{.underline} ī
dēwān-dād** stahmagtar bawēd*

And for its opposition, he, the Foul Spirit, full of death, whittled
forth

[both the dragon]{.underline} in the river ---there are many---[and the
winter]{.underline} set in place by the demons---it is harsher

(*PV*.1.2)

With both subordinate clause and main clause introduced by *-iz*:

*ka-**[iz]{.underline}** az amāh dūr hē ēg-[iz]{.underline} az tis ī
amāh abāz ma est*, *ud ka-[**iz**-it]{.underline} tis ī gētīy nē xūb
estād*

*ēg-[iz]{.underline} amāh ēzēš u-mān franāmēš*

"[both when]{.underline} you are far from us, then, too, do not avoid
(*az \... abāz est-*) our matters, [and when]{.underline} matters of
this world shall not go (*nē \... estād* subj.) well for you,

then, too, you shall sacrfice to us and promote us" (*Dk*.9.39.2; *-ēš*,
optative, Lesson 15)

#### The particle *ā-* (--A) "then"

This particle is rarely used alone; usually, it takes an enclitic
pronoun. In most manuscripts, it usually does not take the connected,
but free form, e.g., MA, TA \<'-m, '-t\> *ā-m*, *ā-t*. Sometimes it is
written together with the following word, e.g.: WtdahA *ā-šāyēd* "then
it is allowed," a¬A \<'LA\> *ā-nē* "then \... not." The sense of "then"
is more or less accentuated, but sometimes it is just a particle to
attach an enclitic to. Whether independent or with enclitic, often it
need not be translated:

##### Without enclitic:

*ka nasāy-ēw az bērōn pad xumb-ēw abāz estēd kē-š may andar
[ā]{.underline} xumb rēman may pāk*

"when a dead thing reaches to the outside of a jar in which there is
wine, [then]{.underline} the jar is unclean, the wine clean"
(*ŠnŠ*.2.30)

*3 sāl urwar harw čē nē abāyēd [ā]{.underline} nē hōšēd*

"for three years, every plant that does not have to, does not dry out"
(*PR*.48.3)

*čē paydāg kū Ahrimen ī gizistag ka-š abāg xwēš-tan kūn-marz kerd
[ā]{.underline} garāntar būd čiyōn ka-š abāg dēwān kerd*

"for it is manifest that, when the accursed Ahrimen performed anal
intercourse with himself, it was a heavier (sin) than (*čiyōn*) when he
did (it) with the (male) demons" (*PR*.8d.2)

##### With enclitic:

*Gannāg Mēnōy dād wattarīh u-š kāmag ēn kū [ā-m]{.underline} ma pursēd
u-m ma šnāsēd čē agar-im pursēd ud šnāsēd az pas ī man nē āyēd*

"the Foul Spirit created badness, and he wished the following: Do not
ask [me]{.underline} and do not recognize me! For if you ask me and
recognize me, you will not follow me" (*Bd*.27.50)

*ēd kū-š andar ān āsmān dādestān čiyōn bawēd [ā-m]{.underline} nē dīd*

"this that: 'what justice there will be in that
heaven'---[I]{.underline} did not see" (*Dk*.7.3.29)

*ka man nēk būd ham [ā-t]{.underline} nēktar kerd ham*

"when I was good, [then you]{.underline} made me better (still)"
(*AWN*.4.14)

*ka xwaršēd-nigerišn būd ud paydāg kū mard abāz šawēd hixr ī
[ā-š]{.underline} az tan āyēd čiyōn -- pad nasāy dārišn*

"when (the dead fetus) has "seen the sun" and (it is) clear that it is a
person(?), (but) goes back (in), how (is) the *hixr* that
[then]{.underline} comes from [her]{.underline} body?" (*ZFJ*.472)

*ōy kē-š zan nē būd [ā-š]{.underline} zan dahēnd zan kē-š šōy nē būd
[ā-š]{.underline} šōy dahēnd*

"he 'who for him there was' = who had no wife, ([then]{.underline}) [to
him]{.underline} they will give a wife, and the woman who had no
husband, ([then]{.underline}) [to her]{.underline} they will give a
husband" (*PR*.48.63-64)

*mardōm ka az gētīy bē šawēnd ka-š ruwān āmār bē kunēnd ēd ka-š kerbag
wēš kū wināh [ā-š]{.underline} bē ō wahišt nayēnd*

"when people go from this world, when they do the counting of his soul,
(in) this (case?), when his good deeds (are) more than his sins,
[then]{.underline} they lead [him]{.underline} to paradise" (*PR*.15b.1)

*ēn kū ān ī ō dām rasēd tā fraškerd [ā-š]{.underline} dānist*

"(the reason was) this that: what would come upon the world until the
Renovation---[he]{.underline} (Ohrmazd) knew" (*Bd*.1.52d)

*u-š Frēdōn hāxt ōy-iz Ohrmazd tar menīd u-š pad ān tar-menišnīh
[ā-š]{.underline} zarmān abar ōbast*

"and he (Ahrimen) made Frēdōn (his) follower; and he (*ōy*, Frēdōn)
scorned Ohrmazd, and, for that scorn of his (*-š*), old age fell upon
[him]{.underline} (*-š \... abar*)" (*PR*.47.9)

*ka-šān anāgīh abar rasēd [ā-mān]{.underline} abāz dāštan nē tuwān*

"when evil comes upon them, ([then]{.underline}) [we]{.underline} will
not be able to hold it back" (*ŠnŠ*.9.13)

*J̌am ō dēwān guft kū ul ēdar zāyēd abēzag ahlaw Zarduxšt kē ašmāh kē dēw
hēd [ā-tān]{.underline} ān ī kerd axwāyišnīh dahēd kū bē ačārēnēd*

"Jam said to the demons: here the pure Righteous Zarduxšt will be born,
who will 'give non-seeking' to that which [you]{.underline}, who are
demons, have done, that is, he will incapacitate you" (*Dk*.7.2.60)

After a non-extant Avestan passage, in which the *ainišti* "lack of
wish" of the demons was mentioned, as in *Yašt* 13.130: *ainištōiš
daēuuō.frakarštaiiå* "the *ainišti* dragged forth by the *daēuua*s,"
with *frakaršta* "dragged forth" understood as containing *kərəta*
"made."

*abar ham dar ēn-iz gōwēd kū ān was ka nigerēnd [ā-šān
wurrōyēd]{.underline} druwandān ān nīrang ī war*

"it says in the same chapter that, when those many watch it, [then they
believe]{.underline} the rite of the ordeal (even if they are) wicked"
(*Dk*.9.40.12)

*ud mad andar ham* (*zamānag*) *ō Waēz ī Ēriǰ [ā-iz]{.underline} raft
abāg Nēryōsang yazd ō Mānušēr*

"and (the *xwarrah*) came in the same (period) to Waēz son of Ēriǰ, [and
then]{.underline} it went with the god Nēryōsang to Manūšēr"
(*Dk*.7.1.29)

*ka-š gugāh abāyēd nīd kū-m ēn tis bē ō tō nē dād [ā-iz-iš]{.underline}
ōh nayēnd*

"when he needs to lead (adduce) a witness (to testify) that: 'I did not
give you this!' [then too]{.underline} they (shall) lead
[him]{.underline} in the usual way" (*PR*.10e.1)

The particle *ā-* is especially common in the Pahlavi translations of
the *Avesta*, e.g.:

***āgāh ham ān kē ham Ohrmazd axwāstār** ēn kū-m ēn atuwānīgīh čē rāy
dānam*

***man ka kam-ramag** kū-m xwāstag kam **ud ka-iz kam-mard ham** kū-m
gund ud abzār kam [ā-iz]{.underline} nē dānam kū čē rāy*

"'I am aware of the one who I am, O Ohrmazd: a non-seeker', (i.e.) this:
that I know why I have this lack of capacity, --- 'I, when I have few
herds,' i.e., my possessions are little, 'and also when (or: even if) I
have few men,' i.e., that my flock and tools (resources?) are few,
[then, too]{.underline}, I do not know: why?" (*PY*.46.2)

***Wahman pid** hē tō pid ī Wahman hē*

***ka-m tō pad hamčašmīh ō ham grift hē** kū-m pad harw 2 čašm dīd hē
[ā-m]{.underline} ēdōn menīd kū pid ī Wahman hē*

" 'you are Wahman's father' \[i.e.\] you are the father of Wahman; ---
'when I seized you together by eye-togetherness,' i.e., I saw you with
(my) two eyes, [then]{.underline} I thought: You are Wahman's father"
(*PY*.31.8)

***amāwand awēšān yazdān** kū awēšān amāwandtar bē kund*

***kē amahrspandān huxwadāyān hudahāgān** [ā-iz-išān]{.underline}
amāwandtar bē kund*

" 'Powerful those gods', i.e., one makes them more powerful. --- 'the
*amahrspand*s, having a good lord, giving good gifts', [then
too]{.underline} one makes them more powerful" (*PVr*.9.4de)

***ka-iz padīrēnd ō druwandān hayārīh** [ā-iz]{.underline} pad xrad ī
awēšān bawēd*

" 'also when they accept help for (= to help) wicked people',
[then]{.underline}, too, it is according to *their* wisdom" (*PY*.32.14)

####  The adverb *ēg* (WwïdA \<ADYN\'\>) 

This adverb is used freely or to introduce the main clause after a
subordinate (temporal, conditional, etc.) clause and has the fuller
temporal meaning "then." It can begin a sentence or answer a preceding
clause, e.g.:

##### Introduces main clause not preceded by subordinate clause:

*[ēg]{.underline} spāsdār būdan*

"[then]{.underline} (= next): to be grateful" (*PN*.30)

*[ēg]{.underline} abar pad ān zamān dēwān hanǰamanēnīd*

"[then]{.underline}, at that time, the demons gathered" (*Dk*.7.2.43)

*[ēg]{.underline} Gannāg Mēnōy awēnāg-frazāmīh rāy pad ān paymānag
hamdādestān būd*

"[then]{.underline} the Evil Spirit, because he did not see the end,
agreed to that pact" (*Bd*.1.26)

##### Introduces main clause after subordinate clause:

*mard ka xešm gīrēd [ēg]{.underline}-iš kār ud kerbag frāmōš bawēd*

"when wrath seizes a man, [then]{.underline} (all) good and other
actions are forgotten for him (= he forgets)" (*MX*.1.17)

*kē-š wināh ud kerbag harw 2 rāst [ēg]{.underline}-iš ō hammistagān
dahēnd*

"he whose sins and good deeds are even (balanced = same
amount)---[then]{.underline} they give him (over) to Hammistagān"
(*Bd*.30.32)

*kē ān kār ī nē dānēd pad kerdan frāz gīrēd ast ī ka ān kār tabāh ud
agār bawēd ud ka was-iz ōy mard kē kār ī xwēš hušnūdag kunēd
[ēg-iz]{.underline}-iš ān wināh ō bun bawēd*

"he wo undertakes to do something he does not know, it happens (*ast ī
ka*) that the work is destroyed and useless; and however much that man
who performs his work is satisfied (who is satisfied with his own work),
[then too]{.underline} that sin accrues to his stock (of sins)"
(*MX*.31.8)

*ka az pušt ī pidar ō aškomb ī mādar šawēd [ēg]{.underline}-iš Astwihād
mēnōyīhā band-ēw andar ō grīw abganēd*

"when he goes from the loins of his father to the womb of his mother,
[then]{.underline} Astwihād in the other world throws a string about his
neck" (*PN*.31)

*kū šud hēnd abar ō ān ī murw pus [ēg]{.underline} franaft ān ī Zarduxšt
frawaš*

"when they (the snakes) set upon the child of that bird,
[then]{.underline} Zarduxšt's fravashi went forth" (*Dk*.7.2.27)

##### In second position in a clause, also in the sense of "then, at that time":

*ud yazd ōy hambedīg abāz dāštan šāyist ayāb nē*

*ud agar abāz dāštan šāyist [čē rāy ēg]{.underline} abāz nē dāšt*

"and was god able to keep the opponent back or not?

and if he was able to keep him bac, [why]{.underline} did he not keep
him back [then]{.underline}?" (*DD*.5.23.6)

*ud [agar ēg]{.underline} abāz dāštan nē šāyist pad abdom abāz dāštan
čiyōn šāyēd*

"and [if]{.underline} he was not able to keep him back
[then]{.underline}, how will he be able to keep him back in the end?"
(*DD*.5.23.9)

##### Preceded by *ud*, which can take an enclitic pronoun:

*ud andar weh-dēn pad gōwišn ī dādār Ohrmazd ō am paydāg kū*

***[ēg]{.underline} ān ī man gēhān frāyēn** kū marag wēš bē kunē*

***[ud ēg]{.underline} ān ī man gēhān wālēn** kū frabihtar bē kunē*

***[ud ē]{.underline}g az man padīrē gēhān srāyišn ud parwarišn** ud
sālārīh ud abar-nigāhdārīh*

"and in the Good *dēn* it is manifest by what Ohrmazd said to am:

'[Then]{.underline} further my flocks!' i.e., make (their) numbers more!

'[And then]{.underline} make my flocks grow!' i.e, make them fatter!

'[And then]{.underline} accept from me to protect and nourish my flocks,
and to be (their) guardian and protector!'" (*Dk*.7.1.21; cited from
*PV*.2.4)

*Ādurbād ī Zarduštān ēw-bār hāwišt-ēw framūd kū az nūn frāz hagriz
paydāg ma bāš*

*u-š pas az ān abar ān hāwišt abaxšīh ud pašēmānīh was dīd [u-š
ēg-iz]{.underline} abar dastwarīh nē būd*.

"Once Ādurbād son of Zardušt ordered a student: 'From now on, don't ever
show yourself (here again)!

And after that, he saw (= experienced) much repentance and regret toward
that student, and (but) [not even then]{.underline} was he (again)
[his]{.underline} advisor" (*ŠnŠ*.8.10)

### Text 14.5

From the *Pahlavi Rivāyat*: *PR*.16b.1-2. -- Ohrmazd performs a *myazd*,
an offering of *drōn* (sacred bread), fruit, flowers, wine, milk, etc.
The fravashis in particular enjoyed these offerings.

*gyāg ēw paydāg kū Zarduxšt az Ohrmazd pursīd kū haguriz u-t miyazd
kerd*

*Ohrmazd guft kū-m kerd*

*čē ka-m gēhān dād ā-m miyazd-ēw bē kerd*

*ka-m gyān ō Gayōmard dād ā-m miyazd-ēw bē kerd*

*ka tō Zarduxšt az mād zād hē ā-m miyazd-ēw bē kerd*

*ka-t dēn az man bē padīrift ā-m miyazd-ēw bē kerd*

*miyazd ēdōn sahīg ī mardōmān harw kār ud dādestān ī frārōn ī frāz
gīrēnd ā-šān pad bun miyazd-ēw bē kunišn ::*

"It is known from one place that Zarduxšt asked Ohrmazd: 'Did you ever
perform a *myazd* (ritual)?

Ohrmazd said: I did!

For, when I established the creatures, I performed a *myazd*. When I
placed the soul in Gayōmard, I performed a *myazd*. When you, Zarduxšt,
were born from (your) mother, I performed a *myazd*. When you received
the *dēn* from me, I performed a *myazd*."

The *myazd* is so worthy that (*ēdōn \... ī*) that every work and good
law that people undertake, at the beginning (to start), they have to
perform a *myazd*.

# Exercises 14

14.1. Translate and rewrite these sentences substituting the past tense
for the present tense:

Advice: First, translate the sentences into English; then turn the
Enlish sentences into the past and into passive (if possible); notice
what needs to be changed; then put it into Pahlavi. Change "now" to
"then," etc. You do not *have to* use enclitic pronouns; you can also
use the normal ones. Do not forget the past of "to be." Example: "now I
(shall) kill him/the enemies" ⇾ "then I killed him/the enemies" = "then
he was/the enemies were killed by me."

1.  *ka 9000 sāl bowandag bawēd, Srōš-ahlīy Xešm bē zanēd, ud hamāg
    gēhān rāmišn ud šādīh bawēd*

2.  *pad ān zamān mazdēsn zamīg kārēnd ud āb abar hilēnd, ud pas urwar
    ul rōyēnd*

3.  *bē kē nē az frārōn-tuxšāgīh ī xwēš xwarēd, ōy ēdōn homānāg čiyōn kē
    sar ī mardōmān pad dast dārēd ud mazg ī mardōmān xwarēd*

4.  *bazzakkar ī druwand ī wināhgār kāmag ī Gannāg Mēnōy hamē warzēnd,
    u-šān pad ān wināh dēw ō dōšox nayēnd*

5.  *pad Čīnwad puhl ī buland ī sahmgen was hamēstār estēnd, čiyōn Xešm
    ī xurdruš ud Astwihād kē hāmōyēn dām ōbārēd ud sagrīh nē dānēd*

6.  *ud pas awēšān dēn dastwar may ud mang ī Wištāspān 3 ǰām ī zarrēn
    purr kunēnd, ud ēk ǰām pad humad ud didīgar ǰām pad hūxt ud sidīgar
    ǰām pad huwaršt frāz ō Wirāz dahēnd*

7.  *ka ēn kanīg andar ān ī andarrōntar kadag nišīnēd,* *az rōšnīh ī az
    im tan bē tābēd rōšntar kū ānōh kū ātaxš burz waxšēnēnd*

In the following sentences there is already one or more enclitics, but
none of them agents. Remember that you can use independent pronouns and
that the postpositions *aziš* etc. can be reinterpreted as *az-iš*;
etc.:

8.  *ō gētīy nē šawam, čē-m anāgīh was padiš kunēnd*

9.  *ud harw kē andar kišwar pērāmōn ī Sāsān estēnd, namāz aw-iš barēnd,
    ud stāyišn ud āfrīn hamē kunēnd*

(from a dream)

10. *ēd ī pad dārišn ī tan ud bōzišn ī ruwān rāy pursē, aw-iš nēk
    pardaz, ud pad kār dār čē-t ēd ast mahist rāh pad dārišn ī tan ud
    bōzišn ī ruwān*

11. *nūn-it nimāyam kārēzār ī abdom, ī Ohrmazd ud yazdān abāg Ahrimen ud
    dēwān kerd, ud būdan ī ristāxēz ud tan ī pasēn, ud šādīh ī andar
    wahišt tā ō hamē ud hamē-rawišnih*

12. *Ahrimen ō dēwān drāyēd kū-š nūn ašmāh kē dēw hēd rēmantom ud wattom
    xwarišn awiš barēd; āwarēnd wiš ud zahr ī mār ud gazdum ud abārīg-iz
    xrafstar ī pad dōšox u-š xward dahēnd*

(the soul of the wicked is received in hell)

14.3. Translate into Pahlavi:

Make sure you analyze the English sentences before you attempt the
translation. Remember the various ways described above of starting a
sentence in ergative.

1.  The Righteous who come/came to paradise constantly praise/praised
    Ohrmazd and the *amahrspand*s. \[two sentences: present and past\]

2.  After the boy had washed his hands, he took his books and went to
    school.

3.  In Xwanirah, many people dwelt. There they were immortal, and
    Astwihād never brought them away to Hell.

4.  When Spitūr had cut am in half, the world became full of evil
    beings, and Dahāg ruled for 1000 years, before Frēdōn killed him and
    his collaboraters.

5.  When the Foul Spirit attacked the dwelling of Ohrmazd, he was
    stunned by the Ahunwar, which Ohrmazd recited to undo him.

6.  Ohrmazd said to Mašīy and Mašyānīy: I have made you (as) humans. You
    are my creatures. When you have praised me, I shall show you what I
    have made for your enjoyment.

7.  When the souls of the wicked came to Hell, they saw there many
    departed ones, who endured much punishment at the hand of the
    demons.

8.  The Mazdayasnians sent Ardā Wirāz to the other world, where he saw
    heaven and hell and the souls of the Righteous. When Ardā Wirāz came
    back to this world, he said to the Mazdayasnians: Greetings to you
    from Ohrmazd and the *amahrspand*s! who sent me to the other world,
    where I saw heaven and hell and the souls of the Righteous.

9.  After he had fled, Ardaxšīr sent his men to Pārs. Then he asked them
    (to come) to his court and gave them an order: go and kill Ardawān!
    They went and killed all the king's men, but they placed Ardawān on
    a donkey and led him to the court, where all the people saw him.
    Afterward, Ardaxšīr seized all the land of Iran and ruled for many
    years, until his son Šābuhr received the kingdom from his father.

10. Zarduxšt said: This Mazdayasnian *dēn* which I have received from
    Ohrmazd, I have never let go! I have never taken the teaching of the
    *dēw*s. And I brought the *dēn* to King Wištāsp, who fought a battle
    over it with the wicked Xyōns. In that battle, many heroes were
    killed. There were some whose souls went to Paradise where they
    experienced joy and happiness, others to Hell, where they
    experienced many kinds of punishments for the heavy sins which they
    had committed.
