# Lesson 15

## Grammar 15

### Possessive personal pronouns

Both Pahlavi and Manichean Middle Persian have possessive pronouns
derived from the personal pronouns. In Pahlavi, the plur. oblique of the
1st sing. and 1st plur.---*manīgān* \<mnyk'n\'\> and *amāgān*
\<LNEk'n\'\>*---*are found in only a couple of places in the *Pahlavi
Avesta*:

***kē** **mizd** **ī** **ō** **[manīgān]{.underline}** **frāz** **dahē**
**ān** **ī ō** **dēnīgān** **Ohrmazd** ān ī ō [manīgān]{.underline}
hāwištān ī man abāyēd dād*

"'(you) who give the fee to [mine]{.underline} (my people), the one for
those of the *dēn*, O Ohrmazd' the one to [mine]{.underline}, (to) my
students, (you) should give" (*PY*.28.6)

***(ān J̌am) kē-š** **ō** **mardōmān** **čāšīd** **kū**
**[amāgān]{.underline}*** ***gōšt** **pad** **bazišn** **xwarēd***

"(that Jam) who taught people: eat the meat of [ours]{.underline} (= our
people) by sharing it out!" (*PY*.32.8)

### Reflexive pronouns

In ergative constructions, the reflexive pronouns normally refer to the
agent, but sometimes to the grammatical subject or other parts of the
sentence.

*xwad* WTwA , nÍPWB \<BNPŠE, hwt\'\> "(my, your-, him-, etc.) self."

*xwēš* ßYwA , nÍPW \<NPŠE, hwyš\> "(my, etc.) own."

From these two, the nouns *xwadīh* "selfness, 'essence'" and *xwēšīh*
"ownership" are formed.

The mss. not infrequently have *xwēš* for *xwad*.

#### Examples with *xwad*:

*[xwad]{.underline} siyā būd u-š kunišn-iz siyā būd*

"he was black himself, and his action too was black" (*Dk*.7.6.7)

*az dām ī gētīy pad mēnōy dād nazdist 6 ān ī 7om [xwad]{.underline} būd*

"of the creation of the world of the living in the world of thought he
first established six; the seventh was [he himself]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.1.52)

*yazd \... mardōm nē ōwōn dārēnd andar ēn gēhān čiyōn [xwad]{.underline}
kāmag u-š pad tan-iz nēktar bē \... čiyōn ān ī pad ruwān sūdōmandtar*

"the gods do not keep/regard a person in the world of the living
(according) as it is [his own]{.underline} wish (for himself) and it is
better for his body, but as is more profitable for his soul"
(*Dk*.6.221)

##### In ergative constructions:

*čim andar gētīy az kunišn ī nēk ī-[t]{.underline} [xwad]{.underline}
warzīd an āgāh nē kerd ham*

"why did you not inform me about the good deeds which [you]{.underline}
[yourself]{.underline} performed (while) in the world of the living?"
(*Bd*.34.12; after the resurrection)

On *[xwad \... xwad]{.underline}*, see below on reciprocal pronouns.

Note the expressions ***xwad ast*** "is itself, is nothing but" and ***ī
xwad ast*** (short also ***ī xwad***) which probably means "that is,
nothing but \... (itself), who/which is nothing but":

*ān widarg kū abar āmad [xwad ast]{.underline} rāh ī ō dōšox kē pad ān
dwārēnd dēw ī druwand*

"that passage where (Ahrimen) came up is [itself (nothing
but)]{.underline} the road to Hell, on which the wicked demons run"
(*WD*.2.5)

*sidīgar ham-hayārīh būdan ī dāmān ēk abāg did ud az ham-hayārīh
ham-spāhīh az ham-spāhīh pērōzīh ī abar dušmen bawēd [ī xwad
fraškerd]{.underline}*

"thirdly: that the creatures together should help one another; for from
helping together comes going in army together, and from going in army
together comes victory over the enemies, which is [itself (nothing
but)]{.underline} the Fraškerd" (*WZ*.1.23)

#### Examples with *xwēš*:

*pad [bahr ī xwēš]{.underline} hunsand bēd ud bahr ī anīy kas ma
apparēd*

"be content with [your own share]{.underline} and do not take the share
of another person!" (*Handarz ī Husraw ī Kawādān* 5)

*abāz ō [xwēš]{.underline} buništ tābēnd*

"they (the heavenly lights) shine back toward [their own]{.underline}
place of origin" (*Bd*.7.9)

*pid ud mād [frazend ī xwēš rāy]{.underline} ēn and kār ud kerbag pēš az
15 sāl bē hammōxtan abāyēd*

"parents should teach [their own child]{.underline} these many works and
good deeds before (it turns) fifteen" (*PN*.34)

##### In ergative constructions:

*Mihr ī tamīg ō xwaršēd māh ī tamīg ō māh ī gōspand-tōhmag mad hēnd
u-[šān]{.underline} ō rahīy ī [xwēš]{.underline} bast hēnd*

"the dark Mihr came upon the sun, the dark moon upon the moon with the
seed of cattle, and [they]{.underline} tied them to their
[own]{.underline} chariots" (*Bd*.5.4a)

*Ohrmazd az ān ī xwēš xwadīh az gētīy rōšnīh kerb ī dāmān ī
[xwēš]{.underline} frāz brēhēnīd*

"Ohrmazd fashioned forth from his own selfdom (essence), from the light
of the world of the living, the shape of [his own]{.underline}
creatures" (*Bd*.1.43)

Occasionally, the pronoun refers to other parts of the clause, e.g.:

*u-[šān]{.underline} kerdārīh [pad dar ī xwēš]{.underline} gōwam*

"and I shall talk about [their]{.underline} activities [in (their)
own]{.underline} chapters" (*Bd*.13.37)

*ēdōn-[iš]{.underline} pad gyāg ī [xwēš]{.underline}* *nimūd*

"thus he showed [it]{.underline} (= each *nask*) [in (its) own
(proper)]{.underline} place" (*Dk*.6D.8)

*harw kerbag ī frāz mad*, *ī bē rāyēnīdan šāyist*, *[pad xwēš
hangām]{.underline} bē rāyēnīd ud ō zamān ī wēš nē spōxt*

"(it is a good thing) to see to every good deed that has come (before
one) that one should be seeing to [in its own time]{.underline} and not
to delay to more time (until more time has passed)" (*rāyēnīd*, *spōxt*:
short infinitives)

The following expressions involving *xwēš* should by now be quite
familiar:

X *xwēš* "belonging to X, that of X";

*ān ī xwēš X* "my (your, his, our, their) own X";

*ō xwēš kun-* (*padīr-*) "to make (receive as) one's own, to
appropriate"

Examples:

*Ohrmazd [xwēš]{.underline} ham*

"I belong to Ohrmazd" (*Dk*.6.169, etc.)

*pad ān ī [xwēš]{.underline} hukunišnīh*

"by [his/one's]{.underline} good actions" (*PN*.32) (= *pad hukunišnīh ī
xwēš*)

*man fradāg šawam abāg [ān ī xwēš zōr]{.underline} Xyōn 15 bēwar ōzanam*

"tomorrow I shall go and, with my own strength, kill 150,000 Xyōns"
(AZ.55)

*Ohrmazd \... az gētīyān bun mardōm [ō xwēš kerd]{.underline}*

"(as) the first of the (creations) in the world of the living, Ohrmazd
[appropriated]{.underline} (made his own) man" (*Bd*.3.14)

*panǰom az mēnōyān Spandarmad. u-š az dahišn ī gētīy zamīg [ō xwēš
padīrift]{.underline}*

"fifth of the beings in the other world (was) Spandarmad; and, of the
creations in this world, she [received]{.underline} the earth [as her
own]{.underline} (to be her own)" (*Bd*.3.20)

*ān brādar u-š pad anīy rāh sazāgīhā ēw ast ēnyā ān guftan rāy stūrīh
[xwēštar]{.underline} bawēd*

"unless (*\... ēnyā*) there is one (brother) who, in some other way, is
(more) suitably (appointed) than him, because of what was said, the
*stūrīh* [belongs more]{.underline} to that brother" (*RAF*.70.2)

##### ***az xwēš*** and ***az ān ī xwēš*** "of/from (one's) own":

*ka dastwar gōwēd kū-m xwāstag frōxt bē [az xwēš]{.underline} nē būd*

"when a *dastwar* says: I sold the property, but it was not [one of my
own]{.underline}" (*MHD*.20.18)

*u-š dastwarēnīd dād ud dēn pad sazāg xwāyišn ī [az ān ī
xwēš]{.underline} nē [az ān ī a-xwēš]{.underline}*

"and (the Creator) established as authoritative (*dastwarēnīd*) law and
*dēn* ('tradition' about) seeking appropriate (mates) from [one's
own]{.underline} (family), not from (a family) [not one's
own]{.underline}" (*DD*.76.6)

About the establishment of procreation and *xwēdōdah*.

##### Expressions for possession and ownership:

In legal language these expressions implies "belonging absolutely," as
opposed to something that is "held" (*dār-*), i.e., temporarily:

*ō xwēšīh (ā)madan*/*rasīdan* "to come into one's ownership, become
somebody's property"

*ō xwēšīh padīriftan* "to receive as one's own"

*ō xwēšīh dādan* "to give to someone to be one's own"

*ō xwēšīh āwurdan* "to bring back to someone's ownership"

*pad xwēšīh būdan* "to be one's property"

*pad xwēšīh māndan* "to remain one's property"

*pad xwēšīh dādan* "to give to be one's property"

*pad xwēšīh dāštan* "to hold as the property (of somebody else)"

*asēm ī [ō xwēšīh ī man mad]{.underline} ud zarr ī [ō xwēšīh ī man
rasīd]{.underline} čand arz*

"how much is the value of the silver that [became my
property]{.underline} and the gold that [became my
property]{.underline}?" (*MHD*.24.6)

*ka gōwēd kū-m ēn xānag pad mānišn dāštan ō tō dād ǰāwēdānīg [pad xwēšīh
dād]{.underline} bawēd*

"when he says: I have given you this house to be your dwelling, (then)
it is [given to be his own]{.underline} forever" (*MHD*.24.13)

*abarmānd ī pad stūrīh abarmānd ī [pad xwēšīh būd]{.underline} nē šāyēd*

"an inheritance in *stūrīh* can not be an inheritance that [is one's
property]{.underline} (belong to him absolutely)" (*MHD*.25.5)

*ān xwāstag abar awēšān [pad xwēšīh mānēd]{.underline} ayāb pad stūrīh*

"does that possession remain to them as [(their) property]{.underline}
or in *stūrīh*" (*RAF*.22.1)

*xwēš tan [pad xwēšīh ī]{.underline} Ohrmazd ud amahrspandān
[dāštan]{.underline}*

"to hold one's body [as the property]{.underline} of Ohrmazd and the
*amahrspand*s" (*PN*.3)

#### *xwēš tan*, *tan ī xwēš*

The meaning "one's own body" is common, but the later use as reflexive
pronoun (as in Persian) is also found. Often it is difficult to
distinguish between the two:

*ēn ruwān ī ōy druwand mard kē-š pad gētīy kūn-marz kerd u-š mard abar
[xwēš tan]{.underline} hišt*

"this is the soul of the wicked man who, in this world, practiced anal
intercourse and let a man upon [his (own) body]{.underline}"
(*AWN*.19.4)

*Ganāg Mēnōy az stī-tārīkīh [ān ī xwēš tan]{.underline} dām frāz
kirrēnīd*

"the Foul Spirit whittled forth his own creation from the \*existential
darkness, (i.e.) [his own body]{.underline}" (*Bd*.1.46)

*pad [tan ī xwēš]{.underline} abē-gumān kū \... tis-iz ǰuttar nē abāyēd
kerdan kū ān ī-š kerd estēd*

"(who) has no doubt [in himself]{.underline} (in his own mind) that one
should do nothing different from that which he has done" (*Dk*.6.23)

*harw kas ōy ī did ēdōn dōst bawēd čiyōn [tan ī xwēš]{.underline}*

"everybody will be as friendly to another as to [himself]{.underline}"
(*PR*.48.102)

*mardōm-dōstīh ān bawēd kē sūd ud nēkīh ī harw wehān ēdōn abāyēd čiyōn
ān ī xwēš ān ī-š pad [xwēš tan]{.underline} nē nēk sahēd pad kas nē
kunēd*

"being a friend of men is the following: he to whom the benefit and
goodness of all good persons are as important (*abāyēd*) as his own (and
who) does not do to anybody (= others) that which does not seem good to
himself" (*DD*.62.25a)

#### *xwēšīhā* "by oneself, alone" and *xwadīhā* "by oneself, of one's own accord"

*ašmāh [xwēšīhā]{.underline} bē nišīnēd*

"sit down [by yourselves]{.underline}!" (*AWN*.1.18)

*ēn ān ī [xwadīhā]{.underline} rasēd ō Ohrmazd yazišn ud stāyišn*

"this is the one who comes [of his own accord]{.underline} to the
sacrificing to Ohrmazd and to praising him" (*Dk*.9.49.6)

##### Note also *xwēšīhā-gāh* \<hwyšyh' g's\> "latrine":

*dar ī [xwēšīhā-gāh]{.underline} pad ān ī daštānestān šāyēd*

"the door of [the latrine]{.underline} can (be used) as that of a
menstruation (hut)" (*ŠnŠ*.2.75)

### reciprocal pronouns

The reciprocal pronoun is a double expression, as in English:

*ēk (\...) did* Y\>WT (\...) WKwïÅ \<'dwk\' (\...) TW[B]{.underline}\>
"one \... another"

*ēk \... didān* WwaD\>WT \... WKwïÅ \<'dwk\' \...
TW[B]{.underline}'n\'\>) "one \... another"

Note: the plural *didān* is rare.

Examples:

*u-[šān]{.underline} dūrīh [ēk az did]{.underline} dūrīh-iz ī az āb ī
Dāytīy čand bālāy ī xwēš būd*

"and their distance [one from the other]{.underline}, as well as the
distance from the water of the (river) Dāytīy, was as much as his
(Gayōmard's) own height" (*Bd*.1a.13; about the Bull and Gayōmard)

*u-[šān]{.underline} rēšag [ēk andar did]{.underline} ōwōn bē widārd*

"and (he) passed their (*-šān*) roots [one in/through the
other]{.underline} in that way" (*Bd*.6c.1b)

*[ēk tā did]{.underline} šud nē šāyēd*

"it is not possible to go (from) [one to the other]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.8.5; about the seven continents)

##### With singular verb:

*mard ēw kē ēk abāg did ǰang kunēd*

"a man who fights--- one with another---, \..." (*RAF*.58.1)

*ka [ēk did rāy]{.underline} ul yazēd ā šāyēd*

"when [one]{.underline} sacrifices [for another]{.underline} (when they
sacrifice for one another) then it is appropriate" (*ŠnŠ*.11.6)

##### With plural verb:

*[ēk ōy ī did]{.underline} rāmēn[ēnd]{.underline}*

"[they]{.underline} cheer up [one another]{.underline}" (*WZ*.35.29)

*ud [ēk ō did]{.underline} nē paywast [hēnd]{.underline}*

"and [they]{.underline} are not connected [to one another]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.1.8)

*[ēk ōy (ī) did rāy]{.underline} wad xwāh[ēnd]{.underline}*

"[they]{.underline} seek bad (things) [for one another]{.underline}"
(*ZWY*.4.13)

Note: on *ōy ī* (like *ān ī*), see Lesson 4.

*[ēk ōy ī didān]{.underline} xwān[ēnd]{.underline}*

"[they]{.underline} call (out to) [one another]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.9.21.19)

*ēg-[išān]{.underline} dumb [ēk ān ī did]{.underline} hamē xward*

"then [they]{.underline} ate [one another's]{.underline} tails"
(*WZ*.15.1)

##### With 1st plural verb in direct speech:

*u-š ēn-iz guft kū ka ōwōn gōwēd kū [ēk ōy ī did]{.underline} pāyēnān
[hēm]{.underline}*

"and he said this too: when he says as follows: 'we are [one
another's]{.underline} guarantor \..." (*MHD*.40.20)

#### Other reciprocal expressions

#### *āgenēn* "together, each other"

*fradom warzišn ī xwēdōdahīh ān būd ī Mašīy ud Mašyānīy kē
[āgenēn]{.underline} brād ud xwah būd hēnd*

"the first performance of the brother-sister marriage was that of Mašīy
and Mašyānīy, who were [each other's]{.underline} brother and sister"
(after *DD*.64.2)

*harw 2 mēnōy pad-iz ǰud-wimandīh ǰuttar hēnd [az āgenēn]{.underline}*

"the two *mēnōy*s (the good gods and the evil demons) differ [from one
another]{.underline} also by their different scope" (after
*Dk*.3.123.41)

*2 hamēstār ī dūr [az āgenēn]{.underline}*

"two opponents far [from each other]{.underline}" (after *Dk*.3.150.2)

*ka gōwēd kū mard 2 [pad āgenēn]{.underline} 200 ō man dahišn*
*[āgenēn]{.underline} kār ēdōn framūd estēd kū rāst*

"when (the creditor) says: two men [together]{.underline} have to give
(= pay) me 200 (drahm), (then) '[together]{.underline}' has been
ordained (by the *mowbedān mowbed* to mean) 'equally'" (*MHD*.40.2)

Note also the use of ***xwad \... xwad***, ***mard \... mard***, and
similar:

*[xwad ō xwad]{.underline} kōxšēnd ud zanēnd ud darrēnd ud kirrēnēnd ud
wišōbēnd*

"they struggle with, strike, tear at, cut up, and destroy [one
another]{.underline}" (*DD*.36.94)

*druwandān [xwad ō xwad]{.underline} druwandēnēnd ud dōšaxwīgēnēnd*

"the wicked themselves make themselves wicked and destined for hell"
(*Dk*.9.42.6)

*u-šān [xwad pad xwad]{.underline} ān ī abārōn arešk abar burd*

"and they brought the evil envy [upon one another]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.27.39)

*[mard az mard]{.underline} pursēnd kū-t pad ruwān dādestān čē būd*

"(after the resurrection) [men ask one another]{.underline}: what was
the judgment upon your soul?" (*Bd*.34.20)

## The verb. Passive

We are already familiar with the passive formations using the past
stem + *baw-* "to be, become" (see Lesson 9). There are two other forms
of the passive, both of which are formed with suffixes, one commonly to
the present stem (*‑īh-*) and one restricted to the past stem (*-t-*).

### Passive in *-īh-*

The present passive stem is formed from the present stem with the suffix
*-īh-*.

The past stem ends in *-īh-ist*, less commonly in *-īh-īd*.

Examples:

*tan drustīh ud dagr-zīyišnīh ud ābād-xīrīh ōy rāy kē
[nibēsīhēm]{.underline}*

"health, long life, and prosperity for him for whom [I am being
written]{.underline}!" (only in introductions to manuscripts)

*pad ān čim Haftōring [xwānīhēd]{.underline}*

"for that reason/therefore [it is called]{.underline} Haftōring (Ursa
Major)" (*Bd*.2.9)

*wināh (ī) pad nihān [kunīhēd]{.underline} nē kerbag*

"a sin that [is performed]{.underline} in secret is (still) not a good
deed" (*Dk*.6.119)

*čē-š dānist kū ka ēbgad rasēd rōz pad ēn 5 hangām
[baxšīhēd]{.underline}*

"for he knew that when the Invasion comes, the day [will be
divided]{.underline} into these five parts" (*Bd*.3.25)

*pad ān abar bē [zanīhist hēnd]{.underline} wispān xrafstarān*

"in that (bucket with rain water) all the evil animals [were struck
down]{.underline}" (*WZ*.3.9)

In subjectless sentences a passive form can be translated using "one,
somebody" (Germ. *man*, Fr. *on*). It can then be replaced by the 3rd
plural active, e.g.:

*kū pad gyān ī xwadāyān [kōxšīhēd]{.underline} pad čē dārē u-š čē
kunišn*

"when [somebody exerts himself]{.underline} (makes an attempt) upon the
soul (life) of lords, how do you regard it, and what should he do?"
(*KN*.10.9)

*az ēk tā dah abzāyēd andarmāh [xwānēnd]{.underline}*

*az dah tā pānzdah abzāyēd purrmāh [xwānīhēd]{.underline}*

"from the 1st to the 10th it waxes (and) [they call it]{.underline}
*andarmāh* 'moon inside';

from the 10th to the 15th it waxes (and) [it is called]{.underline}
*purrmāh* 'full moon'" (*Bd*.26.22)

*ōy kē pad kerbag kerdan dar wišādag nē dārēd ēg-iš dar ī wahišt ud
garōdmān aziš bē [bandīhēd]{.underline}.*

"he who, when doing good deeds, does not keep (his) door wide open, then
the door to Heaven and Paradise [will be closed for him]{.underline}"
(*Some sayings of Ādurbād son of Mahrspand*)

*čiyōn-itān āfrīnēnīd purr-paymānīhā ud bowandag-abzōn-padēxwīhā ōy-iz
ašmāh \... spurr rasād*

*ud dagr pattāyād ud ō nēk-frazāmīh [paywandīhād]{.underline}*

"in the same way you have blessed (me), let it too (the blessing) reach
you complete in full measure and with complete growth and prosperity,

and let it last long and [be connected]{.underline} to (your) having a
good future!" (*DD*.0.3)

[Derived nouns from passives in *-īh-*]{.underline} from basic verbs are
very rare, while those from denominatives/causatives are common (see
Lesson 16).

Note that the passive suffix can be combined with the symbols \<x~1~,
x~2~\>, which can precede or follow the ending:

![Description: YBLWNx1](media/image56.jpeg){width="0.5694444444444444in"
height="0.20833333333333334in"} \<YḆLWNyh-x~1~\> *barīhēd* "is carried"

![](media/image57.jpeg){width="0.8194444444444444in"
height="0.20833333333333334in"} \<YḆLWN-x~2~-yhst\'\> *barīhist* "was
carried"

#### Origin of the passive stem in *-īh-*

The passive marker *-īh-* was probably generalized from a few verbs in
which the Old Persian passives in *-ya-* had produced forms in
*-ih-/-īh-*. Compare:

*škenn-* \<škyn-\> *škast* "break" *ških-* (*škīh-*) \<škyh-\> "be(come)
broken"

*wisinn-* \<wsyn-\> *wisist* "split" (trans.) *wisih-* (*wisīh-*)
*wisist* "split" (intrans.)

(*abesih-ēn-* \<'pysh-yn-\> "cut off, destroy") *abesih-* \<'p̄ysyh-\>
*abesist* "be cut off, be annihilated"

Here *škī̆h-* is from \**škidya-*, *-sī̆h-* from \**-sidya-*.

*abāg bun druz [škihēd]{.underline} ud [abesihēd]{.underline}*

"the *druz* with its origin [is broken and cut off]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.3.105.9)

*abāz-wisinnišnīh rāy kū tā pad 2 bē [wisihād]{.underline}*

"for cutting back, so that [it is split]{.underline} in two"
(*PY*.68.8e; explanation of Av. *paitiscaptaiiaēca*)

### Passive in *-xt* and *-ft*

Some verbs with past stem in *-xt* or *-ft* have a passive, sometimes
intransitive, even active, present stem in *-xt-* and *-ft*, as well.
These passive verbs do not have a special past stem.

Note: See Dhabhar, 1955, pp. 109-112. These forms correspond to older
forms in *-s-* with intransitive-passive meaning; e.g., Parthian
*buxs-*, *āmixs-*, *wiδifs-*, Pahl. *bōxt-*, *āmēxt-*, *wiyēft-*.

##### From transitive verbs:

*kas az ōy nē [bōxtēd]{.underline}*

"nobody [is saved]{.underline} from it (= Time)" (*Bd*.1.42)

*tan-išān abar zamīg ī ast ī ō āb ud ast ī ō urwar ast ī ō sag ēw
[gumēxtēd]{.underline}*

"(when people die) their body (lying) on the ground is either
[mixed]{.underline} into water or plants or stones" (*Dk*.7.8.40)

*nimūdār būd kū fradom Mēdōmāh pas harwisp ox ī astōmand
[hāxtēnd]{.underline}*

"and (this) showed that first Mēdōmāh, then the whole existence with
bones, [will be led]{.underline} (to the *dēn*)" (*WZ*.20.4)

Zardušt dreamed that Mēdōmāh was the first guide of men of those before
Z.

*pad ātaxš ī andar dil kē-š sardīh ud xwēdīh ī az suš abāg
[āmēxtag]{.underline}*

*ham-ēwēnag paymānīgīhā bē tābēd ud hamāg tan garm dārēd*

"by the fire in the heart, which is [mixed]{.underline} with cold and
humidity from the lungs (*suš*)---

in the same manner, it radiates warmth (*bē tābēd*) and keeps the whole
body warm to its proper level (*paymānīgīhā*)" (*WZ*.30.21)

*keš abāz ō keš nē kārišn tā andar ō kār kunišn hamē*

*ka be [āšuftēd]{.underline} ā-š pad Abestāg abāz kārišn*

"what has been ploughed should not be ploughed back into what has been
ploughed until it is to be put to use;

if it [is muddled up]{.underline}, then he should plough it again by
(or: while reciting) the *Avesta*" (*PV*.9.32)

##### From intransitive verbs:

*frāz [franaftēd]{.underline} ō ān ī pahlom ox*

"[he goes forth]{.underline} (\< *franam-*) to the best existence"
(*PV*.18.29)

*ēdōn ō tō gōwam Spitāmān kū ma ǰeh hāzē ō kunišn*

*kū-š zan ma kun \... u-š abāg [ma xuft]{.underline}*

"thus I say to you, Spitāmān, \[quotation from Av.:\] 'do not induce a
wicked woman to "do it"!',

that is, do not make her (your) wife and [do not sleep]{.underline} with
her! (*Dk*.9.20.6)

##### Derived nouns from passives in *-t-*:

*[bōxtišn]{.underline} ī ruwān az harw ēwēnag anāgīh ud rasišn pad-iz
tan ī pasēn*

"[the salvation]{.underline} of the soul from all kinds of evil and also
(its) coming to the Final Body" (*Dk*.5.5)

***tā [ham-taftišnīh]{.underline} (ī) ābān** kū purr bē tābād **kerdārīh
ī mardān***

*kū kār šāyēd kerdan **zardušt***

"'until the waters [having been warmed up]{.underline}', i.e., (until)
it is fully warm, '(there is) the work of men',

i.e., it is appropriate to work, 'O Zardušt!'" (*PV*.4.46)

Derived forms from past stems in *-st* (*āmadišn* is found in Man.
MPers. and the *Psalter*):

*pēš az [abrāstišnīh]{.underline} ī pad xwadāyīh ud gumārdan ī pad
dādwarīh ī ōy kas*

"before that person's [being elevated]{.underline} to kingship and
before he is appointed as judge" (*Dk*.3.387)

*ag-dēnīg [wināstišnīh]{.underline} ī pad āb ud ātaxš*

"(another is this:) the water and fire [being polluted]{.underline}
(coming) from an evil *dēn*" (*Dk*.3.390.3)

*bē dānēd kū az amar petyārag (ī) Ganāg Mēnōy ī druwand kirrēnīd 3 ēn
garāntar*

*[bastišn]{.underline} (ī) wēnišn ī čašm ud nē āšnawišn ī gōš ud sidīgar
druz ī anāštīh*

"know that, of the innumerable adversities that the Foul Spirit whittled
forth, these three are the most serious:

the eye sight [being bound]{.underline} (= closed), the ear's not
hearing, and the third the demon of discord" (*PN*.46)

## Verbs. Ergative with passive.

In the inscriptions and the Psalter, there are no examples of the
ergative with passive forms in *-yh-* and *baw-*, but in Pahlavi this
usage is not uncommon, e.g.:

*tarsāgīg kē Yišōy [ī-šān]{.underline} Mašīhā-iz [xwānīhēd]{.underline}
pad pus ī yazd \... hangārēnd \...*

*grōh-ēw ham Mašīhā rāy gōwēnd kū murd grōh-ēw gōwēnd kū nē murd*

"the Christians who count Jesus, [who is also called]{.underline} Mašīhā
[by them]{.underline}, as the son of god \...

one group say about said Mašīhā that he died, another group that he did
not die" (*DD*.36.76-77)

*ud was ān ī xwēškār mardōm \...*

*u-[t xwēšīhēd]{.underline} ān ī awēšān kerbag ud spās*

"and many (are) people who perform their duties \...

their good deeds and service [will be appropriated by you]{.underline}
(Z.)" (*Dk*.9.24.17)

*ēd ast ān xwarrah kē-[š]{.underline} mardōm awiš
[dahīhist]{.underline}* \[*hēnd*\] (*awiš* + implicit "them" in
\[*hēnd*\])

"this is the Xwarrah that men were given [by him]{.underline}"
(*WZ*.3.74)

#### Passive with *az* "by" and *pad* "by (means of), through"

Passive with *az* "by" is rare:

*mēš bērōn truft ud burd bawēnd [az duz]{.underline} ud rabūd ud darrīd
[az gurg]{.underline}*

"sheep (kept) outside are stolen and taken away [by the
thief]{.underline} and robbed and torn apart [by the wolf]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.3.385.6)

Passive with inanimate agents is quite common:

*ān ī nē [sōhīhēd pad]{.underline} sōhišnān [wēnīhēd pad]{.underline}
gyān wēnišn*

"that which is not [sensed]{.underline} (perceived) [by means
of]{.underline} the senses [is seen by]{.underline} the seeing capacity
of the soul" (*Dk*.3.123.26)

*rāh ī ō ān ī rāst bowandagīh [pad xrad dānīhēd]{.underline}*

"the road to true completeness [is known through knowledge]{.underline}"
(*DD*.6.6)

*gētīy pad ēn 6 tis rāyēnīhēd • pad zamān ud ǰahišn ud dānišn ud hayār
ud abzār ud tuxšāgīh*

"this world is governed by the following six things: by time, chance,
knowledge, a helper, tools, and diligence" (*Dk*.6C.83b)

*ēdōn gōwēd kū-[š pad dandān grift ham]{.underline} ud (ān?) ēk gōwēd
kū-m nē grift*

"he says as follows: he seized me with the teeth! and (that) one says: I
did not seize him!" (after *RAF*.58.5)

### Constructions of result with *baw-*

Quite common in didactic style is what looks like a present passive with
*baw-* in the ergative, but which is most often used to express a
result: "if this happens, then (right away) this will have happened." It
differs from the passive in that it can also be formed from intransitive
verbs, e.g.:

#### Intransitive

*hamē ka ēdōn bawēd miyazd bē ō dēwān [mad bawēd]{.underline}*

"as long as it is like this, the *myazd* [will have come]{.underline} to
the *dēw*s" (*PR*.16b.10)

*ud tā-iz bar hamē barēd wizend ī pad awināhīh ī rād ō bun rasēd ō harw
2 nēm* *[mad bawēd]{.underline}*

"and as long as he carries (away = gains) the yield, (any) damage that
comes to the principal in which the donor is not guilty [will have
come]{.underline} to (becomes the responsibility of) both of them, half
(each)" (*MHD*.39.3)

#### Ergative

*ka-š wināh-ēw tanābuhl kerd estēd drōn-ēw bē yazēd*

*ayāb kerbag ī tanābuhl bē kunēd ā-[š wizārd bawēd]{.underline}*

"when he has committed a sin worth on *tanābuhl*, (and) he performs one
*drōn* sacrifice

or he performs a good deed worth one *tanābuhl*, then (the sin) [will be
atoned]{.underline} for by him (he shall have atoned for)" (*ŠnŠ*.8.20)

*ka-[šān]{.underline} rist [wirāst bawēd]{.underline} čiyōn bawēnd.*

*ka-[šān kerd bawēd]{.underline} waxšišn rōšnīh ī star ud māh ud xwaršēd
andar abāyēd būd ayāb nē*

"when [they shall have restored]{.underline} the dead, how will they be?

when [they have done]{.underline} it, will there need to be waxing of
the light of the stars, and moon, and sun or not?" (*DD*.36.1)

*čiyōn gōwēd kū drāyīd Gannāg Mēnōy ō dēwān kū ēd wād murnǰēnēd ī čēr ī
tagīg ī Ohrmazd-dād*

*čē ka-tān wād murnǰēnīd ā-[tān]{.underline} harwisp dām [murnǰēnīd
bawēd]{.underline}*

"as it says: the Foul Spirit howled to the demons, (saying): Destroy
this valorous, fleet wind set in place by Ohrmazd!

for, if you destroy the wind, then (at the same time) [you will have
destroyed]{.underline} the entire creation" (*Bd*.21.4)

*frazānagīh[-iš]{.underline} ī ohrmazd [hammōxt bawēd]{.underline} kē ō
ohrmazd ān nigēzišn ī fraškerd-kerdārīh*

"he who (has given) to Ohrmazd that exposition of how to perform the
Renovation, he will have taught the foreknowledge of Ohrmazd"
(*Dk*.9.59.12)

*wināh ī hamēmalān ka-š hamēmāl hušnūd [ā-š wizārd bawēd]{.underline}*

"(as for) a sin/crime against one's fellow men, when (= as soon as)
one's fellow man is satisfied, [then he will have resolved]{.underline}
(the sin/crime)" (*PR*.18g.2)

### Perfect (with *est-*) and ergative

In the inscriptions and the Psalter, there are no examples of the
ergative used in the perfect, but in Pahlavi this usage is not uncommon,
e.g.:

*ēn-iz paydāg kū [Ohrmazd]{.underline} ēn dām ud dahišn ī andar gētīy
pad āsn xrad [dād estēd]{.underline}*

"this too is manifest: Ohrmazd [has 'created']{.underline} this whole
creation in the world of the living by means of the Inborn Wisdom"
(*MX*.0.49)

*ēn-iz gōwēd kū [kē]{.underline} yašt nē [kerd estēd]{.underline}
gētīxrīd nē [framūd estēd]{.underline} ǰāmag ahlawdād ō arzānīgān nē
[dād estēd]{.underline} ānōh brahnag*

"this too it says (in the *dēn*) that: [he who has
performed]{.underline} no sacrifices, [has ordered]{.underline} no
*gētīxrīd* (alms), (and) [has given]{.underline} no clothes as alms to
those worthy, (he is) naked there (in Paradise)" (*Bd*.34.26)

*ruwān ī Karišasp anāgīh ī-[š]{.underline} andar dōšox [dīd]{.underline}
[estād]{.underline} rāy bē ō Zarduxšt guft*

"on account of the evil which [he had seen]{.underline} in hell,
Karišasp's soul said to Zarduxšt" (*PR*.18f.3)

*ud am andar xwadāyīh hamāg kār pad hayārīh ī awēšān harw 3 ātaxš
abērtar kerd*

*u-[š]{.underline} Ādur Farnbay ō dād-gāh pad Xwarrahōmand kōf ī pad
Xwārazm [nišāst estād]{.underline}*

"and in the reign of am, all work was done mostly with the help of
those three fires;

and [he had seated]{.underline} (enthroned) the Farnbay fire on a seat
of justice on Mount Xwarrahōmand in Xwārazm" (*Bd*.18.6)

*homānāg ī mard-ēw [ka-š]{.underline} ǰāmag ǰāmag hamāg kust pad tan
saxt andar [kerd estēd]{.underline}*

"like a man, when his various garments are firmly wrapped around the
body" (*Bd*.1a.10)

*ēg Ganāg Mēnōy [a-wēnāg-frazāmīh rāy]{.underline} pad ān paymānag
ham-dādestān būd*

"then the Foul Spirit, [because he did not see the outcome]{.underline},
agreed to that deal" (*Bd*.1.26)

##  Present participles

Three verbal nouns are made from the present stem (present participles)
by means of the endings *-āg* (see suffixes, Lesson 4), *-ān*, and
*-endag* (rare in early Pahlavi).

#### The agent noun /present participle in *-āg*

This participle is an agent noun used as an adjective. It can be negated
and be turned into an action noun in *-āgīh*, e.g.:

*ēn-iz gōwēd kū ān māhīg ōwōn [mārāg]{.underline} kū andar ān ī zufr āb*

*sōzan tēx mālišn āb padiš bē abzāyēd ayāb bē kāhēd dānēd*

"and it also says: that fish (the Wāsī Panǰāsadwarām) is so
[sensitive]{.underline} that, (even) in deep water,

it knows (recognizes if) the touch of water on it (as much as) the tip
of a needle increases or decreases" (*Bd*.24a.5)

*Kang-diz rāy gōwēd kū dastōmand ī pāyōmand*

*ud [estāg rawāg]{.underline} ī hamēšag-wahār pad kamāl ī dēwān būd*

"about the castle Kang (built by Siyāwuš, son of Kāyus) it says that it
had hands and feet,

and was [standing and moving]{.underline}, with eternal spring, on the
head of demons" (*Bd*.32.12)

*3000 sāl dām pad mēnōyīgīh estād kū būd hēnd a-mēnīdār ud
[a-rawāg]{.underline} ud a-griftār*

"for 3000 years, the creation was in the state of *mēnōy*, which have
been, non-thinking, [non-moving]{.underline}, and non-seizing"
(*Bd*.1.13)

*kē az dēn āgāh ēg pad kār ud kerbag kerdan [tuxšāg]{.underline} aziš
[a-wardāgtar]{.underline} bawēd*

"whoever is aware of the *dēn*, then he becomes [diligent]{.underline}
in performing works and good deeds and (becomes) [more
non-turning-away]{.underline} from it" (*PN*.53)

*ud pas frēzwān ast hamāg mardōmān \*gōwizārīhā abar nigerīdan kū pad
kerdan ī ristāxēz ud tan ī pasēn tis-ēw čē [bōzāgīhātar]{.underline}*

"and then it is compulsory for all men to examine closely what single
thing (works) [in the more salutary fashion]{.underline} in making the
resurrection and the Final Body" (*Ōšnar*.55)

#### The present participle in *-ān*

This participle expresses accompanying action and can be used as an
adjective, including as predicative noun, and as adverb:

*Zarduxšt [griyān]{.underline} passox guft*

"Zarduxšt answered [weeping]{.underline}" (*PR*.36.7)

*ēg-im dīd ruwān ī mard-ēw kē [kešān]{.underline} ō dōšox nayēnd ud hamē
zanēnd*

"then I saw the soul of a man whom they lead [dragging]{.underline}
(him) to hell and keep striking" (*AWN*.58.1)

*\
niyāyišn (ī) xwaršēd pad pušt ī stōr šāyēd kerdan ayāb nē \...*

*az Abestāg paydāg*

*ka [estān xēzān]{.underline} ayāb [nišīnān]{.underline} ayāb
[nibayān]{.underline} ayāb [barān]{.underline} ayāb [wāzān]{.underline}
ka aibyāst kū šabīg kustīg dārēd ēdōn radīhā*

"is it appropriate to perform the reverence to the sun on the back of a
horse or not? \...

it is manifest from the Avesta:

when [standing]{.underline}, [getting up]{.underline} or
[sitting]{.underline} or [riding]{.underline} or [driving]{.underline},
when (as long as) one is girded, i.e., one has (wears) the shirt and the
belt, in this way it is according to the (ritual) model" (*Purs*.10)

*ēk ēn kū hēnd az-iz hāwištān ī ka ō yazišn ī yazdān kerdan hamē šawēnd
mēwag hamē āwāsēnd*

*ud agar ān āwāsišn namb-ēw az-iš bē burdan rāy kunēd
[nišīnān]{.underline} kunišn*

"one thing is this: there are even some of the students who, when they
go to perform a sacrifice for the gods, keep drying off the fruits;

and if one does the drying in order to remove (*bē bar-*) (even?) a
single (drop) of moisture from it, one should do it [sitting
down]{.underline}" (*ŠnŠ*.10.5)

pad nišēbīgīh [nirfsān nirfsān]{.underline}

(*Dk*.3.329.10)

[Note]{.underline} ***widerān būdan*** = *widerdan* "to pass on, die"

#### The present participle in *-endag* (*-andag*)

This form is found frequently in the Pahlavi translation of the *Xorda
Avesta* (almost exclusively *kunendag*), where it is probably influenced
by modern Persian, but less frequently elsewhere.

In Pahlavi it is found in some idioms, e.g: *šāyendag* "worthy,"
*šāyendagīh* "worthiness," *zan* (*ziyānag*) *ī šōyendag* "a washing
woman (wife)," i.e. a woman who is performing her ablutions after
menstruation; *ātaxš ī waxšendag* "blazing fire" (also in Man. MPers.),
*wāyendag* "flying thing, bird; *zīndag* "living" and *zīndagīh* "life"
from *zīyendag(īh)*, e.g.:

*buland-ēwāz bē gōwam az anīy amahrspandān abārīg nēk [hayārīh
kunendag]{.underline}*

"with loud voice I speak of the other Amahrspands, the remaining good
[assistance-giving]{.underline} ones" (*PYt*.3.3)

*[dūr-kunendag]{.underline} ast man Ardwahišt amahrspand kē bahr-ēw
[dahendag]{.underline} ast man \...*

"removing, that is (*ast*) I, the Life-giving Immortal Ardwahišt; he who
is share-[giving]{.underline}, that is I \..." (*PYt*. 3.13)

## Text 15.3

From the *Bundhišn*: *Bd*.26.78-83. -- Mss. TD1, fol. 72v, TD2, fol.
88r.

About the specific duties (*xwēškārīh*) of Spandarmad, the Earth. Her
specific epithets are explained. Her epithet *bowandag-menišn* is the
scholastic literal translation of Av. Ārmaiti from *arəm.maiti*
"balanced thinking," but should probably be understood as
"complete/balanced thinking" or "equanimity." In *Dk*.5.9.11, *bowndag
menīdan* is is contrasted with *tar menīdan* "despise," so, perhaps,
also "admire" or similar, cf. Av. *tarō.maiti-* contrasting with
*arəm.maiti*. \[In the Xorde Avesta (*PKX*.3), we find once
*purr-menišnīg Spandarmad* "Sp. (is) 'full thinking'."\]

TD1, fol. 72v TD2, fol. 88r.

![](media/image58.jpeg){width="3.3055555555555554in"
height="2.1666666666666665in"} ![](media/image59.jpeg){width="3.0in"
height="2.3472222222222223in"}

*Spandarmad xwēškārīh parwardārīh ī dāmān ud harw xīr ī pad dāmān
bowandag bē kerdan.*

*u-š gētīy zamīg xwēš.*

*čiyōn gōwēd kū Spandarmad ī weh ī rād ī bowandag-menišn ī kāmag-dōysr ī
Ohrmazd-dād ī ahlawīy.*

*u-š wehīh ēn kū wīdwar ud gilag-ōbār*

(*u-š gilag-ōbārīh) ēn kū anāgīh ī ō Spandarmad zamīg rasēd hamāg bē
gugānēd.*

*u-š bowandag-menišnīh ēn kū hamāg anāgīh ī-š padiš kunēnd hunsandīhā
padīrēd.*

*u-š rādīh ēd kū hamāg dāmān az ōy zīyēnd.*

Note: *kāmag-dōysr*, lit. "having eyes at wish," is the rendering of
Avestan *vouru.dōiθra* "with broad eyes." The redactors of the Pahlavi
text, regularly rendered all words beginning with *v-r-* as *kām(ag)*.

## Text 15.4

From the *Dēnkard*: *Dk*.9.60.4-5. -- Ms. B, pp. \[622-623\] ---
Exegesis on the Pahlavi gloss in Y.45.10e: *ahmāi stōi* "for him to be":
*ud ōy estēd* "and for him stands" *Spandarmad pad duxtarīh* "and for
him stands" (i.e.) "Spandarmad in 'daughter'-hood (= as daughter)." The
commentator compares the *xwēdōdah* relationship between Ohrmazd and
Spandarmad to that assumed between the *xrad* "wisdom" and
*bowandag-menišnīh* "equanimity."

*ēn-iz kū-š **Spandarmad pad duxtarīh** ō Ohrmazd čāšt kē xrad pad
bowandag-menišnīh.*

*ēd-iz rāy xrad bowandag-menišnīh andar kanārag hēnd ī Ohrmazd ud
Spandarmad.*

*ud xrad ān ī Ohrmazd bowandag-menišnīh ān ī Spandarmad.*

*ud bowandag-menišnīh xrad zahag čiyōn Spandarmad Ohrmazd.*

*ud az ēd bē guftan čimīg kū kē bowandag-menišnīh ō xrad paywast ā-š
Spandarmad pad duxtarīh ō Ohrmazd **čāšt bawēd**.*

*ud ēn-iz kū-š ēdōn ān duxtarīh kunišn čāšt bawēd kē ahlāyīh pad
bowandag-menišnīh.*

This too:

He has 'assigned' (*čāšt*) Spandarmad to Ohrmazd as his daughter who
(has?) wisdom with equanimity.

For this reason, wisdom and equanimity are next to Ohrmazd and
Spandarmad.

And wisdom belongs to Ohrmazd, equanimity to Spandarmad.

And equanimity is the child of wisdom, like Spandarmad (that of)
Ohrmazd.

And from this it makes sense to say that, he who has connected
equanimity with wisdom, he will (at the same time) have 'assigned'
Spandarmad to Ohrmazd as his daughter.

And this too:

In this way, he has 'assigned' that daughter-hood as worthy of being
performed whose Righteousness is through/with equanimity.

15.2. Translate into Pahlavi and write in Pahlavi script with
transliteration and transcription:

> 1\. He who is not in charge of himself should be considered poor.
>
> 2\. Zardušt himself said: do good deeds to one another so that your
> own place (*gāh*) will be in paradise!
>
> 3\. He who makes metal happy or harms (it), he will then have made
> Šahrīwar happy or have harmed (him).
>
> 4\. He who commits a sin toward (*andar*) water, and (then) kills
> frogs and the other evil animals living in water, he will have
> 'resolved' (it = the sin).
>
> 5\. The white falcon was created in order to kill snakes, but it
> happens that they are equally strong and they both are intertwined
> with one another and fall dead to the earth.
>
> 6\. It may happen that a man is healthy and active and before six
> o'clock he is sick and inactive and the next day he is mingled with
> the earth and becomes dust.
>
> 7\. He who commits a sin and becomes repentant within a year, then,
> because of that repentance, (his) soul is saved from hell.
>
> 8\. When a *margarzān* has repented for his sin, then he is (only)
> killed at the order of the lords and suffers no other punishment.

### Additional readings 15.2

From the *Dādestān ī dēnīg*: *DD*.63. --- Mss. K35 fol. 177r-v, T60
fols. 100b-101a.

The answers are written in response to questions raised by the
*hu-dēn*s, so *pursēd* is 2nd plural.

*63om pursišn :: ān ī pursēd kū fradom dahišn ī mardōmīh az čē kerd*

*bun-tōhmag ī mardōmān čiyōn-iz būd*

*az Gayōmard kē bē āmad ud čē bē būd*

*Mašīy* \[K177v\] *ud Mašyānīy az kē bē būd hēnd*

*pāsox ēd kū*

*Ohrmazd ī wisp-xwadāy az ān ī asar rōšnīh brēhēnīd āsrō-kerb kē-š dām
ān ī Ohrmazd ud rōšnīh ān ī ātaxš*

##  Additional readings 15.3

From the *Dēnkard*: *Dk*.9.58.17. Ms. B, pp. \[617-618\], DH fol. 318r.

Exegesis on *PY*.43.6d-e:

***awēšān** kē **rad** **hammōzēd pad bowandag-menišnīh** Sōšāns*

***[kē]{.underline} ēd ī tō xrad [padiš]{.underline} nē pad tis bē
frēbīhēd***

He who teaches them the *rad* by Equanimity, (i.e.) Sōšāns;

by which (whom?) this wisdom of yours is in no matter deceived.

*ud ēn-iz kū-š pad **xrad** **bowandag-menišnīh** **hammōxt** bawēd kū
nē **frēftēnd** kē Ohrmazd ēdōn tarsagāy* \[B618\] *čiyōn duxt pid ::*

*ēd-iz rāy čē tarsagāyīh ī duxt andar pid frayistīhā pad āhang ī čihrīg
pad xradīg bowandag-menišnīh ī duxt bawēd*.

And this, too, that by his wisdom (*xrad*) Equanimity is taught so that
they are not deceived who are respectful toward Ohrmazd in this way, in
the same way as a daughter toward her father.

And for this reason too, because the respect of a daughter toward her
father is mostly by natural inclination, by the equanimity of the
daughter inspired by her wisdom.

# Lesson 16

## Grammar 16

### Nominal Compounds

These comprise adjectives (often substantivized) and nouns made from
nouns, adjectives, adverbs, and verbal stems, present and past.

Adjectival compounds can of course also be substantivized with *-īh* and
used as adverbs with *-īhā*.

##### Noun + noun \> adjective \> noun:

*drōw* "lie" *+ dādwar* "judge" *drōw-dādwarīh* "being a false judge /
(sb.) whose judgements are lies/false"

*wināh* "sin" + *kār* "work" *wināh-gār* "one who commits sins, a
sinner, criminal"

*wināh-gārīh* "committing sins/crimes"

##### With plural noun as first member:

*ud ēč drōw ud halagīh ud [dēwān-kāmagīh]{.underline} pad-iš nē*

*ud hamāg rāst ud meh-dādestānīhā ud [yazdān-šnāyēnīdārīhā]{.underline}
guft estēd*

"and there is no falsehood, stupidity, and [anything going according to
what is the wish of the demons]{.underline} in it;

and it is all spoken true and according to (Ohrmazd's) 'greater law' and
[so as to please the gods]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.24.12b)

\< *dēwān kāmag* "the wish of the demons" and [*yazdān šnāyēnīdārīh*
"pleasing of the gods]{.underline}"

Cf. *[yazdān-parist]{.underline}* "someone who serves the gods" (below).

##### Noun + verbal noun \> adjective \> noun:

The second term may be a present stem (these sometimes take *-ag*), an
action noun in *-dār/-tār*, or a verbal noun in *-išn*:

*kerbag* "good deed" + *-kar* "doer" *kerbakkar* "doer of good deeds"

*kerbakkarīh* "doing good deeds"

*uzdēs* "idol" + *parist-* "to worship" *uzdēs-parist* "idol-worshipper"

*gyān* "life" + *abespār-* "consign, give over" *gyān-abespār* "one who
gives his life"

*gyān-abespārīhā* " (fighting) so as to give up one's life

*framān* "order" *+ burdār* "carrier" *framān-burdār* "carrier of the
command \> obedient"

*anāg* "evil" *+ kerdār* "doer" *anāg-kerdār* "evil-doing, evil-doer"

*duškām* "evil wish" *+ kerdār* "doing" *duškām-kerdār* " one whose
doings are from evil wishes

\> sb. whose behavior is according to his evil wishes"

*pārag* "bribe" *+ stanišn* "taking" *pārag-stanišn* "one who takes
bribes"

*pārag-stanišnīh* "taking bribes"

*dēw* "demon" + *ēzag* "sacrificer" *dēw-ēzag* "sb. whose sacrifice is
to the demons"

Note:

*ārzōg* "desire" + *tēz* "quick" *ārzōg-tēzīhā* "as soon as the desire
takes one" (*Dk*.5.24.23)

##### All the following adjectival compounds can also take *-īh* and *-īhā*.

##### Noun + past participle \> adjective:

*yazd* "god" + *āfrīd* "created" *yazd-āfrīd* "god-created"

*Ohrmazd* + *dād* "given, created" *Ohrmazd-dād* "given, created by
Ohrmazd"

*harwisp* "every" *+ pēsīd* "adorned" *harwisp-pēsīd* "adorned with
every (adornment)"

##### Agent noun in *-dār/-tār* + noun:

In these compounds the agent noun governs the second noun:

*wistan* "shoot (arrow) + *tigr* "arrow" *wistār-tigr* "sb. who shoots
an arrow"

*wināhēnīdan* "turn into a sin" *wināhēnīdār-kerbag* "sb. who turns a
good deed into a sin"

\+ *kerbag* "good deed" *wināhēnīdār-kerbagīh* "act of turning a good
deed into a sin"

##### Adjective + noun \> adjective:

*garān* "heavy" + *wināh* "sin" *garān-wināh* "whose sins are heavy;
very sinful"

*rāst* "truthful" + *gōwišn* "speech" *rāst-gōwišn* "of truthful speech"

*ēr* "low" + *tan* "body" *ēr-tan* "respectful, humble"

##### Adverb + noun \> adjective:

*was* "much" + *anāg* "evil" *was-anāg* "who commits much evil"

*dūr* "far" + *ul-barišn* "up-carrying" *dūr-ul-barišntar* "carrying
further upward"

##### Pronoun + noun \> adjective

*čē* "what" + *ēwēnag* "kind" *čē-ēwēnag* "of what kind"

*čē* "what" + *kāmag* "desire, wish" *čē-kāmag* "having what desire"

*kadām* "which(ever)" + *ōz* *kadām-ōz* "having which force"

With *-īh*:

*abāz ō Kāy-Us šud u-š az [čē-ēwēnagīh]{.underline} āgāhēnīd*

"he returned to Kāy-Us and informed (him) of [how matters
stood]{.underline}" (*WZ*.4.15)

*[čē-kāmagīh]{.underline}-iš rāy frāz guft*

"on account of his [having what desire]{.underline} (= desiring what)
did he say (it)?" (*PY*.20.4)

With *-īhā*:

*[kadāmag-ōzīhā]{.underline} kōxšišn*

"[with which]{.underline}(ever) [force]{.underline} one is to fight"
(*DD*.36.64)

#####  Numeral + noun \> adjectives of measure:

These usually have the ending *-ag*:

*sē* "three" + *šab* "night" *sē-šabag* "lasting three nights,
three-night"

*pānzdah* "15" + *sāl* "year" *pānzdah-sālag* "fifteen year-old"

##### Past participle + noun (see also Lesson 19) \> adjective:

These compounds express "(after) having done" sth.

*agar mard tis az kāmag ēn kū was-abestāg ud was-zand ud
[kerd-hērbedestān]{.underline} bawam*

"if any of a man's wish is this: I shall be someone with much Avesta and
much *zand* (= having learned A&Z) and someone [who has 'done'
*hērbedestān*]{.underline} (has 'gone to school')" (*Dk*.6.310c)

## 

## 

## The verb. The optative

Few forms of the optative other than the 2nd and 3rd singular have been
noticed.

The endings are:

Singular

1st *-ē* (*-ēnīy*?) Ä-, ì \<-yḏ\>; ëwY- \<-ynyḏ\>, Y\>wY- \<-ynd\>

2nd *-ēš* ß\`- , ßG- , ˙D\>- , ˙D- \<-yš, -dš\>

3rd *-ē* Ä-, aD-, aÅ-, ì- \<-yḏ, -[ydy]{.underline}\>

Notes:

The 1st sg. ending may be *-ēnīy* in the Pahlavi *Avesta* (cf. subj.
*-ānīy*). For *-ē*, see examples under *kāč* below and in Text 16.1.

The 1st sg. pluperfect ending is *būd ham*, etc. in the examples below.

The 2nd sg. ending is well attested. The common reading of this ending
as *-ē* is erroneous. The final \<-š\> is sometimes written \<-yh\>.

The 3rd sg. ending ì**-** \<-yḏ\> is the oldest and most common. Next in
frequency is aÅ-.

Of "to be" only the 3rd sg. *hē* is known. For the 1st sing., *ham* is
used in the examples below.

The 3rd s. of *baw-* is *[bē]{.underline}* \<byḏ\> (e.g., PV.8.8A) and
*bawē* \<YHWWNy[d]{.underline}\>.

In some manuscripts, we find \<HWEt\'\>, apparently *hād*, for expected
\<HWEyD\> (see examples below), which may go back to older \<HWE\> =
*hē*, with the more common 3rd singular ending (indicative, subjunctive)
added.

Paradigms:

Present Preterite Pluperfect Perfect

Singular

1st *šawē*

2nd *šawēš*

3rd *šawē* *šud hē* *šud būd hē* *šud estē*

Plural

3rd *šawēnd*, *šawēnd hē* *šud hēnd*, *šud hēnd hē*

For the 3rd pl., see the examples below.

Instead of *hē*, the manuscripts sometimes have *-ē* spelled \<-yḏ,
-'ḏ\> and even \<HNA\>, e.g., *būd-ē* "if \... had been," *wēnīhist-ē*
"(then) it would be seen"; *tuwān-ē* "it would be possible," *dād-ē* "if
\... had given"; instead of *hēnd* we sometimes find *-ēnd*, e.g.,
*būd-ēnd*.

### Uses of the optative

The optative was mainly used in two functions: to express a wish or
exhortation and in "irrealis" constructions, that is, statements against
reality.

The optative of exhortation is found mainly in translations of (extant
and non-extant) Avestan texts, notably 2nd singular forms in *-ēš*
corresponding to Avestan forms in *-ōiš*, *-aēša*, sometimes alternating
in the manuscripts with the imperative and the indicative *-ē* or forms
in *-išn* or *-išnīh*.

##### Exhortations:

Negation is *ma*:

*keš frāz [kārēš]{.underline}*

"[you shall draw]{.underline} 'forth' a furrow!" (*FO*.5.283 *karšaci*
*frakāraiiōiš*)

*[ma]{.underline} ōy mard [zanēš]{.underline}*

"[you shall not strike]{.underline} that man!" (*Dk*.7.4.9)

*u-š ma ham-hāgīh dahē ud ma ham-pursagīh ma (ham-)kerdārīh*

*[framāyēš]{.underline} ōy ō pasīy frōd waštan*

*ān ī pērōzgar gōwišn frāz gōwēš Yatā-ahū-wairyō*

"and you shall not accord her (the demon) company, conversation, and
cooperation (sex?);

[you shall bid]{.underline} (her) turn backward (= around);

[you shall utter]{.underline} that victorious utterance, the
*Yatā-ahū-wairyō*!" (*Dk*.7.4.56)

Although she looks like a beautiful woman, her back is full of evil
critters.

*Ardaxšīr ka-š ān saxwan āšnūd guft kū*

*ān rōz [ma bawē]{.underline} kū az tōhm ī Mihrōg\... kas pad Ērān šahr
kāmgār bawēd*

"When Ardašīr heard that speech, he said: [Let]{.underline} that day
[not be]{.underline} when somebody from the seed of Mihrōg becomes
acting according to wish over the land of the Iranians!"
(*KN*.12.6/11.9)

##### Wishes:

Negation appears to be *nē* in simple wishes for the future and *ma* in
past wishes against reality.

*ān ī weh xwadāyīh ī tō Ohrmazd [bē ayābēnīy]{.underline} hamē tā ō
wisp*

"[may I obtain]{.underline} your good rule, Ohrmazd, forever!"
(*PY*.41.2)

Avestan *apaēmā* "may we obtain!" (opt.). -- Mss.: J2, K5 \<-ynyḏ\>,
Mf4, Pt4 \<-ynd\>.

*awēšān-iz kē ahlaw hēnd andar Garōdmān ā-šān xwašīh ud rāmišn rāy ī-šān
ast*

*ā-šān [ān abāyēd kū]{.underline} haguriz ān zamān [nē
rasē]{.underline}*

"and those in Garōdmān who are Righteous, because of the pleasure and
joy which they have,

then (the only thing) they need is: [may]{.underline} that time [never
come]{.underline}!" (*PR*.25.6)

In a relative clause:

***čiyōn hagriz ān dāšn ast** kū ān zamānag hagriz rasēd **ka ō ōy
dahīhēd***

*(ī) **pad tuwān-xwāyišnīh [ayārē]{.underline}** ō ōy ī Zardušt*

"how will there ever be that gift (or: *dahišn* "creature"), that is,
will that time ever come when (somone) will be given (or: set in place,
'created') to/for her,

(who) as much as he is able to seek (*pad tuwān-xwāyišnīh*), [may
assist]{.underline} him, Zardušt?" (*PY*.29.9c)

The soul of the cow is complaining about the deities' choice of Z. as
the one to look after her.

##### 

##### Unreal wishes past:

*ēn-iz kū-š ēdōn kāmag būd Ganāg Mēnōy kū [ma]{.underline} hagriz dām
[frāz brēhēnīd hē]{.underline} ohrmazd ud [ma]{.underline} ēdar ahū'īh
[hē]{.underline} ud ma radīh*

"this too: the Foul Spirit wished: [would]{.underline} that Ohrmazd
[never created]{.underline} the creation and that [there
was]{.underline} [no]{.underline} *ahū*'hood or *rad*hood here!"
(*Dk*.9.29.7)

Note also the following (not optative) expression:

*ēdōn abar menīd kū-[mān]{.underline}-iz 50 sāl [kār ēn abāyēd
būd]{.underline}*

"it occurred (to them) thus: And this is what [we should have been
doing]{.underline} for 50 years (already)!" (*Bd*.14.29; M&M discover
sex)

#### With the particle *kāč* "if only!"

The particle *kāč* (WcÅK k'c\') is sometimes found in the manuscripts
with the optative to express wish, but more often with the indicative,
e.g.:

*\... ī-šān ārzōgīhēd kū [kāč nē zād būd-ēnd]{.underline}*

"\... (such) that they desire: [if only they had not been
born]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.178)

Note: *-šān ārzōgīhēd* is an impersonal construction with a denominative
passive verb (Lesson 17).

*kū-m [kāč]{.underline} xwad* \<NPŠE\> *ud mānīgān rāy diz-ēw pad uzēnag
ī az xwēš [kerd estē]{.underline}*

*u-š an tanīhā andar \*[mānē]{.underline}* *ayāb-im andar ēn diz uzēnag
az harw kas wēš [kerd estē]{.underline}*

".. that: [if only I had made]{.underline} a fortress for myself and my
household from my own expense

and [I were to dwell]{.underline} in it alone or [I had
expended]{.underline} more than everybody in this fortress!"
(*Dk*.6.304c)

For *mānē*, the mss. have: B \<-WNyt\>, K43a \<-WNm\>.

##### The particle *kāč* with hypothetical wish and hypothetical consequence:

*[kāč]{.underline} driyōštar [būd hē]{.underline}* \<HWEyḏ\>
*u-[m]{.underline} anāgīh ī az driyōšīh wēš [dīd ud burd
hē]{.underline}*

*ud nūn āmār andak ud xwārtar abar [būd hē]{.underline}*

"[if only I had been]{.underline} poorer and [I had experienced and
suffered]{.underline} more evil from being poor,

then, now, my reckoning [would have been]{.underline} just a little
(*andak*) and lighter" (*Dk*.6.304d)

*[kāc]{.underline} man hērbed-ēw [būd ham]{.underline} kē-m hanbān-ēw
pad pušt [hē]{.underline}*

*zīyišn xwāstan rāy pad gēhān hamē [raft ham]{.underline} ud gēhān man
zišt pad cašm [būd hē]{.underline}*

*ud gēhān az warz ī man [tarsīd hē]{.underline}*

"[if only I had been]{.underline} a *hērbed* who [would
have]{.underline} a pocket in the back;

to seek a life, I [would go]{.underline} out in the world, and the world
[would appear]{.underline} (*pad cašm būd hē*) ugly to me,

and the world [would fear]{.underline} my miracles!" (*PR*.18f4)

#### 

#### In unreal conditional clauses

The optative is used in conditional sentences introduced by *agar* or
*ka*, in both the if-clause (*protasis*) and the main clause
(*apodosis*).

##### With present + present:

*gōwēd J̌āmāsp bidaxš kū*

*agar diz-ēw ī rōyēn bē [framāyēš]{.underline} kerdan ān-iz ī dar-band
āhenēn bē [framāyēš]{.underline} kerdan*

*awēšan pusarān ud brādarān wispuhragān ī tō rām-šahr Kay-Wištāsp-šā
andar ān diz bē [framāyēš]{.underline} nišastan*

*pas ān-and dušmen az šahr abāz dāšt kē tuwān*

"Jāmāsp the *bidaxš* says:

If [you were to order]{.underline} a castle of brass to be made and
[were to order]{.underline} a bar/locks (?) of iron to be made

and [were to order]{.underline} your, King Kay Wištāsp of peaceful
reign, sons, brothers, and princes, to sit in that castle,

(even) then who (would be) able to hold that many enemies from the
land!"

*[ka]{.underline} [nē]{.underline} sag rāy [hē]{.underline} a-paydāg
[bē]{.underline}* \<byḏ\>

"[if it were not]{.underline} for the stone, [it would be]{.underline}
invisible" (*PV*.8.8A)

*sūd ī yazdān az yazišn [ka-iz]{.underline} ēwāz kam-pādixšāyīh ī dēwān
abar xwad ōy ī yaštār [hē]{.underline} [ēg-iz]{.underline} az
wēš-pādixšāyīh abē-niyāz [sazē]{.underline} hangārd*

"the benefit for the gods of the sacrifice, [even if it
were]{.underline} only less dominion of the demons over the sacrificer
himself, [still]{.underline} (*ēg-iz*) [it would be proper]{.underline}
to consider it as (their) having no need for greater dominion"
(*Dk*.5.24.18)

*abēr tuxšišn ō ham-rasišnīh ud ham-xwarišnīh ī abāg wehān;*

*čē [agar]{.underline} [dānē]{.underline} kas kū čiyōn nēk ham-rasišnīh
ud ham-xwarišnīh ī abāg wehān ka tis ī ōwōn nē mad estēd ī ō wehān šāyēd
dād*

*ēg-iz nān ī xwēš [stānē]{.underline} ud andar ō wehān
[šawē]{.underline} ud abāg wehān bē [xwarē]{.underline}*

"one should make an effort to get together with and eat with good

for, [if]{.underline} someone [knew]{.underline} how good it is to get

then [he would]{.underline} also [take]{.underline} his own bread and
[visit]{.underline} good people and [eat]{.underline} with good people"

##### Subjectless:

*ābādīhā čē wattar [šāyist hē]{.underline} būd*

"Luckily! For [it could have been]{.underline} worse" (*Dk*.6D.7b)

*nēk-iz [hē]{.underline}* (\<HWE''\>) *ānōh pad wahišt ī rōšn ka ēdar-iz
ēdōn nēk* *ud* *wad-iz [hē]{.underline} ānōh pad dōšox ka ēdar ōwōn
anāg*

"[it would have to be]{.underline} good there in the light paradise
since it is this good here (already), too; [it would have to
be]{.underline} bad there in hell since it is so evil here (already)!"
(*DD*.93.10, *Dk*.6.16)

*[kē]{.underline} zāyišnīg ud [kē-iz]{.underline} ārōyišnīg
[hē]{.underline}*

"[be it that which]{.underline} will be born or [that which]{.underline}
will grow" (*MX*.48.23)

##### Past 3rd plural:

See below on Subjunctive *hād* \<HWEt\'\> for *hē* as irrealis.

##### The auxiliary may be omitted in sequences of several verbs:

*agar ēd-ōwōn [nē būd]{.underline} Wištāsp awēšān āwāmīgān Abestāg kē ēd
ēdōnīh aziš paydāg pad drōw [dāšt]{.underline} ud [nē
padīruft]{.underline} ō amāh [nē paywast hē]{.underline}*

"If [it were not]{.underline} in this way, Wištāsp and those of that
time, [would have regarded]{.underline} the Avesta, from which it was
manifest that this was like this, as a lie and [would not have
accepted]{.underline} (it, and) [it would not have been
linked]{.underline} to (= come down to) us" (*Dk*.7.4.63b)

##### With past + present:

*ka nē [ka]{.underline} hambun-iz wināh [kerd hē]{.underline} margarzān
[bawē]{.underline}*

"if not, (even) [if]{.underline} no sin at all [had been
committed]{.underline}, he [would]{.underline} (now) [be]{.underline}
*margarzān*" (*PY*.65.11c)

#### With hypothetical *bē ka* "were it not," *bē ka \... ēnyā* "unless"

Most often this type of sentences shows up with indicative verbs in the
manuscripts.

*[bē ka-m]{.underline} pad xwarrah ī Ohrmazd-bay ud dēn ī mazdēsnān ud
gyān ī Zarēr ī brād sōgand [xward hē]{.underline} ēg-[im]{.underline}
pad ēn 2 tēx ī šamšēr kārd sar [brīd]{.underline} bē zamīg [abgand
hē]{.underline}*

"[were it not for]{.underline} the fact that [I had sworn]{.underline}
an oath by the divine Ohrmazd's Xwarrah, the Mazdayasnian Dēn, and my
brother Zarēr's soul, [I would have cut off]{.underline} your head with
this two-edged sword and [thrown]{.underline} you to the ground"
(*AZ*.52)

*ag-dēn [bē ka pad ēd dārē]{.underline} kū bē mīrēd ēnyā-š tis-iz nē
abāyēd dād*

"an *ag-dēn*, unless [he were to think]{.underline} he was dying, he
need not give anything" (*PR*.14.7)

#### As irrealis in clauses of comparison with *čiyōn ka* "as if"

##### Present optative:

*ēdōn [čiyōn ka-š]{.underline} harw 2 pad abāyist [hē]{.underline}*

"[as if he had]{.underline} need of both" (*Dk*.9.11.10)

*Pusānweh ī Burz-ādur-farnbayān \*guft kū ka pad ān ēwēnag pad ān tis
dādestān ǰuttar nē bawēd*

*[čiyōn ka]{.underline} sālār (ī) būdag [hē]{.underline}*

"Pusānweh, son of Burz-ādur-farnbay, said: when such judgement about
that matter is not different,

[as if]{.underline} (= than if) [he were]{.underline} a natural
guardian" (*MHD*.24.29)

*Wahrām guft kū ka-š andar ān-ēw šōy kerd [ēdōn]{.underline} abāyēd
dāštan [čiyōn ka nē]{.underline} zīndag [hē]{.underline}*

"Wahrām said: when/if she at that time married, it must be regarded [as
if she were not]{.underline} alive" (*MHD*.25.4)

On whether a married but divorced daughter who returns to her father's
family can inherit; W. says that, as soon as she had married out of the
family, she should not be considered a member of her father's family,
but simply as if she was already dead (did not exist to them).

*ud abar pādufrāh ī zan kē tan pad zanīh ō mard ī ahlaw dahēd az-iš abāz
āyēd*

*čiyōn ka-š zūzag bāstān pad haxt [andar šawē ud bē āyē]{.underline}*

*ud brīd-rāhīh ī-š az ān ī pahlom oxān*

"about the punishment of a woman who gives her body in 'wifehood' to a
Righteous man, (then) comes back from it (= reneges on it?):

(it was) just if a hedgehog [were entering]{.underline} her loins [and
coming out]{.underline};

and (about) how her road had been cut off from the Best existence"
(*Dk*.9.17.5)

##### Past optative:

*ud ka frazend ī zāyēd purnāy bawēd harw kār ud kerbag ī ān frazand
kunēd pid ud mād harw dō [ēdōn]{.underline} bawēd [čiyōn
ka]{.underline}-šān pad dast ī xwēš [kerd hē]{.underline}*

"and when the child that is born comes of age, every work and good deed
that that child performs becomes for both the mother and father [as if
they had performed it]{.underline} with their own hands" (*PR*.43.5)

##### Perfect optative:

*ēn-iz kū ka weh-ēw bēš abar mad estēd pad ān bēš bē burd*

*harw kas ēdōn tuxšišn [čiyōn ka]{.underline}-š ō xwad [mad
estē]{.underline}*

"and this too: when some harm has come upon a good person (and) he has
been carried away (died) by that harm,

(then) everybody should make an effort in such a way [as if it had
come]{.underline} upon himself" (*Dk*.8.19.52)

#### In hypothetical relative clauses

##### Present optative:

*dādār mardōm rāy \... abar ān ī nē wēnēnd dādestān wizīd
[ī-šān]{.underline} āgāh būd [tuwān-ē]{.underline}*

"the Creator chose for mankind a judgement about that which they do not
see (something of) [which they would be able]{.underline} to be aware"
(*Dk*.3.332.3)

*mānāg ī ōy čiyōn [kē]{.underline} pus ī dōst ī 2-sālag 3-sālag pad
tōšn-dārišnīh [barē]{.underline}*

"just like he [who would carry]{.underline} a dear two- or
three-year-old son while feeding him (?)" (*Dk*.7.2.34; *tōšn* only
here?)

*awēšān wēnišn ōwōn tēz kū ān ī arγandtom dōšox [ōwōn]{.underline}
wēnēnd [čiyōn]{.underline} mard-ēw [kē]{.underline} čašm abēr wēnāg
andar ēwēnag [nigerē]{.underline}* \<nkylnd\> *tan ī xwēš
[wēnē]{.underline}* \<H[Z]{.underline}YTWNd\> *awēšān-iz weh abērtar
wēnēnd*

"their vision is so sharp that they see the terrible hell [just
like]{.underline} a man whose eye were very seeing (could see very well)
[would look]{.underline} in a mirror and [would see]{.underline}
himself---those see even much better" (*Handarz ī Dastwarān* 22)

*ud abar pādufrāh ī druwandān ēn-iz čiyōn gōspand-ēw kē zīndag pad pāy
ud sar nigōn [āgust estē]{.underline}*

*u-š angust-zahyā-ēw māyišn pad wēnīg [tazē]{.underline}*

"and about the punishment of the wicked: this also is like an animal
which, while alive, [were to be suspended]{.underline} by the feet and
upside down and the \*mucus [were to flow]{.underline} into its nose to
a depth of one finger" (*Dk*.9.17.7)

***nēk bawād ōy mard** ōy mard nēk bawād kē tō bāstān [frāz
yazē]{.underline}*

"'Let it be good for that man!': let it be good for that man who
[were]{.underline} repeatedly [to sacrifice]{.underline} to you"
(*Ny*.5.7c)

#####  Subjunctive *hād* \<HWEt\'\> for *hē* as irrealis:

Some scribes used the (apparent) subjunctive form *hād* \<HWEt\'\> for
*hē* as irrealis:

*pad dēn gōwēd kū agar man [nē dād hād]{.underline} mēnōy ī būm ud deh
harwisp mardōm bē ō Ērānwēz* *[šud hēnd hād]{.underline} xwašīh ī ānōh
rāy*

"it says in the *dēn*: [if I had not established]{.underline} the spirit
of earth and town, all men [would have gone]{.underline} to *Ērānwēz*
because of the pleasantness there" (*Bd*. 31.1)

*[agar]{.underline} nē ēdōn [kerd hād]{.underline} ān rōšnīh ō gētīy [nē
tābēnīd hād]{.underline}*

"[if it had not been done]{.underline} in this way, that light [would
not have shone]{.underline} upon the world" (*Bd*.7.9)

*rōzan nē guft estēd čē [agar]{.underline} bē [guft hād]{.underline}*
*dēwān rāz [bē dānist hē]{.underline}* *ud wizend handāxtan tuwānist
(hē)*

"the heavenly window (of Aries during the 5 *gāhānīg* days) is not
stated (mentioned by name), for [if it had been stated]{.underline}, the
demons [would have known]{.underline} the secret and (would have) been
able to plot harm" (*Indian* *Bd*.5b.6).

Here the *Iranian Bundahišn* has the optatives *guft hē*, *dānist hē*,
*handāxt hē*.

*agar Kay-Husrōy uzdēszār ī pad war ī Čēčast nē [kand hād]{.underline}
\... ēg petyārag ēdōn stahmagtar [būd hād]{.underline} kū ristāxēz ud
tan ī pasēn kerdan [nē šāyist hād]{.underline}*

"[if]{.underline} Kay-Husrōy [had not demolished]{.underline} the idol
temple by the Čēčast Sea, then the adversary [would have
become]{.underline} so much more violent that [it would not have been
possible]{.underline} to make the resurrection and the Final Body"
(*MX*.1.95)

### text 16.2

From *Dēnkard* book VII: *Dk*.7.6.14. -- Ms. B, p. \[501\]. -- About

*ud agar ēd warz xwarrah abdīh ī azabar-nibišt, abar dīd* \[= *dīdan*\]
*ī awēšān kišwar-frazānagān \[ī\] pad paydāgīh ī az Abestāg, paydāg nē
būd*

*(ud) Wištāsp šāh (ud) awēšān kišwar-frazānagān nē dīd hē, ī-šān ēn
Abestāg -- kē paydāg būd* \[= *būdan*\] *[ī]{.underline} ēd and warz
abdīh ō awēšān [aziš]{.underline} paydāg -- \*abē-wābar dāšt ud hišt, ō

### Text 16.4

From the *Ayādgār ī Zarērān*, the "Memorial of Zarēr": *AZ*.40 --
Wištāsp aske his wise minister J̌āmāsp to foretell the result of the
great battle with the Xyōnian king Arzāsp: how many of his sons and
brothers will die.

![Description: AZ 40](media/image72.jpeg){width="5.013888888888889in"
height="2.013888888888889in"}

*gōwēd J̌āmāsp bidaxš kū kāč ka man az mādar nē zād ham*

*ayāb ka zād ham pad xwēš baxt pad rahīgīh bē murd hē*

*ayāb murw-ēw būd hē ō drayāb ōbast hē*

*ayāb ašmāh bayān ēn frašn az man nē pursīd hē*

*bē ka-tān pursīd hē ēg-im nē kāmē bē ka rāst gōwam*

Note: Jamasp-Asana (the ed.) has corrected *hē* \<HWE'y\> to *ham* and
*kāmē* \<YCBEN'y\> to *kāmam*.

16.3. Translate into Pahlavi and write in Pahlavi script with
transliteration and transcription:

1.  By showing you clearly its meaning, I shall now explain the sacred
    word to you.

2.  The soul of the departed, having performed the accounting and having
    expiated (its) sins, arrives in paradise in such a way that its
    place will be there until the Fraškerd and it will have no need of a
    new accounting.

3.  Afterward you shall sprinkle the dead body with an iron (implement).

4.  If those bird-borne or wolf-borne *nasāy*s made a man a sinner, the
    entire existence with bones would never be free of sin.

5.  And the soul of the sinner's father would cry out: If only he had
    not been born and he had never experienced such harsh pain!

6.  One (thing) is this: when he cooled the fire; for, if the fire had
    burnt (on) in the usual way (and) had not been cooled down, fire
    would have stood over (*pad*) all this world of the living in such a
    way that everybody would have fear of burning.

7.  One should walk purposefully, as if one were a man without shoes and
    this whole world were full of snakes, scorpions, evil animals, and
    thorns and he were afraid (had fear) that the evil animals might
    bite him or a thorn might go into his foot. \[note indirect speech
    \> direct speech, lesson 4\]

### Additional Reading 16.4-5

Two texts from the *Mādayān ī hazār dādestān*, "the book of a thousand
judgments, on legal issues connected with a man's primary wife, the
*pādixšāyīhā-zan*, "wife-in-authority" (whose children are his heirs).

The first text deals with the question of guardianship (*sālārīh*),
which can be of three kinds:

*būdag* '(always) been, natural': the guardian is a relative;

*kerdag* 'made, designated': the man has designated a guardian (*sālār*)
while alive (not in this text) \[note: this *kerdag* "made" is different
from *pad kardag* "according to what has been done = custom"\].

*gumārdag*, 'appointed' by a local authority, often the *rad*, highest
religious judicial auhority, when the man dies and there is neither a
*būdag* nor a *kerdag*.

A *stūr* is somebody contracted to produce an heir for a man who can not
or has died.

# Lesson 17

## Grammar 17

## Causative and denominative verbs

From verbs and nouns, adjectives, or adverbs secondary verbs can be
formed by adding the suffix *-ēn-* to the present (occasionally past)
stem of the verb. When formed from a verb, the new verb is causative,
when from a noun or adverb, the verb is 'denominative'. We have already
encountered several such verbs.

Occasionally (e.g., *AWN*), one finds the NPers. suffix *-ān-* instead
of *-ēn-*.

The passive of such verbs is formed [by replacing *-ēn-* by
*-īh-*]{.underline}.

#### Causatives

These are formed from either intransitive or transitive verbs:

##### Intransitive verb:

*abzāy-* "to increase" (intrans.) *abzāyēn-* "to increase, cause to
grow" (trans.)

*abzāyīh-* "to be increased, made to grow"

*est-* "to stand" *estēn-* "to make stand, establish, place"

*estīh-* "to be established, placed"

*ras-* "to arrive" *rasēn-* "to cause to arrive, send"

*rasīh-* "to be caused to arrive, be sent"

*šaw-* "to go" *šawēn-* "to cause to go, send off"

*šawīh-* "to be caused to go"

*āy-* "to come" *āyēn-* "to make come"

*abesih-* (*abesīh-*) "to be cut off, perish" *abesihēn-* "to cause to
perish, destroy"

Note that *abesih-* is not a passive in *-īh*-. It is spelled with short
*-ih-* here to distinguish it from the passives.

##### Transitive verbs:

*ōzan-* "to kill" *ōzanēn-* "to cause (sb.) to kill"

*dān-* "to know" *dānēn-* "to cause (sb.) to know"

Causatives from transitive verbs do not have a passive, which would
coincide with the passive of the simple verb!

##### From past stems in *-d/-t*:

*raft* "went" *raftēn-* "to cause (sb.) to go"

*zād* "born" *zādēn-* "to cause (sb.) to be born"

*burd* "carry" *burdēn-* "to cause (sth.) to be carried, brought"

*kerd* "done" *kerdīh-* "to be caused to be done"

#### Denominatives

##### From a noun:

*tarāzūg* "scales" *tarāzūgēn-* "to weigh"

*appar-* "robber" *apparēn-* "become a robber of" (*PV*.4.1, 7.78-9)

##### From an adjective:

*paydāg* "apparent" *paydāgēn-* "to make appear, reveal, to produce"

*paydāgīh-* "to be made to appear, be revealed"

*āgāh* "aware, known" *āgāhēn-* "to make (sb.) aware, inform"

*āgāhīh-* "to be made aware, to learn"

*nērōgōmand* "powerful" *nērōgōmandēn-* "to make powerful, strengthen"

*pērōzgar* "victorious, victor" *pērōzgarīh-* "to be made victorious"

*frāy* "more" *frāyēn-* "further"

##### From an adverb:

*frāz* "forward" *frāzēn-* "bring/move forward, promote"

*abāz* "backward" *abāzēn-* "bring/move backward"

*wanīy-* \<HWBDW(N)\> *wanīyēn-* \<HWBDW(N)yn-\> "to destroy"

(+ *kerdan/būdan* "destroy/be destroyed") *wanīyīh-* \<HWBDW(N)yh-\> "to
be destroyed"

*nēst* *nēstēn-* "annihilate"

(+ *kerdan/būdan* "annihilate/be annihilated")

Notes:

Derived nouns and adjectives from causative and passive verbs are the
same as from simple verbs, see examples below.

*paydāgēn-* is not infrequently spelled -WwsAtDP for -WwYkAtDP.

In the 3rd plural, verbs in *-ēnēnd* not infrequently have only *-ēnd*
by scribal error, e.g., *paydāgēnd* for *paydāgēnēnd* "they make
manifest, reveal," *frōdēnd* for *frōdēnēnd* "they lower"; --
arameogram: \<S[GY]{.underline}TWNynd\> *rawēnēnd* "they make go
(forth)" (*PV*.3.21d), \<S[GY]{.underline}TWNynnd\> (*PV*.3.11c).

*brēhēn-* "fashion," *kirrēn-* "cut up, cut to pieces; whittle (about
the evil creation)," and *rāyēn-* "arrange" are not derived forms and
have passives *brēhēnīh-*, \**kirrēnīh-* (not found?), and *rāyēnīh-*.

*frāyēn-* was connected with *frāy* by folk etymology, but is a
construct based on Av. *frāδaiia-* "further."

*wāyēn-* "lead (as bride)" is from and old verb (Parth. *wāδ-* "to
lead") no longer used in Pahlavi and is related to *wayūg* "bride."

##### From verbs:

*ud pad-iz wirrōyišn nām rāh mānāg abērāh pēš kam-wizōstārān ī
awizīdār-xīrān dārēnd; ud pad-iš [āyēnēnd]{.underline} ō ān ī ǰāwēdānīg
anāgīh*

"and even in the name of 'belief/faith' (the enemies of the *dēn*)
present (*pēš \... dār-*) to those who investigate little and do not
make decisions about things a non-road like (= as if) a road; and
thereby [they make them come]{.underline} to eternal evil"
(*Dk*.5.24.30a)

*abar hōm ud mang amāh rāy bar ō Wištāšp u-š pad ān abar [frāz
xwārēn]{.underline} dahībed Wištāsp*

"bring (*abar \... bar*) Wištāsp *hōm* and hashish on Our (Ohrmazd's)
behalf, and with that (cup) [make]{.underline} him (*-š*)
[drink]{.underline}, (he,) the landlord Wištāsp" (*Dk*.7.4.85)

*nūn-iz pad gētīy pad ān hangōšīdag andar aškomb ī mādar
[hambawīhēnd]{.underline} ud zāyēnd*

"now, too (= still), in the world [they are formed]{.underline} in the
womb of the mother like that and are (then) born" (*Bd*.1.57)

*pad [hambawēnīdārīh]{.underline} ī bawišnīgān ō gētīyīh wašt ī wēnišnīg
gīrišnīg*

"by [the action of forming]{.underline} those who are to be, (the
*mēnōy* state) was changed to *gētīy* state, which is visible and
tangible" (*Dk*.3.105.2)

*abar [wāyēnīdan]{.underline} ī kanīg az pidarān sālārān kadag ō šōy
wis*

"about [leading]{.underline} a young woman (as bride) from the house of
(her) parents (and/or) guardians to the husband's town" (*Dk*.8.31.6)

##### From nouns, adjectives, and adverbs:

*ān petyāragīh ǰud pad dām-dahišnīh nē [agārīhēd]{.underline}*

"that adversary is only (= can only) [be undone]{.underline} by
establishing the creation" (*Bd*.1.35)

*[dōstīhēnd]{.underline} ō yazd ud [nazdīkīhēnd]{.underline} awiš*

"(people) [will be made friends]{.underline} of the gods and [be brought
close]{.underline} to them" (*Dk*.3.107)

*ān-it mard bundahišnīh az madan ī Tāzīgān ō Ērān šahr
[rawāgēnīdan]{.underline} ī ān-išān dušdēnīh*

"there you have it, man, the original establishment from the coming of
the Arabs to Iran, [the propagation]{.underline} of their evil *dēn*"
(*Bd*.0.2)

*Zarduxšt andar ān ī abēzag rōšnīh hāwand amahrspandān az bundahišn
ōrrōn \... padīruftārīh [rawāgēnīdārīh]{.underline} ī dēn andar gēhān
rāy mēnōyīg tāšīd ud payrāst estād*

"Zarduxšt had been fashioned in that pure light like the amahrspands
already from the original establishment and been equipped for the
reception and [propagation]{.underline} of (= receiving and
[propagating]{.underline}) the *dēn* in the world of living beings"
(*Dk*.5.2.1)

*awēšān ī abar pad Wahman mānēnd Zarduxšt awēšān
[rāmēnīdārīh]{.underline} pad gōwišn*

"Zarduxšt, those who dwell with Wahman, [is their
pleasure-giving]{.underline} (= are they given pleasure) by speech?"

*Pōrušasp ō karb-ēw Dūrāsraw nām kē andar ān deh pad ǰādūgīh nāmīgtar
būd raft u-š az zāyišn ī Zarduxšt abdīh ī padiš paydāg būd
[āgāhēnīd]{.underline}*

"Pōrušasp went to a priest called Dūrāsraw who was best known in that
village, and he informed him about (*az*) the birth of Zarduxšt (and)
the marvels that [had been made known]{.underline} about him"
(*Dk*.7.3.4)

*čiyōn-iš ī pad menišn [āgāhīhišnīh]{.underline}*

"according to his [being made aware]{.underline} (= according as he has
been made aware) by his thought" (*Dk*.7.7.29)

*ōh-iz ān ī dādīgīh andar mardōm kē rāy-šān kār [kerbagīhēd]{.underline}
padiš [ahlawīhēnd]{.underline}*

*ān ī adādīh kē rāy-šān kār [bazagīhēd]{.underline} pad-iš
[druwandīhēnd]{.underline}*

"and thus (is) also the adherence to the law (*dādīgīh*) among men,
whereby (*kē rāy*) their work [is turned into good deeds]{.underline}
(and) [they]{.underline} thereby [are made Righteous]{.underline} (and)
the non-adherence to the law (*adādīh*), whereby their work [is turned
into evil deeds]{.underline} (and) [they]{.underline} thereby (*pad-iš*)
[are made wicked]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.119.9)

*[kerbagēnīdan]{.underline} kār padiš bōxtan ī ruwān*

"(how) [to make]{.underline} a work [a good deed]{.underline} (and)
thereby save the soul" (*Dk*.3.122.6)

*ēk niwāxtan ud [nazdīkēnīdan frāzēnīdan]{.underline} ī wehān*

"one thing is: to extol, [bring close]{.underline}, (and) [bring
forward]{.underline} good people" (*Dk*.3.133.21)

*ud wēš-hunar stāyīdan [frāzēnīdan]{.underline} wēš-āhōg nikōhīdan
[abāzēnīdan]{.underline}*

"and to praise and [bring forward]{.underline} those who have more good
features, (but) scorn those who have more blemishes and [bring them
backward]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.243.9)

*pad-iš [anōdagīhēnd]{.underline} mardōm az šnāxtan ī dādār \... ud
[abāzīhēnd]{.underline} az kerbag ud āyōzēnd* \[for *āyōzīhēnd*?\] *ō
bazag*

"thereby (by the evil wrought by Waran) people [are
alienated]{.underline} from knowing the Creator \... and [they are
brought backward]{.underline} from good deeds and they yoke them to evil
deeds" (*Dk*.3.77.5; cf. *Yasna* 46.11)

*ēdōn purr ast az kēn ud frēb ud wiyābāngarīh
[wanīyēnīdārīh]{.underline} ud wišōbišngarīh \... kū nē ēwāz bē ō
hambedīgān ud padīragīgān bē ō-iz xwēšīgān ud ham-gundān \...
[wiyābānēnāg]{.underline} ud wišōbāg ud [wanīyēnāg]{.underline}* *ud
[kēnēnāg]{.underline}*

"she (the Druz) is so full of hate and deception and [leading
astray]{.underline}, destruction, and ruin \... that she not only
[causes]{.underline} the opponents and adversaries, but also her own
kind and her commilitants [to go astray]{.underline}, and ruins and
[detroys]{.underline} (them) and [incites]{.underline} (them) [to
hate/vengeance]{.underline}" (*DD*.36.5)

*ud [wanīyīhēd]{.underline} zēn ī druxtārīh ud abesihēd čār ī frēbāgīh*

"(but in the end her) tools of lying [will be destroyed]{.underline} and
her means of being a deceiver (= her deception) be cut off"
(*DD*.36.11c)

*pad bowandag-menišnīh [frāyēnēnd]{.underline} gēhān ī astōmand ī
ahlāyīh ud tangīh ō druz dahēnd*

"with equanimity [they further]{.underline} the bony world of living
beings of Order and give the Druz a hard time (gives her 'narrowness')"
(*Dk*.7.7.19) --- On *bowandag-menišnīh*, see Text 15.3.

*[frāyēnīdārīh]{.underline} ī gētīy pad harw-ēwēnag ēwēn*

"[the furthering]{.underline} of the world of the living by every kind
of ritual" (*Dk*.5.5.5)

*ēn kū šnūman ī drōn kū gyāg [paydāgēnišn]{.underline} kū gyāg nē
[paydāgēnišn]{.underline} ud čiyōn [paydāgēnišn]{.underline}*

"this: where (in the ritual) [should one announce]{.underline} the
*drōn* \[*šnūman* "propitiation"\]? where [should one not
announce]{.underline} it? and how [should it be announced]{.underline}?"
(*Q&A*.6.1)

*andar yazišn was nīrang daxšag ud nišān ī mēnōy-zōrīh
[paydāgīhēd]{.underline} ō dēwān [tarsēnāg]{.underline} ud
[bēšēnāg]{.underline} ō yazdān azbāyāg ud [urwāhmēnāg]{.underline}*

"during the sacrifice, many ritual actions [are manifested]{.underline}
as marks and signs of the heavenly strength, which
[frightens]{.underline} and [hurts]{.underline} the demons, (but) invoke
the gods and [give them joy]{.underline}" (*DD*.47.29)

##### From adverbial phrases:

*šahrestān Weh-ardašīr pad 3 xwadāy kerd ud Ardašīr Pābagān
[pad-frazāmēnīd]{.underline}*

"the city of Weh-ardašīr was made under three kings, and Ardašīr son of
Pābag ['finalized']{.underline} (completed) it" (*ŠahrĒr*.40) --- From
*pad frazām* "in the end, finally."

##### With *-ān-*:

*nē [wardānīdan]{.underline} ud nē [hammōzānīdan]{.underline} ī ān zan
kē andar dārišn awiš mad būd*

"(and because of) not [making]{.underline} that wife who had come to him
to keep [turn]{.underline} (from evil) and [make (her)
learn]{.underline}" (*AWN*.68.12)

##### Double causative:

A double causative can be made from derived forms of causative verbs:

*[abzāyēnāgēnīdan]{.underline} ān ī ahlaw pad dānāgīh ud kāhēnīdan ī ān
ī druwand pad dušāgāhīh gēhān*

"[to make]{.underline} a Righteous person [into somebody who makes the
world increase]{.underline} (*abzāyēnāg*) with knowledge and making the
wicked decrease (it) with ignorane" (*Dk.*8.24.10)

##### From present and past stems and in *-d/-t*:

*kē az man ān sūr zinēnēd* (\< *zin-*) *ayāb [triftēnēd]{.underline}*
(\< *trift* "stolen")\
"he who makes them take that meal from me or [cause (it) to be
stolen]{.underline}" (*PY*.11.5)

*ud ēn-iz kū kē menišn ō dēn ī Zardušt dahēd xrad hammōxtēd ēd-iz rāy čē
weh dēn hamāg xrad pad menišn-awiš-dahišnīh [hammōxtīhēd]{.underline}*

"and this too: he who give his thought to Zarathustra's *dēn*, learns
wisdom; and (that is) for this reason that the Good Dēn is all wisdom
(and) one [is caused to learn]{.underline} it by 'giving one's thought
to it'" (*Dk*.9.54.7)

*abar ǰud-āhangīh ī-š abāg [zādēnīdārān]{.underline}*

"about his (Z.) having different leanings from (his) [birth
parents]{.underline}" (*WZ*.11.0)

*dehīgān kanīg pad ǰādūgīh hambasānēnīdan ud abar bērōn kerdan ī az ān
deh ō [zādēnīdārān]{.underline} škeft pahikārīd*

"the villagers argued (*pahikārīd*) strongly with [those who caused her
to be born]{.underline} (= her birth parents) (to make them)
[regard]{.underline} (her) [as an adversary]{.underline} (*hambasānēn-*)
because of (her) sorcery and about expelling her from that village"
(*Dk*.7.2.6)

*abāg zan ī ag-dēn [gādīhēd]{.underline} az ān gādan frazend andar
aškamb frāz bawēd ēg-iš wināh čē*

"someone who [is made to have sex]{.underline} with a woman of an evil
*dēn* (and) a child is conceived in her belly because of that sex, then
what is his sin?" (*RAF*.42.1)

***čiyōn ān druz pahikārēd** kū-š stahmagīh čiyōn bē bawād*

*ast kē ēdōn gōwēd ay čiyōn pad ān druz pahikārīhād*

*kū-š stōw bē [kerdīhād]{.underline} kē az ōy ī rist ō ōy ī zīndag abar
dwārēd pad hamrēd*

"'How does one fight that lie-demon?' that is, how can there be
oppression for/of her?

There is one who says, the meaning is: how is battle to be engaged
against that lie-demon

so that oppression [may be caused to be perpetrated]{.underline} on her,
who runs from the dead onto the living with (= causing) direct
contamination?" (*PV*.9.57) \[only ms. L4 \<krtyh't\>; K1 has
\<-WNyh't\'\> and IM, TU1 \<-WN't\'\>\]

*nasāy ō āb ud ātaxš [burdēnišn]{.underline}* *pad ēč meh-dādestānīh nē
pādixšāy*

"[causing]{.underline} *nasāy* [to be carried]{.underline} (or:
"[causing]{.underline} someone [to carry]{.underline} *nasāy*?) onto
water and fire is not authorized, (not even) by any 'higher law'"
(*RAF*.104.2)
