height="0.25in"} \<-x~2~y wynšn\'\> (or: *barēnišn*?).

## Phraseology

## Adverbs of manner

This is a review of common expressions of manner, most of which are well
known by now.

*ōh* W˚ \<KN\> "thus; in the usual way"

*ēdōn* WWWtdA \<'ytwn\'\> "in this way"

*ōwōn* (WwYwA) WWwYwA \<'wgwn\'\> "in that way"

*čiyōn* (wïDC , WwïDC) WWwïDC \<cygwn\'\> "as, such as; how?"

[Note]{.underline}: in many manuscripts, the spellings OW *ō*, nLW *ōy*,
and W˚ *ōh* are used interchangably.

#### *ōh* "thus; in the usual way"

This is used 1. in its literal meaning of "thus, in this/that way, as
follows" commonly before verbs, but also in other positions; and 2. to
indicate the "unmarked" situation, which does not need to be specified:
"in the usual way."

*ud druz [ōh]{.underline} dōyīd hēnd kū* \...

"and the lie-demons spoke [thus/as follows]{.underline}: \..."
(*Dk*.7.4.39)

*[ōh-i]{.underline}z nazdīkīh ī yazd pad yazd-šnāsīh ud šnāxtan ī yazd
pad dānišn bawēd*

"[and in this way]{.underline}, the closeness of god is by way of
recognizing the god, and recognizing the god is by way of knowledge"
(*Dk*.3.107.3)

*agar [ōh-iz]{.underline} ašmāh dōstīh rāy nibišt pas-iz man dušxwār
sahist az ēd-ōwōn stāyišn*

"if you wrote [in (just) this way]{.underline} because of friendship,
then also it seemed difficult for me from this kind of praise"
(*DD*.0.10)

*harwisp ān ī weh-dahāg yazd ī mēnōy ud kē-iz gētīy \... pad frārōnīh
[ōh]{.underline} abāyēnd yaštan*

"all the deities in the other as well as in this world who give good
(gifts) should be sacrificed to with goodness [in the usual
way]{.underline}" (*PY*.1.19)

*u-š az ōy pursīd Zardušt kū kē mard hē; hād nē pad yašt ī fradom būd az
pēš paydāg*

*u-š dānist kū hōm [ōh]{.underline} rasēd ud ka mad būd ā-š pursīd
abāyist*

"and Z. asked him: 'who are you, man?'

that is, it was not at the first sacrifice, (as) manifest from before
(i.e., earlier),

and he knew: the Hōm will come [in the usual way]{.underline} (i.e., as
before)" (*PY*.9.1)

#### *ēdōn*, *ōwōn*, *čiyōn*

These three are used in a variety of ways, which need to be carefully
distinguished.

*ōwōn* and *čiyōn* can be combined with the demonstrative pronouns
(*ēd/ēn/ān-*, *ān-čiyōn*) and all three with *ham-* for emphasis
(*ham-ēdōn*, *ham-čiyōn*), from which they can be separated by *-iz*
(*ham-iz ōwōn*).

Note especially the use of *ēdōn*, *ōwōn* in the sense of "such" and
"so, to such a degree" with adjectives/adverbs.

*ēdōn* and *ōwōn* are frequently followed by *čiyōn*, either directly or
with intervening words: *ēdōn (\...) čiyōn*, etc.

See also on Adverbial clauses of comparison-result (Lesson 22).

##### *ēdōn* "thus, in this way; so":

*nē ān ī [ēdōn]{.underline} xwarrahōmand ǰādūg bawēd*

"someone [so]{.underline} glorious cannot be a sorcerer" (*Dk*.7.2.8)

*ka frōd nihēd pad ēd dārēd kū āb az nasāy abāz ō āb rasēd ā-š čē
kunišn*

*ul stānišn u-š [ēdōn dūr]{.underline} bē barišn [kū]{.underline} āb ī
az nasāy abāz ō āb nē rasēd -- nē rēman*

"when one lays (the *nasāy* back into the water), thinking: the water
from the *nasāy* will reach back to the water, then what should one do?
--- One should take it up (= lift it) and carry it [so far]{.underline}
away [that]{.underline} the water from the *nasāy* does not reach back
to the water, (then) one is not polluted" (*ZFJ*, p. 494) \[about
removing a carcass from a body of water\]

*bē andar [ēn-ēdōn]{.underline} gumēzagīh hamāg abēzagīhā rawāg būdan nē
bē kōšišnīg(īhā) šāyēd*

"but, in [this kind of]{.underline} Mixture (that we see now), is not
possible for the entire (*dēn*) to become propagated in its pure state,
but (= other than) by fighting" (*Dk*.5.24.14a)

*dānāg (ī) uzmūdag-xrad [ān-ēdōn]{.underline} guft*

"a knowledgeable man whose wisdom had been tested, said [as
follows]{.underline}" (*Ōšnar* 54)

*ka gištag-ēw kē kālbod ī mardōmīh nē paydāg ka sag nimāyēnd čiyōn
nimāyišn; bē nē škāfišn [ham-ēdōn]{.underline} sag nimāyišn*

"when it is a fetus (in) which a human body is not manifest, when they
show a dog, how is it to be shown? It is not to be split open (to
check), (but) should be shown a dog [in the same manner]{.underline} (as
in the preceding cases)" (*ZFJ*, p. 468)

Note the use of *ēdōn \... kū* to explain something:

*Zrēy Frāxkerd pad kust ī nēmrōz kanārag ī Harburz 3 ēk ī ēn zamīg
dārēd*

*ud [ēdōn]{.underline} Frāx-kerd [kū]{.underline}-š 1000 war andar dāšt
estēd*

"the Frāxkerd Sea (is) in the southern direction, alongside (Mount)
Harburz (and) has (= occupies) one-third of this earth;

and (it is) [thus]{.underline} (called) Frāx-kerd (= 'made-wide')
[because]{.underline} 1000 lakes are contained in it" (*Bd*.10.2)

##### *ōwōn* "so, in that way, such":

*u-šān čē wināh kerd kē-šān ruwān [ōwōn]{.underline} garān pādifrāh
barēd*

"what sin did they commit whose soul carries (= suffers)
[such]{.underline} a heavy punishment" (*AWN*.99.3)

*agar [ēd-ōwōn]{.underline} nē būd \...*

"if it were not [in this way]{.underline} \..." (*Dk*.7.4.63)

*[ēd-iz ōwōn]{.underline} nibišt kū \...*

"[and]{.underline} it is written [in the following way]{.underline}:
\..."

*[ān-ōwōn]{.underline} wehīh ud xwarrah*

"[in that manner]{.underline} (as I just explained) (are) goodness and
Xwarrah" (*Dk*.5.4.2)

*ud [ōwōn]{.underline} xwadāy andar Dēn Mazdēsn weh-xwādāy nām ud pad
gēhān pahlom*

"and [such a]{.underline} king's name in the Mazdayasnian Dēn is "good
king" and in the world (at large) "the best" (*Dk*.3.273.3)

*andar [ān-ōwōn]{.underline} pādufrāh*

"in [that kind of]{.underline} punishment" (*Dk*.7.4.69)

*4-ān zōrān ī tan [ham-iz ōwōn]{.underline} pad-iš frāz rawēnd
[čiyōn]{.underline} tazāgān āb pad wād*

"the four 'powers' of the body go forth (moved) by it (= the heart) [in
the same way]{.underline}, [too]{.underline}, [as]{.underline} flowing
waters (moved) by the wind" (*WZ*.30.21)

##### *ōwōn \... ī*, *ēdōn \... ī* "in such a way that":

Here, the *ī* is often missing in the mss. and must be added from the
context; its presence is alsways explicit when it has an enclitic
pronoun, *ī-š*, etc.:

*tis-ēw pad dahān ud wēnīg frāz kunišn [ēdōn ī]{.underline}-š wād ī az
dahān ud wēnīg bē āyēd bē ō ātaxš nē rasēd*

"(when speaking near the fire) one should place something over the mouth
and nose, [in such a manner that]{.underline} the wind from one's mouth
and nose does not reach the fire" (*PR*.37a.3)

*ka [ēdōn ī]{.underline} pad gōmēz ud āb abāyēd šustan ā-š 3 stēr wināh*

"when it is [in such a manner that]{.underline} it needs to be washed
with *gōmēz* and water, then he has a sin of three *stēr*" (*ZFJ*, p.
478)

*ud ēn mānsr ud dēn abestāg harwisp-āgāhīh čiyōn weh mēnōyān
nazd-brahmīhātar pad hamāg āwāz ī gēhānīgān [ōwōn]{.underline} widēmāsīg
[ī]{.underline} widerd az harw ayābagīh ī mardōmān*

"and this sacred word and tradition of the all-awareness of the Avesta,
since (it is spoken) more closely to the manner (*brahm*) of the good
entities in the other world, is [so]{.underline} miraculous in all the
languages of people in this world [that]{.underline} it has gone beyond
all reach of men" (*Dk*.5.24.12)

*ka-šān az frazend-xwāyišnīh-iz nērōg \... an-ēmēdīh rasēd*

*ēmēd ī az zīndagīh bīm (ī) az margīh harw 2 ō nizārīh
[ōwōn]{.underline} rasēd [(ī)]{.underline} az zīndagīh bē-ayās ō margīh
frāz-ayās bawēnd*

*\... [ōwōn]{.underline} wašt bawēd [ī]{.underline}-šān ārzōgīhēd kū kāč
nē zād būd-ēnd*

"when they (people) lose hope even of the power of procreation \...

(then) the hope of life and fear of death both come to tenuousness [in
such a way that]{.underline} (= become [so]{.underline} tenuous
[that]{.underline}) their longing (*-ayās*) for life (goes) away (*bē-*)
and their longing for death (comes) to the fore (*frāz-*).

\... (and their situation) becomes [so]{.underline} changed
[that]{.underline} they are filled with the desire: If only they had not
been born!" (*Dk*.3.178.7)

##### *čiyōn* "how?":

*[čiyōn]{.underline} az ān ī seǰōmand ī bīmōmand ī was-anāgīh axwān ō ēn
ī aseǰ axwān ī apetyārag mad hē*

"[how]{.underline} have you come from that dangerous and frightening
existence with much evil to this dangerless existence without the
Adversary?" (*MX*.1.149)

*ka-š pārag ēw xward ud kē nigerēd xōn wēnēd dādestān ī pārag čē ud
[čiyōn]{.underline}*

"when he has eaten the piece (of skin he bit off his cheek) and he who
looks sees blood, what and [how]{.underline} is the legal situation of
the piece (of skin)?" (*RAF*.86.1)

##### *čiyōn \... ēdōn(-iz)* "as \... thus/so (also)":

*[čiyōn]{.underline}-itān amāh dād hēm amahrspandān [ēdōn]{.underline}
amāh srāyišn dahēd*

"[as]{.underline} (in the same way that, because) you created us, O
*amahrspand*s, [so]{.underline} give us protection!" (*PY*.58.5)

*[čiyōn]{.underline} wināh marag was [ēdōn-iz]{.underline} wizārišnīhā*

"[in the same way that]{.underline} sins are many, [thus
also]{.underline} (are) the resolutions (of sins many)" (*Dk*.5.10.2)

*[čiyōn]{.underline} Wāy ī wattar appurdār ud zadār
[ēdōn-iz]{.underline} Wāy ī weh kōxšīdār ud ham-padīrag ī Wāy ī wattar*

"[as]{.underline} (in the same way that) the bad Wāy robs and strikes
down, [thus also]{.underline} does the good Wāy fight and (in the ) same
(way) against the bad Wāy" (*DD*.29.4)

*andar harw 3 gyāg pāyagīhā; ud [čiyōn]{.underline} gyāg
[ēdōn-iz]{.underline} xwārīh ud nēkīh ud a-xwārīh ud anāgīh*

"in all three places (paradise, etc.), there are (various) levels, and
[as]{.underline} (is; = according to) the place (in each of them: high
or low) [thus also]{.underline} (will there be) comfort and goodness and
discomfort and evil" (*Dk*.5.8.7)

##### *čiyōn bawēd kū*, *čiyōn kū/ka, čim ka* "how come?":

*[čiyōn bawēd kū]{.underline} nasāy ō āb ud ātaxš rasēd padiš wināhgār
nē bawēd*

"[how come that]{.underline} *nasāy* comes to water and fire, and he
(the perpetrator) does not become a 'sinner'?" (*ZFJ*.517)

*[čiyōn kū]{.underline}-t pad zamīg nē hammōxt ō man ān ī abēzag rāh ī
rāst*

" [how come]{.underline} you did not on earth teach me (ind. obj.) the
pure straight road?" (*WZ*.35.42)

See Lesson 14 on constructions with *hammōz- hammōxt*.

*[čiyōn ka]{.underline}-mān pad zīndagān harw nēkīh pad āgenēn būd nūn
tō ō wahišt ud man ō dōšox hamē nayēnd*

"[how come]{.underline} we had every goodness together in life (but) now
they lead *you* to paradise and *me* to hell?" (*AWN*.68.2)

*u-t wehīh ud frārōnīh [čim ka]{.underline} nē hammōxt ham kē-m pas
wehīh ud frārōnīh kerd hē*

"and [how come]{.underline} you did not teach me, me, who (*kē-m*)
afterward would have performed goodness and virtuousness?" (*AWN*.68.10)

##### *čiyōn* conjunction "as, in the way that":

*[čiyōn]{.underline} az dēn ī Mazdēsnān paydāg*

"[as]{.underline} is manifest from the *dēn* of the Mazdayasnians"

*ān mard ka-š ēd-ōwōn abdīh az gāw dīd nē ōzad bē abāz ō Kāy-Us šud
[čiyōn]{.underline}-iš dīd guft*

"when that man saw such a miracle from the bull, he did not kill it, but

*nē amāh pas mazdēsn kēnēnēnd* \[ms. kynynd\] *wēš az [ān

"the Mazdayasnians will not hereafter hate us more than [the
way]{.underline} our own children and sons (do)" (*Dk*.7.9.7)

*ēn yašt ī gētōxrīd kerbag [ham-čiyōn]{.underline} yašt ī nāybar bawēd
ayāb nē*

"is the good deed of this ritual for the dead (*yašt ī gētōxrīd*) just
like the initiation ritual (*nāybar*) or not?" (*DD*.78.4)

*ātaxš ī Warahrān \... [harw čiyōn]{.underline} bē ōzanēd \... margarzān
bawēd*

"[in whatever way]{.underline} one kills a Warahrān fire one is
'death-deserving' (guilty of a capital sin)" (*PR*.18e5)

##### *ēdōn/ōwōn čiyōn* "(just) as, like"

*[ēdōn čiyōn]{.underline} tō* "[like]{.underline} you"

*[ēdōn čiyōn]{.underline} Ohrmazd pad bun-dahišn dād abāz bawēd*

"[just as]{.underline} Ohrmazd had established (it) at the first
establishment, it will become again" (*PR*.48.58)

*[ōwōn čiyōn]{.underline} pad dēn gōwēd kū*

"[as]{.underline} it says in the *dēn*"

##### *ēdōn/ōwōn \... čiyōn* "as/so \... as, like"

*dām ī Ohrmazd pad mēnōyīh [ēdōn]{.underline} parward \...
[čiyōn]{.underline} šusr homānāg*

"the creation of Ohrmazd was nurtured in the world of thought
[like]{.underline} semen" (*Bd*.1.58)

az ātaxš hamāg gyāg dūd abar āxēzēd*

"and he [so]{.underline} soiled every creation [as]{.underline} when
from a fire smoke rises everywhere" (*Bd*.4.27)

*ān (ī) az ān zan pas az bē-widerišnīh ī ān mard zād

"the (child) that was born after the passing of that man becomes

tārān*

## Nouns expressing manner

*ēwēnag* WKwYwˆÅ \<'dwynk\'\> "manner, way, kind"

(*ēwēn* WwYwˆÅ \<'dwyn\'\> "manner, way"

*gōnag* WKWwY \<gwnk\'\> "kind, sort"

*šōn*, *šōnag* WKWwÍ , WWwÍ \<šwn(k)\'\> "manner"

*sān* WwaJ \<s'n\'\> "manner"

*rāh* aåÒ \<l'h\> "way"

*dar* ABV \<BBA\> "kind, issue, way, respect

### Expressions with *ēwēnag* "manner" 

This noun occurs combined with demonstrative and indefinite pronouns and
various adverbs in adjectival function and in prepositional phrases in
adverbial function and can be repeated to indicate indefiniteness.

#### Noun

*abar [ēwēnag]{.underline} ī Ohrmazd dahišnān hamēstār*

"about [the manner]{.underline} of the opponent(s) of Ohrmazd's
creations" (*Dk*.3.48.1)

*[pad harw ēwēnag]{.underline} paristišn ī Ardawān būd ān kanīzag kerd
estād*

"in [every way]{.underline} the service of Ardawān was, that girl had
done it" (*KN*.2.1)

#### Adjectival

*ud ēn-iz guft estēd kū [ēd-ēwēnag]{.underline} wazurg xwarrah ud wehīh
az ham-tōhmag awisānišnīg*

"and this too is said that [such]{.underline} a great *xwarrah* and
goodness is not to be separated from those of the same seed"
(*Dk*.5.4.7) --- About the line of mythical heroes.

*[was-ēwēnag]{.underline} kēš ud wurrōyišn*

"[many kinds of]{.underline} teachings and faiths" (*AWN*.1.9)

*Ādur Gušnasp tā xwadāyīh ī Kay Husrōy pad [ān-ēwēnag]{.underline}
pānagīh ī gēhān hamē kerd*

"until the rule of Kay Husrōy, the Gušnasp fire was protecting (*pānagīh
\... kerd*) the world of the living in [that way]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.18.8)

*Azdahāg andar xwadāyīh ǰuwān zan dēw abar hišt ud ǰuwān mard abar parīg
hišt; u-šān pad dīdarīh ī ōy marzišn kerd; az [ān-ēwēnag]{.underline}
kunišn zangīg būd*

"during his rule, Azdahāg let a demon onto a young woman and a witch
onto a young man, and they had intercourse while he watched; from [that
kind of]{.underline} activity the negroes came about" (*Bd*.14B.2)

*ud [anīy-ēwēnag]{.underline} xwadāy ān kē amaragānīg kam ō xwēš kām ud
xwēš kām ō xwēš xrad handāzēd*

"and [another kind of]{.underline} king (is) the one who measures the
general will against his own will and his own will against his own
wisdom" (*Dk*.3.273.4)

*ud ēdar gōwēd mādayān 3 saxwan andar [hamāg-ēwēnag]{.underline} yazišn
ī Ohrmazd*

"and here he says in particular three sayings about (*andar*)
sacrificing to Ohrmazd in [all ways]{.underline}" (*Dk*.9.49.5)

*anīz was tis ī abd ud saxwan ī ēd 7 frašn hangerdīg-ēw ī az
[harw-ēwēnag]{.underline} dānišn āgāhīh*

"many other wondrous things and sayings (about) which these (= the
following) seven questions (are) a summary from [every way
of]{.underline} knowledge and awareness" (*Dk*.8.14.9)

*bē was [ǰud-ēwēnag]{.underline} ī nē hambedīg ī ēk gētīy būd šāyēd*

"but many (things are) [of different kinds]{.underline}, which can have
no single counterpart in this world (*gētīy* adj.)" (*Dk*.3.142.3)

*andar gētīy \... marg ud seǰ ud niyāz dard ī [ēwēnag
ēwēnag]{.underline} ō mardōmān*

"in this world, death, danger, need, and pain [of various
kinds]{.underline} (came) upon men" (*Bd*.5.3)

#### Adverbial

*ēk ēd ī paydāg bawēd kū did ka az stardīh frāz būd ōy ǰādūg ēg-iš ō
Zarduxšt [ham-ēwēnag]{.underline} drāyīd*

"one (i.e. another thing) is this that is manifest: when that sorcerer
came out of his stupor, then again (*did*) he howled [in the same
way]{.underline} at Zarduxšt" (*Dk*.7.3.43)

*pas-iz abar gōwišn ī ān dastwar kē [anīy-ēwēnag]{.underline} ast
ǰud-dādestānīh nēst*

"and next, there is no disagreement about the sayings of that dastwar
for whom there is (something done?) [differently]{.underline}"
(*DD*.0.21)

*pad bōxtagīh rāstīh [harw ēwēnag]{.underline} abē-gumān būd [ēč
ēwēnag]{.underline} aziš bē [nē]{.underline} estād*

"about salvation (and) truth (one should) [in every way]{.underline} be
without doubt and should [in no way]{.underline} stand away from it"
(*Dk*.4.91)

*ud ēn-iz kū mad ō ōy [kadār-iz ēwēnag-ēw]{.underline} ī-š zast*

"and this too: (the *hōm*) came to him [in whichever way]{.underline}
that he requested (it)" (*Dk*.9.36.5)

([*kadār-iz ēwēnag-ēw* \< *kadār-iz-ēw ēwēnag*]{.underline})

*[čē ēwēnag]{.underline} mad hēnd mēnōyīhā pad hamēstārīh kamālagān
dēwān ō mēnōyān yazdān*

"[in what way]{.underline} they come through the other world for
opposition (i.e., to fight one another): the (demon-)headed demons
against the gods in the other world" (*Bd*.5.0)

##### With prepositions:

*[pad ān-ēwēnag]{.underline} sarmāg \... ud gandagīh dīd kē-m hagriz
andar gētīy [pad ān ēwēnag]{.underline} nē dīd ud nē āšnūd*

"and (I) saw [such]{.underline} heat and stench as I have never seen or
heard (about) [in that way]{.underline} in this world" (*AWN*.18.2)

*ud ka Ohrmazd [pad ēn ēwēnag]{.underline} guft man škoft bē mānd ham*

"and when Ohrmazd spoke [in this way]{.underline}, I remained awed"
(*AWN*.101.6)

*awēšān haft xwahān \... mowbedān [pad ēč ēwēnag]{.underline} pānagīh bē
[nē]{.underline} hišt*

"the mowbeds [in no way]{.underline} relinquished the protection of
those seven sisters (of Ardā Wirāz)" (*AWN*.2.19)

*[pad tis-iz ēwēnag]{.underline} ō Mihrēn ī man pus [ma]{.underline} ē
rasēd pēš az ān ī ka pid pad baxt šawēd*

"let her [not in any way]{.underline} come to (= be given to) my son
Mihrēn before the father goes to his destiny" (*MHD*.G.8)

*Ohrmazd abāg-iz [čē-ēwēnag]{.underline} dānistan ī dām frazām ī kār ō
padīrag ī Ganāg Mēnōy āštīh abar dāšt*

"even though (*abāg-iz*) he knew [how]{.underline} the end (*frazām ī
kār*) of the creation (would be), Ohrmazd offered (*ō padīrag ī \...
abar dāšt*) the Foul Spirit peace" (*Bd*.1.19)

##### *ēwēnag \... ī* "such a manner that":

Cf. *ōwōn \... ī* (above).

*Zand [pad ēwēnag-ēw]{.underline} guft estēd [ī]{.underline} pad mayānag
ī gēhān rawāgtar ud andar gēhān āšnāgtar*

"the Zand has been spoken [in such a manner that]{.underline} it is more
current in the world and better known in the world" (*Dk*.5.24.12a)

*[pad ēč ēwēnag]{.underline} (ī) šāyēd*

"[in any way]{.underline} it is possible" (*RAF*.37.2)

##### With particle *ī* + prep.:

*ud abārīg [ī az ēn ēwēnag]{.underline}*

"and the others [of this kind]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.48.1)

*u-š az awēšān pursīd kū ka ašmāh kerdgār ud abzārōmand paydāg hēd čē
cim rāy kār [ī pad ēn ēwēnag]{.underline} hamē kunēd*

"and he asked them: when/if (= since) you are clearly mighty and
resourceful, why do you keep doing work [of this kind]{.underline}?"
(*Dk*.6D.5)

##### With numerals:

*rāmišn [2-ēwēnag]{.underline}*

"joy is (of) [two kinds]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.63.2)

*saxwan ī [2-ēwēnag]{.underline} ma gōw*

"do not speak words of [two kinds]{.underline} (ambiguous, both good and
bad?)!" (*AAM*.96)

*hunar rāyenīdan pad xūb-burdārīh ī [2-ēwēnag]{.underline} hunar andar
2-gōnag zamānag*

"directing one's talents by (*or* for) supporting well [the two
kinds]{.underline} of talent in the two kinds of times (looking toward
the future or the past?)" (*Dk*.3.66) (see on *gōnag* below)

*ka gōwēd kū ān ī tō sahēd ayāb ān ī tō kāmēd ayāb ān ī tō passandē ayāb
ān ī tō abāyēd harw 4 [ēw-ēwēnag]{.underline}*

"when one says: that which seems (good) you or that which you wish or
that which you like or that which seems fitting to you, (then) all four
are [in one and the same way]{.underline} (= identical)" (*MHD*.43.2)

##### With nouns:

*[āsn-xrad-ēwēnag \... gōšōsrūd-xrad-ēwēnag]{.underline}*

"[in the manner of]{.underline} the in-born wisdom \... [in the manner
of]{.underline} the wisdom acquired-through-the ears" (*Dk*.3.63.2)

*[karb-ēwēnag]{.underline} druz mānēd*

"[the *karb*-kind of]{.underline} lie-demon remains" (*Dk*.7.10.5)

##### Substantivized with *-īh*:

*abar ēwēn ī wastarg šustan wināh ī az [ǰud-ēwēnagīh]{.underline}*

"about the customary way of washing a garment (and) the sin from [doing
it in a different way]{.underline}" (*Dk*.8.38.41)

*abāz ō Kāy-Us šud u-š az [čē-ēwēnagīh]{.underline} āgāhēnīd*

"(Srid) returned to Kāy-Us and apprised him of [how it was]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.4.15)

##### Adverbial with *-īhā*:

*zanišn ī gōspandān abar [čē-ēwēnagīhā]{.underline} dādestān ī ǰud ǰud
zanišn ī pad nigerišnīg-zanišnīh dārišn*

"the striking of cattle: about [in what way]{.underline} the law about
striking (them) separately while striking (them) carefully (*or*
intentionally?) should be kept" (*Dk*.8.24.8)

*čiyōn ō wizārišn ī wināh ī pidar [frayādišnīgtar-ēwēnagīhā]{.underline}
uzēnag kunišn*

"because he should expend [it in such a manner as to be of the greatest
help]{.underline} for the resolution (atonement) of the father's sin"
(*RAF*.141.2)

### 

### Expressions with *gōnag* "kind, sort"

These function much like the expressions with *ēwēnag*, but are not so
common.

*u-šān pad pēm ud panīr ud tis-ēw [az ēn gōnag]{.underline} drōn bē
sāzišn*

"and they should prepare the *drōn* with milk and cheese and [this sort
of]{.underline} things" (*ZFJ*, pp. 532-3)

*agar pad bēl-ēw ayāb taber-ēw tis-ēw ī [az ēn gōnag]{.underline}
ǰumbēnēd ud 3-paywand nē rēman*

"if one moves something [of this sort]{.underline} (of dead matter) with
a spade or an axe and one (moves it) by three (men) connected, one is
not polluted" (*ZFJ*, p. 667)

*ōwōn čiyōn gētīy pahnāy abāg drahnāy rāst mardōm-iz
[ham-gōnag]{.underline}*

"just as the width of this world is equal to its length, men are [of the
same sort]{.underline}" (*Bd*.28.3)

*andar ān āwām \... hamāg mardōm frēftār bē bawēnd ēk ōy did rāy wad
xwāhēnd ud mihr wazurg [ǰud-gōnag]{.underline} bē bawēd*

"in that age all men will be deceived; they will seek bad things for one
another and great love will be [of a different sort]{.underline}"
(*ZWY*.4.13)

*stāyišn yazišn ud azbāyišn ī yazdān hamāg [ēk-gōnag]{.underline}
abestāg-gōwišnīh*

"the praise of, sacrifice to, and invoking of the gods is all [one
sort]{.underline}: saying the Avesta" (*Purs*.31.1)

*ud az-iš \... wēnīšn ī [was-gōnag]{.underline} anāgīh čiyōn paydāg*

"and how is the seeing (= suffering) of [many sorts of]{.underline} evil
manifest from it?" (*Dk*.3.151.5; about the evils of the time)

*an az tō abardar ham [pad was-gōnag]{.underline} xīr*

"I (the goat) am superior to you (the Assyrian tree) [in many
sorts]{.underline} of things" (*DA*.6)

*urwar xwābargar ī was-gōnag* (spelled \<ws-gwnk\'\>) *ī tarr ī zargōn ī
harw gētīyān aziš dārišn ī zīyišn*

"the beneficial moist, green plants [of many sorts]{.underline} from
which all things in this world (get what) supports life" (*StS*.8.5)

*mard (ī) pad ēn ēwēnag ēg-iš [pad ēč gōnag]{.underline} nām-iz ī
hērbedīh yōjdahrgarīh padiš nē sazāg*

"a man (who behaves) in this manner, then [in no way]{.underline} is
even the name of *hērbed* and purifier suitable for him" (*RAF*.9.7)

*u-t nimāyēm \... pādifrāh ī [gōnag gōnag]{.underline} kē dēwān ud
ǰādūgān ō bazakkarān kunēnd*

"and we shall show you [the various kinds]{.underline} of punishment
that the demons and sorcerers perpetrate on the evil-doers" (*AWN*.5.5)

### Expressions with *šōn* (*šōnag*) "way, manner, kind"

These function much like the expressions with *ēwēnag* and *gōnag*, but
are rare.

*ud wattar-dād zandīg ud tarsāg ud yahūd ud abārīg ī [az ēn
šōn]{.underline} hēnd*

"and those with the worst law are the Manicheans, the Christians, and
the Jews and the others [of this sort]{.underline}" (*ŠnŠ*.6.7)

*gandum ud ǰaw ud brinǰ \... ud naxōd ud abārīg ī [az ēn
šōn]{.underline} ī ǰōrdāg xwānēnd*

"wheat, barley, rice \... and peas and the others [of this
sort]{.underline}, which they call 'cereal'" (*Bd*.16.11)

*abārīg-iz ān ī [az ān šōn]{.underline} xwāstag kē dārišn bē grift abāz
nē āwarišn*

"and the remaining property [of that sort]{.underline} which was taken
to 'hold', is not to be brought back" (*MHD*.13.9)

*rōz ī čahārom Wizarš dēw āyēd ud ruwān ī druwandān [pad ān
šōn]{.underline} bandēd*

"on the fourth day, the demon Wizarš comes and binds the soul of the
wicked [in that manner]{.underline}" (*MX*.1.161)

*abar tis tis kū [pad čē šōn]{.underline} dād estēd u-šān hamēstārīh čē
mad*

"about each individual thing: [in what way]{.underline} (as what sort of
thing?) it was created and what opposition came upon them" (*Bd.*24.0,
chapter heading)

*Warestān kē-š war ud passāxt aziš paydāg ud abārīg ī
[ham-šōn]{.underline}*

"the Book on Oaths, from which are manifest oaths and ordeals and the
other things [of the same sort]{.underline}" (*WZ*.28.4)

*ud ast ī az anīy āmēg [pad ham-šōn]{.underline}*

"and there are things that are mixed from other (things) [in the same
way]{.underline}" (*Dk*.4.43)

*abar [šōn ud čār]{.underline} ī-š pad abāz dāštan ī duzz ud gurg az
gōspandān*

"about the [manner]{.underline} (in which) [and means]{.underline} (by
which) he is to keep (*-š dāštan*) thieves and wolves away from the
sheep" (*Dk*.8.23.8)

*abar zamānag rāyēnīdārīh [šōnag]{.underline}*

"about the [ways]{.underline} of managing time" (*Dk*.3.68.1)

### Expressions with *sān* "way, manner, kind"

These function much like the expressions with *ēwēnag*, but are quite
rare:

*abar [sān]{.underline} ī gēhān razm*

"about [the manner]{.underline} of the battle of (= fought by) the world
of the living" (*D*k.3.124.1)

*[sān]{.underline} ī madan ī ō a-wināhīh ēn-iz dō*

"[the ways]{.underline} to come to being without sin are these two"
(*D*k.3.117.2)

*ud kēšdārān kē yazd kāmag harw rōz ō [sān-ēw]{.underline} waštan kēš
\... yazdīh aziš bē*

*pad hudōstīh ī-š kāmēd fradāg kām pašēmān im rōz kām hudōst guft estēd*

"and those having (other) beliefs, whose belief is that god's wish
changes every day into [some]{.underline} (different)
[manner]{.underline} \... (they take) away from him 'divinity';

for (= instead of) the friendliness he wishes: tomorrow (his) wish (will
be) sorry, (although) today (his) wish has been said to be friendly"
(*Dk*.3.396.7)

### Expressions with *rāh* "way"

This usage recalls English "way."

*čiyōn ān pid mardōmān xward [rāh nēst]{.underline}*

"for there is [no way]{.underline} for people to eat that flesh (of a
corpse)" (*DD*.80.11)

*[pad ān rāh]{.underline} paydāgīhēd wazurg sūd ī frayādišnīgīh ī-š az
zīndag-ruwān yaštan*

"[in that way]{.underline} is made manifest the great benefit there is
from performing the 'ritual for the soul-while-alive' to help him (in
the beyond)" (*DD*.16.13a)

***hayār-barišnīh** [pad hamāg rāh]{.underline} hayārīh ud ǰādagōwīh
kerdan*

"'bringing help' (is) helping and interceding [in all ways]{.underline}"
(*PY*.62.1a)

*[pad ēč rāh]{.underline} nasāy pad nigerišn jōyīdan [nē]{.underline}
dastwarīhā*

"[in no way]{.underline} is it according to the *dastwar*s to 'chew
*nasāy*' deliberately" (*RAF*.57.2)

*ān ēk rāh gīrēd ī ahlāyīh ud [ma]{.underline} pad frāxīh ud
[ma]{.underline} pad tangīh ud [ma pad ēč rāh]{.underline} az-iš wardēd*

"take that one path, that of Righteousness, and [do not]{.underline}
turn from it [in any way]{.underline}, [(n)either]{.underline} in
well-being [(n)or]{.underline} (when) in a tight spot (distress)!"
(*AWN*.101.8)

*ud čē ān ī [pad ēč rāh]{.underline} an-āzarm nē kunišn \...*

*pad burdārīh ōy passandišnīgtar kē anāgīh ud petyārag ī-š az Ahrimen ud
dēwān ud wattarān abar rasēd hunsandīhā ud pad kāmag ō grīw padīrēd ud
[pad ēč rāh]{.underline} ruwān ī xwēš [nē]{.underline} āzārēd*

'And what is this that one should [not]{.underline} dishonor [in any
way]{.underline}?

He is the more likable in patience who happily and willingly takes upon
himself the evil and adversity that comes upon him from Ahrimen and the
demons and evil (people), and [in no way]{.underline} harms his soul"
(*MX*.38.18, 31-32)

*ān brādar u-š [pad anīy rāh]{.underline} sazāgīhā ēw ast ēnyā ān guftan
rāy stūrīh xwēštar bawēd*

"unless (*\... ēnyā*) there is that (one) brother who, [in some other
way]{.underline}, is (more) suitably (appointed) than him, because of
what was said, the *stūrīh* belongs more to that brother" (*RAF*.70.2)

##### *pad rāh ī* "by way of, through":

*gōwēd kū Wahuman weh ī amāwand ī āštīh-dādār \... u-š amāwandīh ēd kū
gund ī yazdān ud ān-iz ī ērān ka āštīh kunēnd bē abzāyēnd [pad rāh ī
Wahuman]{.underline} ka-šān andar mayān šawēd*

"one says: Wahuman the good, powerful, peace-giver; \... and his being
'powerful' is this: when the gods' army and that of the Iranians make
peace (and) increase it, (it is) [by way of Wahuman]{.underline}, when
he goes among them" (*Bd*.26.13-15)

*az Abestāg paydāg kū rist-āxēz tan ī pasēn kerdan ud a-margīh winnārdan
[pad rāh ī āštīh]{.underline} šāyēd būd*

"from the Avesta it is manifest that the resurrection, the making of the
Final Body, and the establishing of deathlessness can come about [by way
of peace]{.underline}" (*PR*.62.14)

*ka rad dastwar pad rad dastwar nē dārēd šāyēd ēg-iš kerbag ī kunēd [pad
rāh ī a-srōš-dārīh]{.underline} pad mēnōyān ō frayād nē rasēd*

"when (someone thinks it is) OK when one does not regard a *rad* and
*dastwar* as *rad* and *dastwar*, then (any) good deed that he performs,
[by way of]{.underline} (= because of his) [disobedience]{.underline},
does not come to his (*-iš*) aid in the other world" (*REA*.17.32)

###  EXPRESSIONS with *dar* "issue; kind, category; respect, way"

These usages may have developed from the use of *dar* "door" to indicate
section of a text, as used in *Dk*.8: *u čē andar ham dar* "and anything
(else) in the same section":

*Zarduxšt [abar ān dar]{.underline} az Ohrmazd pursīd*

"Zarathustra asked Ohrmazd about [that issue]{.underline}" (*ŠnŠ*.12.29)

*hagriz ēč anāgīh ō man nē mad kē-m [pad 6 dar]{.underline} rāmišn az-iš
nē padīrift*

"no misfortune has ever befallen me, from which I have not received
happiness [in six respects/ways]{.underline}" (*Dk*.6A.5)

*dastwar guft kū anōšag bēd Ardaxšīr xwarrah ī kayān awiš rasīd pad ēč
čārag griftan nē tuwān \...*

*čārag ī Ardaxšīr [az ān dar]{.underline} xwāhēd*

"the dastwar said (to Ardawān): May you (plur. maj.) be immortal! The
Xwarrah of the *kay*s has reached Ardaxšīr; in no way can he be caught!
\... Seek [another way]{.underline} of (catching him)!" (*KN*.4.24/3.20)

*awēšān kē-šān Abestāg wēš warm ayāb ōy kē zand šāyist nē šāyist weh
dānēd ud kehīh ud mehīh ī [pad ēn dar]{.underline} \...*

"those who have the Avesta more (learned) by heart (*warm*) or he who
knows the *zand* (and) 'what is appropriate (and) not appropriate'
better and what is less and greater [in this respect]{.underline} \..."
(*DD*.46.4)

*[az-iz ēd dar]{.underline} pōryōtkēšān pēšīy xēm wirāstan pasīy xrad
pursīdan čāšīdan*

"and that, for this reason, the teachers of old taught that one should
first cultivate one's character, afterward consult one's wisdom"
(*Dk*.3.113.6)

*ud tar-menišnīh ī dēn abāz-stāyišnīh az-iš ud nē dāštan ī dastwar
xwad-dōšagīhā raft abārīg (ī) [andar ham dar]{.underline}*

"and scorning the *dēn* and 'back-praising' (oneself) from it, and not
having a *dastwar*, and behaving obstinately, and the other (things) [in
that category]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.9.5)

*[pad harw dar]{.underline} andar yazdān spāsdār ham*

"I am thankful to the gods [in every respect]{.underline}" (*NM*.2.1.1)

*[pad harw dar ēw]{.underline} ka sag ōh nimāyišn xūbtar*

"[in each and every respect]{.underline} (in any case?), it is better
when the dog is shown in the usual way" (*RAF*.32.2)

*u-š [pad hamāg dar]{.underline} čē az tōzišn kerdan ī wināh ī pidar ud
kerbag ī ruwān-iz pidar rāy ka wināh ud ērang ud abām ī pidar bē wizārēd
weh kū pad ruwān ī pidar yazišn ud myazd ud anīy kerbag kunēd*

"and, [in all respects]{.underline}, what is regarding (*rāy*) atoning
for one's father's sins and the good deeds also for the father's soul,
when one resolves (atones for) one's father's sins, guilt, and debts, it
is better to perform services for the father's soul, (offer up) *myazd*,
and do other good deeds" (*RAF*.141.3)

*(Srid) ō Kāy-Us [pad was dar]{.underline} frayādišnīg*

"(Srid) was helpful to Kāy-Us [in many respects]{.underline}"
(*WZ*.4.13)

### Expressions with *rang* "color; kind, way"

*ān-iz ī wahārān ārōyišn ī bāmīg wāstar ud urwar [was-gōnag ī
was-rang]{.underline}*

"and the splendid growth in spring, grass and plants [of many sorts and
colors]{.underline}" (*StS*.5.4)

*ud andar-iz pahikār pursišn ī ēk-wizārišn ān ī was-wizārišn
[was-rang]{.underline} bē šnāxtan*

"and, also, (when) in a discussion, to recognize a question that has one
explanation (and) that which has many [variegated]{.underline}
explanations" (*Dk*.4.10.22)

*ōh-iz ān ī ōwōn zofrīhā saxwan ud ēwēn rāstīhā ud
[a-wašt-rangīhā]{.underline} abespārdan šāyistan*

"and that thus (i.e., by learning the *dēn* by heart) it is possible to
transmit words of such deep (meaning) as well as rituals correctly and
[in no way changed]{.underline} (lit. so that their 'colors' remain
unchanged')" (*Dk*.5.24.13)

### EXPRESSIONS with *mar* "number, count; kind, way"

*harw pēšag-ēw ī mardōmān mēnōy-ēw xwēš, gyān harw rōšnīh abāg gyān ōš
bōy abārīg ī [az ēn mar]{.underline} Ohrmazd xwēš*

"every single bodypart of humans belongs to one entity in the other
world: the soul (is) all light (and) together with the soul (!), memory,
conscience, (and) the others [of (in) this number]{.underline} belong to
Ohrmazd" (*Bd*.28.22)

*Ahrimen ī druwand u-š dēwān ud wišūdagān abāg Ohrmazd ud amahrspandān
tis-iz āštīh ud dōšāram ēk abāg did būd šāyēd ayāb nē \... [pad ēč
mar-iz]{.underline} būd [nē]{.underline} šāyēd*

"(it possible) that there will be any peace and love one for the other:
the wicked Ahrimen and his demons and abortions for Ohrmazd and the
amahrspands? --- it is [in no way]{.underline} possible that there will
be" (*MX*.9.1-4)

17.3. Translate into Pahlavi and write in Pahlavi script with
transliteration and transcription:

1.  Do not do battle with a greedy man, and do not harm him in any way!

2.  How is the mixing of water into the earth and in what manner? -- The
    mixing of water into the earth is just like the blood in the body of
    men.

3.  Ohrmazd created Jam, Frēdōn, and Kāy-Us immortal, and thus he turned
    Ahrimen (back), as is well known, and in such a way turned it into a
    greater benefit as that which is manifest.

4.  Do not practice greedy desire so that the demon Greed deceives you
    and the matter of this world becomes tasteless and that of the other
    world is destroyed!

5.  Can one, by diligence, make one's own the goodness that has not been
    allotted or not? -- One cannot, by diligence, make one's own the
    goodness that has not been allotted, but that which has been
    allotted comes sooner because of diligence.

6.  They also held that a small good deed is the cover \[sth. which
    hides\] of a bad deed, for a thick bad deed that is done is less
    manifest because of a small good deed.

7.  Four things are essential, but one in particular is very essential:
    to be a pupil, for those other (thing)s too are known by being a
    pupil.

8.  During the first creation, when Ohrmazd fashioned the Ahunwar from
    the endless light, then the *dēn* was 'created' together with the
    creation.

9.  That good deed that the departed ordered in life is propagated after
    his passing and becomes something that makes him happy in paradise.

# Lesson 18

## Grammar 18

## The Verb. The past stem = past participle = short infinitive

#### Past participle/short infinitive as noun

The past participle/short infinitive can be used as a noun and often to
refer to a preceding action expressed by the same word. It is often used
like English "\...-ing" e.g.:

*ka Garišasp kār mardōm [ōzad]{.underline} būd čē rāy nazdist rist ān ī
ōy kunēnd*

"when (= since) Garišasp's work was [killing]{.underline} people, why
will they do (= raise) his dead body first?" (*PR*.18f.35)

*ud [abar pād]{.underline} ī-š gōspand ī az wāstar kasān ud wināh tōzišn
(ī) [az nē pād]{.underline}*

"and [about keeping]{.underline} one's cattle from (other) people's
grass and the payment for the sin of [not keeping]{.underline} (them)"
(*Dk*.8.23.9)

*mard ēw kē abāg mard ēw ēk abāg did [ǰang kunēnd]{.underline} ān ī jang
kunēd [andar ān ǰang-kerd]{.underline} ōy ī did pad dandān gīrēd*

"two men who [fight]{.underline} with each other; the aggressor [in that
fight]{.underline} grabs the other with the teeth \..." (*RAF*.56.1)

*\[\...\] \... ān mard [az ān zad]{.underline}* \<MHYTNt\'\> *\... murd
būd*

"\[if a man [is struck]{.underline}\] (and the pain does not subside
within 3 or 7 days and) that man has died [from that
striking]{.underline} \..." (*MHD*.F.2)

*[pad guft]{.underline} ī dastwarān ōwōn nibišt kū*

"[according to the saying]{.underline} of the *dastwar*s it is thus
written: \..." (*MHD*.25.6)

*ud pad-iz abārīg was čim zīndag-gōwišnīg saxwan az ān ī [pad
nibišt]{.underline} mādagwartar hangārdan čimīg*

"and it is logical that also in other matters the word from the living
speech should be regarded as more essential than that [in
writing]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.24.13)

*ka pid duxt ī abornāy pad zanīh bē [dahēd]{.underline} duxt agar \...
[pad ān dād]{.underline}* \<YHBWNt\'\> *a-hunsand* \...

"if a father [gives]{.underline} away a minor daughter in wifehood, if
the daughter (once adult) is not happy (does not agree) [with that
giving]{.underline} \... (*MHD*.E.9)

*ka mard zan kē sālār ī pad nāmčišt ud stūrīh ī kas nēst
[gād]{.underline} ud [pad ān gād]{.underline} frazend zāyēd*

"if a man [has had intercourse]{.underline} with a woman who has no
specific guardian and is not the *stūr* of anybody and (if) a child is
born [from that intercourse]{.underline} \..." (*MHD*.30.3)

*ka Farrox abāg Mihrēn paymān kunēd kū agar ō Kuwār [šawam]{.underline}
ēnyā dram 50 bē daham [pad šud]{.underline} Farrox paydāgēnišn*

"if Farrox makes an agreement with Mihrēn that 'unless [I
go]{.underline} to Kuwār, I shall give (you) 50 drahms,' (then) Farrox
has to inform (him) of [(his)]{.underline} going" (*MHDA*.5.18)

##### The long infinitive used in the same function:

*weh-dēn mard kē zan ī ag-dēn [gād]{.underline} [az ham
gādan]{.underline} ābustan bawēd ēg-iš frazend ag-dēnān dādan rāy
zamānīg tanābuhl ēw wināh*

"a man of the Good Dēn who [has had intercourse]{.underline} with a
woman from an evil Dēn (and) she becomes pregnant [from said
intercourse]{.underline}, then (s)he incurs a sin of an immediate
*tanābuhl* for giving a/the child to those of evil Dēn" (*REA*.42.2)

#### 'Absolute' constructions

These can be characterized as verbless clauses meaning "while sth.
happens, once sth. has happened" and are similar to the Latin absolute
ablative and the Sanskrit absolute locative, cf. Eng. *all things
considered*.

##### Adjective plus noun:

*[zīndag pidar]{.underline}* "while the father is alive" (*RAF*.62.2)

##### Past participle plus prepositional phrase:

*ud [mad ō pornāyīh]{.underline} pēšagān wizīnēd*

"and, [(once) having come of age]{.underline}, (the child) chooses a
trade" (*WZ*.31.1)

*[mad ō 9-sālag]{.underline} frāz raft abar ān ī ōy zanišn*

"[(once) having come to the age of nine]{.underline}, (Frēdōn) went
forth (bent) upon his smiting (= smiting him = Dahāg) (*Dk*.7.1.26)

##### Past participle plus noun or pronoun:

This construction is quite common (cf. the compounds in Lesson 16).

It is identical with a *ka-*clause with fronted verb, but without *ka*,
cf.:

*[ka kand xwēd]{.underline} pāk* \> *[kand xwēd]{.underline} pāk* "[when
the wet (part) has been eliminated]{.underline} (it is) clean"
(*PV*.16.2)

Examples:

*uzīd ān zamān*

"once that time has passed" (*MHD*.E.1)

*ēdōn druwand ruwān [frōd murd tan]{.underline}*

"thus (also) the soul of the Wicked, [once the body has
died]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.108.13)

*ud pad-iz ān hamīh ī frawahr waxšōmand \*bōy [widerd tan]{.underline}
abāg ahlaw ruwān*

"and also by that togetherness (= by being together) with the *frawahr*,
which contains the growth, the consciousness (*bōy*), [once the body has
passed on]{.underline}, (is) together with the soul of the Righteous
one" (*Dk*.3.123.38)

*hērbedān hāwištān būd hēnd pad hammōxtan ī az xwēš hērbed hāwišt-iz
[hammōxt dānišn]{.underline} hērbed bawēd abāg hammōxtār andar ēk tan
bawēd*

"the *hērbed*s have been students by learning from their own *hērbed*,
and the student, as well, [once (they) have been taught/learned the
knowledge]{.underline} (Avesta and Zand), becomes a *hērbed*: he will be
in one body together with the teacher" (*DD*.44.3)

*pad ān ī škefttar dard bēš [bē ōzad tan]{.underline} ruwān wišād ō ul
ahrāmādan \... abāg ahlawān āsānīhād ud šnāyīhād pad ān abardom āsānīh
šnāyišn*

"[once the body is slain]{.underline} by that very harsh pain (and)
harm, the soul, (now) released for rising up \..., will be made relaxed
and pleasured in that highest rest and pleasure" (*Dk*.3.358)

*u-š pad abardomīh ī ham srišwadag estēnīd rōšn Xwar ud bāmīg Māh ud
xwarrahōmandān starān u-š payrāst kū [mad petyārag]{.underline} wāzēnd
ud gardēnd pērāmōn ī dām*

"and in the uppermost of said third, he set in place the bright Sun, the
shiny Moon, and the Xwarrah-filled stars, and he aranged (it) so that,
[once the Adversary had come]{.underline}, they would fly (above) and
turn around the creation" (*DD*.36.21-22)

*u-šān [kerd kām]{.underline} ī dādār fragānēnīd was kār ī gēhān-sūd*

"and, [having performed]{.underline} the Creator's [wish]{.underline},
they (= M&M) laid the foundation for many actions benefiting the world
of the living" (*Dk*.7.1.10)

*abar duxt kē [a-kerd šōy]{.underline} kē nē pid ud nē mād ud nē-iz
[widurd pidarān]{.underline} ā-iz az brādarān pad šōy ud nē-iz xwēš tan
pad sālārīh bē dād pādixšāy*

"about a daughter who, [having not yet married]{.underline}, who has
neither father nor mother, and [her grandparents (?) having not yet
passed on]{.underline}, then it is authorized (that she be given) by
(her) brothers to a husband, but it is in no way (authorized for her) to
give herself in guardianship (to somebody) (*Dk*.8.43.11)

*pad zōdīh ī Sōšāns ud hamīh ī 6'ān hamān fraškerd-kerdārān ul-uzišnīh ī
wispān rōšn-tōhmagān rāy yašt ī fraškerd-kerdārīh frāz srāyēnd*

*[kerd yašt]{.underline} \... abar xwānēd Sōšāns kū* *ul estēd tanōmand
hēd*

"with Sōšāns as *zōd* (chief priest) and together with (*pad hamīh ī*)
the same six Renovation-makers recite the Renovation-making ritual for
the rising up of all those of the seed of light;

[having performed the ritual]{.underline} \... Sōšāns calls out: Arise!
You have bodies!" (*WZ*.35.19-20)

*[widerd man]{.underline} xwāstag ī man xwēš tō xwēš*

"[once I have passed on]{.underline}, the property that is mine will be
yours" (*MHD*.J.9)

With preverb:

*[abar nīd]{.underline} Spitāmān Zardušt [sag]{.underline} zard 4-čašm
ayāb spēd zard-gōš*

*ān druz ī Nasuš abāz dwārēd ō abāxtar nēmag*

"Sp. Z., once a yellow dog with four eyes or white with yellow ears has
been led to (the dead body),

(then) that *druz*, the Nasuš, runs back to the northern direction"
(PV.8.16cd)

##### In adverbial phrases:

*widārd-garāntom-aweštābīhā*

"having suffered the heaviest oppression" (*Dk*.5.24.9)

⇽ *widārd aweštāb* "having suffered oppression"

##### With verb + *-iz* "even when \...":

*abornāyīg [murd-iz pid]{.underline} dūdagīh ōwōn čiyōn nūn-iz čē-š
tis-iz tis juttar bē nē bawēd*

"the family (situation of) an under-age child, [even]{.underline} (when)
[the father is dead]{.underline}, (remains) just as it is now, for none
of it becomes at all different" (*MHD*.37.42)

##### Noun plus past participle:

These have sentence syntax, but are rare:

*ēk-bar [sag ō dast grift]{.underline} baršnūmgar ēn gōwišn frāz gōwišn*

"[once]{.underline} the man who carried a *nasāy* alone [has taken the
dog by his hand]{.underline}, the person administering the *baršnūm*
should say forth the following utterance: \..." (*ZFJ*.627)

*sidīgar garzišn ī az ǰeh kē-š pad, [daštān abar rasīd]{.underline},
gand ud rēm ī az daštān aw-iš rasēnīdan ud xīndagīh ud stardīh ī az-iš*

"the third complaint (by the fire) is about the evil woman who, [once
the menses have come upon]{.underline} her, for (*pad*) causing foul
smell and filth from the menstruation to come upon it (the fire) and how
it becomes sick and faint from it" (*Dk*.9.11.5)

*pad ōy frazend bawēd (ī) [pas az wināh kerd]{.underline} zāyēd*

"(the penalty for breaking an oath) is with that child that is born
[after the sin was committed]{.underline}" (*PV*.4.10D)

## The nouns in *-īh* 

As we have seen, the derived abstract nouns in *-īh* are extremely
versatile. Here are some more examples.

#### "Being something, the fact that something is"

*ō [laškarīgīh]{.underline} ud [spāhīgīh]{.underline} šudan*

"to go [to be an army soldier]{.underline} (*laškar*, *spāh*)"
(*REA*.11.1)

*abar tuwān (ī) harw kas pad bōxtan ī az [druwandīh]{.underline} ud
xwēšēnīdan [ahlawīh]{.underline}*

"about every person's ability to be saved from be(com)ing *druwand* and
appropriate (make one's own) be(com)ing *ahlaw*" (*Dk*.3.339.1) -- Note
that *ahlawīh* means being one of the *ahlaw*s; here it probably refers
to after death, when the *druwand*s are separated from the *ahlaw*s.

*burzāwand Kay-Wištāsp čiyōn az dēn abar [bawēdīh]{.underline} ī andar
ān hangām ēd abdīh āgāh būd \...*

"when the exalted Kay-Wištāsp became aware from the *dēn* of [the fact
that]{.underline} this miracle [was to be]{.underline} (= happen) at
that time \..." (*Dk*.7.6.4)

*wēš-awiš-[madārīh]{.underline} ī xrad rāy*

"because of the fact that wisdom [comes to (them) more]{.underline}
(often)" (*MX*.56.20)

⇽ *ēd rāy čē xrad wēš awiš mad* "because wisdom came to (them) more
(often)"

*Kay-Wištāsp abar [bawēdīh]{.underline} ī andar ān hangām ēd abdīh āgāh
būd*

"Kay Wištāsp was made aware of [the fact that this miracle would
be]{.underline} (happen) in that time" (after *Dk*.7.6.4)

⇽ *ēd abdīh andar ān hangām bawēd* "this miracle will be in that time"

#### 'Quotational' *-īh*

One common usage, especially frequent in exegetical texts, is that of
'quoting' a word to explain it.

*pad [waxšwarīh]{.underline} wābarīhist hēnd*

"they were recognized as 'prophets'" (*Dk*.7.1.3)

⇽ *wābarīhist kū waxšwar hend* "it was recognized that: they are
'prophets'"

*u-m [mardōmīh]{.underline} az Mahrīy ud Mahriyānīy*

"and my [humanity]{.underline} (the fact that I am *mardōm*) is from
Mahrīy and Mahriyānīy' (*PN*.2)

⇽ *mardōm ham* "I am a human"

*ud ka pad [nasāyīh]{.underline} warōmand*

"when there is doubt with regard to [its being '*nasāy*']{.underline}"
(*ZFJ*, p. 546)

⇽ *warōmand kū nasāy ayāb nē* "it is in doubt whether it is a *nasāy* or
not"

*kē-š handām ī tarr abar rasīd [hixrōmandīh]{.underline} kē-š ān ī hušk
abar rasīd ēdōn čiyōn wars nāxun ī hušk ka bē āb bē šōyēd pāk*

"(a place) which a moist bodypart has come upon, (should be regarded as)
[being 'containing *hixr*']{.underline}; that which a dry (bodypart) has
come upon, such as dry hair, nails, when one washes with water, (it
becomes) clean" (*ZFJ*, p. 546)

⇽ *pad ēd dārišn kū hixrōmand* "it should be regarded as 'containing
*hixr*'"

*u-m warzišn ud xwēškārīh ud frēzwānīh ēn kū Ohrmazd pad [astīh
hamē-būdīh hamē-bawēdīh ud anōšag-xwadāyīh ud akanāragīh ud
abēzagīh]{.underline}. Ahrimen pad [nēstīh ud wanī-būdīh]{.underline}
menīdan*

"what I have to do and my duty is this: to think about Ohrmazd as
(*pad*) [being, always having been, and always going to be, as having
undying kingship, being unlimited, and being pure]{.underline}, (but)
Ahrimen [as not being and as being destroyed]{.underline}" (*PN*.3)

⇽ *Ohrmazd ast hamē būd ud hamē bawēd u-š xwadāyīh anōšag ud akanārag ud
abēzag* "Ohrmzd is, always was, and always will be, and his kingship is
immortal, limitless, and pure"

#### Groups of people

The suffix *-īh* is also used to denote religious or social groups:

*āzādīh ud wazurgīh ud dahīgānīh*

"the freeborn, the grandees, and the land-owners" (*ZWY*.4.7)

*druzīh az druz ō ohrmazd dahišn kōšišnīg mad estēd*

"[the lie-demons]{.underline} came from the Lie for the purpose of
battling Ohrmazd's creatures" (*Dk*.3.167.2)

*tōxt dušmad dušhūxt dušhuwaršt abāg frayādāg ud rāmēnāg mēnōy ī xwēš
humad hūxt huwaršt bē ō garōdmān ayāb ō wahišt ayāb ō hamēstagān ī
ahlawān ānōh kū-š andar [ahlawīh]{.underline} gāh ast awiš franāmēd*

"once one has expiated one's evil thoughts, etc., one proceeds together
with the helping and pleasing spirit of his good thoughts, etc., to
Garōdmān, the Best (Existence), the Intermediary place of the Righteous,
to where one's place is in [the community of the Righteous]{.underline}"
(*DD*.23.6)

*čihrōmēhan ī ahlaw abāg wazr ī pērōzgar abāg 53 mardān raft ī hāwištān
ī amāwand ī buland \... ī sīžd-sneh kū-šān dēw ud [wattarīh]{.underline}
aziš tarsēnd*

"Č. the Righteous, with the victorious cudgel, went with 53 men, (his)
students, tall and mighty \... with fearful weapons, i.e., the demons
and [all the bad ones]{.underline} fear them" (*Dk*.7.8.45--66)

## Phraseology 2

## Expressions of similarity

In addition to phrases with *čiyōn* expressing similarity, there are a
number of other words used in phrases signifying "like, similar to."
Most of these are combined with *ī* and prepositions and, like *ēwēnag*
(Lesson 17), can be combined with *ēn*, *ān*, *ham-* and *ōwōn* and
*čiyōn* and can be used as adverbs in *-īhā*.

> *handāzag* WKcåDwA \<hnd'ck\'\> "(same) measure, etc; like manner"
>
> *hangōšīdag* WKtdÍwYwA \<hngwšytk\'\> "like manner"
>
> *mānāg* WkAwa˜ \<m'n'k\'\> "like"
>
> *homānāg* WkAwa˜wA , WkAwaÂA \<h(w)m'n'k\> "like"

### *handāzag* "measure, amount" 

As a noun, this means "measure, amount, same measure/amount, degree,
extent; same/like manner, like manner," but is also used in the sense of
"analogue, example, similar, comparable (to)." The derived noun
*handāzagīh* means "similarity, analogy."

##### As noun:

*harw ān kē ō dōšox ōbast ēg-iš andar dōšox pādifrāh [pad ān
handāzag]{.underline} bawēd [kē]{.underline}-š wināh kerd estēd*

"everyone who has fallen into hell, then, in hell, his punishment will
be [in that measure/amount]{.underline} (to) which he has committed
sins" (*REA*.39.26)

*ka sidōš bē mānēd ōy kē pad nē yaštan wināhgār ā-š tōzišn ērang
[handāzag čiyōn]{.underline} ān ī gāhānbār nē yaštan*

"when the *sidōš* (ritual) remains (unperformed), (then) he who is
guilty of not performing the ritual, his atonement and guilt (are) [the
same amount as]{.underline} for not performing the *gāhānbār* ritual"
(*RAF*.144.2)

*ēg awēšān druzān, ham-čiyōn sag ayab way frāz ō nasāy nigerēnd, ān gāh
dāštan nē šāyēd ōšmārēnd bē ō wizandišn ud wihēzišn estēnd;*

*ud az mehmānīh ī-šān padiš bahrag bē kāhēd ud [ham
handāzag]{.underline} ān nasuš nizārīhēd*

"then, they figure (*ōšmārēnd*) (that), as soon as the dogs or birds
look at the corpse, those lie-demons cannot hold on to (their) place
(inside the carcass and) begin to tremble and move about;

and their share diminishes from their lodging in it, and that carcass
demon is weakened [to the same degree]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.24.28a)

*u-š [ham-handāzag]{.underline} ī zōr ud nērōg ī-šān az ān ī ōy wināh
ǰād ān tā bē ō fraškerd zamān an-āsānīhā dardēnēnd ud bēšēnēnd ud pad ān
ī Wizarš nīdārīh a-kāmagīhā āyēd bē ō dōšox*

"and (the demons), giving him no respite (*an-āsānīhā*), cause him pain
and harm [to the same extent]{.underline} as (= in proportion to) the
strength and power that is their share from that sin of his until the
time of the Renovation,

and led by (*pad \... nīdārīh* \< *nay-*) (the demon) Drag-off, against
his will, he comes to hell" (*DD*.31.5)

*kerbag-iz [pad-ham-handāzagīhā]{.underline} kunīhēd*

"and good deeds are performed [to the same amount]{.underline}"
(*FO*.25b.706)

\[\< *pad ham handāzag* "to the same amount\]

*ud ka abāyišn wārēnēd ud [abāyišn-handāzagīhā]{.underline} sūd-abgārīhā
abar gyāgān rōdestāgān baxšēd*

"and when it is needed, (the wind) makes it rain, and it distributes
(the rain) over the places and districts [in the needed
amount]{.underline}, (thereby) providing benefit (for them)" (*DD*.92.5)

##### In comparisons:

In comparisons, *handāzag* can take the particle *ī* *(ī)*, an enclitic
pronoun, and often the preposition *pad*.

It can be combined with demonstrative pronouns, *čiyōn*, and *ham-*
"same."

*ud abārīg-iz ēk ēk kār ī gēhān pad uzmāyišn [handāzag ān]{.underline} ī
bizišk rāy nibišt*

"and also the other individual actions of the world (are to be put) to
the test, [just as that]{.underline} which was written about the doctor"
(*Dk*.3.229.6)

*u-š xwarišn [pad handāzag ī ān]{.underline} ī andar gētīy gandagtom
pūdagtom rēmantom ud a-xwašīhtom*

"and its (the soul of the wicked) food is [just like that]{.underline}
which is the most foul, rotten, filthy, and unpleasant in this world"
(*DD*.31.6)

*sahīg kamar nigerēnd ud sēnag stabr mānēnd kū-[mān]{.underline} nēst
kas [handāzag]{.underline}*

"the worthy look at (their) *kamar* \[kind of belt or collar, sign of
distinction\] and remain with their chest thick (= puffed out?)
(thinking:) no one is [like us]{.underline}!" (*PT*.37.20: *Abar Xēm ud
Xrad ī Farrox Mard*)

*dānāgīh ān ī pad nērōg ī dānāg čiyōn wēnāgīh ān ī pad nērōg ī wēnāg
čašm;*

*u-[š handāzag ēd-iz ī]{.underline} xwāstagōmand, ud xwāstag ān ī
xwāstagōmand padiš xwāstagōmand bawēd*

"knowledge is what is in the power of the knowledgeable man, just as
ability to see is what is in the power of the eye, which is seeing;

and [its comparandum/analogy is this too]{.underline}: someone
possessing property; and property is that whereby (*ī \... padiš*)
someone possessing property comes to possess property" (*Dk*.3.253.3)

*u-š ān pādifrāh az druz mēnōy ī xwēš wināh [pad ān ēwēnag ud
handāzag]{.underline} abar rasēd ī-š \*āzārd ud bēšīd*

"and that punishment comes upon him from the Lie in the other world,
which is his own sin, [in that (same) manner and
measure/amount]{.underline} as he (himself) harmed and hurt (things)"
(*DD*.31.9)

*wašt-gōhrīh ī az wattarīh [az ān handāzag ī]{.underline} zandīg (ī)
abar gyān zēfān gōwēd kū*

*agar wināh kunē ēg-iš gōhr wašt bawē abar guft bawēd*

"(the soul's) substance being changed from (= because of) evilness [is
analogous to what]{.underline} is ascribed to (*abar guft bawēd*) the
Zandīg (= Manichean) who maliciously (*zēfān*) says about the soul: if
you commit a sin, then its substance would be (opt.) changed"
(*Dk*.3.272.10)

*ka ān spurrgar frēstag ī ast Sōšāns parwānag ud Ērman pad zamīg paydāg
bawēd [pad ham-handāzagīh]{.underline} pad 30-sālag bē ō mēnōyān
ham-pursēd*

"when that messenger who will make all complete, that is Sōšāns the
guide, and Ērman appears (sing.) on earth, (S.) will, at the age of
thirty, [in the same manner]{.underline} (as his two brothers), converse
with the divine beings" (*WZ*.34.48)

*ēd-iz rāy čē mard dānāgīh pad ēn 2 rāh waxšēnēd ayāb xwad gōwēd ud
hammōzēd ayāb bahr ud ābādīh ō dānāgān [handāzagēnēd]{.underline} kē
guftār ud hammōxtār bawēnd ī dānāgīh*

'because a man increases knowledge in the following two ways: either he
speaks it himself and teaches (it) or he [compares]{.underline} (its)
share and prosperity (advantage, gain?) to the knowledgeable ones who
speak and teach knowledge" (*Dk*.9.53.9)

### *hangōšīdag* "like manner" 

This alone or with *pad* and/or *ī* also functions as a pre/postposition
meaning "like."

It can be combined with demonstrative pronouns, *(ōwōn) čiyōn*, and
*ham-* "same," as well as with other words of similar meaning.

*mardōm-iz [pad hangōšīdag]{.underline} kustīg pad mayān dārēnd*

"[similarly]{.underline}, too, people have the *kustīg* around their
waist" (*Bd*.28.15b)

*nūn-iz mardōm andar gētīy [pad ēn hangōšīdag]{.underline} mīrēnd*

"people in the living world, now too (= still) die [just like
this]{.underline}" (*Bd*.7.12a)

*nūn-iz [pad ān hangōšīdag]{.underline} draxt ul rust estēd*

"now, too, trees have grown up [just like that]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.14.10)

*pad asmān [ham-hangōšīdag]{.underline} az abāxtarān tīr xwarāsān
spāhbed*

"in the sky (in the heavens), [likewise]{.underline}, of the planets,
Tīr is the general of the East" (*Bd.*5A.4)

*ud abar [an-hangōšīdagīh]{.underline} ī Zardušt pad-iz wasīh ī kerbag*

"and about [there being no one similar]{.underline} to Zardušt also in
terms of the large number of (his) good deeds" (*Dk*.9.43.10)

*abar rāstīh ī-mān ud ērangīh ī hambedig-gōwišnān kū*

*ka-iz ān ī az warz-kerdīh ud xwarrah-kārīh ud amahrspandān
gugāy-abāgīh*

*ud abārīg ān-ēwēnag abd ud [bē az hangōšīdag]{.underline} paydāg
rāyēnišnīh ī pad ahlaw Zarduxšt*

"about our truth and the heresy of those who say against (us):

also when (\~ the fact that) what was made manifest from wonders being
performed and activities through Xwarrah and the accompanying testimony
of the *amahrspand*s

and the other wondrous and [matchless/incomparable]{.underline} (things)
of that kind which were arranged (*rāyēnišnīh*) by Righteous Zarduxšt"
(*Dk*.5.22.2)

*stāyišn ī paristišn ast ī \*wāspuhragānīhā dādār xwēš pad dahišnān nē
sazēd*

*čiyōn stāyišn ī dādār pad mēnōyān mēnōyīh ud wisp-āgāhīh ud
wisp-tuwān(īh) ud wisp-xwadāyīh ud hammist ī-š
[hangōšīdagīhā]{.underline} xwēš*

"some (*ast ī*) praise and service belong especially to the Creator
(and) is not suited for (His) creatures,

since the praise of the Creator (is) for being a *mēnōy* among *mēnōy*s
and all-aware and omnipotent and the lord of all and everything
(*hammist*), which [similarly]{.underline} belongs to him"
(*Dk*.3.241.2)

[With a subordinate clause]{.underline}:

*[hangōšīdag ī ka]{.underline} hu-fraward pidar-imān az astōmand axwān
ēwarzīd*

"[Like when]{.underline} our blessed father traveled from this bony
world" (*NM*.2.1.5)

##### With *čiyōn*:

*[čiyōn ān-iz hangōšīdag]{.underline} ī andar dēn gōwēd*

"[just like that too]{.underline} which it says in the Dēn" (*NM*.1.2.3)

*[ōwōn čiyōn]{.underline} rēšag ī draxtān andar zamīg widerēd
[hangōšīdag]{.underline}, xōn ī andar rahagān kē zōr ō hamāg tan dahēd*

"[just like]{.underline} the roots of trees pass through the earth, (so
also does) the blood in the veins, which gives strength to the entire
body" (*Bd*.6C.4)

*nē weh az ān kunišn warzēd [pad hangōšīdag čiyōn ka]{.underline}-š mard
ī ahlaw \... stūrīh abar škast hē*

"he does no better act (than) [like if]{.underline} he were to break the
*stūrīh* ('proxy' marriage) of a Righteous man" (*Purs*.75.6; one of the
worst sins ever, since it deprives a man who died without an heir of the
possibility of acquiring one)

##### With *handāzag*:

*frēzwānīg ud afrēzwānīg-iz kerbag-warzīdārīh kē dānāgān was [hangōšīdag
handāzag ī]{.underline} pad ahlāyīh-warzīdārīh abāyišnīg aziš āwurd*

"the performance of good deeds (that are) obligatory and non-obligatory
duties, from the knowledgeable ones have brought out many [similar
similes]{.underline} as needed (*abāyišnīg*) for performing
Righteousness" (*REA*.17.25)

*abārīg az [ham-nimūnag ud handāzag hangōšīdag]{.underline} kerdan
dāštan čimīgīhā*

"doing and keeping (all) the other things [of the same type and of
similar sort in the same way]{.underline} (as those mentioned) makes
sense (*čimīgīhā*)" (*DD*.47.41)

### *mānāg* "resembling, similar to, like " 

This is the "present participle" in *-āg* of *mān-* "to resemble," also
used as a pre- or postposition. It very rarely takes the preposition *ō*
or *ham-* and can be combined with a demonstrative pronoun and *ham*.

##### *mān-*:

*spram-ēw kadām hu-bōytar \... spram-ēw yāsemīn hu-bōytar čē-š bōy [ēdōn
čiyōn]{.underline} bōy ī xwadāyān [mānēd]{.underline}*

"what flower smells the best? \... the jasmine flower smells the best,
for its smell [is just like]{.underline} (resembles just like) the smell
of rulers" (XK.68-69)

##### As adjective:

*u-tān nibišt [ēn mānāg]{.underline} kū ast ī az čāštag-ēw ēwēnag ī nē
šāyēd*

"and what you wrote is [like this]{.underline} that it sometimes is from
a kind of teaching that is not permissible" (*NM*.2.2.4)

*ud [mānāgtar]{.underline} andar pēšēn zamānag būd az hāwištān kē-šān
āgenēn duš-sāzagīh ud hamēmālīh kerd*

"and there was (even) [more similar]{.underline} (cases) in former times
from students who fitted badly together and (constantly) quarreled"
(*DD*.87.12)

##### Pre/postposition:

*kēšdārān was [ēn-mānāg]{.underline} kerd saxwan*

"the holders of (other) faiths, have said much [like this]{.underline}"
(*Dk*.3.240.6)

*guft estēd kū pāsdārīh ēd bawēd kē ēn tan diz [mānāg]{.underline} bē
kerd u-š pās abar frāz kūnēd*

*u-š yazd andar dārēd ud dēw andar awiš nē hilēnd*

"it is said: 'keeping watch' is this: (someone) who has made this body
[like]{.underline} a fortress and appoints a guard over it; and he keeps
the gods inside it, and they do not let the demons into it"
(*Dk*.6E.34a)

*ud ham dēn kustīg-bandišnīh [mānāg xwarrah]{.underline} ī mayān ī
xwarrahān yazdān*

*čē xwad ast pad abāgīh ī ox ud dil kē gyāg ī menišn ud xānag ī gyān*

"and that same/aforementioned tying of the kusti, (i.e.) Dēn, is [like
the Xwarrah]{.underline} among the Xwarrahs of the gods: for it is
itself in company with the mind and heart, which is the place of the
mind and the house of the soul" (*DD*.38.29)

##### With *čiyōn*:

*[mānāg ī ōy čiyōn]{.underline} kē pus ī dōst ī 2-sālag 3-sālag pad
tōšn-dārišnīh barē*

"just like him who were to carry a dear two- or three-year-old son
holding it in a *tōšn* (= ?)" (*Dk*.7.2.34) --- cf.
*[homānāg]{.underline} ī ōy \.... čiyōn* in *PV*.3.42 cited above

##### In compounds:

*ēk ān nam ī \... bārīkīhā ud [dūd-mānāgīhā]{.underline} ud
māzanīg-kerbīhā ul hanǰīhēd*

"one is the moisture that is drawn up (from rivers, etc.) finely
(*bārīkīhā*), [in a way resembling smoke]{.underline}, and taking the
form of giants (?)" (*DD*.92.3)

*gyān ka az tan ī mardōmān frāz stānēnd čiyōn bē šawēd*

*pad ān homānāg guft estēd ī čiyōn ka az ātaxš suxrīh ul uzīhīhēd \...*

*gyān-iz pad atōšagīh andar tan nē estēd ud [ham-mānāg]{.underline} bē
šawēd*

"when they take the soul from peoples' bodies, how does it go?

it is said (to be) just like when redness goes up from the fire (and
when the fire is not fed, it goes out),

the soul too, when not fed, does not stay in the body, but goes away [in
a similar way]{.underline}" (*DD*.22.1-2).

*andar warzišn (ī) daštān-marzīh-iz [az
mānāg-zahāg-sōzišnīh]{.underline} ast gast bīmgen*

"while having intercourse with a menstruant there is a frightening foul
smell [from]{.underline} (something) [like burning a child]{.underline}"
(*DD*.77.4)

##### *mānāgēnīdan/mānāgīhistan* "to liken to, be likened to":

*ōy kē pad čand mardōm [ō yazd mānāgīhistan]{.underline} šāyēd: [yazd
mānāg]{.underline} dānāg xwadāy mard ī ahlaw*

"(as for) he who, to the degree a person can [be likened to a
god]{.underline}: a knowledgeable king (and) Righteous man is [like a
god]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.126.5)

### *homānāg (ō)* "similar (to), like" 

This term, presumably from *ham-mānāg*, is somewhat more frequent than
*mānāg*. It usually takes the preposition *ō*, but sometimes *pad* or
*ī*, is often preceded by *čiyōn*, and is also used as a postposition.
It is often combined with other terms of similarity.

*xīr ī gētīy [ō čē homānāg]{.underline}*

"[what]{.underline} are the matters of this world [like]{.underline} (=
similar to)?" (*AWM*.110)

*abārīg mardōm \... [homānāg]{.underline} hēnd [ō]{.underline} abārīg
stārag ī xwurdag ī pad asmān hēnd*

"the other persons are [just like]{.underline} the other small stars
that are in heaven" (*MYF*.2.61)

##### With *handāzag*:

*[pad ān homānāg čiyōn]{.underline} gētīyān az xwarišn ī urwāzišnīgīh
frazāmīhēnd, ān-iz ruwān mēnōyīg frazāmišn rāmišn
[ham-handāzagīhā]{.underline} awiš rasišnīg, u-š pad nimāyišn ī ō
gētīyān nām Mēdyōzarm rōγn*

"[just like]{.underline} that (the gods' food), when those in this world
are perfected from eating (such) blessedness,

perfection and joy in the other world will also reach that soul (of
theirs) [in the same way]{.underline};

and when it is shown to those in this world it's name is Spring Butter"
(*DD*.30.12)

*pas 2 čašm ī zrēy bē ō zamīg wišāyīhist \... čē [handāzag homānāg
ī]{.underline} čašm ast kē harw gardīh ud harw rēmanīh bē ō kustān
abganēd*

"next, two sources of the ocean were opened up to the earth \... which
are [analogous to the eye]{.underline}, which throws every dusty thing
and every pollution to the sides" (*WZ*.3.24)

##### With *hangōšīdag*:

*ud ēn-iz [hangōšīdag]{.underline} šīr [homānāg]{.underline}*

"and this is [just like]{.underline} milk" (*Bd*.15.11a)

##### With *čiyōn*:

*u-m dīd ruwān ī mard-ēw kē-š dēwān [čiyōn]{.underline} sag
[homānāg]{.underline} hamē darrēnd*

"and I saw the soul of a man whom the demons, [just like]{.underline}
dogs, were tearing apart" (*AWN*.48.1)

*dām ī Ohrmazd pad mēnōyīh ēdōn parward kū tarrīhā estād a-mēnīdār
a-griftār ud a-rawāg [čiyōn]{.underline} šusr [homānāg]{.underline}*

"Ohrmazd's creation was nurtured in the state of *mēnōy* in such a way
that it was moist, unthinking, ungrasping, unmoving, (and) [just
like]{.underline} semen" (*Bd*.1.57)

*mēnōy ud gētīy [ēdōn homānāg čiyōn]{.underline} darbuštīh 2*

"this world and the other world are just like two fortresses"
(*MX*.0.31)

*pas kālbod ī mardōmān [ōwōn homānāg čiyōn]{.underline} draxt-ēw ka
kārēnd ud rōyēd ud abzāyēd ud waxšēd*

*škennēnd ud brīnēnd ud \*wēzēnd ud abar ō ātaxš nihēnd ud ātaxš sōzēd
ud gugārēd ud Wād ī Ardāy andar gēhān parganēd*

"next, people's bodies are [just like]{.underline} a tree when they
plant it and it grows and increases and becomes bigger, (and then) they
break it and cut it in pieces and clean it and place it on the fire, and
the fire burns it and digests it, and the Righteous Wind scatters it
throughout the world" (*PT*.10.4)

*[homānāg]{.underline} ī ōy Spitāmān Zardušt dēn ī mazdēsnān az mard ī
ahlaw frāz mālēd harwisp dušmad ud dušhūxt ud dušhuwaršt
[čiyōn]{.underline} wād-ēw ī škuft-tag ka tēz āyēd ud dašt frāz mālēd ud
kāhīzagīh ud tis-ēw bē bard*

"[in just such a way]{.underline}, Spitāmān Z., does the Mazdayasnian
*dēn* wipe away all bad thoughts, bad words, and bad deeds from the
Righteous man, [as]{.underline} the wind in its fast run---(i.e.) when
it comes quickly---and wipes the plain and carries away straw and
(other) things" (*PV*.3.42)

Here *[homānāg]{.underline} ī ōy \.... čiyōn* renders the Avestan phrase
*mąnaiiən ahe \... yaθa* "just like."

##### Postposition:

*u-š mard (ī) ǰuwān ī 15-sālag [homānāg]{.underline} ō ǰahīy nimūd*

"and he (Ohrmazd) showed the Jahīy a man [like]{.underline} a 15
year-old youth" (*Bd*.4.7)

*u-m dīd ān ī ǰādag-gōwān ud āštīh-xwāhān ruwān \... kē-šān rōšnīh ī
star ud māh ud xwaršēd [homānāg]{.underline} aziš hamē waxšīd*

"and I saw the souls of intercessors and peace-seekers, from whom light
[like]{.underline} (that of) the stars, moon, and sun shone forth"
(*AWN*.15.9)

##### *homānāgīh*:

*brēhēnīd zamīg [pad homānāgīh ī]{.underline} mard-ēw*

"he fashioned the earth [comparable to/in analogy with]{.underline} a
man" (*Bd*.1a.11)

*u-š frawahr ī artēštārān ī ahlawān gurd-asp nēzag dast pērāmōn ī ān
darbuštīh [ōwōn]{.underline} bē gumārd [čiyōn homānāgīh (ī)]{.underline}
mōy abar sar, [hangōšīdag]{.underline} ī awēšān kē darbuštīh pās pāyēnd*

"and he appointed the warrior faravashis of the Orderly, with valiant
horses and spears in the hands, around that fortification (numerous)
[just like]{.underline} (= as many as) the hairs on a head, [like
those]{.underline} who mount the guard of the fortification" (*Bd*.6a.3)

### *hamgenīh* "equality, one and the same"

*dēwīh druzīh harw 2 [hamgenīh]{.underline} ast kē nar ud mādagīh gōwēd*

"being a *dēw* and being a *druz* are both [one and the
same]{.underline}: there is one who says: 'male- and femaleness'"
(*PV*.3.7B)

*gyāg ud rōstāg harw 2 [hamgenīh]{.underline} ast kē ēdōn gōwēd ay gyāg
ān gyāg kū mardōm abar nē mānēnd ud rōstāg ān gyāg kū mardōm abar
mānēnd*

"*gyāg* 'place' and *rōstāg* 'district' are both [one and the
same]{.underline}; there is one who says: the meaning is (*ay*): *gyāg*
is the place where people do not dwell; *rōstāg* is the place where
people do dwell" (*PV*.1.1D)

\[428\]. -- About *xēm* and *xrad*. -- Note the differences between the
mss.

*u-šān ēn-iz ōwōn dāšt kū*

*xēm kē xrad andar nēst ēdōn (ho)mānāg čiyōn xānīg ēw ī rōšn ud anāhōg
kē bast estēd ud ō kār nē hamē šawēd*

*ān xēm kē xrad abāg ōwōn mānāg čiyōn xānīg ēw ī rōšn anāhōg (kē) tuxšāg

###  Text 18.2

From *Dēnkard* book IX: *Dk*.9.53.2. -- Mss. DH, fols. 309r-v.

![](media/image91.jpeg){width="4.777777777777778in" height="2.5in"}

![](media/image92.jpeg){width="4.138888888888889in"
height="0.3611111111111111in"}

*ēn-iz kū kē Ohrmazd pad tan mehmānēnīd ā-š **ahlomōγān**-iz dēn ī
Ohrmazd **rawāg** **kerdan** kerd bawēd*

*ēd-iz rāy čē ahlomōγān ahlomōγīh ī Ahrimen dēn saxtag nē, bē pad
Ohrmazd-dēn-nāmīh rawāg tuwān kerdan*

*ud ahlomōγīh āsrōnīh ud ahlomōγān āsrōnān brādarōdīg hamēstār hēnd*

*ud hamē ka āsrōnīh ud āsrōnān amaragānīhā pērōzīhēnd ahlomōγīh ud
ahlomōγān amaragānīhā **wānīhēnd*** ∵

*ud ka ahlomōγīh ud ahlomōγān amaragānīhā čērīhēnd āsrōnīh ud āsrōnān
amaragānīhā nizārīhēnd*

### Text 18.3

From the *Dēnkard* book IX: *Dk*.9.52.15. -- Mss. DH, f. 309r, B, p.
\[600\].

About god's gifts to men, which are still [owned]{.underline} (*xwēš*)
by god, although they are [in the possession]{.underline} (*dārišn*) of
men, who can profit by their use.

![](media/image93.jpeg){width="6.111111111111111in"
height="1.9305555555555556in"}

![](media/image94.jpeg){width="6.125in" height="2.0416666666666665in"}

*ēn-iz kū kē nēkīh pad xwēšīh ī yazdān dārēd ā-š mardōm, pad mizd
stadan, ō yazdān āyōxt bawēd* ∵

*ēd-iz rāy čē, nēkīh pad xwēšīh ī yazdān dāštan rāy, pad hayārīh ud
šnāyišn ī wehān dārēd u-š mardōm handāzag aziš gīrēnd ud kunēnd u-šān
kerbag (ī) bawēd, pad mizd stadan, ō yazdān āyōzēnd*

"This too: he who holds goodness (that is actually) in the possession of
the gods, he will have 'yoked' men to the gods in order to get a
reward/prize;

and this is because, in order to keep goodness (that is) in the
possession of the gods, by the assistance and approval that good people
hold and from which men take (their) example and act(?), they 'yoke' the
good deed(s) they receive (*-šān \... bawēd*) to the gods in order to
get a reward/prize"

Cf. *PY*.30.10 *ēdōn tēz āyōzēnd ō mizd stad* \...;

*PY*.49.9c *kē pad dēn pahlom āyōzēd mizd kū-š mizd dahēnd*.

### 

### Text 18.4

From the *Mādayān ī hazār dādestān*: *MHD*.40.2-3 (Macuch 1993, chap.
22, f. 55).

![](media/image95.jpeg){width="6.0in" height="3.1944444444444446in"}

*ka gōwēd kū mard 2 pad āgenēn 200 ō man dahišn* \[ms. \<YHBšn\'\>\]
*āgenēn kār ēdōn framūd estēd kū rāst* ∵ o ∵

When (the creditor) says: two men together have to give = pay me 200
(drahm), (then) 'together' has been ordained (by the Mowbed of Mowbeds
to mean) 'equally'.

*ka gōwēd kū mard 2 200 az man abām stad gyāg-ēw nibišt kū mowbedān
mowbed guft kū ham-ēwēn az mard-ēw bē xwāstan pādixšāy čē dārišn āgenēn
barēnd ud {hmn} ham-xwāstag hēnd* ∵ o ∵

When he says: two men borrowed 200 from me, (then) it is written in one
place that the Mowbed of Mowbeds said: (the creditor) is authorized to
request (the debt) in total (?) from *one* man, for they carry 'holding'
together and are co-owners of the property.

*ka gōwēd kū mard 2 az man abām stad pad ēn šōn frāz guft čiyōn ka-šān
āgenēn stad hē*

*u-š pad handāzag ēn gōwēd kū ka gōwēd kū ēn xwāstag mard 2 xwēš ud nē
gōwēd kū-šān pad āgenēn xwēš*

*būd kē guft kū: kū nē paydāg kū čand ōy ud čand ōy, bē ǰār-ēw kār ēdōn
framūd estēd kū rāst xwēš* ∵ o ∵

When he says: two men took up a loan from me; he said (this) in such a
way as if they took it up together;

and regarding the amount of it (*-š*) he says as follows: When he says:
"This property belongs to the two men," but he does not say that it
belongs to them together,

(then) there was one who said: "When it is not evident how much for
*him* and how much for *him*, but (?), once and for all, it was ordained
that it belonged (to them) equally."

Note: the function of *bē* is not clear here.

18.3. Translate into Pahlavi and write in Pahlavi script with
transliteration and transcription:

1.  In the Dēn it says that men's bodys are analogous to this world, for
    this world has been made from a drop of water, and men too are made
    from a drop of water.

2.  Ardā Wirāz asked: Whose soul is this? -- The Righteous Srōš and the
    divine Fire answered: "This is the soul of that wicked man who, in
    this world, did not keep straight (his) bushels, cups, weights, and
    measures"

3.  The demon Drag-off seizes the soul of the wicked and drags it to
    hell. Then a young woman unlike other young women comes to meet him.
    The soul of the wicked says: "Who are you, than whom I have never
    seen any bad young woman 'badder' and uglier than you." *duš-kanīg
    duštar*

4.  The soul of the Righteous, while the body is alive, is a good
    companion, once the body has passed on, it is immortal and ready for
    the Renovation

5.  When mortality came upon Gayōmard, the light went out of his body
    like red, hot iron when one strikes a hammer *pōdag* on it and it
    becomes black. Now, too, people in this world die in this manner.

6.  Just as in this world the Xwarrah of the Dēn of the Mazdayasnians
    has 'jumped' into the firmament like a star-studded *kusti* with
    three strands fashioned in the other world, in a similar way people
    too have a *kusti* at the waist with three strands.

7.  They also held this: That 'character' in which there is no 'wisdom'
    is like a clear and unsullied source that is dammed up and is not
    put to use. And that 'character' with which there is 'wisdom' is
    like a clear and unsullied source that a diligent man sets upon and
    puts to use and dams up for cultivation and (then) it gives profit
    ('fruit') to the world.

# Glossary of words in the Texts and Exercises 18

##### Idioms:

*abām stan-* take up a loan

*abar est-* step on; be in charge of, take care of (?)

*abar nih-* endow

*andar ō kār kun-* put to use

*ānōh kū \... awiš* to where

*azabar ān gugāyīh gugāy* above that witness (is) the witness (that)

*abāz abespār-* release (from servitude)

*ātaxš nišān-* establish, endow, "enthrone" a fire

*bastan* here: dam (up), channel

*dādan dah-* note the use as "estblish" in creation context

*dārišn* 'holding', but not necessarily 'owning' (*xwēšīh*)

*dārišn bar-* 'carry possession'

*ēd rāy čē* for the reason that, because

*ēk ān ī* one case is that of \...

*frāz az* after

*frāz padīr-* receive

*frāz warz-* = *warz-*

*hamē ka* as long as

*hamist (ud) hamāg* all

*ǰār-ēw* in sum, all in all, all told; once and for all

*kār framāy-* apply (?), use

*nihādag nih-* make an endowment

*mizd stadan* obtain a reward

*nisēy kerdan* abort; note that *nisēy* is spelled like *nasāy*!

*nūn-iz* now too, still (Pers. *hanuz* "still")

*ō kār šaw-* be used

*ō warz band-* \$\$

*pad dāštan* having in one's care

*pad handāzag* regarding the size/amount

*pad petīt baw-* be repentant

*pad tan* "in/with body," indentured (servant)

*pad tēz-rawišnīh* quickly

*paydāg kun-* here: make public, advertise

# Lesson 19

## Grammar 19

### The Perfect participle of state in *-ag*.

A past participle of state (perfect participle) is made from the past
stem with the ending *-ag*. Participles from transitive verbs have
passive meaning. Examples:

*[āfrīdag]{.underline} ham nē [būdag]{.underline}*

"I am someone [created]{.underline}, not someone (who has always)
[been]{.underline}" (*PN*.2)

*mardōmān tan [passāxtag]{.underline} ī az ast ī saxt pid ī sust*

"men's bodies are [fitted together]{.underline} from hard bones and soft
flesh" (*DD*.16.8)

*[xastagān]{.underline} ud [wistagān]{.underline} darmān burdan*

"to bring medication to the [wounded]{.underline} and [those shot by
arrows]{.underline}" (*Dk*.8.26.26)

*xwarišn ī [sāxtag]{.underline} ēn čiyōn nān ud gōšt ī
[puxtag]{.underline} ud [brištag]{.underline} ud xwardīg ī
[kerdag]{.underline}*

"'prepared' food is such as bread, cooked and fried meat and (uncooked?)
eatables that have been made(?)" (*ŠnŠ*.2.48)

*menišn ī Wištāsp šāh ud wasān was ān ī [nihuftag]{.underline} xīr
āškārag guft*

"(Z.) spoke many a [hidden]{.underline} matter (so that it was) clear to
the mind of King Wištāsp and the many" (*Dk*.5.2.8)

*hušk ka [rustag ayāb brīdag]{.underline} u-š nasāy andar gumēxtēd čiyōn
bawēd*

*passox: ān ī and gyāg bē tāšišn; abārīg pad sāl-drahnāy; šōyišn kār*

"when it is a dry (plant), [grown or cut]{.underline}, and some *nasāy*
is mixed into it, how will it be?

answer: so much area (as the *nasāy* has touched) is to chopped off; the
rest (will be clean) after a year; (then) it needs (*kār*) to be washed"
(*ZFJ*, p. 436)

*hišt būd kē guft kū ān ī zanīh rāy andar barēd čiyōn pēšīgān ud
wāspuhragān bē barēd ud windišn ī andar zanīh ēw bē mānēd u-š kardag
ōwōn abāg kū [saxtag]{.underline} bē šawēd*

"(regarding) releasing (a women from a marriage), there was one who
said: that which she 'carries in' for the marriage she 'carries out,'
such as 'priors' and 'special' (things), and let the income from during
the marriage remain; and the established custom (*kardag*) is for him
(the husband): 'what is [passed]{.underline} goes away'" (*MHD*.19.8;
ch. 4, p. 4, MM. p. 85)

*ka hamāg [nihuftag]{.underline} ayāb hamāg [āhuftag]{.underline} barēnd
šāyēd ayāb čiyōn •*

*hamāg [nihuftag]{.underline}; nē hamāg [āhuftag]{.underline} ǰud az ān
nisēy ī az kadag bē āwarēnd ēnyā nē šāyēd*

"is it OK when they carry it all [covered]{.underline} or all
[uncovered]{.underline}, or how is it?

(when) all [covered]{.underline} (it is OK, but) not (when) all
[uncovered]{.underline}, except that aborted fetus which they bring out
of the hut" (*ZFJ*, p. 531)

*kē parwardārīh ī dāmān pad frārōnīh kunēd ā-š wahuman-ohrmazd-zahagīh*

*ud kē ān ī-š andar dārišn xūb dārēd ā-š ohrmazd-wahuman-pidarīh gāh
bawēd ::*

*ud harw frārōn parwardār ān ī-š parwardag-frazendīh andar-iš ēdōn bawēd
čiyōn wahuman andar ohrmazd*

*ud harw frārōn dām pānag abar ān ī-š pādag-pidarīh ēdōn čiyōn ohrmazd
abar wahuman*

"whoever takes care of the creatures by good behavior, then it is (like)
Wahuman being Ohrmazd's child;

and, whoever keeps well whatever is in his keeping, then it is (like)

and every well-behaved caretaker, whatever is in his (*-š \...
andar-iš*) 'having taken-[care]{.underline} of his children,' is just
like Wahuman (being) in Ohrmazd's (care);

and every well-behaved watcher of the creatures, whatever is his 'having

u*d bē nigerēd kū az dušmen pad kēn zadan čē rēš ud ziyān ud
