##### *paywastag ō* (*pad*) "connected with":

*tarsagāyīh ī andar pidarān u-šān paristišn [paywastag]{.underline} ast
[ō]{.underline} tarsagāyīh ī andar dādār u-š paristīšn*

"respect for parents and serving them is connected with respect for the
'creator' and surving him" (*Dk*.9.55.6)

*[paywastag]{.underline} ast kehān ī gēhān [pad]{.underline} mehān ī
gēhān*

*čiyōn wehīh winnārišn pad dānāgīh ud dānāgīh xwad ast dādīh*

"the smaller of this world are conneced with the greater of this world;

like the upholding of goodness with being knowledgeable and being
knowleadgeable is nothing but justice" (*Dk*.3.244.2)

##### *būdag kerdag gumārdag* "having been, made, appointed":

Three legal terms applied, for instance, to the question of who should
be a guardian if the former guardian passes away: someone who 'has been'
in the family, that is, the 'natural' successor as guardian, such as the
oldest son; someone 'made, assigned as' guardian by the former guardian;
or, when the first two cases do not apply, someone 'appointed' by
'guardians of the age,' in practice, the town judge (*rad*) or the
*mowbed*, by the criterion of being the 'more suitable' (*sazāgtar*),
often the one who is the *nazdist-paywandtar* 'the closer relative.'

*ān ī kerdag ān bawēd (ī) kadag-xwadāy andar xwēš zīndagīh sālārīh ī
dūdagān dādestān awiš kunēd u-š dūdag-sālārīh kerdagīhā*

*ud ayāb mard ēw ōšyār ī 15-sālag (ī) pad sālārīh šāyēd pad pusarīh
padīrēd agar-iš pad pašn xwēš kunēd*

*ud ān ī būdag ān ī ka kadag-xwadāy az āwām bē šāwēd ēg-iš pus-ēw
tanī-zād ī ōšyār ī 15-sālag ast ham pus dūdag-sālārīh būdagīhā*

*ān ī gumārdag ān ī frāz az widerānīh ī kadag-xwadāy pad dūdag-sālārīh
sazāgtar u-š āwām-sālārān gumārēnd*

*u-š dādestān gumārdagīhā*

"the *kerdag* is the one to whom the master of the house, during his
lifetime, assigns the legal decision of 'guardianship of the families',
and his guardianship of the family is 'by dint of having been assigned';

or else he receives (= adopts) a 15-year-old male of sound mind who is
appropriate for being guardian, as his son, if he makes him his own by a
contract;

the *būdag* is the one who when the master of the house goes away from
(this) age, then he has one son born from his own body, of sound mind,
and fifteen years of age, said son will be guardian of the family 'by
dint of being *būdag*';

the 'appointed' is the one who after that passing of the master of the
house is the 'more suited' for being guardian of the family and the
'guardians of the age' appoint him, and the legal decision is 'by dint
of having been appointed'" (*REA*.5.3-6)

### The use of the participle in *-ag* as a "conjunctive participle"

The form is sometimes used to express "after having done such and such"
(cf. the Latin and French gerunds):

*ud az Kurdān mard 1000 ōzad abārīg [xastag]{.underline} dast-gīr* *kerd
ud az Kurdān-šā abāg pusarān brādarān frazendān was xīr ud xwāstag ō
Pārs wisēy kerd*

"and he (Ardaxšīr) killed one thousand of the Kurds, the rest, wounded,
he captured; from the king of the Kurds with (his) sons, brothers, (and)
children, he dispatched stuff and property to Pārs" (*KN*.5.11)

*andar rāh Haftānbōxt ī Kerm(ān) xwadāy pad-iš [pahikōftag]{.underline}
ān hāmōyēn xīr ud xwāstag bunag az ān aswārān ī Ardaxšīr bē stadag ō
Kulālān dastkerd-ēw ī Kulāl ānōh kū Kerm bunag dāšt āwurd*

"on the way, Haftānbōxt, lord of Kermān, having fallen upon him (and)
having taken all the stuff and property and equipment from those
cavalerists belonging to Ardaxšīr, brought it to Kulālān, a landed
property in Kulāl, where Kerm had (his) camp" (*KN*.6.1)

##### The form used in an ergative construction:

*ān-[iš]{.underline} ī ōy gōwišn [padīruftag]{.underline} Ašwahišt
pāduxšāy az-iš stad tašt ī nēk u-š pad ān frāz xwārēnīd*

"[he]{.underline} (*-š*) [having received]{.underline} that speech of
his (Ohrmazd) (*ān \... ī ōy*), Ašwahišt, the (heavenly) ruler, took
from him (Ohrmazd) the good cup and made him (Wištāsp) drink from it
(*Dk*.7.4.85-6)

##### With *-īhā*:

The adverbial form of the participle of state probably indicates reason,
cause:

*Walaxš ī Aškānān Abestāg zand čiyōn abēzagīhā andar āmad estād
hammōg-iz ī aziš*

*---harw čē az wizend ud āšuftkārīh ī Alkasandar ud ēwār ud rōb ī
Hrōmāyān andar Ērān-šahr [pargandagīhā]{.underline} [abar
nibištag]{.underline} tā čē uzwān-abespārišnīg (ī) pad dastwar mānd
estād andar šahr čiyōn frāz mad estād---*

*nigāh-dāštan ō šahrīhā ayādgār kerdan framūd*

"Walaxš of the Arsacids ordered a memorandum to be sent to the towns
that the *Avesta* and the Zand were to be preserved the way they had
come down in pure form, as well as the teachings from it---everything
that, [having been written up]{.underline}, (survived) [in scattered
form]{.underline} from the damage and disarray caused by Alexander and
the looting and pillaging by the Romans in the land of the Iranians,
including (*tā čē*) the oral (tradition) that had remained authoritative
(*pad dastwar*) in the land the way it had come down" (*Dk*.4.3.3/24)

*mad ō ham-pursagīh ī Ohrmazdud az (ōy) padīrift dēn*

*Ahrimen ud was dēwān ud druzān pad bīm-nimāyišnīh \... ud pahikārišn ud
xwāyišn ud hāzišn aw-iš āmad hēnd*

*ud hamāg a-padīrišnīhā ud [zadagīhā]{.underline} stōwīhā az-iš wašt
hēnd*

"(Z.) came to the conversation with Ohrmazd (and) received the Dēn (from
him).

Ahrimen and many demons and lie-demons came to show him fear, fighting,
seeking, and persuading;

and all turned away from him without being received, having been struck
down, and defeated" (*Dk*.5.2.6)

## Phraseology 3

## Adverbs and other expressions of time

Among the adverbs of time, place, and manner, some function only as
adverbs, while others can also be prepositions (sometimes in combination
with other prepositions), preverbs, or conjunctions (sometimes combined
with prepositions and/or other conjunctions).

Many expressions are made from nouns meaning "time" and similar.

Some refer exclusively to time or place, others to both time and place
(see Lesson 20).

On the times of the days, months, and years, see Lesson \$\$.

### Exressions of time

#### "First" and "last"

> *fradom* âLwA , MWtÒP \<pltwm, AWLA\> "first, in the first place"
>
> *fradomīg* WiMWtÒP \<pltwmyk\'\> "initial"
>
> *abdom* MwY\>cÅ \<'p̄dwm\> "last, at last, in the end"
>
> *abdomīg* WiMwY\>cÅ \<'p̄dwmyk\'\> "final"

Note: Expressions meaning "first" are often followed by *pas* "then."

#### *fradom* "first, at first, in the first place" *pad fradomīh* "at first, in the beginning"

*ud ān kē nē mad estēd [fradom]{.underline} awiš nē rasēd*

"and (the misfortune) that has not come (befallen him), will not come to
him [in the first place]{.underline}" (*Dk*. 6.126)

*u-š xrad ud kām ud kār ud zamān a-wardišnīg ast az
[fradomīg]{.underline} handāzišn*

'and His wisdom and will and act and time are something immutable from
the [initial]{.underline} planning" (*Dk*.3.208.5)

*hamāg dām ud dahišn ī Ohrmazd apetyārag, ēdōn abāz bawēd čiyōn ān ī-š
[pad fradomīh]{.underline} brēhēnīd ud dād*

"the entire creation of Ohrmazd (will be) free from adversity; it will
again be the way he fashioned and established it [in the
beginning]{.underline}" (*MX*.7.16)

#### *abdom*, *pad abdom*, *pad abdomīh* "at last, in the end":

*hamāg mardōmān andar ayōxšust bē widerēnd ud druwandān az wināh
[abdom]{.underline} pad ān pāk bawēnd*

"all people will pass into that (molten) metal (stream), and through it
the evil-doers will [finally]{.underline} become clean of (their) sin"
(*PR*.48.70)

*ma ēn ī man kerb frāz xwarēd kē-m Ohrmazd [abdom-iz]{.underline} abāz
kunēd pad tan ī pasēn*

"do not devour this form of mine, which Ohrmazd will
[finally]{.underline} make for me again at the Final Body!" (*WZ*.30.32;
the dead fearing dogs and vultures)

*zan ī pad-gōhr wizīn čē ān weh ī [pad abdom]{.underline} husrawtar*

"choose a wife with pedigree, for he is best (off) who, [in the
end]{.underline}, has the better fame" (*MX*.1.31-32)

*ristāxēz pad [abdomīg]{.underline} bē-abesīhēnišnīh ī petyārag bawēd
(ī) xwābar dādār ud hamāg mardōm zīndag abāz kunēd*

"the Resurrection will happen/come about at [the final]{.underline}
'cutting off' (annihilation) of the Adversary by the merciful Creator,
and he will make all people alive again" (*Dk*.5.8.8)

*ka druwand hēnd ā (ēk abāg did ōh) nē rasēnd [pad abdomīh]{.underline}*

"if they are evil, then they will not come together in the usual way [in
the end]{.underline}" (*PR*.36.4)

#### "First," "next," "again"

> *ahīy* yZK \<KZY\> "first, at first"
>
> *nazdist* Wt∆∂¸W , Wt∆Î¸W , WtjgZW \<nz(d)st\'\> "first, at first"
>
> etc. Wt∆¸W , WtjZW
>
> *did* YWT \<TW[B]{.underline}\> "next, again" (also pronoun "other,
> second")

#### *ahīy-* \<KZY\> "at first, before, earlier, sooner"

*nūn anīy šahriyār paydāg \... ud az awēšān aγrātar kē-mān
[ahīy]{.underline} dīd hēnd*

"now another prince appears, and he is more excellent that those whom we
saw [at first]{.underline}" (KNRm/KSM §28)

*ōwōn nibišt kū-m --- ō xwēš kerdan kār ud kerbag ī az
[ahīy]{.underline} nišāst ī ān ātaxš rāy --- ān ātaxš pad warahrānīh ō
dādgāh nišāst*

"thus it was written: I set down (established) that fire as
Warahrān-fire in its lawful place in order (*rāy*) to appropriate the
deeds and good deeds from that fire's being established
[first]{.underline}" (*MHD*. J.34, p. 110, ch. 42)

*ka brād stūrīh [ahīy]{.underline} ō xwāyišn kerd [kū]{.underline} xwah
pad ān stūrīh xwah nē bē brād gumārišn*

"when/if a brother submitted a request for the *stūrīh* [sooner
than]{.underline} the sister, (then) not the sister, but the brother
should be appointed to that *stūrīh* (to be *stūr*)" (*MHD*.37.17, p.
43, ch. 19)

*paydāg kū [ahīy]{.underline} rōšnīh būd [pas]{.underline} framān sazist
dād*

"it is obvious that the light was [first]{.underline},
[then]{.underline} it was appropriate to command!" (*ŠGW*.13.90-91)
(criticism of Genesis 1)

##### *čand ahīy* "as soon as possible, the sooner (the better)" or "no sooner \... than \...":

*[čand ahīy]{.underline}* *xwadāy ī dēnīg bē rasād dēn-burdārān az dēn
nēkīh rasād*

"[the sooner]{.underline} a ruler according to (or: uupholding) the
*dēn* shall come, (the sooner) the goodness from the *dēn* will come to
the *dēn*-carriers" (ColDkB)

*ēdōn weh ka ēn 3 wināh [čand ahīy]{.underline} az gēhān bē barīhēd*

"this is better: when these three sins are removed from the world [as
soon as possible]{.underline} (= the sooner these \... are the removed,
the better)" (*Dk*.6.275)

*hamāg zōhr Ādur Farnbay ud Ādur Gušnasp ud Ādur ī Burzēnmihr ud abārīg
ādurān ātaxšān ī pad dād-gāh nišāst estēnd [čand ahītar]{.underline}
hamēšag-sōz hamēšag-yazišn ud hamēšag-zōhr bawānd*

"Hamāzōr to the Farnbay Fire, the Gušnasp Fire, the Burzēnmihr Fire and
the other fires that are seated in their proper place; let them, [the
sooner (the better)]{.underline}, be ever-burning, ever receiving
offerings, and ever receiving oblations!" (*Sūr saxwan* 6)

#### *nazdist* "first, at first"

Superlative of *nazd* "close."

*ān zand āgāhīh [nazdist]{.underline} abar bunyādīh ī Ohrmazd ud
petyāragīh ī Gannāg Mēnōy*

*[pas]{.underline} abar čiyōnīh ī gēhān dām az bundahišnīh tā frazām
čiyōn az dēn ī Mazdēsnān paydāg*

*pas abar xīr kē gēhān dārēd pad wizārišn ī čē'īh ud čiyōnīh*

"that knowledge from the Zand (is) [first]{.underline} about the
foundation (made) by Ohrmazd and the adversity of the Evil Spirit;

[then/next]{.underline} about the nature of the creation of living
beings from the first creation to the end, (as) manifest from the Dēn of
the Mazdayasnians;

[then/next]{.underline} about the stuff the world has (i.e., consists
of) with an explanation of what and how it is" (*Bd*.1.0)

#### *did* "next, again"

*u-š dām ī gētīy mēnōyīhā dād u-š [did]{.underline} bē ō gētīyīhā dād*

"and he (first) established this world in that world; [next]{.underline}
he established it into this world" (*Bd*.1.52)

*[did]{.underline} harwisp-āgāhīh ī Ohrmazd rāy harw čē-š andar dānišn ī
Ohrmazd kanāragōmand*

"[second/next]{.underline}, about the omniscience of Ohrmazd: everything
which (is) in his knowledge, Ohrmazd's, is limited" (*Bd*.1.9)

#### Expressions with *bun* "bottom, beginning," *sar* "top, end," *padisār* "beginning," *frazām* "end"

For *sar-nigūn*, see Lesson 20.

> *bun* WWWB \<bwn\'\> "bottom, beginning"
>
> *sar* :J , nÍwL \<LOYŠE, sl\> "head, top, end"
>
> *padisār* laJTP \<pts'l\> "beginning"
>
> *frazām* AcÒP \<plc'm\> "future, end"

##### "Top and bottom, beginning and end":

*āb mard nē zanēd \... āb-iš ul wazēnēd kū-š [ul ō sar]{.underline}
āwarēd u-š āb nigūn wazēnēd kū-š [frōd ō bun]{.underline} bard*

"the water does not strike down a man, the water makes makes him fly up,
i.e., it brings him [up to the top]{.underline}, and the water makes him
fly downward, i.e., it carries him [down to the bottom]{.underline}
(*PV*.5.8ad)

*čāh ēw ka [az bun tā sar]{.underline} hamāg āgur kerd estēd u-š sag ēw
andar bē mīrēd u-š handām-ēw abāz ō āgur estēd ān čāh dādestān čē*

"a well, when it is all made with bricks [from the bottom to the
top]{.underline} and a dog dies in it and one of its limbs reaches
(*abāz ō \... estēd*) a brick, (then) what is the legal situation of
that well?" (*RAF*.44.1)

*u-m dīd ruwān ī mard-ēw kē [sar tā pāy]{.underline} škenǰag abar nihād
estād ud 1000 dēw azabar frāz kōft ud pad garān anāgīh ud saxtīh hamē
zad*

"and I saw the soul of a man over whom, [from head to foot]{.underline}
(= from head to toe), a *škanǰag* (some torture instrument) had been
placed and a thousand demons banged on it and kept striking (it/him)
with heavy evil and firmness (maliciously and brutally)" (*AWN*.31.1)

##### *pad bun* "in the beginning, in the first place"

*āsmān pad star-pāyag estād frōd ō tuhīgīh āhaxt ī-m [pad
bun]{.underline} nibišt kū andarg buništ ī rōšnān ud tamīgān būd*

"the sky stood on the star-level; (the Foul Spirit) dragged it down to
the emptiness, which I wrote [in the beginning]{.underline} that it was
between the (two) principles: light and darkness" (*Bd*.4.10a)

*ān kē xrad āsn-xrad nē bowandag ēdōn homānāg čiyōn mādag kē gušn nē
padīrēd čē mādag kē gušn nē padīrēd bar ōwōn nē dahēd čiyōn ka [pad
bun]{.underline} gušn nēst*

"he who does not have inborn wisdom completely is just like a female who
does not receive the male; for a female who does not receive the male
will give (produce) no fruit, just as if there were no male [in the
first place"]{.underline} (*Dk*.6.262)

##### *az bunīh* "from the beginning," *pad sarīh* "at/in the end":

*māh pad 100 ud 80 rōz abāz ō ān gyāg āyēd ī [az bunīh]{.underline} bē
raft*

"in 180 days, the moon comes back to the place (from) which it went out
[in the beginning]{.underline} (to start with)" (*Bd*.25.27)

*dastwarān zamān rāy guft kū zamān [az bunīh]{.underline} a-kanārag būd
pas bē ō kanāragōmandīh wašt ud [pad sarīh]{.underline} abāz ō
a-kanāragīh wardēd*

"the *dastwar*s said about time: [from the beginning]{.underline}, time
was limitless, then it turned (= changed) into limitedness, and, [in the
end]{.underline}, it will turn back to unlimitedness" (*Dk*.3.267.4)

*zamān [az bunīh]{.underline} a-kanārag būd pas bē ō kanāragōmandīh wašt
ud [pad sarīh]{.underline} abāz ō a-kanāragīh wardēd*

"[from the beginning]{.underline}, time was unlimited; then it changed
to being limited; and, [at the end]{.underline}, it will change back to
being unlimited" (*Dk*.3.267.4)

*[pad sarīh]{.underline} ōy (ī) andar Pārs mardōm bē abesīhānd bē
huzārag ī pad Kāzrūn drayā bārīhā tā bē nē mānēd az ān*

"[in the end]{.underline}, the people in Pārs will be annihilated;
except (*bē \... tā*) a few along the shores of the sea by Kazerun, none
of those will remain" (*Bd*.33.30)

##### In legal discourse *az bunīh* sometimes has the meaning of "starting all over again":

*ka az daštān šustan 3 rōz pad pākīh nišast ud did daštān bawēd*

*čiyōn [az bunīh]{.underline} 4 rōz bē pāyišn ud rōz ī panǰom ōh šōyišn*

"when she has sat clean for three days from washing (after) menstruation
and then becomes menstruant again,

she has to wait for four days just as [from the beginning]{.underline}
and wash in the usual way on the fifth day" (*ŠnŠ*.3.17)

A similar idea is expressed by *abāz ō bun šawēd* "it goes back to the
beginning, starts all over again," usually the search for a replacement:

*ka xwāstag ruwān rāy paydāg kunēd ud pad dāštan ō Farrox dahēd ud
Farrox gīrēd ud dārēd*

*widerd Farrox ud pad paywand ī Farrox bē rawēd u-š ōy ī sālār wināh
padiš kunēd ud appār bawēd*

*ud čiyōn Dād-farrox guft sālārīh [abāz ō bun šawēd]{.underline} nē ō
Farrox*

"when somebody publicizes an endowment 'for the soul' and gives it to
Farrox for keeping, and Farrox receives it and keeps it;

Farrox having died, and (the money) goes in the family (offspring) of
Farrox, and the guardian commits a sin with it and it is lost;

then, as Dādfarrox has said, the guardianship ['goes back to the
begininng']{.underline}, not to Farrox('s heirs)" (*MHD*.26.38)

##### *pad sar* "finished, concluded" in legalese:

*pad ēw-gōwišnīh ud 2-gōwišnīh būd kē guft kū dād [pad sar]{.underline}
bawēd*

"when it has been said once and twice (that 'I give it'), there was one
(authority) who said that the giving is [concluded]{.underline}"
(*MHDA*.3.11)

*māh Frawardīn rōz ī Hordad \... hazārag ī Xwaršēdarān bun bawēd ud ān ī
Zarduxštān [pad sar]{.underline} bawēd*

"On the day of Hordad in the month of Frawardīn (1/6), the millennium of
Xwaršēdar (= Ošīdar) will begin and that of Z. will be finished"
(*MāhFr*.30)

##### Note *sar pad sar*, probably like Persian *sar-be-sar* "throughout, completely"; similarly *sarōmandīhā* (?)

*u-š az abāxtar andar kunišn u-š [sar pad sar]{.underline} abāz
widārišn*

"and he should be introduced into (the purification area) from the
north, and he should be made to traverse (it) [throughout]{.underline}"
(*PV*.9.32L)

*garmīh pad sardīh ud xwēdīh pad huškīh [sarōmandīhā]{.underline}
ānāftan*

"to remove [throughout]{.underline} warmth by means of cold, moisture by
means of dryness"

(*Dk*.3.162.4)

#### *padisār* "beginning"

##### *az padisār* "from the beginning":

*az pas ī awēšān 18 rōd az ham bun-xān frāz tazīd hēnd*

*čiyōn gōwēd kū ēdōn zūd zūd ēk azpas ōy ī did bē tazīd hēnd čiyōn
mard-ēw kē Ašemwohū-ēw [az padisār]{.underline} bē gōwēd*

"after those (two rivers: the Weh and the Ārang), eighteen rivers flowed
forth from the same source;

as it says: they flowed as quickly one after the other as a man who
recites one *Ašemwohū* [from the beginning]{.underline}" (*Bd*.11.2-3)

##### *pad padisār*, *padisārīg* "from first to last, one after the other":

*kadām ōšmurd ī āsrō fradom az srawān [pad padisār]{.underline} tā ān
(ī) abdom*

"which is the first of the sacred words recited by the priest, [one
after the other]{.underline} to the last one?" (*Dk*.8.28.5)

##### 

*u-š nimūd xwēš čihrag āsmān handāzagīhā \...*

*ud 6 amahrspand pad-iš ham-bašnīh paydāg būd hēnd*

*ōwōn kū [padisārīg]{.underline} harw ēk az ān ī did angust ēw homānāgīh
paydāgīhist*

"and he (Ohrmazd) showed (Z.) his own shape similar to the sky \...

and the six *amahrspand*s appeared in the same height as he (as tall as
he)

in such a way that they were made manifest [one after the
other]{.underline}, each from the next, just like fingers" (*WZ*.22.9)

#### *frazām* "end, completion"

*[pad frazām]{.underline} bē ō druzān wēmārīh ī garān-margīh ī spurr
(rasēd) ud ō dām ī yazdān bēšazišnīh ud zīndagīh*

"[at the end]{.underline}, sickness and heavy mortality (will come) to
the lie-demons, and to the gods' creation healing and life" (*DD*.36.59)
--- Note also *pad-frazāmēnīdan* "to finalize, complete" (Lesson 17).

*pad 3-uzmāyišnīh [sar frazām]{.underline} rasišn hām-dahišn rawāgīh ud
hamāg mardōm padiš āstawānīh ud abar-estišnīh*

*pad dādār kām ud framān fraškerd tan ī pasēn abar* (?) *kerdan paydāg*

"through the three trials \[to propagate the Dēn by Z. and his two
son\], [in the end]{.underline}, will come (its) propagation throughout
the whole world, and all people will profess it and abide by it; by the
will and command of the Creator, the making of the Renovation and the
Final Body will be manifest" (*Dk*.3.29.14)

*az bun-dahišn ka dām dād [tā ō frazām]{.underline} kū Ganāg Mēnōy agār
bawēd paymānag-ēw 12,000 sāl kū kanāragōmand*

"from the first creation, when the creation was established, [until the
end]{.underline}, when the Foul Spirit will be undone, there is a
measure of 12,000 years, which is 'limited'" (*Bd*.1.41)

*ēg Ganāg Mēnōy awēnāg-[frazām]{.underline}īh rāy pad ān paymānag
ham-dādestān būd*

"then the Foul Spirit, because of not seeing [the end]{.underline},
agreed to that deal" (*Bd*.1.26) (Ohrmazd has proposed that they would
fight for 9000 years)

*pad 600 sāl-iz hammis hamāg kōfān ī ǰud az Harburz frazāmīg būd hēnd*

In 600 years all the mountains together except Harburz were completed"
(*WZ*.3.30)

##### *frazām ī kār* "how it will be in the end":

*Ohrmazd abāg čē-ēwēnag dānist ī [frazām ī kār]{.underline} ō padīrag ī
Gannāg Mēnōy šud u-š āštīh abar dāšt*

"Ohrmazd, although he knew [how it would be in the end]{.underline},
went toward the Foul Spirit and offered him peace" (*IndBd*.1.19)

##### *ō frazām āwurdan* "to complete":

*ka kār ud dādestān was frāz gīrēd tis-iz bē [ō frazām nē
āwarēd]{.underline}*

"when one takes on to much 'work and law' [one does not
complete]{.underline} anything" (*PR*.26.4)

#### "Still, (not \...) yet"

> *nūn-iz* CWWK \<KONc\> "still"
>
> *ahanūn-iz* cDWwaÅ, cDWWwaÅ \<'hnw(n)yc\> "still, (not \...) yet"
>
> *ahanūz (\... nē)* CWwïjA, CWwaÅ \<'hnwc, 'synwc\>

The spelling CwaÅ = \<AHR(N)c\> is also found (e.g., *KN*.4.17).

*u-š [ahanūz]{.underline} guft kū dēn padīr*

"and [still]{.underline} he said: receive/accept the *dēn*!"
(*PR*.46.20)

*ān xwarrah ī xwadāyīh [ahanūz]{.underline} aw-iš [nē]{.underline}
rasīd*

"that glory of kingship has [not yet]{.underline} reached him"
(*KN*.3.15)

*ka-š nasāy xward ud [ahanūz]{.underline}* \<'synwc\> *[nē]{.underline}
gugārd estēd bē mīrēd ēdōn bawēd čiyōn hambān-ēw kē nasāy andar*

"when (the sheep) has eaten *nasāy*, but it is [not yet]{.underline}
digested, (and) it dies, it will be like a pocket in which there is

#### *ēw* and *ēwīg*

The common word *hamē* is from earlier *hamēw*, that is *ham-ēw*, with
*ēw* presumably from earlier *āywa-*, Avestan *āiiu-* "time/life
period," instrumental *yauua* "ever." The form *ēw* is found in the
phrase *andar ān ēw*:

*ēn dādestān abāg ān ī guft estēd kū ka hambāy-ēw tōzišn \[\...\] waxš
kerd estēd [andar ān ēw ka]{.underline} hambāy mad estēnd ǰud az
pahikārišn ī hambāyān bē wizārēd ān ī wizārēd pad wizārdan abārīg
ham-bāyān niyābēd abāz xwāst pādixšāy*

"this judgement (goes) with that which has been said: when a partner has
paid (*tōzišn \... kerd*) \[ms. broken out\] interest,
[whenever]{.underline} (during that \*time? when) the partners are
present (and the one) resolves (the issue) without taking the partners
to court, (then) that which he resolves is incumbent upon (*niyābēd*)
the other partners (too) to resolve, (and) he is authorized to request
back (what they owe him?)" (*MHD*.34.8)

*ka sāl pad petītīgīh bawēd u-š yašt ī nōg-nāywar abāz kunišn u-š
tanābuhl ī ruwānīg bē wizārišn*

*u-š kār kerbag (ī) pēš az ān kerd abāz rasēd ān ī [andar ān
ēw]{.underline} xwēš nē bawēd*

"When he is penitent for a year, then he (*u-š*) must redo the ritual
for novices (*nōg-nāywar*), and (thus) he must expiate for the
*tanābuhl* sin on his soul.

And the deeds and good deeds he has performed before that (apostasy),
come back. Those (= the new ones) he performs [at that time]{.underline}
(while he was apostate) will not be his (*xwēš*)." (*Nir*.23.7)

*urwāhmen-ox pad gyān zīyē tā ān šab zīyē pad rāmišn zīyē ay
[ēwīg]{.underline} zīy ēn ān ī ātaxš āfrīn (ī) bāstān ōh kunēd*

"you will live with yor soul filled with mind bliss (?) until the night
(= for as long as) you live; you will live in joy, that is, live [for a
long time]{.underline}! --- this is the fire's blessing, which he
repeatedly makes thus" (*Ny*.5.16)

(the corrresponding text in Y.62.10 has *a-xīndag zīy* "live without
sickness!")

#### "Ever, always" "never":

*hamē* áÂA \<hm[ydy]{.underline}\> "always"

*hamēšag* WkßgmA \<hmyšk\'\> "always"

*hamwār* lAnA \<hmw'l\> "always"

*hagriz* (*haguriz*) (cÒWkA) cÒkA \<hk(w)lc \> "ever"

*hagriz* (*haguriz*) *\... nē* âL \... (cÒWkA) cÒkA \<hk(w)lc \... LA\>
"never"

*ǰāwēdānīg* WIwAtDwaD \<y'wyt'nyk\'\> "eternal"

*fraškerdīg* WITWkßLP \<plškrtyk\'\>. "lasting to the Renovation

*tay-ā-tay* 1YTA 1YT \<tyḏ 'tyḏ\> "uninterruptedly, continuously"

#### *hamē* "always, constantly"

This adverb is occasionally used freely in the above meaning, but most
often it is used with verbs (sometimes seprated from the verb) to
indicate progressive action "keeps/kept doing":

*Ohrmazd bālistīg pad harwisp-āgāhīh ud wehīh zamān ī akanārag andar
rōšnīh [hamē būd]{.underline}*

"Ohrmazd [was ever]{.underline} on high in omniscience and goodness
(for) an unlimited time in the light" (*Bd*.1.1)

*paywastag [hamē]{.underline} pad šab \... ān kanīzag pad nihān ō
nazdīkīh ī Ardaxšīr [raft]{.underline}*

"constantly, at night, that young woman [would go]{.underline} secretly
to Ardaxšīr" (*KN.*3.3)

##### With *tā*:

*tā hamē hamē-rawišnīh* "forever and ever"

*[tā hamē]{.underline} ān ī wēš-abzārtar gāh meh bahr wēš handāxtan
sazāg*

"(it is) [forever]{.underline} appropriate to regard the position of the
more resourceful as greater (and his) share as more" (*DD*.46.7)

##### *tā hamē \... tā* "for ever (= the entire period) until"

*ka gōwēd kū ēn ō tō daham bē xwāhišn ud agar bē dahēd [tā
hamē]{.underline} pad azišmānd graw abespārišn [tā]{.underline} bē
abespārēd*

"if he says: 'I am giving this to you,' it can be requested
(immediately); and if he gives it away (to someone else), he must hand
over a guarantee for what is owed (to be kept) [for the entire period
until]{.underline} he hands over (the thing he gave him)" (*MHDA*3.9)

##### *hamēyīhā* "lasting forever":

*agar zamān ī kārēzār ī-š nē kunam ēg tuwān kerdan pad dām ī man čiyōn
padest abar burd ud kōxšišn ud gumēzišn ī [hamēyīhā]{.underline} aziš
būd*

"if I do not set a time for the battle with him, then he will be able to
do to my creation as he threatened and from it (there will be) fiighting
and mixture [that will last for ever]{.underline}" (*Bd*.1.24)

##### *hamēyīg* "eternal":

*and frayist nēkīh ī mēnōy az ān ī gētīy čand ān ī akanārag ud
[hamēyīg]{.underline} az ān ī kanāragōmand ud gēhānīg*

"the goodness of that world is as much more \[lit. most\] than that of
this world as what is unlimited and [eternal]{.underline} (is more) than
that which is limited and belonging to the world of the living"
(*DD*.25.7)

*frasast kanārag nē kerd čim ēn ast čē harw tis ud harw kas kanārag ast
ud Ohrmazd [hamēyīgīhā]{.underline} dād rāy akanāragōmand ast*

"no limit is made to the *frasast*: the reason is because everything and
everybody has a limit; and because Ohrmazd created (everything to last)
[eternally]{.underline}, it is unlimited" (*PR*.56.4) (*drōn* and
*frasast* are small breads consumed during the *yasna*; the *drōn* has a
raised edge, the *frasast* none)

#### *hamēšag* "always"

*tā pēš ka Ēbgad mad [hamēšag]{.underline} nēmrōz būd ast Rabihwin*

"before the Assault came, it was [always]{.underline} noon, that is,
Rabihwin" (*Bd*.3.25)

*guft estēd kū dārūg ēk ud wāzag ēk dārūg paymān-xwarišnīh ud wāzag
[hamēšag-menīdārīh]{.underline} ī ahlāyīh*

"it is said: one remedy and one word: the remedy is eating in
moderation, and the word is [always to think]{.underline} about
Righteousness" (*Dk*.6E.17)

*sōzāg bawē andar ēn mān [hamēšag-sōz]{.underline} bawē andar ēn mān*

"you (the fire) shall be burning in this house, you shall be
[ever-burning]{.underline} in this house" (*PY*.62.3a)

#### *hamwār*, "always, constantly"

*ud Sāsān šabān ī Pābag būd ud [hamwār]{.underline} abāg gōspandān būd*

"and Sāsān was Pābag's shepherd and was [constantly]{.underline} with
the animals" (*KN*.1.6)

*ud abāg-iz [hamwārīhā]{.underline} kōšīdan ī-šān nūn-iz ēk ō did čand
pattūgīh ud a-wardišnīg estād nē šāyistan*

*ī pad-iz ham-čim tanān andar gumēzagīh pas-iz pad ēd šōn hambedīgān
āgenēn a-sāzišnīgīhā andar-iz ēw tan \*hamēšag-kōšīdārīhā* \[ms.
*mēšag-*\] *kardag ham-parwandīh*

and (also about the fact that) in spite of their
[constantly]{.underline} struggling, even now, with one another, there
cannot be as much patience and refusal to turn back

as, also for the same reason, (there is) for the bodies in the Mixture,
yet, the opponents having acted together in this way (*pad ēd šōn*) in
such a way that they cannot be fitted together (*a-sāzišnīgīhā*) and by
constantly (?) fighting in one and the same body, (in spite of all that)
a connectedness" (*Dk*.4.10.10; about warm and cold, dry and wet)

#### *hagriz* (*haguriz*) "ever," *hagriz \... nē* "never"

*ēd-iz az awēšān saxwanān saxwantom pad-kārtom kē [hagriz]{.underline}
frāz guft*

"and this is of (all) those words the 'most word' (i.e.) the most
effective (of those) which (have) [ever]{.underline} been uttered"
(*PY*.19.10)

*Gannāg Mēnōy [hagriz]{.underline} tis ī frārōn [nē]{.underline} menēd
[nē]{.underline} gōwēd [nē]{.underline} kunēd*

"the Evil Spirit [never]{.underline} thinks, says, or does anything
good" (*Bd*.1.55)

*u-š dīd pad rōšn-wēnāgīh Ohrmazd kū Gannāg Mēnōy [hagriz]{.underline}
az petyāragīh [nē]{.underline} wardēd*

"and (as for) Ohrmazd, he saw with his clear-sight that the Evil Spirit
would [never]{.underline} turn away from adversity" (*Bd*.1.35)

*kē-š [nē haguriz]{.underline} mih menīd u-š [nē haguriz]{.underline}
mih guft u-š [nē haguriz]{.underline} mih kerd*

"who has [never]{.underline} thought anything crooked and has never
spoken anything crooked and has [never]{.underline} done anything
crooked" (*Pursišnīha* 17.2; cf. *Yt*.19.95)

#### Expressions with *nūn* "now" 

#### 

##### *nūn*, *nūn-iz* CWWK , WWK\<KWN(c)\>:

*xwarišn ud mizag 1000 ān and čand ān ī [nūn]{.underline} ast bawēd*

"food and taste will be a thousand times as much as it is
[now]{.underline}" (*PR*.48.59)

*[nūn-iz]{.underline} pad gētīy pad ān hangōšīdag \... zāyēnd*

"[even now]{.underline} (still), in this world, they are born in that
manner" (*Bd*.1.57)

##### *ō-nūn* WWKwA \<'wKON\> "now, currently":

*ēn rad (ī) [ō-nūn]{.underline} rad mowbed nēst*

"the *rad* who is [currently]{.underline} *rad* is not a mowbed"
(*RFS*.2.1)

*u-šān astīh ēd kū [ō-nūn]{.underline} hēnd u-šān nēstīh ēd kū
[pas]{.underline} nē bawēnd*

"and their 'be-ing' is this: they are [now]{.underline}; and their
not-be-ing is this: they shall not be [hereafter]{.underline}"
(*PY*.12.4b)

*guft az dahībed dēn paydāgīh kū*

*tō ēn xēm ēn dēn kē xrōsag ast xwistag [ō-nūn]{.underline} ō ham kunē
Kay-Wištāsp kū bē padīrē tō ēn xēm ēn dēn*

"it was said from the manifestation of the *dēn* to (?) the 'land-lord'
(Wištāsp):

Assemble [now]{.underline} this *xēm*, this Dēn, for which there is
ridicule and persecution (= which is ridiculed and persecuted), o
Kay-Wištāsp, that is, receive, you, this *xēm*, this *dēn*!"
(*Dk*.7.5.6)

Note: *xēm* is usually translated as "character, temperament," which
seems to fit poorly into this context.

##### *tā nūn* "until now, by now":

*mardōmān guft kū \... dānēm kū [tā nūn]{.underline} was frasang zamīg
šud u-tān griftan nē tuwān*

"the people said: we know that, [by now]{.underline}, he has gone a
distance of many frasangs, and you will not be able to catch him"
(*KN*.4.10-12)

##### *az nūn frāz* "from now on":

*nimūd dādār ō awēšān ǰōrdāy-kārišnīh čiyōn pad gōwišnīh Ohrmazd paydāg
kū*

*ēd tō Mašīy gāw u-t ēd ǰōrdāy u-t awēšān abzār ī abārīg ud [az nūn
frāz]{.underline} tō weh dānē*

"the Creator showed them (= M.&M.) how to plant barley (grain), as it is
manifest by Ohrmazd's utterance:

this, Mašīy, is your cow, and this is your barley, and those are (all)
your other tools, and [from now on]{.underline} you will know better"
(*Dk*.7.1.11)

##### Combinations with *nūn*:

*ēd-iz az awēšān saxwanān saxwantom pad-kārtom kē hagriz frāz guft [tā
nū]{.underline}n frāz gōwēd [ō-nūn]{.underline} frāz gōwīhēd [az-iz nūn
frāz]{.underline}*

"and this is of (all) those words the 'most word' (i.e.) the most
effective (of those) which (have) *ever* been uttered (i.e.) [until
now]{.underline}, is uttered (i.e.) [now]{.underline}, will be uttered
(i.e.) [from now on]{.underline}" (*PY*.19.10)

*az Abestāg paydāg kū-š nē tis grift kē-š nē ruwān rāy grift [tā
nūn]{.underline}*

*ud nē tis gīrēd kē nē ruwān rāy gīrēd [az-iz nūn frāz]{.underline}*

"he has seized nothing who has not seized (it) for his soul, [by
now]{.underline}; and he will seize nothing who does not seize it for
his soul, also [from now on]{.underline}" (after *MX*.0.27--30 and other
texts; note: "seize" coresponds to "win, gain" in the original Avestan)

#### Expressions with *nōg* "new" and derivatives 

> *nōg* WKWW \<nwk\'\> "anew, newly, recently"
>
> *nōgīhā* aåDKWW \<nwkyh'\> "anew, again"
>
> *nōgānag* WKwAKWW \<nwk'nk\'\> "newly, recently"
>
> *nōgwar* LWKWW \<nwkwl\> "anew, again"

#### *nōg* "anew (again), newly, recently"

*abar ān ī-š [nōg]{.underline} pad ham-pursagīh ī Tarsāg mard-ēw
Bōxt-Mārīy xwānēnd pursīd*

"about that which he [recently]{.underline} asked in a discussion with a
Christian man they call Bōxt-Mārīy" (*Dk*.5.23.0)

*ka az stardīh frāz būd ōy ǰādūg ēg-iš did ō Zarduxšt ham-ēwēnag drāyīd*

*Zarduxšt pāsox ān ham guft*

*[nōg]{.underline} a-kār būd mar ud stard čand drang ī 20 asp ī purr-pēm
dōsišn kē dōsīdār ēk bawēd*

"when that sorcerer came out of his 'coma', then he again howled at
Zarduxšt in the same way;

Z. gave the same answer;

[again]{.underline} the villain was incapacitated and stunned for as
long as it takes to milk twenty mares full of milk whose milker is one
(person only)" (*Dk*.7.3.42

##### *az nōg* "anew, again, afresh":

*ud was kārēzār didīgar abāg (Frāsiyāb) kerd tā spōxt ō Turkestān abgand
Ērān šahr [az nōg]{.underline} ābādānēnīd*

"and (Rōstahm) fought many other battles with (F.) until he was pushed
back and thrown (back) to Turkestān; the land of the Iranians was
[again]{.underline} made prosperous" (*Bd*.33.10c)

*hudēnān pēšōbāy widurd ēn rad (ī) ō-nūn rad mowbed nēst; harw kē ōy rāy
mowbed xwānēd tā nōg gumārd ēw [az nōg]{.underline} hu-dēnān pēšōbāy ēw
nē bawēd u-š wināh ī garān bawēd*

"the leader of the *hudēn*s has passed away; the *rad* (who) is
currently *rad* is not a *mowbed*; everyone who calls him *mowbed* until
a new (*rad*) has [again]{.underline} been appointed as leader of the
*hudēn*s---(that) is not (OK), and he incurs a heavy sin" (*RFS*.2.1)

##### *pad nōg* "anew, again, afresh":

*ān xūbtar ka rāspīg nōg ō yazišn rasīd zōd āgāh kunišn kū rāspīg [pad
nōg]{.underline} ō yazišn mad*

"it is better, when the assistant priest has newly come to the ritual,
that the main priest should be informed that the assistant priest has
[again]{.underline} come to the ritual" (*Nir*.2.7)

##### *nōgīhā* "anew, again":

*ud ka waxšēd ō purrīh rasišn ī hamwarīh ī xwaršēd ud ēbārag āyēd ud
hām-šab wēnīhēd*

*[nōgīhā]{.underline} nirfsēd ud abāz rasēd ō hamwarīh ī xwaršēd ud
šawēd ō brāh ī xwaršēd*

"and when (the moon) waxes (it means) it comes to be side-be-side with
(*hamwarīh*) the sun, and it comes in the evening and is seen all night;

[again]{.underline} it wanes and returns to being side-by-side with the
sun and goes (in)to the brilliance of the sun" (*DD*.67.6)

##### *nōgānag* "newly, recently":

*čē agar ašmāh \... ēn abārīg-iz ī čiyōn-it [nōgānag]{.underline}
rasīdag bē nē hilēd \...*

"for, if you do not abandon these other (practices) as (they) have
[recently]{.underline} come to you \..." (*NM*.2.8.2; see Additional
Readings 12.3)

##### *nōgwar* "anew, again":

*ka šust bē rīyēd ayāb bē ka az-iš tan paydāg ā-š [nōgwar]{.underline}
gōmēz xwarišn u-š abāz šōyišn*

"(someone who has eaten *nasāy*,) when he defecates/urinates after he
has been washed, or except when (something) is visible (coming?) from
his body, then he should drink *gōmēz* [again]{.underline} and wash
again" (*ZFJ*, p. 515)

####  "Time" (Fr. *fois*, Germ. *Mal*)

*bār* lAB \<b'l\> "time"; in compounds

*ǰār* LwaD \<y'wl\> "time

*ēw ǰār*, *pad ēw ǰār* "once, at once, at the same time"

*harw ǰār* "every time, whenever"

*ǰārīhā* "at times,"

*ǰār ǰār* "every time, again and again"

*ǰār-ēw* "all in all, all told; once and for all, right away(?)"

#### *bār*

*ka-š gād [ēw bār]{.underline} bē dād bīm pad tan ēwar*

"when she has offered sex [once]{.underline}, (then) fear for (his) body
is certain" (*PR*.34d2)

*Wehdād pad passox guft kū ma agar az ēn hād kū agar [ēw
bār]{.underline} ō ahlāyīh taft ham hagriz bē nē afsard ham*

"Wehdād answered: perhaps it is because of this: if, [once]{.underline},
I became hot for Righteousness, I never cooled (again)" (*Dk*.6D.10)

*ka ō čand pus pad xwāstag-dārīh dahēd ēd ka pēš ud pas dahēd ud ēd ka
[pad ēw bār]{.underline} dahēd hamē hamāg-tōzišn hēnd*

"when/if he gives several sons (a part of the heritage) 'to hold as
their property', whether (*ēd ka*) he gives one before and (one) after,
or whether he gives (it) [at once]{.underline}, (then) they will always
have to pay all (of any debts owed)" (*MHD*.41.5, p. 60, ch. 23)

*az ān gyāg harw 2 [pad ēw bār]{.underline} bē dwārēnd*

"the two of them run away from that place [at once]{.underline}"
(*PR*.48.83)

*Gōšurūn čiyōn ruwān ī gāw ī ēkdād az tan ī gāw bērōn āmad pēš gāw bē
estād čand 1000 mard ka [pad ēk bār]{.underline} wāng dārēnd ō Ohrmazd
garzīd*

"Gōšurūn, that is, the soul of the Bull Established-Alone, came out of
the body of the bull, stood before the bull, and complained to Ohrmazd
as (loudly) as 1000 men when they shout [at the same time]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.4A.2)

#### *ǰār*

*zūzag pad hamēstārīh ī mōr ī dānag-keš dād estēd čiyōn gōwēd kū zūzag
[harw ǰār]{.underline} ka andar mōr āšyānag mēzēd 1000 mōr bē ōzanēd*

"the porcupine was established to oppose the grain-pulling ant; as it

*ka-š brād 2 ud xwah-ēw ān gyāg ud ān xwah abāg brād-ēw ham-bāy u-š brād

šawēnd pad čāštag ī Abarg sālār pad ān ī Mēdōmāh ham-bāyīh gōwēnd kū
ka-š ast ā-š abar ōh mānēd*

"when he has two brothers and one sister, and that sister is the partner
of one brother and the other brother has guardianship over her, and both

has it (already?), then (the property) remains with her in the usual
way" (*MHD*.25.7, p. 22 ch. 25. -- 'partner' implies sharing of

*ud ka xwāstag ō čand mard ī šahr [pad ēw ǰār]{.underline} pad xwēšīh
dahēd hamgōnag čiyōn ān-iz ī pus*

"and when he gives the property to several landsmen to be theirs [all at
once]{.underline}, (then) it is just as the (case) of the son, too"

*dēn widārīg awiš rasīd ān ī pad hāzišn ī menišn gōwišnīg ud nimāyišnīg

dēn šawēd*

"(he) to whom the *dēn* comes in passing, is the one who, when his
thought is led to it, holds on to the *dēn* in words and actions (and),

again]{.underline} (?) comes back to the *dēn*" (*Dk*.3.225.12)

*Mihrēn pad 3 ǰār [ǰār ǰār]{.underline} pad 3 bahr ēw bahr Farrox xwēš
būd guft \... xwāstag hamāg Farrox xwēš*

"three times, [every time]{.underline}, Mihrēn said one third belongs to
Farrox \... (so now) the property all belongs to Farrox" (*MHD*.H.4, p.
95, ch. 40)

*ka pēšēmāl pad hunsandīh ī ǰādaggōw ī pasēmāl dādestān ast ī
[ǰār-ēw]{.underline} az rāyēnišn hišt*

*ayāb dādwar pad hunsandīh ī ǰādaggōw ī pēšēmāl ud ǰādaggōw ī pasēmāl
ǰādaggōw ǰādaggōw ī pasēmāl [ǰār-ēw]{.underline} az gōw wisēy kunēd xūb*

"when the accuser with the agreement of the advocate of the defendant
has, [once and for all]{.underline}, left some of (*ast ī*) the

all]{.underline}, has excluded the (replacement) advocate of the
advocate of the defendant from speaking, then it is OK" (*MHD*.6.6, p.
75, ch. 30)

*čand awēšān mihr ī tō kē Ohrmazd hē čandtom ī ka bē drōzēnd wināhgār ōh
bawēnd*

*u-š guft Ohrmazd kū 6 ahlaw Zardušt ay [ǰār-ēw]{.underline} 6 gōwēd*

"How many are those contracts of yours, you who are Ohrmazd, at most,
which, when they belie them, they become 'sinners' in the usual way? ---
And Ohrmazd said: Six, Righteous Zarathustra, i.e., he says six [once
and for all/right away]{.underline}" (*PV*.4.1-2)

*ka-š mihrōdruzīh ī Mihrōg ud abārīg mardōmān Pārs pad (ān) ēwēnag āšnūd
[ǰār-ēw]{.underline} ēn handēšīd kū az kōxšišn (ī) Kerm bē abāyēd
pardaxtan*

"when (Ardaxšīr) heard about Mihrōg and the other people of Pārs
breaking their deals in that way, (then,) [right away]{.underline}, he

*pas šāhān šāh ō Māh-husrōy Anōš-husrōy framūd kū [ǰār-ēw]{.underline}
pad tis ī ēn rēdag abar rasēd 12,000 drahm ī purr dahēd*

"then the king of kings ordered M. A.: see to this young man [right

### 

### Expressions with words for "time"

> *zamān* WwaÂY , WwaÂZ \<zm'n\', dm'n\'\> "time"
>
> *zamānag* WKwaÂY , WKwaÂZ \<-k\'\> "time"
>
> *hangām* ÂEwA \<hng'm\> "time, specific time; season"
>
> *rōzgār* lAKCwL \<lwck'l\> "(passing) time; daily salary"
>
> *tāyag* WiAT \<t'yk\> "time, period" (e.g., menstrual)
>
> *gāh* aåD , saD \<g's, g'h\> "time" (of the day, etc.)

For WwaÂY, we commonly find WwaÂY\>.

#### *zamān*

The word *zamān* (*zamānag*) is used on the whole as in English.
Distinguish *zamān* used for *zaman* "hour" (below).

##### *ēn/ān zamān*:

*[ān zamān]{.underline} abāg yazdān wēš būd estād*

"at that time he was more with the gods" (*PY*.9.1c)

##### *čē zamān* "when?":

*čē zamān bē widerd*

"when did he pass?" (*KN*.4.9/3.9)

##### *(andar/pad/tā) \... zamān* "at/during/until \... time":

*tā-š sag bē nimāyišn ēdōn čiyōn [andar ān zamān]{.underline} bawēd
[ka]{.underline}-š gyān šawēd*

"until (the showing of =) one has shown it (the dead body), it is like
[during that time when]{.underline} his soul leaves" (*ŠnŠ*.2.56)

*agar ān mard [andar ēn zamān]{.underline} frāz šāyist dād Ganāg Mēnōy
ēn stahmagīh nē būd hād* \[for *hē*\]

"if it had been possible to set forth that man (who would protect
Gōšurūn) [during this time]{.underline}, the Foul Spirit would not have
had this oppression (been able to oppress the world)" (*Bd*.4A.3)

*čiyōn-iš guft pad dēn kū [andar ān zamān]{.underline} spurr-pādixšāy
bawam man kē Ohrmazd ham*

"as he said in the *dēn*: [during that time]{.underline} I shall become
a full king, I who am Ohrmazd" (*DD*.6.3)

*ud [ka]{.underline}-š 9 sāl ast [pad ān zamān]{.underline} bē pādixšāy
dād*

"and when she is nine years old, [at that time]{.underline} one is
authorized to give (her in marriage)" (*PR*.34b.2)

*ēg [abar pad ān zamān]{.underline} dēwān hanǰamanēnīd*

"then [at that time]{.underline} the demons gathered" (*Dk*.7.2.43)

*[pēš az ān zamān]{.underline} bērōn nē kerdan čim*

"why (is it) not (possible) to evict him [before that
time]{.underline}?" (*Dk*.5.24.7)

##### *andar zamān* "immediately, right away":

*ud ǰahišn ī abāyēd būdan rāy andar zamān ān kanīzag ābustan būd ud
Ardaxšīr aziš zād*

"and because what is destined must come to pass, right away, that young
woman became pregnant, and Ardaxšīr was born from her" (*KN*.2.1)

##### *ham zamān* (*pad, andar* +) "at the same time; immediately, instantaneous(ly)":

*u-š [ham zamān]{.underline} kas frēstīd (ī) Šābuhr xwānd*

"and [at the same time]{.underline} he sent someone (who) called Šābuhr"
(*KN*.14.13)

*[andar ham zamān]{.underline} kas mad kē Šābuhr ō ānōh nīd*

"[at the same time]{.underline} someone came who took Šābuhr there"
(*KN*.11.14)

*u-š urwar zahr ōwōn burd (ī) [ham zamān]{.underline} bē hōšīd*

"and he brought poison upon the plant in such a manner (that) it dried
out [immediately]{.underline}" (*Bd*.4.17)

*[pad ham zamān]{.underline} nizār ud wēmār būd ud pēm bē šud frāz
widerd*

"[at the same time]{.underline} (= right away), (the Bull) became weak
and sick, (its) milk came out, and it passed away" (*Bd*.4.20)

*čē agar-iš bē bāš [pad ham zamān]{.underline} guft ēg-iš ranǰ ud āsān
[ham zamān]{.underline} sazēd būdan*

"for if he (= Adonay) said "Be!" [instantaneously]{.underline} (= taking
only a moment), then his trouble and rest would be [right
away]{.underline}" (*ŠGW*.13.105; why did God need the sabbath?)

*šāhān šāh andar zamān rēdag ō pēš xwāst u-š guft kū*

*hunar-šāyendagīh ī tō abāyēd ka* (for *kū*) *ān šagrān rāy zīndag ō
amāh āwarēd*

*ud rēdag [pad ham zamā]{.underline}n šud*

"The king of kings summoned the boy at once and said:

'It behoves you, who are so talented, that you (all) bring Us those
lions alive!'

And the boy went [right away]{.underline}" (*Husrōy ud rēdag* 112--113;
-- note *rāy* direct object as in Persian)

##### *ēč zamān \... ma* "not for any length of time, not at all":

*[ēč zamān ma]{.underline} pāy*

"[do not]{.underline} linger [for any length time]{.underline}!"
(*KN*.10.15)

##### *čand zamān*, *čand-drahnāy zamān* "for how long?":

*abar wināh ī nasāy pad wināhgārīh niganēnīdan [čand zamān]{.underline}
agārīh (ī) zamīg (ī) andar nigān kunīhēd*

"about burying a *nasāy* intentionally: ([for) how long]{.underline} is
the earth in which it it buried useless?" (*Dk*.8.44.11)

*mardōmān-zad kū pad dādestānōmandīh zūr-zad pad a-dādestānīh tangīh-zad
pad xafag ā-š [pad čand zamān]{.underline} ā-š ān druz ī Nasuš abar
dwārēd*

"(someone) struck by men, i.e., according to the law/by justice; struck
by deceit, (i.e.) by lawlessness/injustice; struck in a tight place,
i.e., by the noose---in how much time = how long does it take (before)
the lie-demon, the Nasuš, rushes upon him?" (*PV*.7.3)

##### *dagr/dagrand zamān*, *dagr-zamānīhā* "for a long time":

*[dagr zamān]{.underline} Ohrmazd rāy yazišn ud hampursagīh ī frārōn
kunēnd*

"[for a long time]{.underline} they sacrifice to and converse with
Ohrmazd" (*AW*N.4.14)

*anōš xwar čē [dagr-zamānīhā]{.underline} ēdar rāmišn wēnē*

"drink nectar! for you shall see (experience) happiness here [for a long
time]{.underline}" (*AWN*.10.3)

[*pad zamānag* "at the proper time, when time is right"; *pad-zamānīg*
=]{.underline}

3.215.8 (4) ōy kē pad wattarīh ōstīgān pad wehīh an-ōst

pad pahrēz-azišīh hamēšag-menišn

paywand-awišīh ǰārīhā ud pad-zamānag

wisānag kār dōšišn

#### *hangām*

This often has the nuance of proper time, season (for sth.).

*ēn-iz pursīd Zarduxšt az Ohrmazd kū [hangām]{.underline} kadār ī ka
gōšt nē abāyēd xwardan*

"Z. asked Ohrmazd this too: which is the (proper) [time]{.underline}
when one should not eat meat?" (*ŠnŠSup*.17.1)

*ān kē [hangām]{.underline} nē paydāg hamē ka frāz estēd ā šāyēd*

"that (sacrifice) whose [(proper) time]{.underline} is not manifest, as
long as he 'stands forth' (continues? KK) it is appropriate"
(*Nir*.28.7)

*harw čē wiškuftag ud hu-bōy ud pad dast-warz mardōmān [hangām
hangām]{.underline} bawēd ayāb bun hamwār ast ud [pad
hangām]{.underline} wiškōfēd nōg-šāg škōfag hu-bōy \... abārīg az ēn šōn
gul xwānēnd*

"Everything that has blossoms, smells nice, and becomes (i.e., grows up)
[from season to season]{.underline} by the handiwork (i.e., cultivation)
of men or always (= permanent) has a trunk and blossoms [in (its own)
season]{.underline} (with) with new branches, blossoms, fragrant \...
and the other (growing thing) of this sort, they call 'flowers'"
(*Bd*.16.13)

##### *pad hangām ī* 'at the time of":

*[pad hangām]{.underline} ī zāyišn šīr abāz ō pestān āyēd kē padiš
frazend parwālēd čiyōn hamāg šīr az tōhm ī narān bawēd*

"[at the time]{.underline} of birth, the milk comes back to the breasts,
by which (the mother) suckles the child; for all milk comes from the
males' seed" (*Bd*.15.5b)

##### *hangāmīhā* "according/at to the (right) time(s)":

*ēwēn zīndag-ruwān framūdan hangōšīdag sidōš ēdōn niyābag kū \...
ātaxš-ēw andar yazišn rōšnīhēd [hangāmīhā]{.underline} bōy ī pāk
bōyīhēd*

"ordering the *zende-ruvān* ritual is like the *sidōš*; it is fitting
that a fire is lit during the sacrifice and that clean fragrant
(firewood) is made to exude fragrance [at (all) the right
times]{.underline}" (*DD*.80.12)

#### *rōzgār*

This often implies passing time or specific times within a passing time,
e.g., seasonal festivals.

It also means "(daily) salary."

*windišn ī az sālārān nē [andar zamān]{.underline} bē [pad
rōzgār]{.underline} \... ēmēdēnišn*

"one should hope for gaining (something) from the chiefs [not right
away]{.underline}, but [over time]{.underline}" (*Dk*.6E.43d)

*Rašn rōz [rōzgār]{.underline} sabuk ud harw kār ī kāmē kerdan andar
frārōnīh kun*

"On the day of Rašn, the [time]{.underline} is easy (?), and every
activity you wish to do, do it in 'goodness'" (*AAM*.136)

*Wazurg-mihr Bōxtagān abar awēšān sālār kerd ud [rōzgār-ēw
wizīdag]{.underline} pad nēk ǰahišn ud yazdān hayārīh ō Hindūgān
frēstād*

"he made Wazurg-mihr son of Bōxtag their headman and sent him to India
[at a chosen time]{.underline} with good omen and the help of the gods"
(*WČ*.33)

*Mardak anšahrīg rāy ōwōn nibišt kū pad nazdist azišmānd
[rōzgār]{.underline} and-čand dādestān rāyēnīdan rāy andar abāyēd abārīg
bē abespārišn*

"regarding a slave, Mardak wrote as follows: at the first 'obstruction'
(of justice), as much of [the daily salary]{.underline} as is needed for
managing the procedure (is deducted from it?), the rest must be handed
over" (*MHD*.22.6, ch. 7)

*[andar rōzgārān]{.underline} pad wēš-gīrišnīh ī gētīyīg zōr saxwan-šnās
bawēd frāz-raftār*

"[with time/as time goes by]{.underline}, (the child), by acquiring more
of the strength of this world, gets to know talking and walking)
(*WZ*.31.1)

#### *tāyag*

This often has the nuance of "(prescribed) time period, waiting period."
It is often spelled *tāyag* WiAWT as if *tuhīg*.

*ud ka pus 2 duxt-ēw ud pid ān gyāg; pus harw 2 ud pid [pad ēw
tāyag]{.underline} mīrēnd pusarān ǰud ǰud handōxt ī xwēš 1 drahm ast ud
pid xwāstag 75 bawēd*

"and when (there are) two sons and one daughter and a father in that
place; both sons and the father die [within one (short period of?)
time]{.underline}; the amassed (wealth) belonging to the sons,
individually, is one *drahm* and the property of the father is 85
(*drahms*) \..." (*MHD*.B.2, p. 81, ch. 33)

*čē-m stāyišn ān kāmag ī [pad xwēš pāyag ud tāyag]{.underline}*

"for that is my wish: a praise [according to my own position and
time]{.underline} (in service?)" (*DD*.0.11)

*u-š pad harg ud bār pad grawagān dāštan [tā ān tāyag]{.underline} guft
ka abām bē wizārēd*

"and (the thing lent) is assigned (*guft*) to him (the lender, for him)
to keep as security for duties and expenses [until that
time]{.underline} when (= until such time as) (the borrower) pays back
the loan" (*MHD*.33.19, p. 40, ch. 18)

The lender has the right to any profit from the item (animal, piece of
land, etc.) lent to the borrower.

*[ka]{.underline}-š [ka]{.underline} tāyag padiš bē šud tis ān rasēd ī-š
bē šustan nē tuwān ā-š dast ōh šōyišn u-š wāz ōh gīrišn*

"when (= if) ---when [the]{.underline} (waiting) [period]{.underline}
has passed for her (*-š \... padiš*) --- something (some menstrual
matter) arrives that she cannot wash off (because of what she is doing),
then (when she is free) she should wash the hands in the usual way and
she should take the *bāǰ* in the usual way" (*PV*.16.11E)

[*wisānag* "exceptionally"(?)]{.underline}

*Dk*.3.215.9

#### *āwām* "age" (of the world):

*[āwām]{.underline} pad hu-xwadāyīh ud hu-dēnīh dānāgīh ud dād wirāstag
hambāstag mardōm kāmag-zīyišnīh bōxtagīh abērtar bawēd*

"knowledge and law having been reetablished by good rule and adherence
to the Good Dēn, (then) [the age]{.underline} will be more (about) all
people's living (as long/well as) they wish and salvation" (*Dk*.3.66.3)

*ka ōy mad kē abē-bandīh ud an-aybiyāghanīh pad dād framūd škefttar ud
garāntar seǰ [andar āwām]{.underline} ōwōn paydāgīhist*

"when *he* came who ordered lack of bondedness and girdedness to be
legal, a more fierce and heavier affliction was thus revealed i[n (that)
age]{.underline}" (*DD*.38.24a)

*[andar āwām āwām]{.underline} ō harw kē rāy baxt estēd čiyōn ān ī
abāyēd madan abar rasēd*

"[in age after age]{.underline}, whatever ought come to him to whom it
has been allotted will come" (*MX*.26.11)

#### *ǰāwēdān*, *ǰāwēdānīg*; *fraškerdīg* "for ever and ever"

These two adjectives are used in legal and similar texts about
situations that are supposed to last forever:

*hamē-zīndag ī petyāragōmand ǰāwēdān-dard*

"living forever with the Adversary is eternal pain" (*DD*.36.29a)

*ka gōwēd kū-m ēn xānag pad mānišn dāštan ō tō dād
[ǰāwēdānīg]{.underline} pad xwēšīh dād bawēd*

"if he says: I have given you this house to be yours to dwell in, (then)
it is given to be his own [forever]{.underline}" (*MHD*.24.13, Macuch,
chap. 10)

*ēwāz ahlāyīh nām [fraškerdīg]{.underline} ud kunišn ī frārōn pad ēč kas
appurdan nē tuwān*

"only Righteousness (and a good) name [last until the
Renovation]{.underline}, and good deeds can be taken from nobody"
(*AWM*.3) -- Note *pad* instead of common *az*.

*kē-š xwēš anšahrīg gād pad xwēš estēd [fraškerdīg]{.underline}-iz bē
pādixšāy dādan*

"someone who has had sex with his own servant---she remains his
property(?)---(and) he is authorized to give her (in marriage to someone
else) [to last until the Renovation]{.underline}" (*ZFJ*, p. 592)

*ka gōwēd kū-m tā 10 sāl ayāb gōwēd kū-m pas az 10 sāl bahr ī pusīh rāy
ēn xwāstag ō tō dād bahr ī pusīh [fraškerdīg]{.underline} dād bawēd*

"when (the testator) says: I have given this property for ten years or
he says (I shall have given this property) after ten years to you as the
share for being (my) son, then it shall (thereby) be given [to last
until the Renovation]{.underline}" (*MHD*.41.18, Macuch, chap. 23)

#### *sazišnīg*, *frasāwand* "transient"; *asazišn(īg)* intransient" 

Literally, "sth. that is bound to pass."

*xīr ī gētīy hamāg [sazišnīgīh]{.underline} ud wardišnīgīh*

"things of this world are all [something that will pass]{.underline} and
change" (*AWM*.2)

*ud gētīy ast kanāragōmand ud [sazišnīg]{.underline} ud kāhišnīg ān ī
asar-rōšnīh ast [asazišnīg]{.underline} akāhišnīg*

"and this world is something (*ast*) limited, bound to pass, and bound
to diminish; the Endless Light is something that will not pass and not
diminish" (*DD*.30.19)

*šādīh ī ōstīgān [a-sazišn]{.underline} gētīyīg šādīh ī ō mēnōyīg urwāhm
paywastag*

*ān ī an-ōst ud [sazišnīg]{.underline} gētīyīg šādīh ī az mēnōyīg rāmišn
brīdag*

*ud bēš ī ōstīgān gētīyīg bēš ō mēnōyīg pīm paywastag*

*ud ān ī [sazišnīg]{.underline} gētīyīg bēš ī az mēnōyīg pīm brīdag*

"the stable joy [that does not pass]{.underline} is the joy in this
world that is connected to the bliss in the other world;

the instable (joy) [that does pass]{.underline} is the joy in this world
that is cut off from the happiness in the other world;

and the stable suffering is the suffering in this world that is
connected to the pain in the other world;

and the suffering [that does pass]{.underline} is the suffering in this
world that is cut off from the pain in the other world" (*Dk*.3.323.2-3)

*u-šān ēn-iz ōwōn dāšt kū mard ān farroxtar kē ēn xīr ī gētīy (ī) ēdōn
[frasāwand]{.underline} andar ō ān ī [afrasāwand]{.underline} gumēzēd kū
ka az gētīy sazēd pad mēnōy bawēd*

"and they held this too: that man is the most fortunate who mingles
these matters of this world that are so [transient]{.underline} with
that which is [intransient]{.underline} that, when he passes from this
world, he will be in that world" (*Dk*.6.180)

#### *drang* "period, duration, while" 

*ud mardōmān xwāstag xrad ud pānag xēm ud hambār kerbag weh čē ēdar
[drang]{.underline} andak ēwarz zūd*

"and for humans (their) property is wisdom, their protection is
'character', what they have stored up is good good deeds, for [the
duration]{.underline} here is short, the journey (hence) soon"
(*Dk*.6A.6c)

*u-š [drang]{.underline} ī andar gētīy pad dahišnān petyāragīh 6000 sāl
paydāg*

"and its (= the Mixture) [duration]{.underline} in this world with
opposition to the creations is manifest (from the *dēn* to be) 6000
years" (*Dk*.3.329.7)

*[andar drang]{.underline}-iz 9 hazangrōzim ān ī padiš wanīyīhēd xwad
druz*

"[in the period]{.underline} of nine centuries (= during the 9-century
period) is also the one in which the Lie herself will be destroyed"
(*DD*.36.9)

*ud abardom ēwēnag az dādār wisp-āgāhīh rāyēnīdārīh ud wisp-tuwānīhā ōz*

*[andar drang]{.underline} ī ō fraškerd hangām druzīh hamāg
anabāz-bawišnīg wišuftan*

*bun druz anabāz did ārāyišnīg abesistan weh-dēn āgāhīh*

"and the supreme kind (of counterattack comes) from the Creator's
omniscience, his organizing, and his strength (wielded) with
omnipotence:

[during the period]{.underline} (leading) up to the Renovation, to rout
the entire Lie-demonhood (so that it) will not again come into
existence; to cut off the original Lie (so that it) will not again a
second time (be able) to organize (her army?);

(thus is) the awareness from the Good *dēn*."

(*Dk*.3.162.12) --- About how Spenāg Mēnōy counters the attacks of the
Lie.

##### *drang kerdan* "to linger, tarry":

*ud nā-kām-tazišnīhā rawēnd abāz estād ud [drang kerdan]{.underline} nē
hilēnd*

and (the souls) go unwillingly; they do not permit them to stop (and
remain) behind or [linger]{.underline}" (*DD*.20.7)

##### *-drang* "duration, (for) the duration of"

This means the same as *-drahnāy* (*-dranāy*) \[Lesson 13\], but is
quite rare:

#### 

*[andar drang]{.underline}-iz (ī) 9 hazangrōzim ān ī padiš wanīyīhēd
xwad druz*

"\... and [during the period of]{.underline} nine centuries---those in
which the Lie herself will be destroyed" (*Dk*.36.9)

*ka ān mard 30 sālag bawēd ān xwaršēd bē estēd pad bālist ī āsmān [10
rōz- 10 šab-drang]{.underline}*

"when that man (= Z.) is thirty years old, yonder sun will stand (still)
at the highest of the sky [for]{.underline} (the duration of) [ten days
and ten nights]{.underline}" (*Dk*.7.8.58)

*xwaršēd az ān ī ka axtar-ēw bē hilēd tā ān ī did bē ayābēd
[mayān-drang]{.underline} and-čand mard-ēw sag-ēw abar stānēd bē wihēd*

"from the time the sun leaves a 'house' until it reaches (it) again,
[the time in between]{.underline} is as much as (when) a man picks up a
stone and throws it" (*Bd*.2.22)

*ēk ēwēnag [huzārag-drangīg]{.underline} pattūdan*

"\... (that) one kind of (contrary forces) lasts (only) [for a little
while]{.underline}" (*Dk*.3.142.4)

#### *tay-ā-tay* "continuously"

*9-šabag dāštan sāmān ēn kū pas šustan ī-š pad pišag 3 rōz-šabān
[tay-ā-tay]{.underline} bē pāyišn ud ēk bār bē šōyišn*

"the scope of keeping the '9-night' (period) is this: after washing with
the knotted stick, one should wait 3 days and nights
[continuously]{.underline} and (then) wash once" (*REA*.34.2)

*3 šabān-rōz nē pādixšāy nigerēd rōz ī čahārom ā-š bē nigerēd ka pāk ā-š
tāyag gīrišn az ān frāz*

*ēw šabān-rōz [tay-ā-tay]{.underline} bē pāyišn u-š pas bē šōyišn pāk*

"for three nights and days he does not look (at her to see if there is
still blood); on the fourth day he looks at her: if she is clean, she
should take the *tāyag* from then on; she should wait for one night and
day [continuously]{.underline}, and then she should wash, (and she is)
clean" (*ZFJ*, p. 583)

#### *rōz-šabān*, *rōzān-šabān*, *šabān-rōz*, *šabān-rōzān* "day and night, night and day = 24 hrs."

*awēšān dēn dastwarān ud haft xwahān [7 rōz-šabān]{.underline} pad ātaxš
hamēšag-sōz ud bōy-wizarāg nīrang ī dēnīg Abestāg ud zand bē guft ud
nask yašt ud gāhān srūd ud pad tārīk pās dāšt hēnd*

"for seven days and nights, those *dastwar*s of the Dēn and the seven
sisters recited formulas from the Dēn, Avestan and Zand, chanted the
Gathas, and kept vigil during darkness" (*AWN*.2.17) -- Note the
Persian-type past tenses without ergative.

*čiyōn tan kāmag kū kāmagīhā [pad rōz šab]{.underline} bē xufsēd ān ī
ruwān kāmag ka (pad) tan [rōzān-šabān]{.underline} xrad ī ahlawān
xwāhēnd*

Just as the body's wish is that it may sleep [at day and at
night]{.underline} as it wishes, (thus) the soul's wish, when (= as long
as) it is in the body, is to seek, [day and night]{.underline}, the
wisdom of the Righteous" (WZ.30.45)

*pursišn* ∵ *mardōm ēw kē dandān frōd šawēd tā čand āb nē abāyēd
xwardan*

*passox* ∵ *čiyōn man dānam [šabān-rōz]{.underline} ēw*

"Q.: a person whose toth (comes loose) and goes down (he swallows it),
for how long should ne not drink water"

A.: As far as I know, [for one night-and-day]{.underline}" (*RAF*.49)

### Compounds with numerals

Compounds indicating number of days, etc., have various meanings
depending on the contexts:

\-*rōzag* period of X days, enough for X days

*-šabag* period of X nights

*-māhag* period of X months

*-sālag* X years old, X-year-old

*az pōryōtkēšān weh-dēn-nigēzīg gōwišn*

*ōy nēk kē hamē nēk u-š tan drīst abar xwēš tan pādixšāy u-š pihw ī
[ēw-rōzag]{.underline} nē zad estēd*

"from the speech of the teachers of old containint the teachings of the
Dēn: he is well who is always well and his body healthy, in charge of
his own body, and food [for one day]{.underline} has not been 'struck'
(diminished) for him" (*Dk.*3.245.3)

*pursēd kū pad xānag (ī) mardōm ka widerān bawēd*

*andar [3-šabag]{.underline} gōšt tāzag čē rāy ka nē xwarēnd ud ka
xwarēnd čē ǰuttarīh bawēd*

"you ask why it is it, when someone dies in people's houses, when, for
[a three-night period]{.underline}, they do not eat fresh meat, and when
they do eat, what is different?" (*Handarz ī dastwarān ō weh-dēnān* 34)

*zan ī ābustan [az ēw-māhag tā 10-māhag]{.underline} ka-š zāyišn zamān
gumānīg kū-š andar aškamb murd estēd āb xwardan*

"a pregnant woman, [from the first to the tenth month]{.underline}, when
her delivery is in doubt whether there is a dead fetus in her womb, is
(allowed) to drink water (even though the sacred water might then come
in contact with *nasāy*)" (*ZFJ*, p. 467)

*u-š pas wād brēhēnīd pad mard kerb ī ǰuwān ī [15-sālag]{.underline}*

"and then he fashioned the wind in the form of a
[15-year-old]{.underline} young man" (*Bd.*1a.5)

#### *zaman* "hour"

This word is occasionally confused with *zamān*.

*ān 3 panǰag ī mādagwar az xwēškārīh nē muštan*

*tuwān-tuxšāgīhā kerbag andar warzīdan*

*ud xwurdag-iz ī [zaman]{.underline} ī aziš az kerbag nē tuhīgēnīdan*

*ud pad-iz abārōn bazag mēnōy ān [zaman]{.underline} nē bēšīdan*

"those three principal pentads are not to be 'wiped clean' of doing
one's duties,

(rather) good deeds are to be performed during (them) as diligently as
possible;

and, one is not to empty even a small (part) of [the hour]{.underline}
of them;

and one is also not to harm the divine (model) of that
[hour]{.underline} with evil bad deeds" (*Dk*.3.259.5)

*ōš ī mardōmān [andar harw zaman zaman]{.underline} frāz rasēd*

*bīm ēwāz pad ān gāh ī ka ōš frāz rasēd ēg mard tis ī abārōn hamē menēd*

*ōh-iz pēš az ān (ī) mard frārōn-kunišn bawēd ēg ruwān dušmen bē bawēd*

"death of men arrives [at every and any hour]{.underline}; fear arrives
only at the time when, when death arrives, then a man keeps thinking
something bad; and thus, (even) before he becomes a man doing good
deeds, he becomes an enemy of (his) soul" (*Dk*.6.236)

*spāsdār ham az dādār ī weh ī abzōnīg ī menōyān ud gētīyān mahist ī
ka(-š) frāz brēhēnīd tō Hordad \...*

*kē ēč gyānōmandān aziš ǰud [ēw zamān]{.underline} pattūdan nē tuwān*

"I am grateful to the good Creator, who makes increase, greatest among
those in this and that worlds, that (*ī ka*) he fashioned forth Hordad
\...

without whom (*kē \... aziš ǰud*) none of beings with souls can last for
[an hour]{.underline}" (*StS*.6.2)

# Texts 19

#### Text 19.1

From the *Ardā Wirāz-nāmag*: *AWN*.38.1-3. -- Mss. K20 f. 16r, M51b f.
173r, pict. 47. -- About polluting the fire, water, and people with
*hixr* and *nasāy*.

![](media/image116.jpeg){width="3.875in" height="2.2083333333333335in"}

![](media/image117.jpeg){width="3.0833333333333335in"
height="2.3055555555555554in"}

#### Text 19.2

From the *Zand ī pargard ī J̌ud-dēw-dād*: *ZFJ*.515--6. --- Ms. TD2, pp.
516--6. -- About a pregnnant woman eating *nasāy*.

![](media/image118.jpeg){width="4.0in" height="2.1805555555555554in"}

![](media/image119.jpeg){width="3.5in" height="2.9722222222222223in"}

*ka zan ābustan (nasāy) xwarēd ōy aburnāyīg ēg-išān dādestān čiyōn •*

*ka-š nē [hangām]{.underline} ī zād u-š bīm ī rēš ī pad aburnāyīg nēst
šustan pādixšāy*

*ud aburnāyīg-iz pad xward dārišn*

*nasāy paymānag hambun-iz ān bawēd ka mizag-iš dānēd ayāb ōbārēd*

*ka-š [hangām]{.underline} ī zād ayāb pad aburnāyīg* \[516\] *rēš bawēd
[ō-nūn]{.underline} nē pādixšāy šustan*

*ud ka bē zād ayāb ō tuwānīgīh rasīd ā-š ōh šōyišn*

*aburnāyīg [ō-nūn]{.underline} a-tuwānīgīh rāy pad gōmēz ud āb šōyišn*

*pišag-šnās bawēd ayāb ō 7-sālagīh rasīd ā-š pad pišag šōyišn tā*

*tā ō 7-sālagīh ayāb pišag-šnāsīh rasēd pādixšāy ka-š nē pahrēzēnd*

*hamē tā 9-šabag bē dāšt ōh pahrēzišn*

*ud aburnāyīg ka pišag-šnās bawēd ayāb ō 7-sālagīh rasēd ā-š pad gyāg
Nasuš abar dwārēd*

#### Text 19.3

From the Pahlavi Rivāyat (*PR*.25.1-6). Mss. BL ff. 38v-39r, Tc, pp.
79-80. -- Z. asks Ohrmazd how much longer it will take until Renovation
and is upset when Ohrmazd tells him 3000 years. Ohrmazd comforts him.

![](media/image120.jpeg){width="3.8194444444444446in"
height="3.875in"}![](media/image121.jpeg){width="3.888888888888889in"
height="1.3472222222222223in"}

![](media/image122.jpeg){width="3.6805555555555554in"
height="1.4166666666666667in"}![](media/image123.jpeg){width="3.8055555555555554in"
height="4.208333333333333in"}

*ahlāyīh ēdōn sahīg ud wazurg ud arzōmand ī gyāg ēw paydāg kū Zardušt az
Ohrmazd pursīd kū*

*čand zamān abāz ō  ān fraškerd zamān kū  fraškerd-kerdārīh bawēd ud
tan ī pasēn ∵*

*Ohrmazd \[Tc80\] guft kū 3000 sāl Zardušt*

*Zardušt bē grīst u-š guft kū  zamān dagrand abāz ast*

*Ohrmazd guft kū ēn zamān u-t  dagrand ma ē sahēd*

*čē ruwān ī  ahlawān tā  andar Garōdmān hēnd ā-šān ēn-and zamān ī 3000
sāl ā-šān and drahnāy pad čašm*

*u-š ēdōn xwār sahēd čiyōn kanīzag ēw abāyišnīg ī 15-sālag ud mard-ēw ī
ǰuwān ī wīst-sālag*

*ka-šān ēk abāg did andar ō xānag ēw kunēnd*

*u-šān pad wastarg ī narm bē xwābēnd \[BL39r\]*

*ud mērag ō ziyānag pad gyān dōšāram*

*u-šān ān abāyēd kū ān šab haguriz rōšn ma bawād*

*awēšān-iz kē ahlaw hēnd andar Garōdmān ā-šān xwašīh ud rāmišn rāy ī-šān
ast*

*ā-šān ān abāyēd kū haguriz ān zamān nē rasē* ∵

#### Text 19.4

From the *Mādayān ī hazār dādestān*: *MHDA*.5.35 (p. 23, ch. MM., p.
170). -- About timing in legal contexts.

![](media/image124.jpeg){width="5.5in" height="2.861111111111111in"}

*ka gōwēd kū tā ēw* \[ms. *ēd*\] *sāl ēn tis ōwōn kunam;*

*agar tis az ān ī ka-š ēd abar nē gōwēd ēg-iš hamāg abāyēd kerdan andar
ēw sāl hamē ōh kunišn.*

*ud agar tis az ān ī ka-š ēd sāl abar nē gōwēd ēg-iš [ēw
ǰār]{.underline} kunišn andar-iz ēw sāl [ēw ǰār]{.underline} kunišn*

*čiyōn ka gōwēd kū war warzam u-š [ēw ǰār]{.underline} warzišn ayāb
gōwēd kū kār ī tō kunam u-š hamāg ōh kunišn*

"when one says: by this year I shall deal with this matter just as
(necessary?);

if he says nothing about when he (shall have taken care of it), then he
must take care of all of it, and it must be done within one year;

and if says nothing about *when* during this year, then he must do it
[once]{.underline} (= some time?) and [once]{.underline} within one
year;

just as when one says: I shall swear an oath, and he must do it
[once]{.underline}, or he says: I shall do this work of yours, and he
must do it all in the usual way (= as promised?)"

#  Additional readings 19

#### Additional reading 19.1

From the *Dēnkard*: *Dk*.6.200. -- Ms. B, p. \[404\], K43 ff. 209r-v.

![](media/image125.jpeg){width="4.0in" height="2.0416666666666665in"}

![](media/image126.jpeg){width="4.125in" height="0.8055555555555556in"}

![](media/image127.jpeg){width="4.125in" height="2.486111111111111in"}

*u-šān ēn-iz ōwōn dāšt kū xwār / xīr ī gētīy*

*čē andar ēw rōz šāyēd būd ka mard / (ī) fradāg drust ud kārīgar ud
dūr-ēmēd*

*pēš az [6 zaman]{.underline} wēmār ud akārag ud anēmēd estēd ud pēš az
šabān mīrēd*

*ud ast-iz ī rōz ī didīgar nē bawēd ka bē zamīg gumēxtēd xāk bawēd*

*mardōmān ōwōn handēšišn kū*

*šāyēd būd ka ān mard man ham u-m pad ān ēwēnag awiš rasēd*

*ud pas-iz xīr ī gētīy čē rāy frāybūdīhā abar tuxšēm*

It happens that a man who yesterday was healthy, active, and with hopes
for a distant (future),

and within [six hours]{.underline} is sick, inactive, and without hope
and dies before night time,

And sometimes it is not yet the next day when he is mixed with earth and
becomes dust.

People should think as follows:

"Perhaps I am that man and it will happen to me just like that!

So then, why do I strive for things of this world so it will be more?"

#### Additional reading 19.2

From the *Dēnkard*: *Dk*.6D.4. -- Ms. B, p. \[452\].

![](media/image128.jpeg){width="4.819444444444445in"
height="4.305555555555555in"}

*gōwēnd kū Husrōy Anōšag-ruwān guft kū*

*ēn 3 wāzag wāzag xwadāyān pāduxšāyān tuwānīgān abārīg-iz harw kas bē
šnāxtan ud kār az-iš kerdan awizīrišnīgīhā andar abāyēd •*

*ēk frasāwandīh bē šnāxtan • ud ēk ēr-menišnīh • ud ēk hunsandīh ∵*

*čē pad šnāsagīh ī frasāwandīh ī xwēš bē šnāxtan (ī) ān ī [andar-iz ēk
rōz-šabān]{.underline} bē šāyēd madan*

*ud pad ēr-menišnīh xwēš menišn pad ēn warm bē kunēd kū*

*ān-iz ī / duščihrtom \[duščihrtom\] anāgīh ī andar gēhān ast \<wsm\>
šāyēd burdan ō-iz man šāyēd madan*

*pad hunsandīh ka-š anāgīh ī pad ān ēwēnag awiš rasēd ī čārag xwāstan nē
šāyēd*

*kāmagīhā pad-iš hunsand bawēd ud wad dōgānag bē nē kunēd*

*ēk ān ī az anāgīh ī frāz rasēd • ud ēk ān ī az ahunsandīh*

*guft estēd kū*

*kē pad ān ī mad estēd hunsand ēg-iš niyāz nē paydāg*

*čē kē hunsand tuwānīg ud kē pen-āmār ačārag*

*abar pahlom ud wattom / āwām nišān daxšag ud bar ī harw \*dō* \[ms.
\<ALBA\> *čahār*\]

*az nigēz ī weh-dēn* ∵ *hād /*

*āwām pahlom \*hangerdīg pad nišān āsnūdagīh ī frayist mardōm xēm pad /
frahang (ī) ān (ī) ērān dēn*

*u-š bar wirāstagīh payrāstagīh ī āwām pad / dānāgīh ud hammis hunar ud

# Lesson 20

# Grammar 20

## the Verb. 

## Politeness expressions with *framūdan*

*ān ī[-tān framūd nibištan]{.underline} abar ayāsišn ī ō ham-wēnišnīh ud
ham-pursišnīh ī man mihrbānagīh ud dēn-dōstīh ī xwad* "that which (as
for that fact that) you wrote about longing for seeing one another and
asking one another, (that was) your own friendliness and love of the
*dēn*" (DD.0.4)

### Constructions with *dāštan* expressing state resulting from a previous event

The verb *dāštan* "have, hold, keep" is sometimes found in constructions
reminiscent of the English perfect "I have done," but the use is
restricted to a certain set of verbs, those that can express a state, It
is found with past participles and perfect participles in *-ag*, e.g.:

##### With a past participle:

*Srid abar šud ō wēšag dīd hēnd wasān parīgān kē-šān zafr [wišād
dāšt]{.underline} u-šān abar xrōsīd\* kū ōzan ma abaxšāy*

"Srid went to the thicket, (where) he saw many witches who kept their
mouths wide open and howled: Kill (the bull)! Have no pity!"

*mēnōy ī āsmān artēštār homānāg baxt kē ayōšustēn zrēy [paymōxt
dārēd]{.underline}*

'the divine sky was \$\$ like a warrior who has on a metal armor"

ud ka būd pad dād ī haft kišwarān ā-š\* [paymōxt dāšt]{.underline} kb'h
ī az 7 pōst kē-š xwarrah ī 7 amahrspandān padiš būd \$\$

*u-š āsmān pad ēwēnag ī warr-ēw [nihuft dāšt]{.underline}*

"and he wore the sky like a piece of clothing"

##### With a perfect participle:

*2 šagr āmad kē \*asp-ramagān az gyāg ī xwēš [spōxtag
dār]{.underline}*[ēd]{.underline}

*xwēš-tan pad brahmag xwarāsānīg [ārāstag]{.underline} dāšt*
(*KN*.9.1/8.2)

### *dārēd* expressing "being in a place"

This usage is also in modern Persian.

*mayān ēn zrēy ī Frāxkerd ud ān ī Pūydīg pahlūg-ēw [zrēy
dārēd]{.underline} kē war ī Sadwēs xwānēnd* "between this Fraxkerd Sea
and Pūytīg Sea, to one side [a lake is situated]{.underline} that they
call Lake Sadwēs" (*Bd*.10.9)

## conjunctions 1. Coordinating

### Connecting conjunctions

> *ud*, *u-* W , cÅ \<W, AP̄-\> "and (then)"
>
> *ham \... ham* "both \... and"
>
> *ēd ī \... ēd ī* "both \... and, whether \... or"
>
> *ay* Ä \<'y\> "that is"
>
> *ā-* --A \<'-\> "then"
>
> *ān* ã \<ZK\> "therefore"
>
> *-iz* C \<-c\> "also, as well, even"

*ud* "and, then"

This conjunction is mostly coordinating, but is sometimes used to
introduce the main clause after a subordinate clause, in which case it
may be translated as "then" or left out in the translation. Sometimes
one has the impression that the conjunction only has the function of
supporting an enclitic pronoun.

*ka ō ānōh frāz mad ham u-m dīd ān ī widardagān ruwān*

"when I came to that place I saw the souls of the departed"(AW)

*ka-šān nišast abar abārīg ruwānān u-šān kerbag asmān-bālāy estād*

"when they sat above the other souls their good deeds stood as high as
the sky" (AW)

*ham \... (ud) ham*

*[ham]{.underline} ān ī wahārān bar [ud ham]{.underline} ān ī zamestān
bar [ud ham-iz]{.underline} az ān ī hāmīn pādēz bar ī was-ēwēnag ud purr
sūd ī was-nēkīh kē [ham]{.underline} hangad [ham]{.underline} driyōš
aziš zīyišn dārišn*

(*StS*.7.4)

*harw 2 mihr ast [ham]{.underline} abar ahlawān ud [ham]{.underline}
abar druwandān*

"he contract belongs to both: [both]{.underline} upon the Righteous
[and]{.underline} upon the wicked" (*AWN*.52.3)

*ka pēšēmāl pad tōzišnōmandīh gugāh ēw abāg ayāb dō ud pasēmāl nakkīrāy
war kē warzišn ∵*

*ka az kustag ēw gugāh ēw az kustag ēw dārišn war kē warzišn ∵*

*pad harw dō dādestān pēšēmāl weh-dādestāntar [ud ham]{.underline} ān kē
nakkīrāy [ud ham]{.underline} ān kē dārišn abāg*

*[ham]{.underline} xwad pad war warzišn [ud ham]{.underline} pad war
abāz ō pasēmāl dāštan*

(*RAF*.72)

*ēd ī \... ēd ī*

*Dk*.3.82.5

*kūnmarz wēš-grāyīh rāy [ēd ī]{.underline} pēš [ēd ī]{.underline} pas
ēwtom*

"because anal intercourse is such a 'heavy' sin, [both the
one]{.underline} in front [and the one]{.underline} in back is one and
the same" (*REA*.29.8)

#### *-iz*

We are quite familiar by now with this enclitic particle. Not that it
can also be used with negations and sometimes in slightly unusual ways,
e.g:

*ka abar nē wārēd ān ī sūdīmand wārān ī az tō Tištar rādīhā
abar-wārišnīh*

*ēg-išān [nē]{.underline} zargōnīh bawēd ī tāg warg \...
[nē-iz]{.underline} bar bowandag xwālom sazāgwār ī xwaš-mizag*

"when that profitable rain (coming) from your generously raining it
down, o Tištar, does not rain,

then branch (nor) leaf will [not]{.underline} have (any) greenness,
[nor]{.underline} (any) sweet, suitable, sweet-tasting fruit"
(*StS*.13.5)

*ka pad kafš ud šalwār murd čiyōn* ∵ *kafš ud šalwār rēman band pāk •*

*ka pad šalwār bun band ī kafš murd estēd [kafš-iz šalwār]{.underline}
rēman*

"How is it when he died with shoes and trousers? -- The shoes and
trousers are polluted, the band is clean.

When he is dead with the trousers and the bottom band of the shoes? --
[both shoes and trousers]{.underline} are polluted" (*ZFJ*, p. 511) --
The exact reality of the description escapes us.

*abar astīh ī harw dō azabar ān gugāyīh gugāy*

*az-išān yazdān [mānāg-iz]{.underline} dānāg dēw ud druz mānāg ī
duš-āgāh mardōmīhā*

"about the existence of both (gods and demons) is a witness superior to
the above (two) testimonies:

of them (= the two), [similar]{.underline} to the gods (is)
[also]{.underline} the knowledgeable one, and similar to the Druz are
various people with bad awarenes" (*Dk*.3.123.43)

### Disjunctive

*ayāb* WPwïÅ \<'dwp\'\> "or"

*ayāb \... ayāb* "either \... or"

#### *ayāb \... ayāb*

*yazišn mayānag nē bawēd [ayāb]{.underline} ō yazdān [ayāb]{.underline}
ō dēwān rasēd*

"there is no middle (regarding) the sacrifice: it goes
[either]{.underline} to the gods [or]{.underline} to the demons"
(*ŠnŠ*.9.5)

*ǰumbišn dō ēwēnag bawēd [ayāb]{.underline} kāmīg čiyōn az mardōm
[ayāb]{.underline} čihrīg čiyōn az ātaxš*

"movement is two kinds: [either]{.underline} by will, as by people,
[or]{.underline} by nature, as by the fire" (*Dk*.3.147.5)

*ān dō [ayāb]{.underline} harw 2 hāwand-pāyag [ayāb]{.underline} ēk meh
ud ēk keh ud pāyag menēnd xwēš tan*

"those two consider themselves [either]{.underline} both of the same
rank or one greater and one lesser" (*Dk*.3.381.7)

*ka-š Nasuš abar abāz dwārēd ā-š čē kunišn kē pāk abāz bawēd •*

*[ayāb]{.underline}-iš yōǰdahrgar hušnūd kunišn [ayāb]{.underline}-iš
abāz šōyēd*

"when the Nasuš rushes upon him again, then what should he do so that
(for *kū*) he becomes clean again? --- he should [either]{.underline}
satisfy the purifier [or]{.underline} one washes him again" (*ZFJ*, p.
643)

#### *če \... čē* "whether \... or"

*ka mard-ēw xwāstag pad stūrīh ī xwēš paydāg kerd ud pad dāštan harw 2
sāl ēw sāl ō Farrox ēw sāl ō Mihrēn dād Farrox Mihrēn ǰud ǰud pad ān
xwāstag* yō hē pascaētā \[Av. 'he who (remains) after him"\] *ōh bawēd*

*čē ēd-iz pādixšāy ka bē ō zanān dahēd*

(*MHD*.37.39, p. 47, ch. 19)

#### *ēd kē \... ēd kē* "whether \... or"

*ka ō čand pus pad xwāstag-dārīh dahēd [ēd ka]{.underline} pēš ud pas
dahēd [ud ēd ka]{.underline} pad ēw bār dahēd hamē hamāg-tōzišn hēnd*

"when/if he gives several sons (a part of the heritage) 'to hold as
their property', [whether]{.underline} he gives one before and (one)
after, [or whether]{.underline} he gives (it) at once, (then) they will
always have to pay all (of any debts owed)" (*MHD*.41.5, p. 60, ch. 23)
