## Phraseology

### Expressions of Place, Direction, and Place or Time

### "here, there, where"

> *ēdar* nMtÒ \<LTME\> "here"
>
> *ānōh* nMT \<TME\> "there"
>
> *kū* à \<AYK\> "where"
>
> *harw kū* à AWK \<KRA AYK\> "wherever"

#### *ēdar* "here"

*ud [ēdar]{.underline} paydāgīhist wazurg abdīh*

"and here a great miracle was revealed" (*Dk*.7 passim)

*ēn dašt nēk ud gōr [ēdar]{.underline} was*

"this plain is fine and wild asses are plentiful here" (*KN*.2.18/1.37)

*az star-pāyag tā ō [ēdar]{.underline}* 34,000 *frasang. ud az ēn gyāg
tā ō āsmān ī azēr 69,000 frasang*

"from the star-level to here is 34,000 parasangs, and from this place
(here) to heaven below is 69,000 parasangs" (*PR.*46.7)

##### *ēdar* "here, in this case":

*ka xwāstag pad dād bē dahēd ka-iz-iš ō zan [ēdar]{.underline} ēg-iz
xwarišn ud dārišn ī zan abornāyīg abāz āwarišn*

"if someone gives (his entire?) property as donation, also if it is to
(his) wife, then, [in this case]{.underline}, he still has to bring back
(enough) for food and upkeep of his wife (and any) minor child'
(*MHD*.27.6)

#### *ānōh* "there"

*[ānōh]{.underline} kū ka ēd kanīg nišīnēd rōšntar kū ānōh kū ātaxš burz
waxšēnēnd az rōšnīh ī az im tan bē tābēd*

"[there]{.underline} where that young woman is sitting, it is brighter
than there where they light a tall fire from the light that shines out
from this body" (*Dk.*7.2.8)

*Ardaxšīr ka ān saxwan āšnūd menišn ō wirēxtan [az ānōh]{.underline}
nihād*

"when Ardaxšīr heard that speech he set his mind on fleeing [from
there]{.underline}" (*KN.*3.9/2.8)

*[pad ham-ānōh]{.underline} pad Asnwand kōf frāz ātaxš-gāhīhā nišāst*

"(Kay Husrōy) established (*frāz \... nišāst)* (various) fire temples
there [in that very place]{.underline} on Mount Asnwand" (*Bd*.18.8^12^)

#### *kū* "where, where?"

*[ānōh]{.underline} frāz mad hēnd [kū]{.underline} 2 murw pad
pus-xwāyišnīh nišast hēnd*

"they arrived [there where]{.underline} two birds were sitting (engaged)
in 'seeking a son' (= having sex)" (*Dk*.7.2.24)

*kū panǰom ēn zamīg āsāntom kū mēnōy ēn zamīg āsānīh az čē wēš*

*u-š guft Ohrmazd kū pad ān abar frāyist mēzēnd pah ud stōr [ān gyāg kū
padiš]{.underline} parwarēnd*

"[Where]{.underline} fifthly (in) this earth is it the most peaceful,
i.e., from what is there most peace for the Spirit of the Earth?

And Ohrmazd said: whereone small and large cattle urinate the most
(i.e.) [in the place where]{.underline} they raise them" (*PV*.3.6bc)

*[kū]{.underline} fradom ēn zamīg an-āsāntom kū mēnōy ī ēn zamīg
dušxwārīh az čē wēš*

*u-š guft Ohrmazd kū pad Arzūr grīwag Spitāmān Zardušt pad dar ī dōšox*

"[Where]{.underline} firstly (in) this earth is it the most unpeaceful,
i.e., from what is there most discomfort for the Spirit of the Earth?

And Ohrmazd said: on the Ridge of Arzūr, Spitāmān Zardušt, at the gate
of hell" (*PV*.3.7bc)

*harw kū*

This adverb functions as an imperative, even replacing the imperatives

"Come here, so that I can hand over to you the treasure and property of
your fathers (and) grandfatehrs!" (AJ̌.16.46)

drōzan būd*

"[you are not welcome]{.underline}, (you) magician sorcerer, for your

### "direction"

Direction is most commonly expressed by suffixing *-rōn* to adverbs and
*-nēmag* "side" to nouns and adverbs; *‑ālag* "side" is occasionally
found with nouns.

#### With *-rōn*

The compounds in *-rōn* are very common from the inscriptions on.

*\... rōn* WWwL \... \< \... lwn\'\> "in the direction of"

*ō \... rōn* WWwL \... OW \<OL \... lwn\'\> "toward, to (the direction
of)"

*az \... rōn* WWwL \... N \<MN \... lwn\'\> "from (the direction of)"

*andarrōn* WWwLx , WWwlYwA \<'ndlwn\', BYN-lwn\'\> "inside"

*bērōn* WWwlYB \<bylwn\'\> "out(side)"

*ōrrōn* WWwLwA \<'wlwn\'\> "hither, on this side"

*az \... ōrrōn* WWwLwA \... N \<MN \... 'wlwn\'\> "from \... hither,
from \... until now"

*parrōn* WWwLP \<plwn\'\> "thither, on the farther side"

*ulrōn* WWwL a¬aÒ "upward"

*frōdrōn* WWwL WTwLP \<plwtlwn\'\> "downward"

Note: *ōrrōn* was long thought to be *ō-rōn*.

Here probably also belong:

*frārōn* WWwlaÒP \<pl'lwn\'\> "\*forward" ⇾ "'morally' good"

*abārōn* WWwlApA \<'p̄'lwn\'\> "\*backward" ⇾ "'morally' bad"

"Go in that direction!" (PV.21.4d; gloss to *parrōn*)

##### *\*frōdrōn* "downward"

Only *ō frōd rōn* (?):

*ān*)

##### *az andarrōn-/andarg-nēmag* "inside, within"

*ma-iz pas-iz mazdēsn ān zamīg kārēnd ud ma āb abar hilēnd kū pad ān
abar sag ayāb mard bē widerd [az andarrōn-nēmag ī]{.underline}
sāl-drahnāy*

water upon it, on which (*kū pad ān abar*) a dog or man has passed away
[inside]{.underline} a year" (*PV*.6.2a)

*nē pēm panīr ud zōhr ud gōšt zōhrag ō barsom abar barišn [az
andarrōn-nēmag ī]{.underline} sāl-drahnāy*

neither milk, cheese libations nor meat oblations should be brought onto
the barsom [inside]{.underline} (for the duration of) a year"
(*PV*.7.77b)

See also examples under *nigūn* and *rōn* (above).

[*ān ālag*\$\$]{.underline} "in that direction" (*ŠĒ*.18)

"those (waters) stand in well-springs [inside]{.underline} the ocean"

"let them place then on the ground, [inside]{.underline} the house!"

parrōntar az anyān mazdēsnān*

"let him sit in a secluded place, [inside]{.underline} the house,
farther away from the other Mazdeans!" (*PV*.9.33a)

*ēn-iz kū ma-iz tō* pad *[nigūn-ālagīh]{.underline} pad hammōzišn

dōšox*

"and this too: let them not deceive you [by downward-ness]{.underline}
by (their) teaching, i.e., they deceive you in such a way that you fall

#### *kōs* "side"

*ham dēnīg parwand dēnīg nīrangīhā pērāmōn ī tan azabar ī ān ī wahumanīg
wastarg haspīhēd čiyōn ham-kōs-parwandišnīh ī xrad kē-š dēn tōmag*

"that very (*ham*) girdle of the Dēn (the kusti) is fastened around the
body above the garment of Wahuman (the shirt), like the girding of
wisdom on all sides, which is the seed of the Dēn" (*DD*.38.22)

#### Phrases with *gyāg* "place"

##### *abar/pad gyāg* "on the spot":

*gōr abar gyāg murd*

"the wild ass died [on the spot]{.underline}" (KN)

*kē margarzān ka ō dād weh-dēnān āyēd [pad gyāg]{.underline} ahlaw
bawēd*

"he (someone) who is *mararzān*, when he comes to the law of those of
the good Dēn, becomes Righteous [on the spot]{.underline}" (*PR*.7.4)

##### *pad gyāg* "in (one's proper) place, present, appropriate"

*kanīzag [pad gyāg]{.underline} nē būd*

"the young woman was not [in]{.underline} (her) [place]{.underline}
(present)" (*KN*.4.1/3.1)

*Ahrimen-iz gētīy pahikārišnīg škastan nē tuwān*

*nē-iz mārīg-ēw andar abestāg ud zand pad hambasān-gōwišnīh ī ēk ō did
paydāg kerdan ud drīst-dār(īh) ī ham saxwan [pad gyāg]{.underline}*

"neither is Ahrimen able to crush this world by (being) combative,

nor is there a single word in the Avesta and the Zand (or any)
contradictory statement (*hambasān-gōwišnīh ī ēk ō did*) to be found
(*paydāg kerdan*); and it is [appropriate]{.underline} to regard said
words (the Avesta and the Zand) as sound" (*Dk*.5.24.16a)

##### *harw gyāg* "everywhere":

*muhrag ī suxr kē dārēd [harw gyāg]{.underline} abāyišnīg bawēd*

"he who has a red precious stone, will be attractive
[everywhere]{.underline}" (*PR*.64.5)

##### *kadām gyāg* "where?"

*ān wināhgār abāg ān ǰeh ī rōspīg [kadām gyāg]{.underline} šud*

"[where]{.underline} did that criminal go with that whore of a
prostitute?" (*KN*.3.5/3.5)

##### *kū gyāg* "where?"

*u-š guft mēnōy āb kū \... nūn ka petyārag mad ān mizag [kū
gyāg]{.underline} estēd*

"and the Spirit of Water said: now that the Adversary has come,
[where]{.underline} is that (good) taste?" (*Bd*.4.14)

*āmār ī pad ruwān pad wināh ud kerbag kē kunēnd u-š [kū
gyāg]{.underline} abar kunēnd*

*ud ka-šān pādifrāh kerd ēg-išān gyāg kū bawēd*

"who performs the accounting on the soul for (its) sins and good deeds?
and [where]{.underline} do they do it over it?

and when they have punished them, then where will their place be?"
(*DD*.13.2)

##### *ān gyāg* "there, then, in that case"

*ka brād 2 ud xwah-ēw [ān gyāg]{.underline} xwah sālārīh pad brād ī meh*

"when there are two brothers and one sister, [in that case]{.underline}
the guardianship of the sister is with the older brother" (*MHD*.25.15)

*mardōm [az ān gyāg]{.underline} tā ān (ī) ka Pišyōtan āyēd bē ō Ērān
šahr nē āyēnd*

"[from that point]{.underline} (in time) until Pišyōtan comes, people
will not come to Ērān šahr" (*PR*.49.17)

*[az ān gyāg]{.underline} paydāg ī Ohrmazd ō Zarduxšt guft kū*

"[from that place]{.underline} (in the Dēn) it is manifest that Ohrmazd
said to Z." (*ŠnŠ*.9.8)

*rōd Dāitīy [ān gyāg]{.underline} bē āyēd [ī]{.underline} kār pad*
auuaēpaēm *kunēnd*

"the river Dāitīy comes (flows) in [that place where]{.underline} they
perform *auuaēpaēm*" (*PV*.1.2)

*māh pad 1080 rōz abāz ō [ān gyāg]{.underline} āyēd [ī]{.underline}*
(IndBd. *kē*) *az bunīh bē raft*

"the moon comes back to [that place]{.underline} (from which) it went in
the beginning in 1080 days" (*Bd*.25.27)

#### *pēš* "before" (time)

*ud anīz būd hēnd [pēš az]{.underline} Zarduxšt waxšwar ī andar dēn
mazdēsn a-guft nām*

"and there were also other prophets [before]{.underline} Zarduxšt whose
names have not been spoken in the Mazdayasnian religion" (*Dk*.7.1.43)

*kē wars ud nāxun pad nigerišn bē abganēd ēg-iš dēwēzagīh čiyōn kerd
bawēd •*

*ān mardōm kē pad-iz sūdagīh kunēd ēg-iš dēwēzagīh ēdōn kerd bawēd čiyōn
[ō pēš]{.underline} gōwam*

*agar pad kustīg bastan kerbag bawēd ēg xarān ud uštarān ud aspān
[pēštar]{.underline} šawēnd ō wahišt kē šab ud rōz 7 bār ud did pad
aškomb bastag dārēnd*

"if there is *kerbag* in tying the *kustīg*, then the donkeys, camels,
and horses, who night and day have (a girdle) tied around the belly
seven times and again, will go to paradise sooner (than a Zoroastrian)"
(*GA*.10.1)

#### *pēš* "before" (place)

*Gōš-urūn čiyōn ruwān ī gāw ī ēk-dād az tan ī gāw bērōn āmad [pēš
ī]{.underline} gāw bē estād*

"Gōš-urūn, that is, the sould of the Bull-established-alone, came out of
the body of the bull (and) stood [before]{.underline} the bull"
(*Bd*.4a.2)

*ud ān ī ēr ud ān ī abar ud ān ī [pēšīhā]{.underline} ud ān ī
[pasīhā]{.underline} wād čiyōn-im abāyišnīgtar ō sūd- ud hayārīh-abāgīh
ī man tēz ud pattāxt bē rasād*

"and the wind that is below and above, and the one (coming from) [in
front]{.underline} and that from [in the back]{.underline}, let it come
bringing benefit and assistance to accompany me in the way I shall need
it the most!" (*StS*.22.7)

#### *pas* "after, then, next" (time)

*[pas]{.underline} Ohrmazd Ahunwar frāz srūd*

"after (that)/[next]{.underline} Ohrmazd recited the Ahunwar"
(*Bd*.1.28)

*rōz māh waxšēd az xwaršēd [pastar]{.underline} abar āyēd ud
[pastar]{.underline} frōd šawēd ud ān rāy wēš wēnīhēd*

"during the day, the moon waxes (and) rises [later]{.underline} than the
sun and goes down [later]{.underline} , and therefore it is seen more
(often)" (*DD*.67.5)

##### *pas-iz* "even then":

*ōy ī duš-āgāh ud wad-xēm mard [ka]{.underline} was-iz ō burzišn ud
tuwāngarīh ud pādixšāyīh rasēd*

*[pas-iz]{.underline} pad ān nēkīh ud pādixšāyīh burzīdan nē abāyēd*

"the man who is ignorant and of bad disposition, even when he comes to
much praise, wealth, and authority,

[even then]{.underline} one should not praise (him) for that goodness
and authority" (*MX*.56.32)

*ān kē kār abāg wehān wehīh padīred ud kē abāg wattarān wattarīh bē
[pas-iz]{.underline} harw 2 pad uzmāyišn dārišn*

"he whose work receives goodness with good people and he whose (work
receives) badness with bad people---

but [even then]{.underline} they should both should be put to the test"
(*MX*.59.12)

*[ka-iz]{.underline} pad xwarrah-kārīh ud bōxt-pahikārīh ud harw ēwēnag
ī paygāmbarān ud waxšwarān daxšag paydāgīh*

*ud ān ōwōn abāg ēwarīg gugāy wābarīgānīhist*

*[pas-iz]{.underline} rām-šā Kay Wištāsp bīm ī dēn petyārag anīz būd
wihān kē rāy-iš dēn-rawāgēnīdārīh ēg padīrift*

*ka-š dīd wazurg xwarrah ud rāz hammist*

"even when (the *dēn*) was proved to be true by the actions of Xwarrah,
by coming out of the battle safe and sound (*bōxt-*), and every kind of
manifestation of signs by messengers and prophets and that kind of
certain witness,

[even then]{.underline} it was fear of another adversary of the *dēn*
that King Wištāsp of peaceful rule that became the reason why he
accepted to propagate the *dēn*, when he saw the great Xwarrah together
with the secrets" (*Dk*.5.2.11)

##### *pas pas*:

*abar čiyōn padīrēnd payγāmbarān ī pēš az Zarduxšt ēn dēn ud čiyōn āmad
ī abēzag hu-fraward Zarduxšt ī Spitāmān. ud kē āyēnd [pas
pas]{.underline} āwurdārān ī ham abēzag weh-dēn*

"about how the prophets before Z. will receive this Dēn and how the pure
Z. Sitāman of good Fravashi came; and (about) those who shall bring said
Dēn will come [afterward one after the other]{.underline}" (*Dk*.5.1.7)

*ēk ān ī [pas pas]{.underline} az pēš-kēdīgīh ī Zarduxšt abar-gōwišnīh ī
dēn ō Wištāsp ud kišwarīgān paydāgīhist*

one (other thing) is that which became manifest [later again and
again]{.underline} from the prophesy of Z. that he told Wištāsp and
those in his land about the Dēn" (*Dk*.7.5.6)

***hu-wīr** kū abāyišnīg ī purr-šnāsag pad ān ī [pas pas]{.underline}
abāyēd kerdan*

"having good memory, i.e., seemly, fully recognizing what must be done
[later again and again]{.underline} (?)" (Ny.5.11d)

##### *az pas (ī)* "after, next after; from behind":

*az pas ī awēšān 18 rōd az ham bun-xān frāz tazīd hēnd*

'after those (two rivers) eighteen rivers flowed forth from the same
source" (*Bd*.11.2)

*ēn rōd ān was ars ast ī mardōmān [az pas ī]{.underline} widerdagān az
čašm bē hilēnd*

"this river (is made of) those many tears that people let from their
eyes after the departed" (*AWN*.16.4)

*u-[šān]{.underline} warrag-ēw ī abēr stabr [az pas]{.underline} hamē
dawīd ī az ān nēkōgtar būdan nē šāyist*

"and a very sturdy ram ran [after them]{.underline} than which there
could not be any more handsome" (*KN*.4.11)

*dēwān sang kand ud [az pas]{.underline} hamē handāxtand*

"the demons dug up stones and threw after (them) (AWN.49.1)

*dēwān az pas pad mār ī šēbāg hamē zad*

'the demons struck (them) with slithering snakes from behind" (AWN.50.1)

*Ādurbād guft kū margīh wattar [az pas]{.underline} druwandīh*

"Ādurbād said: Mortality is the worst [next after]{.underline}
wickedness" (*Ādurbād ī Mahrspandān ud Šāhān šāh*)

##### *az ān pas* "after that; consequently, therefore" (?):

*ud [az ān pas]{.underline} pad Ōšīdarmāhan hazangrōzim nazd frazāmīh
abāz ō kōšišn mad ud škeft kōšīd*

"and [after that]{.underline}, in the millennium of Ōšīdarmāh, close to
the end, he came back to fight and fought violently" (*Dk*.3.407.7a)

*ēn-iz paydāg kū Ādurbād rāy frazend-ēw tanīg-zād nē būd ud [az ān
pas]{.underline} abestān ō yazdān kerd*

"this too is manifest: Ādurbād had no child born from his loins and he
[therefore]{.underline} placed his trust in the gods"

##### *pad pas* "backward":

*u-š ruwān [pad pas]{.underline} ō dōšox hamē dwārist*

"and his (the slanderer's) soul kept running [backward]{.underline} into
hell" (*AWN*.29.4)

#### *pas* "after, back" (place)

*ēg ōy mar ā-š [ō pasīy]{.underline} gaw abāz rānēnīd*

"then that villain brought his hands (*gaw*: daēvic)
[backward]{.underline}" (*Dk*.)

#### *pēš \... pas*

*Ohrmazd [pēš az]{.underline} dām-dahišnīh nē būd xwadāy ud [pas
az]{.underline} dām-dahišnīh xwadāy ud sūd-xwāstār ud frazānag ud
ǰud-bēš āškarag ud hamē-rāyēnīdār ud abzōnīg ud harwisp-nigerīdār būd*

"[before]{.underline} the creation was established, Ohrmazd was not

*ud [az pēš]{.underline} šud Srōš-ahlaw ud Ādur-yazd ud [az
pas]{.underline} abē-bīmīhā man Ardāy Wirāz*

*frāz ō ān ī tomīg dōšox andarrōntar šud ham*

"and Srōš the Righteous and the divine Fire went [in front]{.underline}
and I, Ardāy Wirāz [behind]{.underline} without fear" (AWN.53.4)

*ǰāmag ud tis ī pad tan dārēd [pēšīh ud pasīh]{.underline} nē āmār čē
harw čē pēštar kunēd šāyēd*

"do not count (= take into consideration) [as being before and
after]{.underline} of the garments and (other) things she is wearing
(when she starts menstruating), for it is OK the sooner she does it"
(*ZFJ*.566--7)

*u-š ō ōy druz guft kū Zarduxšt ī Spitāmān \*az awēšān amāh hēm kē
mādagān nēkōg [az pēšīy]{.underline}-nēmag ud duš-zišt [az
pasīy]{.underline}* (\<AHLyh\>)

"and the lie-demon said to him: Spitama Zarduxšt, we are of those who
(are) pretty females [from the front]{.underline} and very ugly [from
the back]{.underline}" (*Dk*.7.4.59)

*az-iz ēd dar pōryōtkēšān [pēšīy]{.underline} xēm wirāstan

Note *pēš* 'the next" in the sense of what is before one and has not yet

*andar J̌ud-dēw-dād haft ēwēnag tis guft estēd ka mard wihān ī margīh ān
bawēd tā [gāh ī pēš]{.underline} padiš andar āyēd Nasrušt abar nē
dwārēd*

does not rush upon him until it comes into (it becomes) [the next
*gāh*]{.underline} (time of the day)" (*ŠnŠ*.10.32)

#### Phrases with *gāh* "(special) time"

#### *gāh* "(special) time"

See also Lesson 22 on the times of the day, etc.

and the goodness of paradise and the evil of hell [at that

*Ardawān hambun-iz nē pād aweštāft*

"Ardawān did not linger at all, (but) made haste;

when he came to another place, he asked the people (there): "[what

*ud [pad hamāg gāh]{.underline} sagr ud padēx bē bawēnd ud tis-iz

##### *gāh gāh* (*ēw gāh gāh*) "occasionally, once in a while" *or* "again and again"?:

#### *ǰud*

#####

7 kay harwīn kas ōšōmand*

severn *kay*s, all persons are mortal" (*PN*.15; cf. Pers. *be-joz*
\$\$)

##### *ǰudīy*:

This rare form is used with *kun-* to mean "separate." The formation is
like *wanīy kun-*. In the followong passage, Mihrābān in the ms. L4
wrote 1YtDwY \<ywytyD\>, but in K1 he wrote the more common form
*ǰudāg*.

*pad-im kadār gōwišn wānē kū-m stōw bē kunē u-m pad kadār gōwišn bē
ačārēnē kū-m az dām [ǰudīy]{.underline} bē [kunē]{.underline}*

"With which utterance will you vanquish me, i.e., will you suppress me?
And with which utterance will you disable me, i.e., will you separate me
from the creation?" (*PV*.19.8b; the Foul Spirit speaking to Ohrmazd)

*dagr* "long"

Note the following expression:

*[dagr nē mad]{.underline} kū Ādurbād rāy frazend-ēw būd*

"[it did not take long]{.underline} before Ādurbād got a child" (*Andarz
ī Anōšag-Ruwan Ādurbād Mārspandān* 1)

\[Answer\] Yes, people belong to Ohrmazd by having faith in the Good Dēn
by the choice (inspired) by (their) wisdom.

And (they) belong to Ohrmazd in particular by being more inside the Good
Dēn.

By being most inside the Good Dēn, they are equal to the gods.

And they are outside belonging to Ohrmazd by not having faith in the
Good Dēn.

And they are more outside Ohrmazd by having faith in the Worse (Dēn).

And by being most inside the Worse (Dēn), they are equal to the demons.

## Subordinating conjunctions

*agar* (WtÅ HT\') "if"

*čē* (nM ME) "because"

*čiyōn* (\$\$) "because"

*ka* (tÂA AMT) "when"

*kū* (à AYK) "that, than, where"

*tā* (YW , Y\>W OD) "so that"

*ma agar* (WtÅ oA AL HT\') "unless; lest (with verbs of fearing)"

*[ma agar]{.underline} az ēn hād kū agar ēw-bār ō ahlāyīh taft ham
hagriz bē nē absard ham* "unless it is for this reason: If once I became
incensed for Righteousness, I never cooled off" (*Dk*.6D.10)

*Ardašīr tarsīd kū [ma agar]{.underline} mardōm ī deh wenēnd ud šnāsēnd
ud griftār kunēnd* "Ardashir was afraid that the people of the village
might see, recognize, and (capture (them)" (KN)

*[kū ma]{.underline} pad wēš-zīyišnīh pad tuhīgīh ī az pahlomīh wināhād
rasād ō wattom rāyēnišnīh ī ast druwandīh*

(*Dk*.3.106.4)

The conjunctions *ēg*, *ka*, and *kū* commonly take enclitic pronouns:

*ēg-im* (MwsA), *ka-t* (TtÂA), *kū-š* (Íà), etc.

*čiyōn ka*:

*dīd čiyōn ka xwaršēd az sar ī Sāsān bē tāft*

### Nominal---"that"---clauses

Note: *kū* is the most common Pahlavi conjunction and in addition to its
local meanings has the very general meaning of "that," "because," and
"so/in order that"; it also introduces explanations: "namely, that is."

*kū* "that":

*čiyōn dēn gōwēd kū*

*ēn-iz guft kū*

*mowbedān mowbed ka-š dīd kū \...* "when the supreme mowbed saw that
\..."

*u-š bē\--z nigerīd kū*

*Pābag nē dānist kū*

*u-š čim ēn kū*

*ka dānēd kū kū ka-iz nē dānēd* "When he knows where (it is) and when he
does not know" (*Dk*.8.19.60)

*[bīm]{.underline} ī [az]{.underline} [ān]{.underline} rāy
[kū]{.underline} agar-išān frazendān sidōš nē framāyēnd* "for fear that,
if the children do not order a *sidōš* for them" (*DD*.80.8)

*pad ān kū*

*ruwān ka ō ham rasēnd ān ī ōy ī nēk dastwar ī ruwān-dōst ruwān burzēnd
[pad ān kū]{.underline}-š nē rēšēnēd ud az dōšox pād*

Dk.9.20.1

*agar* "whether":

*frōd ward šnāsam agar tō hē Spandarmad* "come down (so) I may know
whether you are Spandarmad"

## Adverbial clauses of result

Subordinate clauses introduced by *ī* and *kū*

The relative particle is occasionally used where we might expect *kū*,
most often in clauses of comparison, but sometimes elsewhere:

ō*wōn (\...) ī*, *ēdōn (\...) ī*

būd*

With comparatives:

### Use of *And* and *čand*

##### Combinations with *and* and *čand*:

*ēn-and*, *ēd-and* "this much/many"

*ān-and* "that much/many"

*ān-and \... čand* "(x times) as much/many \... as"

*ham-and \... čand* "just as much/many \... as"

*andak andak* "little by little"

*čand-ēw* "several, a few"

*ēw*-*čand* "a little, a few, some"

*gyāg-ēw frāz mad ham u-m dīd ruwān ī mardōm [ēw-čand]{.underline} kē
pad ham estād hēnd* "I came to a place, and I saw [some]{.underline}
people who stood together" (*AWN*.6.1)

*and čand* (YWC YwA, YWcDwA \<'nd-cnd\>) "as/so much/many as," *and \...
čand* "as/so (much/many) \... as"

*harw čand* "however much"

Examples:

#### *and* "so much":

*az and sāl* "for/since so many years"

#### *čand \... and*

Word order imitating Avestan:

*[čand]{.underline} xwāstār ud tuwānīg ham [ān-and]{.underline}
hammōxtam xwāyišn ī ahlāyīh kār ud kerbag*

"[as much as]{.underline} I am seeking and have the strength, [that
much]{.underline} I learn the seeking of Righteousness, (i.e.) work and
good deeds" (*PY*.28.4c)

#### *čand* + comparative/superlative "the \...-er the \...-er," "as much as possible": 

This phrase often includes *šāyēd* "is possible," e.g.:

*[čand]{.underline} wad-āmēzišnīh [wēš]{.underline} wād ī bazag
[stahmagtar]{.underline}*

thereby" (*StS*.23.2)

*[čand]{.underline} dāšn [purrtar]{.underline} dahīhēd kerbag meh-sūdīh
wēš*

"[the more fully]{.underline} a gift is given, the greater the superior
benefit of the good deed" (*DD*.84.2)

*ud agar ka-š wēmārīh-ēw padiš wasān biziškān nigerīd dānāgān passandēnd
[čand abērtar]{.underline} pad yōǰdahrēnīdan ī az ōwōn wizendīg Nasuš
dīd nē āhōg*

"and if, when many doctors have noticed an illness on her, those
knowledgable agree, (then there is) all the more no blemish (attached to

*pad im rāh ān ī widardān tan [čand awināhīhātar]{.underline} šāyēd

"in this way, the bodies should be kept properly [as little exposed to

*ud ān ī and abzār ī az hamist weh-dahišnān [čand

##### *harw dō*:

*xēm xrad andar nēst ud xrad xēm andar ud dēn harw 2 andar xrad ud xēm*

"there is no *xēm* in *xrad*, and in *xrad* there is *xēm*, and in *dēn*
(there are both): *xrad* and *xēm*"

(*Dk*.6.5)

Note the word order in:

##### *was* "enough":

Although this is a common use of Perian *bas*, it is relatively rare in
Pahlavi and found especially in the *ZFJ*, e.g.:

(*ZFJ*.489, 578, 667)

*pad-iz čāštag ī Mēdyōmāhīg guft estēd kū ka ōy kē hamē šōyēd pišag
šnāsēd ēg-iš yōǰdahrgar ēk [was]{.underline}*

And in the teaching of the followers of Mēdyōmān it is said that he who
washes frequently(?) and knows the *pišag*, then one purifier is
[enough]{.underline} for him." (*NM*.1.6.3)

##### *pad was-maragīh* "in large numbers":

"the Tāzīgs in large numbers overran the land of the Iranians"
(*Bd*.33.25)

*u-š aziš paydāgīhēd kū [kē abzār ud kē kam]{.underline} ka-š tis andar

##### *pad wēšīh*:

*9 nāy drahnāy pad drahnāy ud 3 w pad pahnāy pērāmōn bē ē kanēd*

šāyēd*

"let him dig nine *nāy* in length and three in width all around;

when he digs it [more]{.underline}, it is fine, [less]{.underline} is
not fine" (*ZFJ*, p. 622)

##### *pad wēšistīh* "at the most, at a maximum":

*ka parahōm xwarēd ā-š esm bōy ēw tāg az kust ī dašn bē nihišn*

*u-š hōm ud urwarām pad čandīh bē paydāgēnišn*

*hōm [pad kamistīh]{.underline} 3 grih [pad wēšistīh]{.underline} 30
grih urwarām andar ān ī pad nēmag*

"when he drinks the *parāhōm*, he should place one twig of firewood and

and he should advertise the *hōm* and the plant by (saying) how much:

30 knots, the plant \$\$" (*PNir*.28.25)

*tā pad baršnūm w šustan ā-š az āb ud ātaxš [kamak]{.underline}
pahrēzišn*

"until washing with the *baršnūm*, (s)he should stay a little away from
water and fire" (*ZFJ*.538)

##### *pad kamist(īh)* "at (the) least, at a minimum" 

Cf. *pad wēšistīh* "at the most, at a maximum," below.

*[pad kamist]{.underline} pad xīr ī mēnōy pad ēn and gumān nē bawēd kū
harw gōnag tis-ēw ast*

"[at least]{.underline} he has no doubt regarding mattes of the other
world about this much: every kind of thing exists" (*Dk*.6.241)

*abar dād ī Ohrmazd harw ēk az urwarān [pad kamistīh]{.underline} ō ēk
wēmārīh ānāftārīh*

"about how Ohrmazd established each of the plants for removing at least
one illness" (*Dk*.8.37.15)

*pad kemistīh* NM.1.7.1

\$\$

*pad nidomīh* NM.1.7.1

## Expressions of reason and cause

*čim kē rāy* "the reason why"

*abē-čim*

*az ham bun* "for the same reason, from the same cause"

*az/pad ān ī* "because of the fact that"

*(az) ān bahr rāy*

*ēd rāy* "for this reason"

*[ēd rāy]{.underline} star ī agumēzagīh xwānīhēd* "for this reason they
are called 'the unmixed stars'" (Bdh)

*pad ān čim* "for that reason"

*[pad ān čim]{.underline} Haftōring xwānīhēd* "for that reason it is
called Haftōring" (Bdh)

*az ēn/ān mar* "on that account"

*hamāg nēst-tisīh \... bē ō mardōmān [az ān mar]{.underline} mad*
(*PR*.8a.9)

*Bd*.9.45, *MX*.54.5, *Dk*. 6.71, *MHD*.4.10, *AWN*.1.13

pad ēd mar

*pad hu-čašmīh mar pad kas-iz nē drōzē*

"for the sake of benevolence, do not deceive anybody" (*StS*.18.3)

*ē-mar*?

*D*.5.24.22a

mar āyēd "is counted" (*ZFJ*, p. 586)

*čē rāy* "because of which"

*Bd*.21b.4-5

*kē rāy* "because of which"

Note: *kē rāy* can also simply be the relative pronoun + *rāy*:

*[kē rāy]{.underline} kunēd nē framāyēd ēg-iš dādestān čē ast*

"what is the law for (him) who performs (a ritual, but) does not command
(one to be performed)" (*DD*.79.1)

*čē rāy* "for what reason, why"

*[čē rāy]{.underline} xwarrah ī xwēškārīh pad gēhān was ast harw kē ān ī
weh warzēd ud kunēd ā-š arz*

(Bd.17A.1\*)

Note also [pad bahr ī xwēš]{.underline} "on his own account, for his own
part" (*Dk*.6.71, 80)

*az ān jādag (rāy)* "for that reason"

*[az ān jādag rāy]{.underline} ōš pēštar ud margīh saxttar*

"\$\$" (PT27. *Handarz ī Dastwarān ō Weh-Dēnān* 35)

*az ān jādag ōš pēštar ud margīh saxttar* "\$\$"

(*WD*.7.4)

### Various phrases made by repetition

Repetition of a noun, adjective, or adverb is quite common. The list
below is not complete.

On *ēwēnag ēwēnag* and *gōnag gōnag* "of various kinds," see Lesson 17.

##### *andak andak* "little by little":

*andak andak hamē raft*

"it went forward little by little" (*KN*.7.1)

*ud ēn-iz kū andar gētīy mardōm kē sad sāl bē zīyēd kem kū ān kē sad sāl
nē zīyēd*

*ud zīndagīh [andak andak]{.underline} sazīhistan ud hanǰaft zīndagīh
zan ud xwāstag \<ud\> abārīg gētīyīg ādān hamāg pad ēw-bār hištan ud ō
anīy kas madan*

And this too, that in this world, a person who lives a hundred years is
less (rarer) than one who does not live a hundred years,

and that life passes [little by little]{.underline}, and, once life is
completed, that one leaves wife, property, and the other wordly wealth
all of it at once and that it comes to someone else" (*Dk*.9.16.10) ---
(note the infinitives listing things)

##### *āwām āwām* "in various ages, from age to age":

*ud ristag-kunišn nišānīhā [andar āwām āwām]{.underline} ō paydāgīh mad*

"and sectarianism appeared in various ages" (*Dk*.5.3.5)

##### *bāy bāy* "repeatedly" (?):

*abar zamānag [bāy bāy]{.underline} druz ō spenāy-mēnōy dāmān škefttar
kōšišn*

"about the time of the Lie's repeatedly fighting the more fiercely
against the creations of Spenāg Mēnōy" (*Dk*.3.407.1)

##### *dast pad dast* "continously" (?) (NP. *dast be dast*):

*u-š az dēwān garānīhā [dast pad dast]{.underline} rasēd*

"and various 'heavy' (sins) will [continuously]{.underline} come upon
him (the apostate) from the demons" (*DD*.40.4)

##### *ēk ēk* "one by one, individually":

*ēn kū gōspandān ud gāwān ud abārīg čahār-pāyān handām [ēk
ēk]{.underline} kadām yazd xwēš ud ǰud ǰud čiyōn abāyēd yaštan*

"(as for) this: to what god does the [individual]{.underline} members of
sheep, cattle, and other quadrupeds belong and how should one sacrifice
(them) individually?" (*PR*.59.1)

##### *gyāg gyāg* "(in/to) different places":

*mardōmān gyāg gyāg bē burd* "people carried (the plant) to different
places" (PR)

*gyāg gyāg frāz burd hēm* "I was brought to place after place" (AW)

*ēn rōdīhā bun ēk ast ud pad [šahr šahr]{.underline} ud [gyāg
gyāg]{.underline} pad [nām nām]{.underline} xwānēnd* "these rivers have
one origin and are called in various lands and various places by various
names (in each land, each place, by each their names)" (*Bd*.11a.31)

##### *hangām hangām*

harw čē škuftag hu-bōy andar warz ī mardōmān hangām hangām bawēd

(*Bd*.16.13)

tā māh Šahrīwar ī ka ō Šīrāz āmad ham u-m hangām hangām andak ī
pardazišn būd u-m ham pursišn nigerīd

(*DD*.0.15)

##### *huzārag huzārag* "little by little":

*[huzārag huzārag]{.underline} āhōg ī padiš wišēbīhēd*

"little by little, the sins (caused) by it decline" 3.212.10 (see the
Texts)\$\$

##### *ǰār ǰār* "every time, time and time again":

*ka xwāstag ī-išān kerd kū kas kē Mihrēn xwēš būd gōwēd xwēš*

*Mihrēn pad 3 ǰār [ǰār ǰār]{.underline} pad 3 bahr ēw bahr Farrox xwēš
būd guft*

*gōwišn harw 2 kār xwāstag hamāg Farrox xwēš*

"when a property, (about) which they announced (*kerd*): 'the person
whom Mihrēn says it belongs to, (to him) it belongs, and Mihrēn has said
three times, [every time]{.underline}, that one third is to belong to
Farrox,' (then) both statements are valid (*kār*), (and) the entire
property belongs to Farrox" (*MHD*.H4, Macuch chap. 40)

*ēg-im dīd ruwān ī zan-ēw kē uzwān brīd ud čašm kand \... ud [ǰār
ǰār]{.underline} tan ī xwēš pad dandān grift ud gōšt hamē ǰūd*

"then I saw the soul of a woman who cut her toungue and gouged out her
eyes \... and, [time and time again]{.underline}, she grasped her own
body with her teeth and kept chewing the meat" (*AWN*.81.1)

##### *ǰud ǰud*, *ǰud-iz ǰud tan* "separately, individually":

*was dēw būd hēnd kē-šān [ǰud ǰu]{.underline}d duškunišnīh ī xwēš
gōkānīg ōšmurd*

"there were many demons, who enumerated [separately]{.underline} in
detail their evil-doings" (after *Bd*.4.3)

*andar ān stardīh kamālīgān dēwān [ǰud ǰud]{.underline} dawīd hēnd kū
abar āxēz pid ī amāh*

"during that unconsciousness (of the Evil Spirit), the demons with
(demon) heads [individually]{.underline} shouted: get up, our Father!"
(*Bd*.4.2)

*kadār-iz-ēw mardōm handāzišn ī ō ruwān-bōzišnīh sazēd \...*

*[ǰud-iz ǰud tan]{.underline} dēn-burdārān abērtar pad rawāgīh ud
wābarīgānīgīh ud rāst-paywandišnīh ī dēn mazdēsn*

"it is proper for each and every person to plan for the salvation of his
soul \...

for those bringing the *dēn*, [individually]{.underline}, by
propagating, validating, and transmitting it correctly" (*Dk*.3.54)

##### *kardag kardag* "piece by piece":

*ka nasāy ēdōn pūdag ī ka-š ēdōn bē tuwān āwurdan ī ka kardag kardag bē
brīnēd ā pas-iz bē brīnēd bē āwarišn*

"when the dead thing is (only) so rotted that, when one is able to bring
it out in such a way that one cuts it piece by piece (and) then too one
cuts it, (then) one should bring it out" (*ŠnŠ*.2.92)

##### *mayānag mayānagīhā* "in the very center":

*urwar pad ān ī mayānag mayānagīhā pahrēz ud dārišn \... čiyōn-iš
niyābag*

"(for) the plant, being in the very center (of the six creations, there
is) care and uphold \... as is fitting for it" (*Dk*.5.19.25) (the 6
creations: man, beast, metal, earth, water, plants corresponding to the
6 amahrspands)

##### *nē nē* "not at all"

*nē nē-iz* (*AZ*.42).

##### *nōg nōg* "ever anew, again and again":

*[Nōg-nōg]{.underline} dēw ān ī [nōg nōg]{.underline} az wināh dāmān
kunēnd awiš ǰahēnd*

"the demon [Again-and-again]{.underline} is the one who, from the sins
the creatures commit, jumps upon then [again and again]{.underline}"
(*Bd*.27.53)

*ān ī gōwēnd kū ka mard bē ō wināhgārīh wardēd ēg-iš [nōg
nōg]{.underline} ōš brēhēnēnd*

"(about) that which they say that, when a man turns to committing sins,
then they predestine a death for him [again and again]{.underline}"
(*DD*.70.2)

*wārān (ī) az dādār čim niyāzōmandīh ī gēhān nōg nōg rasišn ī huškīh ō
gēhān (rāy?) pad xwēdīh bēšāzēnīdār ud waxšēnīdār*

"the reason for the rain from the Creator is, (because?) the drought
comes upon living beings again and again, living beings' need for
humidity, which heals and makes grow" (*Dk*.3.112.2)

##### *pēšag pēšag* "limb by limb":

*u-š pas pas ka nē [pēšag pēšag]{.underline} bē ēdōn čiyōn zan ī daštān
pad gōmēz ud āb bē šōyēd ā-iz šāyēd*

"and in every following instance, when one does not wash (the person to
be cleansed) by individual limbs, but in the way a menstruant women,
with *gōmēz* and water, then too it is appropriate" (*ZFJ*.629)

##### *rōz rōz* "day by day, daily"

*ud tan-iz ud grīw wirāyišn pad ān čihr ī nē rōz rōz abāg paristārīh
ōwōn wardišnīg būd sazāgīhā*

"and also cultivating (one's) body and 'self' by means of that 'nature'
which will not change like that day by day with (= according to) the
service (one performs, means acting) appropriately" (*Dk*.5.24.29)

##### *tām tām* "very little":

*ka kas xwarišn xwarēd ayāb pad xwarišn ayāb pad dandān dahān brīnēd xōn
āyēd [tām tām-iz]{.underline} sneh āgāhīh bawēd xwarišn ān ī andar dahān
bē abganēd pad ān brīn nasāy šud pādixšāy ka (pad) pišag nē šōyēd*

"when someone eats food (and) cuts (his) mouth with the teeth either on
the food or with the teeth and blood comes (out), (but) he notices [only
a very little]{.underline} sore, and he throws out the food that is in
the mouth, (then), for that piece of *nasāy* coming loose (*šud*), is he
authorized not to wash (with) the *pišag*?" *ZFJ* (TD2, pp. 670--71)

*ēn 3 [wāzag wāzag]{.underline} xwadāyān \... bē šnāxtan \... andar
abāyēd*

"rulers need to know these three individual words" (*Dk*.6D.4)

##### *wēš wēš* "more and more":

*ud \*kē ašmāh was yazēd drōzantar abar-menišntar bawēd*

*ud az ān drōzanīh ud abar-menišnīh mahist yazišn abzāyēnd kū wēš wēš ōh
kunēnd*

(*Dk*.9.32.4)

*ōš ī mardōmān andar [harw zaman zaman]{.underline} frāz rasēd* "a
person's death comes in [any given hour]{.underline} (in each his hour)"
(*Dk*.6.236)

##### *zamānag zamānag* "at various time periods":

*abārīg wasān frahīdagān ēwēnagān ud ristagān ī andar āwām āwām [zamānag
zamānag]{.underline}*

"and the many and numerous other customs and practices [in the
various]{.underline} ages and [time periods]{.underline} (in each age
and each time period)" (*DD*.36.14)

zūd zūd *Dk*.7.7.27

Numerals:

*[dō dō]{.underline} pad āb frōd šawēnd ud abāz āyēnd*

### Negations \$\$

### Adverbial clauses of time, place, and manner

*čand* "as much, as many"

*čiyōn* "as, when, because; that is"

ham-čiyōn Kirm zafar abāz y'p̄t kū xōn xward Ardaxšīr rōy widāxtag pad
zafar ī Kirm andar rēxt ud Kirm čiyōn rōy ō tan mad pad dō škāft (KN
8.10-11)

ud mār ān-iz ast kē zahr pad čašm dārēd ud pad nigerišn mardōm bē ōzanēd

az ān ī ka

Often Pahlavi uses *ka* where we would use "that"

###  *bawēd ka*, šāyēd būd ka "it happens when (that), there are occasions when"

*čē šāyēd [bawēd ka]{.underline} ān kē abāg wehān būd estēd ka ō
wattarān rasēd wattar* "for it is possible (and) [it happens
that]{.underline} someone who has been with the good people, when he
comes to bad people (becomes) bad" (*Dk*.6.178)

#### Embedded *ka*-clauses:

##### *ka* clause embedded in *ka* clause:

*[ka]{.underline}-š* -- *[ka]{.underline} tāyag padiš bē šud* -- *tis ān
rasēd ī-š bē šustan nē tuwān [ā]{.underline}-š dast ōh šōyišn u-š wāz ōh
gīrišn*

"when (= if) -- when the time (= waiting period) has passed for her (*-š
\... padiš*) --- something (some menstrual matter) arrives that she
cannot wash off (because of what she is doing), [then]{.underline} she
should wash the hands in the usual way and she should take the *bāj* in
the usual way" (*PV*.16.11E)

*[ka]{.underline} andar ān tāyag ī -- ka gyān bē šawēd ēg-iš sag ō pāy
bast estēd*

*ayāb warāγ-ēw ēg-iš pad sar hamē parrēd -- [ēg]{.underline}-iš Nasuš
abar dwārēd*

[When]{.underline} (= if) at the time, when the soul leaves, then a dog
is tied to his (= the dead person's) foot,

or (when) a crow then is flying onto his head, [then]{.underline} (at
that time) the Nasuš runs upon him" (*ZFJ*.505)

=

= ka-š sag-ēw andar pāy bast estēd u-š Nasuš abar ōh dwārēd pas ka-š dīd
ā-š zanēd (*PV*.7.2\'A) \$\$ \> Texts

*andar ān zamān ka gyān bē šawēd* *ka-š sag-ēw andar pāy bast estēd
pas-iz nasuš abar ōh dwārēd* (*ŠnŠ*.2.1)

##### *ka* clause embedded in relative clause:

*gōwāgīh ēd bawēd kē ōy kas rāy ǰādag-gōwīh kunēd ī ka-š ān nē ǰādag-gōw
kas-iz ǰādag-gōw nēst*

"'eloquence' is this: someone who advocates for a person who, when (if)
he is not his advocate, (then) he has no advocate at all" (*Dk*.6.91)

which is performed (for him) after (his) passing, is not counted at the
Third Dawn and the Balance, but, at the time when it is publicized, it
comes to the joy of the soul" (*DD*.7.4)

*ka* (tÂA AMT) "when, if"

*ka \... -iz*

(MX.56.32) \$\$

*pas* "after(ward)"

*pas Widrafš ǰādūg abar ō pāy estād* "then Widrafš the sorcerer rose"

*u-š pas mayānag ī zamīg suft* "next he pierced the earth"

Mēnōy pas abar čiyōnīh ī gēhān dām* "that knowledge from the Zand (is)

*dām-dahišnīh ī mēnōyīhā gōwam ud pas gētīyīhā* "I shall talk about the
creation of the creatures in the world of thought, and then in the

The first mountain (that) grew up (is) Hariburz Baγbaxt. And from that,

*u-š ō ōy druz guft kū Zarduxšt ī Spitāmān kū awēšān amāh hēm kē mādagān
nēkōg az pēšīy nēmag ud duš-zišt az pasīy ma man ō pasīy framāyē* "and
to him she said, the demoness \[to Zarduxšt Spitāma\]: We are (those)
who are females (who are) beautiful from in front but very ugly from

## Expressions of (un)willingness

*pad kām*, *kāmīhā*, *kāmagīhā*, *kāmagōmandīhā* "willingly, at will"

*nē pad kām* "unwillingly"

*agāmāy* "unwillingly"

*andar a-kāmagīh ī* "against the will of"

*a-kāmagīhā*, *a-kāmōmandīhā*, *akāmagōmandīhā* "unwillingly" (Man.
*agāmagīhā*)

*xwad-kāmagīhā*, *xwēš-kāmīhā*, *xwēš-kāmagīhā* "of one's own free will"

*pad kām agāmāy* "willingly unwillingly, willy nilly"

*čē-gāmag* etc., see Lesson 12.

Examples:

[*kāmag \... nē kāmag*, *kāmagōmandīhā ud a-kāmagīhā*]{.underline}

"willingly, non-willingly = willy nilly"

*ō ān ruwān gōwēd kū druwand [ka-t kāmag ka-t nē kāmag]{.underline} abar
ēn pad gām raftan abāyēd*

"(its actions) say to that soul: O wicked one, whether you wish or not,
you must step on this edge" (*Bd*.30.27)

*ka-š anāgīh-ēw pad ān ēwēnag awiš rasēd ī čārag xwāstan nē šāyēd
[kāmagīhā]{.underline} pad-iš hunsand bawēd*

"when an evil of that kind comes upon him, for which no remedy can be
sought, he is [willingly]{.underline} content with it" (*Dk*.6.6D.4)

*petītīg būd rāy mādagwar tis ēn kū wināh nē kunēd
[xwēš-kāmīhā]{.underline}*

"as for being repentant, the main thing is this: one does not sin [of
one's own free will]{.underline}" (*MX*.51.16)

*mard ān farroxtar kē čand šāyēd dōšox pad gētīy bē barēd bē ō ruwān nē
spōzēd;*

*u-šān pad gētīy burdan ēd guft kū andar gēhān harg ud ranǰ ī mad nē
wizīrēd bē ka ōh kunīhēd*

*ud mardōm pad čār [kāmagīhā]{.underline} awiš nē šawēnd ǰud az frēzwān

ēdōn-iz abāg duš-xwadāyān*

*ud abāg duš-xwadāyān pad ēd kār kū tā anāgīh kem kunēnd*

'Ohrmazd said forth. Why (*čē \... rāy*) did he (*-š*) say forth: the
Righteous in that world and this world?' (i.e.) for the sake of the
goodness in that world and this world.

'Because of what wish of his did he say it forth?' (i.e.) because of
what need did he say (it) forth?

So that he would be the one 'to make his rule grow', as well as the one
ruling at will.

'As much as' (it is) for 'the Righteous' one should say thus in order
that one becomes 'the one who makes grow', as well as the one who is
'not one ruling at will'.

This means: those who manifest words (to the effect) that just as the
Xwarrah of the Kays (is) with the (good) rulers, it is also with the bad
rulers.

This means: (it is) with good rulers in order that they do more goodness
and with bad rulers in order that they do less evil.

*abar ul hišt ī-š gētīy ārzōg grift ī-š ahlāyīh rāh*

*ēn-iz paydāg kū ka 20-sālag būd [andar a-kāmagīh]{.underline} ī pid ud
mād frāz wašt az xānag bē šud*

*u-š bē pursīd kū kē ast [ahlāyīh-kāmagtar]{.underline} driyōšān
parwardārtar*

*u-šān guft kū ān ī kehist pus ī Tūr ī Urwaytīy kē harw rōz ǰāmag āhenēn
ī asp-bālāy ast*

*purr az nān ud pēm abārīg xwarišn bē ō driyōšān dahēd*

*Zardušt bē ō ān gyāg šud*

*u-š ham-ayārīh abāg driyōšān parwardārīh rāy čand 2 mard ī aγrīy
xwarišn frāz ō driyōšān burd kār kerd*

About he (= Z.) relinquished this-wordly desire and took the road of
Righteousness.

This too is manifest: When he was twenty-years old, against the will of
his father and mother, he turned away (and) left the house.

And he asked: Who is the one who is (*kē ast*) more desirous of
Righteousness (and) and the more caring for the poor?

And they said: That is the smallest son of Tūr ī Urwaytīy, who, every
day, has an iron bowl, deep as the height of a horse, full of bread and
milk and the other (usual) foods (and) gives the poor.

Zardušt went to that place.

And because he shared assistance with the poor and cared for them, he
brought the poor as much food as two prima men (which) did the job.

*u-š xward nē pad* (not TD) *urwāzišn ud frazāmišn bē pad niyāz ī-š az
āz aweštābīhēd* (TD \<'c\'št'p̄yhyt\'\>)

*ud gursag ud tišnag dārēd*

**3.** And the demon Drag-off cruelly leads (the soul) bound, and he
leads him to hell.

And with him are the demons in that world, who were brought into
existence from his sins, in many forms and shapes:

like those who wipe out and those who cause wounds, those who practice
killing, destroyers, ill-shaped villains with sinful customs,

and the uncouth, the polluted, destroyers, biting and tearing evil
animals,

foul winds, dark ones, foulsmelling ones, burning, and .?.,
foul-smelling, inexpiable oness,

and (all) the other many who cause (men) to sin and cause them pain,

who are (all) like those who harm in this world, are with (him) in the
other world.

**4.** And in the same measure (as) the strength and power that was
given to them from his sins,

they cause him pain and harm relentlessly until the time of the
Fraškerd.

And by Wizarš leading him, he comes to hell (but) unwillingly (and) is
brought into the presence of the Foul One.

And he is made to regret the deception from having desires \*caused by
lust.

And he longs for (going) from hell back to this world, and (has) a
fierce desire for good deeds.

**5.** And his food (is) in the measure of that in (this world), (but)
the foulest, most rotted, most polluting, and providing no pleasure in
the highest degree.

And eating is not for pleasure and for becoming full(?), but from need
(to) which he is impelled from greed and (which) keeps him hungry and
thirsty.

*gazāgān*: T has \<p'k'n\'\> with \<p-\> instead of \<yc- = yp̄-\>,
similarly in *frēbišn*, T \<plpšn\'\>.

*nayēd*: 1st time TD \<'yt\'\>, T \<n'yt\'\>, 2nd time \<YZLWNyt(\') =
[DB]{.underline}LWNyt\>.

*Wizarəš*: 1st time TD \<yly'\>, T \<wyl'š\>, 2nd time TD \<wyzlw'\>?, T
\<wyzl'š\>, with the Av. *ə* spelled \<-'-\>.

*hambūsīd*: TD \<hmwwsyt\'\>, with only the down-stroke of the \<-b-\>,
as also in *bēš-kerdārān*.

*handēmānīhēd*: in T, the passive suffix \<-yh-\> is spelled usually
spelled \<-š-\>.

\<wlyk\>*īhā*: editors have read \**waranīgīhā* from *waran* "lust."

# Lesson 23

## The spelling of Avestan words 1. Vowels

Avestan words were adapted to the Pahlavi sound system to varying
degrees. Some became common words, but some were only quoted in special
contexts. Most of these words are proper names of gods, seasons, etc.,
but there are also other technical terms.

Sometimes the names are found in various forms. Quite commonly, a
genuine Persian form is used next to the Avestan form. Occasionally,
more than one learned Pahlavi form of an Avestan word was in use.

See Buyaner, 2009.

Short *a* is sometimes spelled [']{.underline} after *y* before
consonants:

ï\>ΩyM , ï\>ΩadM \<my'zd, myzd\> *myazd* (a ritual meal) Av. *miiazda-*

WtjaDCwY \<ywcy'st\'\> *yuǰyast* (a measure) Av. *yujiiasti* = 16
*hāθra*

The word *ǰeh*, *ǰahī(y)* "whore" (Av. *jahī*), plur. *ǰahīn*, *ǰehīn*,

Imitations of the Avestan spelling as well as other spellings are also
found. The initial \<y-\> often has the diacritic of \<ǰ\> or is written
double, and the Avestan j is often added above the word. The scribes
obviously had difficulties with this word, which they tended to identify
with various other familiar words, e.g.:

PV.7.23-24. -- About eating *nasāy*.

*dādār*

*čiyōn awēšān mard yōǰdahr hēnd ahlaw Ohrmazd kē nasāy frāz xwarēnd ī
sag ī bē widerd ayāb mardōmān*

*u-š guft Ohrmazd kū a-yōǰdahr hēnd ahlaw Zardušt*

*awēšān-iz mard gilistag-kirrēnišn hēnd*

*Abarg guft ay gilistag-išān bē kanišn ud dil-kirrēnišn hēnd \...*

*ēn az Abestāg paydāg*

*ān bawēd ka-š nasāy [pad wināhgārīh]{.underline} ǰūd estēd rēman
margarzān u-š šōy nēst*

*pad ēn nīrang ī az Abestāg paydāg bē ōzanišn*

*ka-š pad [a-wināhīh]{.underline} ǰūd estēd ā-š šōy ast u-šān pad kardag
warr gōmēz ōh dahišn*

Creator!

How can those men become pure, Righteous Ohrmazd, who eat dead matter
from dead dogs or men?

And Ohrmazd said: they are impure, Righteous Z.!

And those men should have their dens cut down.

Abarg said: the meaning is (that) their dens should be dug out and their
hearts should be cut out \...

This is manifest from the Avesta:

That is the case when he chewed dead matter [deliberately]{.underline};
(he becomes) *margarzān* and there is no wash (by which he can become
pure).

According to this ritual that is manifest from the Avesta, he shall be
killed.

When he chewed it not deliberately, then there is a wash, and they
should give him, as is the practice, ash and *gōmēz* in the usual way.

*ZFJ*, p. 670

*kē nasāy [pad wināhgārīh]{.underline} xwarēd rēman ī margarzān šōy
nēst*

*ka [a-wināhīh]{.underline} xwarēd rēman pad pišag šōyišn*

He who eats dead matter deliberately, is polluted and *mararzān* and
there is no wash.

When he eats it not deliberately, he shall be washed with the *pišag*.

*ZFJ*, p. 653

*wināh ī nasāy-ǰōyišnīh čiyōn*

*nasāy [pad]{.underline} xwēš [kāmag]{.underline} ǰūd xwad paydāg čē dil
kandan abāyēd*

*ān ī [agāmāy]{.underline} ud [nē pad kām]{.underline} andar ǰast rēman
ud margarzān nē bawēd*

How is the sin of 'chewing dead matter'?

Chewing dead matter by his own free will is obvious, for one should tear
out his heart.

He who did it unwillingly and not by free will---he incurred pollution,
but does not become *margarzān*.

Additional reading 18.\$\$

From the ZFJ: about

*ŠnŠ*.2.105--6, cf. *ZFJ*.515--6 (Lesson 19\$\$)

*zan ī ābustan kē nasāy [pad wināhgārīh]{.underline}-iz ǰōyēd rēman ud
margarzān u-š šōy nēst*

*ud abornāyīg ka pišag-šnās bē bawēd ā-š warr ud gōmēz ōh xwarišn u-š ōh
šōyišn*

*abornāyīg ī az ēk-barān zāyēd ka-š pid ud mād harw 2 nasāy [pad
wināhgārīh]{.underline} ǰūd estēd ān ī zāyēd pad gyāg pāk čē zāyišn
rēman nē bawēd*

A pregnant woman who 'chews' *nasāy* deliberately is polluted and
*margarzān*, and there is not 'washing' for her.

And when the child becomes (old enough) to 'know the *pišag*', then it
should crink ash and *gōmēz* in the usual way, and it should wash in the
usual way.

A child that is born from a 'one child' (?) (woman), when its father and
mothe have both 'chewed' *nasāy* deliberately, that which is born is
clean on the spot, for being born does not become polluted.

# Lesson 24

## Orthography: special forms of letters

An unusual connection of \<l\> to the top of \<y\> is found in K43,
e.g., ![](media/image150.jpeg){width="0.5in" height="0.25in"}
\<SLYtl'n\>.

In final position, especially at the end of lines, we also find letters
written with an extra flourish, e.g.: òAK (J2) for lAK \<k'l\>;
![Description: Macintosh HD:Users:POS:Files:WMIranian:Pahlavi
Primerƒ:LAWHL K20b
12r.tiff](media/image151.png){width="0.5833333333333334in"
height="0.25in"} \<LAWHL\>,
![](media/image152.png){width="0.5416666666666666in" height="0.25in"}
\<krt'l\> (K20b 12r);
![](media/image153.jpeg){width="0.5138888888888888in" height="0.25in"}
\<''yT \'\> (DD, T60).

Some scribes write final \<-t\> with a flourish like Avestan T (e.g.,
K20). See AWN.4.14 K20, 26.

For cD, we sometimes find ñÁ and ñD, differing from P and cD (e.g.,
M51); for C we find Ñ; and for \<'c\> very rarely a form looking like
Avestan K.

In some manuscripts (e.g., J2), \<k\> is often written with an open
"head," and I \<yk\> sometimes looks like cÁ \<yc\> or P \<p\> (e.g.,
K20b); for \<ZK\>, Mihrābān often writes ![Description: Macintosh
HD:Users:POS:Files:WMIranian:Pahlavi Primerƒ:ZK K20b
14r.tiff](media/image154.png){width="0.25in"
height="0.2222222222222222in"} (e.g., K20a) which in K20b is read as c¸
\<ZC\> . In a few manuscripts (K43), kG \<yk\> is the standard spelling
rather than I \<yk\>.

Some scribes often connect K \<k\> to the left, making it
indistinguishable from \<y\>, but then fairly regularly distinguish the
two by other features, e.g., the top of the "head": T44
![](media/image155.png){width="0.8888888888888888in"
height="0.19444444444444445in"} \<Y[K]{.underline}OYMWNyt\'\>.

The ending aD \<-yh\> is frequently, especially at the end of lines,
abbreviated as óD, in some mss. (e.g., K43) as ‑S. A similar abbrevation
is occasionally found for wY,e.g, óÅ \<'yn\> (K20 f. 102r l. 6). A
similar shape is very occasionally found for final \<y/d\>: óD /óD\>.

There are some special ligatures with \<-z-\>, e.g. z Š \<yz\>:
![](media/image156.jpeg){width="0.375in" height="0.19444444444444445in"}
\<myzd\> (K35 162v), \<mzd\>: M51, 83/19, K18_43, TD23_26,

![](media/image157.png){width="0.7222222222222222in"
height="0.2222222222222222in"} \<YZLWNšnyh\> with \<‑y-\> connected to
the upper part of the following \<-z-\> (e.g., \<w[yz]{.underline}l'š
[YZ]{.underline}LWNt'lyh\> K35 130r); note also
![](media/image158.jpeg){width="0.5416666666666666in" height="0.25in"}
\<YZBHWN-\>.

The actual shapes of the letters vary considerably among the various
manuscripts, e.g., an \<'\> can be connected with a following letter
from below:

![](media/image159.jpeg){width="0.7083333333333334in"
height="0.2638888888888889in"} \<'pyt[yd]{.underline}'lk\'\> *apetyārag*
"without the Adversary" (*Dēnkard* ms.
B:);![](media/image160.jpeg){width="0.4166666666666667in"
height="0.2222222222222222in"} \<pwhl\> (K43 f. 192v).

the word \<byš\> is 2x in the first line, one with regular and one with
pointed y

and at the beginning of the 2nd line with pointed y.

Note how these \<yš\> differ from \<h'\> in \<ch'lyhwm\> "14th\"

## expressions of permission and ability

*dastwarīhā*, *a-dastwarīhā* "(not) according to the *dastwar*s"

*pad dastwar* (*Dk*.9.13.2) "according to a *dastwar*"

*ud-ka-iz-išān pad ān ī niyābag gugārd xwēš tan kē andar frēzwānīg
sālārīh dāštan nē tuwān ahlawdād xwāstan [dastwarīhā]{.underline} [pad
čār ud tuwān]{.underline}*

*az aǰgahānīhā zīyistan ayāb a-tuxšišnīhā xwēš tan kē andar sālārīh
abē-zīyišn bē hišt [nē dastwarīhā]{.underline}*

"and also when they are not able to maintain themselves by what they
have suitably digested, (then) it is [according to the
*dastwar*s]{.underline} to ask for alms [as best they can]{.underline};

someone who has left himself (= leaving oneself) in guardianship without
being provided with enough to live because of laziness of lack of
diligence, is not according to the *dastwar*s" (*DD*.45.7)

*kē-iz [a-dastwarīhā]{.underline} bē ō kas may dahēd u-š padiš māstīhēd
harw wināh ī ōy mast az ān mastīh kunēd ham-wināh*

"and he who gives wine to somebody [against the rule of the
*dastwar*s]{.underline} and (the other) gets drunk from it, (then,) he
(is) participant in every sin (*harw wināh \... ham-wināh*) the drunk
person commits because he is drunk" (*DD*.50.4)

*pādixšāy* "authorized"

*pādixšāyīhā*, *a-pādixšāyīhā* "(not) authoritatively, because (not)
having the authority to do so"

*ka zan ābustan sarmāg saxt rēman bē bawēd ud bīm kū kōdag wizend rasēd*

*bē pādixšāy šustan ayāb nē •*

*bīm ī kōdag wināhīdan pad margarzānīh ī warōmand nē
[pādixšāy]{.underline} šustan*

*agar šōyēd wizend andar-iš ǰahēd margarzān*

"when a woman is pregnant, there is strong heat, and she becomes
polluted, (and there is) fear that harm may come to the child, is she
authorized to wash or not? --- (when there is) fear of damaging the
child, because of potentially becoming *margarzān*, she is not
[authorized]{.underline} to wash; --- if she washes and harms occurs (to
the child), she is margarzān" (*ZFJ*.635-36)

*harw čiyōn-iš weh bē tuwān āwurd [pādixšāy]{.underline} stadan nihādan
kešidan, ǰud az āb [nē pādixšāyīhā]{.underline} burdan*

"in whatever way he is best able to bring (the *nasāy* our (of the
water) it [is authorized]{.underline}: taking (up), putting down,
dragging; (but) carrying it outside (i.e., above) the water [is not by
authority]{.underline} (not autorized)" (*PV*.6.29I)

*gyāg-ēw nibišt kū ka-š pad xwēšīh būd ī dastwarān guft*

*ka-iz ēn nē gōwēd kū-m ka [pad ān dastwarīh]{.underline} xwēš ēg-iz-iš
[pad dastwarīh]{.underline} ī ōy ī guft bawēd kū-m xwēš*

*čē anīy ēwēnag būd nē šāyēd*

*Wahrām guft kū ka pēšēmāl gōwēd kū ēn xwāstag Ādur-farnbay xwēš būd
(az?) Ādur-farnbay ō Mihrēn az Mihrēn ō man mad ud man xwēš ud
[a-pādixšāyīhā]{.underline} Farrox dārēd*

*Farrox pad nakkīrāy pad nē ēdōnīh ī ān hamāg tis ēdōnīh ī xwēš abāz
abāyēd guftan*

"in one place it is written: when he spoke (= referred to) the
'belonging' (*pad xwēšīh būd*) of the *dastwar*s (= what the *dastwar*s
said about 'belonging'), (then) --- even when he does not say this: 'it
belongs to me according to that decision of the *dastwar*s, then, too,
it will be for him according to the decision of the *dastwar*s that he
referred to: 'it belongs to me'; for it can be in no other way;

Wahrām said: when the plaintiff said: 'this property belonged to
Ādur-farnbay; (from) Ādur-farnbay it came to Mihrēn, from Mihrēn it came
to me, and it is (now) mine; and Farrox holds it (i.e., has it in his
possession) without having the authority to do that'; (then), to counter
this (*abāz*) and repudiate it (*pad nakkīrāy*), Farrox must speak to
why that whole thing (what has just been explained) is not like this and
to why it belong to him'" (*MHD*.20.6) --- Note the difference between
*dārēd* "holds/has in his possession" without it necessarily belonging
to him (*xwēš*).

*pad-dād*, *a-dādīhā* "(not) according to the law, (not) appropriate,
(not) deserved"

##### *pad-dād* "according to the law, appropriate, deserved":

*panǰom rawāg-dēnīh rāy kerbakkarān mizd bazakkarān tōzišn
[pad-dād]{.underline} nihādan*

"the fifth (advice) is, for the sake of propagating the *dēn*, to
assign, 'according to the law', reward to those who do good and
repentance to those who do evil" (*PT*.30.11)

*kē xwēš tan pad dādwarīh ud dādestān dārēd ēg sūd ī xwēš rāy ōy ī did
ziyān ud ān-iz ī-š [pad-dād]{.underline} nē nēk sahēd pad kasān nē
kunēd*

"someone who maintains himself in (observance of) justice and the law,
then he does not do damage to another people for his own benefit, nor
(does he do to him) that which does not seem good to him (even though it
is something) he (should do) 'according to the law'" (*Dk*.6C.73)

*kē hu-srawtar -- ān kē nēkīh pad mardōmān kerdan
[pad-dād]{.underline}tar dārēd*

"who has the better reputation? -- he who regards doing good to people
is 'more according to the law'" (*AWM*.141--2, *PT*.24)

##### *a-dādīhā* "against the law, inappropriate(ly)"

*ēn ruwān ī awēšān druwandān kē-šān pad gētīy stōr gāw ud gōspand
[a-dādīhā]{.underline} ōzad kušt*

"this is the soul of those wicked persons who, in the world of the
living, killed and butchered kine and sheep [against the
law]{.underline}" (*AWN*.74.4)

*ēn rōd ān was ars ast ī mardōmān az pas ī widerdagān az čašm bē hilēnd
ud šēwan mōyag ud grīyistan kunēnd*

*ān ars [a-dādīhā]{.underline} bē rēzēnd ud ō ēn rōd abzāyēd*

"this river is all those tears which people shed after those departed
and grieve, lament, and weep;

they pour out those tears [inappropriately]{.underline}, and they add to
this river" (*AWN*.16.4--5)

*kār ud ranǰ bār ī garān a-dādīhā abar nišast ī wattarān nē framūdan ud
[a-dādīhā]{.underline} sālār nē hištan ud aboxšūdārīhā ud ēwēnīhā
dāštan*

*"one should not order* (animals to perform) work and labor (or to
carry) heavy burdens, (or allow) bad people to sit on (= ride them),
nore leave them to someone who guards them
[inappropriately]{.underline}, but keep them with mercy and according to
custom" (*Dk*.5.19.14, cf. *PV*.15.22)

*čāragōmandīhā*, *ačārag*, *ačārīg*

*pad čār*, *pad čār ud tuwān* "when one can help it, deliberately"

The precise meanings of these phrases can be difficult to determine.

\$\$"when one can help it, deliberately"

šāyēd andar gumēzišn ī ō nasāy rāy ōšmārdan ī gand*

"and it is as [inevitable]{.underline} (for) damage to come (to the
creations) in the Mixture as it is also not possible to enumerate (\~
evaluate?) the (amount of) stench on account of (= caused by) something

*u-š [ačāragīhā]{.underline} petyārag a-kār kerdan rāy zamān frāz
brēhēnīd*

*u-š čim ēn kū Ganāg Mēnōy ǰud pad kārēzār nē agārīhēd*

*kārēzār wizārišn ēn kū kār-ēw [pad čār ud čāragōmandīhā]{.underline}
kerdan abāyēd*

"and [having no other way out]{.underline}, in order to incapacitate the
Adversary, he (= Ohrmazd) fashioned forth Time´

the reason for this (was) this: the Foul Spirit is not undone except by
battle',

the interpretation of 'battle' (*kār-e-čār*) is this: one should perform
an action [as best one can]{.underline} and [according to one's
means]{.underline}" (*Bd*.1.36--7)

bawēd* "that person was destroyed (= will be destroyed) who after this
day trusts and relies on any women in the world" (*KN*.9.7)

# Appendix: Adverbs, preverbs, Prepositions, postpositions, and ambipositions

*abĀg* (NTwL \<LWTE\>)

"with, together with"

*Sāsān \... hamwār [abāg]{.underline} gōspandān būd*

"Sāsān was always [with]{.underline} the (domestic) animals"

*u-[š]{.underline} Zarduxšt [abāg]{.underline} rawēd*

"and Zarduxšt walks [with him]{.underline}"

*ka Pišyōtan āyēd ēg-[iš]{.underline} sad ud panǰāh mard
[abāg]{.underline} bawēnd*

"When Pišyōtan comes, then 150 men will be [with him]{.underline}"

*ān mard ī-[š abāg]{.underline} pad asp kē*

"who is that man who is [with him]{.underline} on the horse?"

*kārēzār abāg Kirm kerdan rāy kas frēstīd Burzag ud Burzādur ō pēš xwāst
[abāg]{.underline} uskārd ud was drahm ud dēnār ud paymōzan stad*

"for fighting the battle with Kirm, he sent somebody (to get) Burzag ud
Burzādur (and he) asked them before him, discussed [with]{.underline}
(them), and (they) received much money and clothes" (*KN*.8.2)

"even with, in addition to, despite" MHD \$\$

*[abāg-iz ēd kū]{.underline} hamāg stahmag [pas-iz]{.underline} andar ēn
zamān stahmagtar bawēd*

"[in addition to the fact that]{.underline} (=in addition to the fact
that) they are all fiercely (cold), [after that]{.underline}, during
this period, it is (even) more fierce" (*PV*.1.3)

***nikōhēm dēw** hād [abāg-iz ēd kū]{.underline} ka-m ahlāyīh stāyīd ā-m
dēw nikōhīd bawēnd ā-šān [pas-iz]{.underline} pad ǰudāgīh bē nikōhēm*

"**I scorn the demons**, i.e., in addition to the fact that, when I
(already: in *Y*.11.19) praised Righteousness, the demons will also have
been scorned, [after that]{.underline} I scorn them separately"
(*PY*.12.1)

*[abāg-iz]{.underline} škeft kōxšīdārīh ī druz ud garān wišōbišn ud
zūrīh ī ō dēnīgān mad estēd [pas-iz]{.underline} pad yazdān xwābarīh
nūn-iz radān mowbedān \... pad cand gyāg hēnd kē pad-iz ōwōn dādestān
šnāxtan ud dānistan ī rāh awēšān wišādag* \$\$

*[abāg-iz]{.underline} ān ī zarduxšt az dēn abar wattarīh waštag-dēnīh ī
zahag ī purr-marg karbān ī wištāsp anīz was kay ud karb ī abar dar ī
wištāsp hamīh ī-šān abar ōš ī zarduxšt wirāstan \... āgāh būd*
(DK.7.4.64)

*[abāg-iz]{.underline} xwadāyīh ud pādixšāyīh ī-š abāg
[pas-iz]{.underline} ēd rāy čē mardōmān az wirrōyišn šud estēd nē
abzāyēd* \$\$ (*Dk*.6.21)

*ān y juwān [abāg-iz hunarāwandīh]{.underline} ō ān bowandagīh ī
hunarāwand pad dād-mehīh bawēd nē mad estēd*

"that youth, [even in spite of]{.underline} having all the good
qualities, has not arrived at that perfection that a person of good
qualities has because having reached adulthood" (*Dk*.3.30)

##### *abāg \... ham-čim*:

5.19.24-25

##### *abāg \... hammis*:

##### *az \... abāg*:

*xwēš-pāyagīhā kadār-iz-ēw hu-dēn; ka pad kām xwadāyīh ī-š abar xwēš
gētīy ud mēnōy xūb dārēd rāyēnēd ēg-iš ān pahlomīh ī abar gētīy xwadāyīh
[az]{.underline} mēnōyīg burzišn [abāg]{.underline}*

*"each and every one is hu-dēn according to his own station; when h*e
governs at will the sovereignty he has over his own *gētīy* and *mēnōy*,
then the excellence he has over the sovereignty of his *gētīy* (comes)
[with]{.underline} the approval of (his) *mēnōy*" *Dk*.3.389.10

*[abāg-iz]{.underline} ān ī nibišt kū ka gōwēd kū xwāstag ī ō xwēšīh ī
amāh āgenēn ēd-iz čē ō xwēšīh ī amāh ǰud ǰud mad ān ī āgenēn mad ud ǰud
ǰud mad rāy guft bawēd nigerīdan*

"[and together with = in addition to]{.underline} that which is written
that, when he says that "the property that came to us together and this
whatever came to us separately," (then) one must look closely at that
which came "together" and that which came 'separately'" (*MHD*.20.12)

*az \... abāgīh*

"with, together with"

*ābādīh [az]{.underline} ahlāyīh [abāgīh]{.underline}* "prosperity
together with rightousness" *PY*.28.2 (Av. *āiiaptā aṣ̌ā hacā*)

*pad abāgīh ī*, *pad \... abāgīh*

"with, together with"

*[pad]{.underline} awēšān zēy [abāgīh]{.underline}* 'together with those
weapons"

*abar* (q , Q \<QDM\>)

"on, onto, upon":

This adverb/preverb expresses 1. upward movement, 2. movement onto or
toward. In some cases *abar* may continue an OIr. preverb and have no
specific meaning.

*ō Ohrmazd tar menīd u-š pad ān tar-menišnīh ā-[š]{.underline} zarmān
[abar]{.underline} ōbast*

"he scorned Ohrmazd, and, for that scorn of his, old age fell [upon
him]{.underline}"

*ān xwāstag [abar awēšān]{.underline} pad xwēšīh [mānēd]{.underline}*

"that possession remains [with them]{.underline} as their own"

*abar artēštār ī a-tōšag kē pad rawišn [abar]{.underline} wāstar ud
jōrdāy ud gōspand [frāz rasēnd]{.underline} kē fšēy aziš bēgānag* "about
soldiers without provisions, who, during their march, come across
pastures, grains, and beasts, whose shepherd is absent" (*Dk*.8.22.6)

*u-[š]{.underline} mardōm kē xwarišn nēst [abar]{.underline} [frāz
rasēnd]{.underline}*

"and some people who have no food come upon him" (*Dk*.6E.31g)

#####  *abar* "about, concerning":

*ān zand-āgāhīh nazdist [abar]{.underline} bunyādīh ī Ohrmazd ud
petyāragīh ī Gannāg Mēnōy pas [abar]{.underline} čiyōnīh ī gēhān dām az
bundahišnīh tā frazām*

"that knowledge from the Zand (is) first about the original
establishment of Ohrmazd and the adversity of the Foul Spirit, then
about the nature of the creation of living beings, from the original
creation to the end"

*ud ašwahišt passox gōwēd kū tō [ān]{.underline}-iz āgāh hē abzōnīg
[abar]{.underline}*

"And ardwahišt answers: 'You also are aware [of that]{.underline}, O you
who make increase'" (after *Dk*.7.2.18)

##### *abar* "in addition (to)":

*Ohrmazd pad ān gāh hangerdēnīd-dām bawēd kū kār-ēw [abar]{.underline}
nē abāyēd kerdan andar ān ka-šān rist wirāst*

"at that time, Ohrmazd's creation will be completed, that is, nothing
[in addition]{.underline} needs to be done when they have restored the
dead" (*Bd*.34.22)

##### With *ābustan*:

*pad ham šab [abar]{.underline} Ohrmazd ī Šābuhrān ābestan būd*
(KN.13.22/12.23)

##### *abar ō*:

*pas Widrafš ǰādūg [abar ō]{.underline} pāy estād*

"then Widrafš the sorcerer stood on his feet"

*agar Zarduxšt frōd barēm* *[abar ō]{.underline} astōmandān gēhān*

"if I bring Zarduxšt down to the bony world of the living"

##### *abar pad* "at (the time of)":

*ēg [abar pad]{.underline} ān zamān dēwān hanǰamanēnīd*

"then at that time the demons gathered"

##### *abar \... rāy* "about":

*[abar]{.underline} 5 xēm ī āsrō [rāy]{.underline}*

"about the five qualities of the priest" (*Dk*.8.28.5)

See also *pad \... abar*; *ēr*.

Preverb:

*abar hištan* "let get up" (*AWN*.54.6)

*Sām abar āxēzēd* "Sām rises"

*Kāy-Us abar grift xwadāyīh ī haft kišwar* "Kay Us took up the rule of
the Seven Continents"

*pas ō ātaxš abar mad* "next he came upon the fire"

*u-š zamīg xrafstarān abar hišt*

"And he let loose noxious creatures upon the earth" (Bd.4.15).

*pad marnǰēnīdan tag abar kerd*

"he attacked in order to destroy (it)"

*pādifrāh ī az yōǰdahrgarān abar rasēd*

"the punishment that comes upon (them) from those who make (the world)
ritually pure"

*abar raft hēnd pad xwēškārīh u-šān kerd kām ī dādār*

"they went about their duties and did the wish of the Maker"

*abar raft ō zadan ī an-Ērān*

"he went to crush the non-Iranians"

*ēg frāz raft Pōrušasp u-š awēšān wastarg abar šust*

"then Pōrušasp went forth and washed their garments"

*ēn ān ast ān ī pahlom ēwēnag ī andar frārōn-tuxšīh [abar]{.underline}
xwarrah xwāyišn* (*Dk*.3.135.3)

### *abāz* "back"

This adverb/preverb expresses backward movement and "backward" action
and return (local or temporal), repetition, remainder, and retention
(hold back).

*abāz ō xwēš buništ tābēnd* "they (the heavenly lights) shine back
toward their own place of origin"

*ud tar-menišnīh ī dēn abāz-stāyišnīh* "and the scorning of the
Religion, foreswearing (it)"

*pas abāz ō pēš ī Ardawān šud* "then he went back to Ardaxšīr"

*Ardawān ka-š pad ān ēwēnag āšnūd abāz wašt* "when Ardawān heard that,
he turned back"

*az kū mad hēm ud abāz ō kū šawēm* "from where did I come, and to where
do I go back?"

*Tērag ī Hariburz ān kē-š star māh ud xwaršēd padiš andar wardēnd padiš
abāz āyēnd* "the top of Hariburz (is) the one upon which the stars,
moon, and sun turn around (and) come back to"

*u-m ān zan ud ān frazend ī-š andar aškamb ī mādar abāz ayād būd* "and I
remembered again that woman and the child in the womb of the mother"

*ēdōn čiyōn Ohrmazd pad bundahišn dād abāz bawēd* "as Ohrmazd had
established (it) at the original establishment, it will become again"

*kanīzag ān saxwan čiyōn-iš ō Ardawān guft \... pēš ī Ardaxšīr abāz
guft* "the girl repeated to Ardaxšīr what she had told Ardawān"

*3 rōz abāz būd tā pas bē zād* "3 days remained until he then was born"

*ka az 3,000 sāl gētīy-estišnīh anēbgatīg 330 sāl abāz būd* "when 330
years were left of the 3000 years of being in material state without the
Invasion"

*ān sāl wārān bawēd. sāl ī fradom sē bār pad hāmīn sē bār pad zamestān
abāz estēd* "that year there will be rain; the first year it ceases
three times in summer (and) three times in winter"

*az dām petyāragīh abāz dārēd* "he withholds the adversity from the
creation"

*pad frārōnīh bēš az dāmān abāz dāram* "by doing good I keep harm away
from the creatures"

*ud ka 330 sāl abāz būd* "and when 330 years remained"

*andar* (x \<BYN\>)

*andar* expresses movement inside (and similar) and is used
idiomatically with some verbs.

"in, among; within"

*Ohrmazd bālistīg \... [andar]{.underline} rōšnīh hamē būd* "Ohrmazd was
up above [in]{.underline} the light";

*mān mānāg [kē]{.underline} harw tis [andar]{.underline} pāyēd* "like a
house [in which]{.underline} he guards everything."

*u-š kōšk asēmēn ud dandānag zarrēn u-[š]{.underline} čahārdah kōf
[andar]{.underline} u-[š]{.underline} haft rōd nāydāg
[andar]{.underline} u-[š]{.underline} haft murw kē-š pānagīh pad
xwadāyīh šāyēd kerdan [andar]{.underline}* "and it has a silver turret
and golden crenelations, and there are 14 mountains [inside
it]{.underline} and seven deep rivers [inside it]{.underline}, and there
are seven birds [inside it]{.underline}, which he can protect by his
reign"

*pad-iz kerbag ud kerdagān paristišn ī yazd ud stāyišn ī-š weh dahišnān
[kē andar]{.underline} mardōm ān ī madayān* "serving god with good deeds
and praising his good creations, [among whom]{.underline} mankind is
special" (*Dk*.5.24.26a)

"with respect to, toward"

*Ohrmazd [andar]{.underline} ōy [ačārag]{.underline}* "Ohrmazd (was)
helpless [with respect to]{.underline} (= against) him."

*[andar]{.underline} hamahlān [ērtan]{.underline} ud čarb ud hučašm būd*
"he was humble and amenable and benevolent with respect to (= toward)
those of equal social standing!"

*Dk.*3.175.6

ēk ān ī pad aburd-framānīh ī andar xwadāyān margarzānīhēd

*Dk.*3.175.7

ēk ān ī zan ī kē pad a-tarsagāhīh andar šōy margarzānīhēd

"in, during"

*[andar]{.underline} ān kārēzār* "in/during that battle."

*bē*

This preverb is sometimes used in its original meaning of "out, away,"
but more often it is a purely grammatical particle, whose exact function
is not altogether clear. In most cases it probably indicates finished
action.

*bē* "out(side), away (from)"

*Pābag šab-ēw pad xwamn dīd čiyōn ka xwaršēd az sar ī Sāsān bē tāft ud
hamāg gēhān rōšnīh kerd* "one night Pābag saw in a dream as if the sun
was shining from Sāsān's head and made the whole world bright" (KN)

*Ardaxšīr huram bē būd* "Ardaxšīr was happy" (KN)

*ud nē az tan bōy bē wardišnīh rāy az weh dēn ī mazdēsnān abāz nē estam*
"and not for the turning of the conscience out of the body will I stand
back from the good Mazdayasnian religion" (PN)

*mardōm-iz ka-šān murdan nazdist gōšt ud šīr ud pas az nān xwardan bē
estēnd* "And people, too, when they are to die, first desist from (=
stop) eating meat and milk" (Bd.34.1)

Contrast *andar* and *bē*:

*dēwān xwāhišn ud ōnāmišn ānōh kū Wourubaršn ud Vourujaršn kišwar ud az
ānōh andar āyēd ud bē dwārēd* (Bd.28.21)

*bē*, verbal particle

*Pābag ka-š tan-bahr ud čābukīh ī Ardaxšīr bē dīd dānist kū* "when Pābag
saw the physique and agility of Ardaxšīr he knew that" (KN)

*gurbag ud sag ī andar xānag būd hēnd xwarišn bē xward ud abar \*gyāg
murd hēnd* "the cat and the dog who were in the house ate the food and
died on the spot" (KN)

## Word order. Emphatic word order

Word order can be relatively free. Thus, lowering of subject: direct
object - verb - subject is relatively common. Sometimes it is necessary
to know the context to decide which is which, and sometimes the sentence
may lack a relative pronoun.

*abar čē kerdan ī ka 2 mard-ēw ham-rāh hēnd ēk mard-ēw ī ahlaw bē zanēd
ān ī did ka abē-bīm ka bīmōmand* "about what to do when two men (walk,
travel) on the same road and one is a Righteous man (and) the other
kills him: (2 scenarios:) when there was no fear (it might happen) and
when there was fear" (*Dk*.8.20.3)

or:

"\... one is a Righteous man (whom) the other kills \...

[abē-bīmīh]{.underline} ī-šān \[az kerdan ī ān diz\] [az
dušmenān]{.underline}

[u-m]{.underline} az harw kas [gyāg]{.underline} frāxtar hē

[ān ēk]{.underline} ī pad gētīy [bar]{.underline} nē wēnīhēd

Karišasp guft kū Ohrmazd [wahišt u-m Garōdmān]{.underline} bē dah
(*PR*.18f.16)

"It is said in the *dēn*: Wrath rushed in from of Ahrimen and howled:

'I am not going into the world of the living, for the Lord Ohrmazd has
placed three things in the world of the living that I can not mix
(pollute).'

Ahrimen howled: 'Tell me, what are those three things?' Wrath howled:
'Gāhānbār, the *myazd*, and *xwēdōdah*.'"

## Text 14.3

*Dēnkard* 9.60.4-5

Exegesis on the Pahlavi gloss in Y.45.10: *ahmāi stōi* "for him to be":
*ud ōy estēd* "and for him stands" *Spandarmad pad duxtarīh* "and for
him stands" (i.e.) "Spandarmad in daughterhood (= as daughter)." The
commentator compares the *xwēdōdah* relationship between Ohrmazd and
Spandarmad to that assumed between the *xrad* "wisdom" and
*bowandag-menišnīh* "complete thinking," where *bowandag-menišnīh* is
the scholastic literal translation of Av. Ārmaiti \< *arəm maiti*
"appropriate thinking." This exegesis combines this with the next
strophe (Y.45.10), in which *arəm-maiti* "appropriate thinking" is
contrasted with *tarō-maiti* "inappropriate thinking, scorn," Pahl.
*tar-menišnīh*.

*ēn-iz kū-š [Spandarmad pad duxtarīh]{.underline} ō Ohrmazd čāšt kē xrad
pad bowandag-menišnīh.*

*ēd-iz rāy xrad bowandag-menišnīh andar kanārag hēnd ī Ohrmazd ud
Spandarmad.*

*ud xrad ān ī Ohrmazd bowandag-menišnīh ān ī Spandarmad.*

*ud bowandag-menišnīh xrad zahag čiyōn Spandarmad Ohrmazd.*

*ud az ēd bē guftan čimīg kū kē bowandag-menišnīh ō xrad paywast
ā-[š]{.underline} Spandarmad pad duxtarīh ō Ohrmazd [čāšt
bawēd]{.underline}.*

*ud ēn-iz kū-[š]{.underline} ēdōn ān duxtarīh kunišn [čāšt
bawēd]{.underline} kē ahlāyīh pad bowandag-menišnīh.*

This too:

He has 'assigned' Spandarmad to Ohrmazd as his daughter who (has?)
wisdom with complete thinking.

For this reason, wisdom and complete thinking are next to Ohrmazd and
Spandarmad.

And wisdom belongs to Ohrmazd, complete thinking to Spandarmad.

And complete thinking is the child of wisdom, like Spandarmad (that of)
Ohrmazd.

And from this it makes sense to say that, he who has connected complete
thinking with wisdom, he will (at the same time) have 'assigned'
Spandarmad to Ohrmazd as his daughter.

And this too:

In this way, he has 'assigned' that daughter-hood as worthy of being
performed whose Righteousness is through/with complete thinking.

## Text 14.1

*Bundhišn* 36A.1

"It is said in the *dēn*: Wrath rushed in front of Ahrimen and howled:

'I am not going into the world of the living, for the Lord Ohrmazd has
placed three things in the world of the living that I can not mix
(pollute).'

Ahrimen howled: 'Tell me, what are those three things?' Wrath howled:
'Gāhānbār, the *myazd*, and *xwēdōdah*.'"

### Compound verbs: nouns + verb

There are numerous verbal expressions made with a nominal form plus a
verb. The most common such auxiliary verbs are active *kerdan*,
*dāštan*, *griftan*, *burdan* and passive *būdan*:

*wanīy kerdan* - *wanīy būdan* destroy - be destroyed

*ǰudīy kerdan* separate

*tabāh kerdan* - *tabāh būdan* damage, destroy - be damaged, be
destroyed

*ayād kerdan* - *ayād būdan - pad ayād dār-* remember

*namāz burdan* do reverence (to: *ō*)

### Additional Readings 12.3

From the introduction to the *Dādestān ī dēnīg* by Mānuščihr (*DD*.0.8).
-- Mss. TD4, pp. 169--70, T60a, f. 2v, K35, f. 100v.

*abāg-iz škeft-kōxšīdārīh ī druz ud garān wišōbišn ud zūrīh ī ō dēnīgān
mad estēd*

*pas-iz pad yazdān xwābarīh nūn-iz radān mowbedān dastwarān dādwarān ud
abārīg-iz dēnīgan ud dēnīgbedān ī kustag kustag*

*ud anīz hērbedān* \[TD4_170\] *ud mowmardān ī ōšmurd-mānsr ī
dranǰēnīd-zand ī uskārd-dādestān ī āgāh-dēn ī nimūdār-čim ī
wizīdār-kerbag pad čand gyāg hēnd*

*kē pad-iz ōwōn dādestān šnāxtan ud dānistan rāh awiš-išān wišādag*

Even with the harsh struggle with the Lie and the heavy throwing into
confusion and crookedness that befell those of the *dēn*,

even then, by the clemency of the gods, there are in several places even
now, in several districts, *rad*s, *dastwar*s, judges, and the other
adherents to the *dēn* and chiefs of the adherents to the *dēn*

and other *hērbed*s and *mowbed*s who have memorized the sacred words,
have grasped the *zand*, and have studied the law, who are aware of the
*dēn*, who show its meaning, and determine what are good deeds,

for whom, too, the road to being acquainted with and having knowledge of
the law is open.

Note: *kē \... rāh awiš-išān* for *kē-šān \... rāh awiš* "for whom the
road to (*pad*) \... "
